en: The Mahāyāna-sūtra of the King of Great Teachings: The Samādhi of Direct Realization of the True Compendium of All Tathāgatas, Volume One.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Chao Feng Da Fu, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

Translated by the Dharma-transmitting Master, the Purple-robed Śramaṇa Subject Shi-hu, and others, by Imperial Decree. Part One: The Extensive Ritual Manual of the Vajradhātu Great Maṇḍala, Part One of One. Thus have I heard:

At one time, the Bhagavān, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana—endowed with all the various supreme samādhis and wisdoms empowered by the vajras of all Tathāgatas, and having attained the excellence of all Tathāgatas...
Having received the supreme empowerment of the Dharma King who wears the Victorious Jewel Crown over the three realms,
he is the master of the great yoga of the omniscient wisdom (*sarvajñajñāna*) of all Tathāgatas;

he is able to perform the various activities of the equality of the omniscient seals (*sarvajñamudrā*) of all Tathāgatas, fully accomplishing everything for the entire realm of sentient beings without exception.
The one whose intention is to eternally abide as the great compassion of the vajra body, speech, and mind of all [beings] throughout the three times;
who is exhorted and praised by all Tathāgatas; who dwells within the vast maṇi-jewel palace in the celestial mansion of the King of Akaniṣṭha;

and who is adorned with various colored pearl garlands, necklaces, and bells of fine silk— [He is] the one whose intention... (as above). Please provide the full text for a complete translation. I have provided a translation based on the portion you supplied. If you would like me to continue or refine this further, please provide the remaining text.
Banners were interspersed and draped about, and when stirred by a gentle breeze, they produced harmonious and elegant sounds;
adorned with various ornaments such as half-moons and full moons, he was accompanied by a multitude of ninety-nine koṭis of great bodhisattvas, namely:
the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, and the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sāgaramati, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī,
the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samacittotpādadharmacakrapravartin, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Gaganagañja,
and the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sarvamāramanadalanīya— these and other such Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas were the leaders.
Furthermore, Tathāgatas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges manifest themselves to those devas, even filling Jambudvīpa like sesame seeds.

Within each and every one of those immeasurable and innumerable bodies of the Tathāgatas, there appear immeasurable and innumerable Buddha-fields, and within each of these Buddha-fields, this secret Dharma-gate is once again proclaimed.
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, because all Tathāgatas interpenetrate one another, dwells in equanimity within the vajras of body, speech, and mind of all space.
Because all Tathāgatas are infinite, for the sake of the Great Being of the Awakening Wisdom of the All-Vajra Realm,
he reveals the treasury of wisdom born from the vajra-consecration of all atoms throughout the entirety of space,
bestows the great jewel of the consecration of Great Vajra Wisdom, and extends it pervasively throughout all of space.
Through the wisdom of *tathatā*, one manifests as a perfectly awakened Buddha;
because the intrinsic nature of the bodies of all Tathāgatas is pure, the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is likewise pure.
Because the supreme activities of all Tathāgatas are non-empty, they manifest all forms throughout the entirety of space, leaving nothing remaining.

In the realm of sentient beings, he gives rise to all supreme practices of sublime discipline and extensively performs all kinds of peerless and unsurpassed deeds; from this, all worthy sages are born, namely:
the Great Beings of the firm great enlightenment of all Tathāgatas, and the Samādhi of the Hook-summoning of all Tathāgatas.
The sovereign mastery of wisdom cherished by all Tathāgatas; the well-performed deeds of all Tathāgatas;
the great consecration-jewel of all Tathāgatas; the solar radiance of all Tathāgatas;
the great maṇi-jewel banner of all Tathāgatas; the great laughter of all Tathāgatas; the great purity of all Tathāgatas.
The Pure Dharma; the Great Wisdom of all Tathāgatas; the Great Wheel of all Tathāgatas;
the Secret Speech of all Tathāgatas; the various unfailing activities of all Tathāgatas;
the wondrous, firm, and solid armor of the great diligence of all Tathāgatas; and the Vajrayakṣa who universally upholds and protects all Tathāgatas.
The Wisdom Seal of the Vajra-Bond of the Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas.
A summary verse of these noble deities says:
"Vajrasattva, the Honored Samantabhadra, Amoghasiddhi, and Vajrarāja."
Māra is Vajrarāga; Vajrasādhu is the King of Supreme Joy.
The Noble Ākāśagarbha is Vajraratna; Mahāprabha is called Vajraprabha. Sudratnadhvaja is Vajradhvaja; Mahāhāsa is called Vajrahāsa.
The Vajra Dharma capable of observing with sovereign ease, The sharp wisdom-vajra of Mañjuśrī,
The vajra cause of all maṇḍalas, Speechlessness itself is the vajra speech,
The various activities are the vajra activity, And the armor of diligence is the vajra protection.
Fierce and devouring with adamantine fangs, firmly grasping the adamantine fist;
marked by the adamantine hook, arrow, and joy; the jewel, sun, banner, and great laughter;
the lotus, sword, and exquisite wheel-speech; the karma-armor, fear, and firm persistence.
Beginningless and endless, eternally tranquil; Violent and wrathful, yet profoundly patient.
Yakṣas and rākṣasas, virtuous and fearless; Majestic, fierce, and greatly prosperous.
Umā, Lord of Heaven, and Lord of the World; Firm, supreme faculties, and great silence.
The World-Protectors, those dwelling in space and on earth, the three times and the three realms,
the great elements that perform good deeds for the benefit of sentient beings, and all the ancestors of the Śvetas.
Birth-and-death and nirvāṇa are always thus; that which truly transmigrates is vast indeed.
The Mahāyāna Dharma of the pure awakened nature constantly benefits those within the three realms of existence.
He is the Trilokavijaya born of tranquility; the Lord born of tranquility who is able to subdue;
the firm sovereign of the wondrous and supreme stage; the Dharma of the Great Wisdom Pāramitā.
All the gates of liberation of all bodhisattvas, All the supreme practices of all Tathāgatas,
The perfectly awakened, beneficial mind of all Buddhas— All such enlightenment is unsurpassed.
Vairocana, the most supreme Honored One, naturally upholds all right mindfulness;
The Mahāsattva’s Great Wisdom Seal gives birth to the Buddha-activities of samādhi;
He accomplishes the bodies of all Buddhas and awakens sentient beings for their constant benefit.
That great root is Mahākāla himself; great passionate attachment is great bliss.
He is the supreme among all great skillful means, the Great Sovereign of all victorious palaces.
At that time, the virtuous Great Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, possessing the great bodhicitta, dwelt within the hearts of all Tathāgatas.

Then, all the Tathāgatas manifested themselves, filling this buddha-field like sesame seeds, and having gathered together, they proceeded to the seat of awakening where the Bodhisattva Sarvārthasiddhi was seated. There, they manifested their saṃbhogakāya forms and addressed that bodhisattva, saying:
"O son of noble family!
If one cannot know the true wisdom-patience and the various difficult practices of all Tathāgatas, how can one realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*?
"Therefore, you should now arouse a spirit of heroic vigor for the sake of accomplishing what is to be done.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvārthasiddha, having been thus alerted by all the Tathāgatas, arose from the *asaṃpramoṣaka* samādhi, prostrated at the feet of all the Tathāgatas, and addressed them, saying:
"World-Honored Tathāgatas!"
"Please instruct me: how should one practice?
What is true wisdom-patience?
Then all the Tathāgatas, with one voice and in unison, spoke these words to that bodhisattva:
“O Mahāsattva! You should contemplate the samādhi of your own mind; such practice is true patience. You should then recite the mahāvidyā accomplished through its own nature, as you wish, saying:
‘Oṃ citta-prativedhaṃ karomi. At that time, that Bodhisattva addressed all the Tathāgatas, saying:
"Because all the Tathāgatas have instructed me, O Bhagavān, I see the appearance of a pure lunar disc within my own mind.
The Tathāgatas said:
“Good son! The self-nature of the mind is luminous clarity, just as various cultivated practices are accomplished as they are performed, and just as white cloth is easily dyed.”

At that time, because the self-nature luminosity of the minds of all Tathāgatas was perfected through the fulfillment of their activities, they spoke again to that bodhisattva this great vidyā-mantra:
“Oṃ āḥ jñānamudrābandhaya me. By means of this very vidyā-mantra of natural accomplishment, they caused him to generate the mind of great awakening (*mahābodhicitta*).
At that time, having received the instructions for generating the bodhicitta from all the Tathāgatas, that Bodhisattva again addressed the Tathāgatas, saying:
“World-Honored Ones!
Just as the Tathāgatas possess the mark of the pure lunar disc, I likewise perceive the mark of the pure lunar disc within my own mind.”
The Tathāgatas said:

"The hearts of all Tathāgatas arise from the heart of Samantabhadra; they are equal and firm like well-performed conduct. Because the firm cause of the 'accomplishment of what is to be done' arises from the heart of Samantabhadra for all Tathāgatas, one should contemplate the vajra-mark within the pure lunar disc of one's own heart."
He spoke this great vidyā-mantra:
"Oṃ tiṣṭha vajra. Then that bodhisattva addressed the Tathāgatas, saying:
"World-honored Tathāgatas!"
"I have already beheld the wondrous vajra-mark within the pure lunar disc.
The Tathāgatas said:
"You must make firm this true vajra of the great Samantabhadra-mind of all Tathāgatas."
He spoke this great mantra:

"Oṃ vajratama kuṃkhaṃ. At that time, throughout the entire realm of space, the Great Vajra Realm of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas interpenetrated one another; through the power of the empowerment of all Tathāgatas, they merged into the Sattvavajra.

Then all the Tathāgatas bestowed upon the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvārthasiddhi, who was endowed with virtue, the secret name Vajradhātu, and immediately conferred upon him the consecration by means of the Great Vajra Consecration Rite.
At that time, the Great Bodhisattva Vajradhātu addressed all the Tathāgatas, saying:
"World-Honored Tathāgatas!
I perceive the bodies of all the Tathāgatas as being my own body."
The Tathāgatas said: "O Mahāsattva!

Being fully endowed with the various marks of the Sattvavajra, you should contemplate the images of the Buddhas according to the principle. You should recite the Great Mantra of the Innate Accomplishment (svabhāvasiddha) as you desire, saying the mantra: [mantra]"

"Oṃ yathā sarvatathāgata-satya-haṃ. When all the Tathāgatas had thus spoken, that Great Bodhisattva Vajradhātu, perceiving his own body to be identical with the bodies of all the Tathāgatas and about to attain perfect enlightenment, prostrated himself before all the Tathāgatas and addressed them, saying:
"I pray that the World-Honored Ones, all the Tathāgatas, grant me their empowerment; may the perfect, equal, and right enlightenment I am now realizing become firm in all its applications."
At that time, all the Tathāgatas entered into the Vajradhātu Tathāgata’s Sattvavajra.

Then, the virtuous Great Bodhisattva Vajradhātu, in a single kṣaṇa, having manifested perfect enlightenment through the equalizing wisdom of all Tathāgatas, immediately entered the secret samādhi of the supreme wisdom-seal of the vajra-equality of all Tathāgatas. He directly realized the self-nature purity of the equalizing wisdom of the Dharma of all Tathāgatas and accomplished the wisdom of the self-nature radiance of the equality of all Tathāgatas; thus, he became a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.

Then all the Tathāgatas emerged from the *sattvavajra* of all Tathāgatas; they conferred upon him the empowerment using the great *maṇi* jewel of Gaganagañja, and having well established him as the source from which the various activities of all Tathāgatas arise through the dharma-wisdom of Avalokiteśvara, they all proceeded to the Vajramaṇiratna-śikhara-kūṭāgāra atop Mount Sumeru.

At that time, the Tathāgata Vajradhātu, having received the empowerment of all the Tathāgatas, dwelt in accordance with the principle within each respective direction amidst the lion thrones of all the Tathāgatas.

At that time, the Tathāgatas Akṣobhya, Ratnasaṃbhava, Avalokiteśvararāja, and Amoghasiddhi—these Tathāgatas, by means of the body empowered by the World-Honored One Śākyamuni Tathāgata as the embodiment of all Tathāgatas, because they had perfectly and equally realized all things—surveyed all directions universally and sat down in each of the four quarters according to their respective positions.
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, not long after having realized the awakening of the Samantabhadra-mind of all Tathāgatas,
and having received the supreme consecration of the great maṇi-jewel born of space from all Tathāgatas,
awaited the supreme perfection of the Dharma-wisdom of Avalokiteśvara of all Tathāgatas.
Having attained the *samādhi*, within the unerring and unimpeded teachings on the various activities of all Tathāgatas,
he fulfilled his deeds and perfected his aspirations; for the sake of the empowerment of the very bodies of all Tathāgatas,
he entered the *samādhi* of the Great Bodhisattva Samantabhadra of all Tathāgatas, giving rise to the empowerment of the *sattva*.
The Vajra Samādhi—this is called the Mahāyāna Direct Realization Samādhi of all Tathāgatas—issued forth from the hearts of all Tathāgatas as their own heart-mantra. He spoke this great vidyā-mantra:

“Vajrasattva. As soon as it issued from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, the virtuous Great Bodhisattva Samantabhadra appeared simultaneously as a multitude of moon-discs. Having completely purified the great bodhicitta of all sentient beings, he remained surrounding all the Tathāgatas.

These lunar discs emerged from the wisdom-vajra of all Tathāgatas and immediately entered the heart of the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana; because they are wondrously firm by virtue of the nature of Samantabhadra, they abide in the *samādhi* of Vajrasattva.
Through the empowerment of all Tathāgatas, they merge into a single entity, forming a garland of five-peaked radiance that pervades the entirety of the realm of empty space.

Within this, there appeared the form of a vajra composed of the vajras of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas. This sign emerged from the hearts of all Tathāgatas and rested within the palms of the Buddhas. Thereafter, from within the vajra, there manifested the pure and wondrous radiance of the vajra-sign, endowed with various supreme colors and forms, universally illuminating all worlds.
Furthermore, from the gate of adamantine radiance, there appeared images of Tathāgatas equal in number to the atoms of all worlds,
pervading the entire dharma-realm and interpenetrating one another, reaching the ultimate limits of the realm of empty space and universally filling the ocean-like clouds of all worlds,
fully endowed with the universal wisdom and supernormal powers of equality of all Tathāgatas.
Generating the great bodhicitta of all Tathāgatas, accomplishing the various sublime practices of Samantabhadra,
serving all Tathāgatas, proceeding to the site of enlightenment to crush the armies of Māra,
realizing the fruit of the supreme, equal Great Bodhi of all Tathāgatas, turning the wheel of the true Dharma, throughout the entirety of...
For the sake of all other realms of sentient beings, he extensively performs every act of rescue, benefit, and happiness;
he accomplishes the supreme siddhi of the samādhi-wisdom and supernormal powers of all Tathāgatas, and manifests the playful mastery of the supernormal powers of all Tathāgatas.

Because the nature of Samantabhadra is wondrously firm within the *vajrasattva-samādhi*, they merge into a single entity. From this, the body of the Great Bodhisattva Samantabhadra is born; he dwells within the heart of the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, and utters these verses:
"O, how marvelous! I, the pure Samantabhadra, Am the firm Sattva, spontaneously arisen.
From that firmness which is fundamentally bodiless, The body of Vajrasattva appears."

At that time, the body of the Great Bodhisattva Samantabhadra descended from the heart of the World-Honored One and dwelt in accordance with the principle within the moon-disc before all the Tathāgatas, once again requesting instruction.

At that time, the World-Honored One entered the Vajra Samādhi of the Wisdom of All Tathāgatas, partaking in the ethical discipline, meditative concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation of all Tathāgatas. From great skillful means and the power of great diligence, he arose from the samādhi of great wisdom and turned the sublime wheel of Dharma, extensively providing rescue and benefit for the entire realm of sentient beings without exception.

Acting as the sovereign of all, he caused them to universally obtain satisfaction and happiness, even up to the attainment of the supreme Mahāyāna realization-samādhi and the excellent siddhis of the equal wisdom and supernormal powers of all Tathāgatas. He then placed the vajra of the accomplishment of all Tathāgatas into the palms of the hands of the Great Bodhisattva Samantabhadra—who had been consecrated by the crowns and silken ribbons of the bodies of all Buddhas belonging to the Great Universal Wheel-Turning Kings of all Tathāgatas.
Thereupon, all the Tathāgatas bestowed upon him the name Vajrapāṇi and conferred upon him the empowerment through the Vajrapāṇi Empowerment Rite.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi manifested a posture of lofty elevation; with his right hand, he playfully brandished the vajra, placed it at his heart, assumed a gesture of heroic valor, and spoke this verse:
“This is the supreme vajra Accomplished by all the Great Awakened Honored Ones.”
"Now it has been bestowed into my palm; it abides as the vajra-mark within the vajra.

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the samādhi of the Great Bodhisattva Amogharāja, giving rise to the Sattvavajraketu-samādhi. This is called the Samādhi of the Hook-Summoning of All Tathāgatas.

Then, the hearts of all Tathāgatas issued forth from his own heart, and he spoke this great mantra: "Vajrarāja" (Vajra-ra-ja). As soon as the hearts of all Tathāgatas had issued forth, the virtuous Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi became the Great Vajra Hook of all Tathāgatas. Having manifested, he entered the heart of the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, and merged into a single essence.

From this, the form of a great vajra hook appeared, abiding within the palm of the Buddha. Then, from that vajra hook-form, there emerged Tathāgata images equal in number to the atoms of all worlds, performing such deeds as summoning all Tathāgatas. Having displayed the miraculous play of the Buddhas throughout all worlds, that nature of the King Amogha, being wondrously firm within the Vajrasattva-samādhi, merged into a single unity and gave birth to the body of the Great Bodhisattva Amogharāja. Abiding in the heart of the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, he spoke these verses:
“Great is this Amogharāja of mine! The vajra-born vajra hook, From which all Tathāgatas emerge.”
Universally observing all Buddhas, one invokes them all with equanimity to bring about accomplishment.

At that time, the body of the Great Bodhisattva Amogharāja descended from the heart of the World-Honored One, abiding in accordance with the principle within the lunar disc to the right of all Tathāgatas, and again requested instruction.

At that time, the World-Honored One entered the Vajra Samādhi of the Invitation of All Tathāgatas. By means of this Invitation of All Tathāgatas Samādhi, he universally summoned all sentient beings throughout the entire realm of existence without exception to bring them benefit, causing them all to attain satisfaction and happiness, and even leading them to obtain the supreme siddhi of the empowerment of the assembly of all Tathāgatas.
Thereafter, he took that great vajra hook and placed it into the palms of the hands of the Great Bodhisattva Amogharāja.
At that time, all the Tathāgatas bestowed upon him the name Vajrāṅkuśa and conferred the empowerment through the rite of the Vajra Hook Empowerment.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrāṅkuśa, using the great vajra-hook bestowed upon him, summoned all the Tathāgatas and spoke this verse:
“This is the supreme, unsurpassed vajra-wisdom of all the Great Awakened Ones;
it can summon all the accomplishments of the Buddhas and all the most excellent siddhis.”
The Mahāyāna-abhisamaya-samādhi-mahākalparāja Sūtra Spoken by All Tathāgatas, Fascicle One.
The Mahāyāna-abhisamaya-samādhi-mahākalparāja Sūtra Spoken by All Tathāgatas, Fascicle Two.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Śīladharma, Dharma-transmitting Master and Imperially Conferred Purple Robe, Subject Śramaṇa Shihu et al., by Imperial Decree.

The First Part, Section Two, of the Extensive Ritual Manual of the Vajradhātu Great Maṇḍala. At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the samādhi of the Great Bodhisattva Māra, giving rise to the *Sattvādhiṣṭhānavajrasamādhi*. This is called the "Samādhi of All Tathāgatas Following Delight. Then, the heart-mantra of all Tathāgatas issued forth from his own heart, and he spoke this great vidyā-mantra:

“Vajra-rāga. As soon as this emerged from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that Vajradhara endowed with such virtues became the flower weapon of all the Tathāgatas; having manifested, he immediately entered the heart of the Bhagavān Mahāvairocana Tathāgata and merged into a single essence.
From this, the mark of the Great Vajra Arrow appeared and rested within the palm of the Buddha.

Then, from that mark of the Vajra Arrow, there emerged Tathāgata images equal in number to the atoms of all worlds, performing all the activities of the Tathāgatas according to their inclinations. Having extensively performed these deeds throughout all worlds by means of the miraculous play of the supernatural powers of all Buddhas, that Māra-nature, due to its exquisite firmness within the Vajrasattva Samādhi, merged into a single entity and manifested as the body of the Mahābodhisattva Māra, dwelling in the heart of the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana.
He spoke this verse:
"How great! My own fundamental nature is pure, yet all defilements arise spontaneously within it.
Because it is fundamentally pure and free from all stains, it is therefore tamed by means of those very stains."

At that time, the body of the Great Bodhisattva Māra descended from the heart of the World-Honored One and dwelt, according to principle, within the lunar disc to the left of all Tathāgatas, once again requesting instruction.

At that time, the World-Honored One entered the *samādhi* of the Vajra of Delight according to the Wishes of All Tathāgatas. By means of the *samaya* of the Vajra that Subdues All Tathāgatas, he caused all sentient beings throughout the entire realm of existence, without exception, to feel delight; he enabled them all to obtain satisfaction and happiness, even attaining the supreme *siddhi* and most excellent fruit of the *māra*-activity of all Tathāgatas. He then placed the vajra-arrow into the palms of the hands of the Great Bodhisattva Māra.
Then all the Tathāgatas bestowed upon him the name Vajracāpa and conferred upon him the empowerment through the Vajracāpa Empowerment Rite.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajracāpa performed the act of *māraṇa* toward all the Tathāgatas with that vajra-arrow.
He spoke this verse:
"This is the Great Awakened Honored One of all, Whose stained wisdom is pure and free from blemish.
Because those stained phenomena harm purity, He therefore constantly bestows all peace and happiness."

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the *samādhi* of the Great Bodhisattva King of Joy, giving rise to the *vajra-samādhi* empowered by the *sattva*. This is called the "Supreme Joy *Samādhi* of All Tathāgatas. Then, the heart-mantra of all Tathāgatas issued forth from his own heart, and he spoke this great *vidyā*: "VAJRA-SA-DU.

As soon as it issued from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, that Vajradhara endowed with such merit manifested the form of Vajrasādhu. He then entered the heart of the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, and merged into a single entity. From this, the image of Vajrananda appeared and remained within the palm of the Buddha.

Thereafter, from that image of Vajra-Ānanda, there emerge Tathāgata images equal in number to the atoms of all worlds, extensively performing all manner of deeds such as proclaiming "Excellent! (sādhu).

Having extensively performed deeds throughout all worlds by means of the miraculous play of the supernatural powers of all Tathāgatas, that nature of the King of Supreme Joy, being wondrously firm within the Vajrasattva-samādhi, merged into a single entity and gave rise to the body of the Great Bodhisattva King of Supreme Joy, who dwelt in the heart of the Bhagavān Mahāvairocana Tathāgata.
He spoke this verse:
"How great is this, how excellent is this of mine! This is indeed the supreme wisdom of all.
If one can sever conceptual discrimination, One will give rise to ultimate, great joy."

At that time, the body of the Great Bodhisattva Pramuditārāja descended from the heart of the World-Honored One, abiding in accordance with the principle within the lunar disc behind all Tathāgatas, and again requested instruction.

At that time, the World-Honored One entered the *samādhi* of the Vajra of Equal Joy of All Tathāgatas. By means of the *samaya* of the Unsurpassed Supreme Joy-Wisdom of All Tathāgatas, he performed all acts of benefit and joy for the entire realm of sentient beings without exception, causing them everywhere to obtain satisfaction and happiness, even unto the attainment of the supreme *siddhi*-fruit of the flavor of the unsurpassed joy of all Tathāgatas. He then placed the image of the Vajra-Joy into the palms of the hands of the Great Bodhisattva Mahāpramuditārāja.
Then all the Tathāgatas bestowed upon him the name Vajraprīti and conferred upon him the empowerment of the Vajraprīti Empowerment Ritual.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajraprīti took the image of Vajraprīti he had been granted and, toward all the Tathāgatas, manifested the gesture of the Vajra-Excellent Joy, speaking this verse:
“This is the Honored One of all Great Awakenings, Who can manifest the signs of universal excellence.”
"Skillfully performing all as Hevajra, may the wondrous joy of the Vajra increase.

This is the Great Bodhicitta, the samādhi that summons all Tathāgatas, the great rapture of the wisdom that accords with the defilements of all Tathāgatas, and the Mahāsattva of the Great Samaya of all Tathāgatas.

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the Great Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha Samādhi, giving rise to the Vajra-Samādhi of Jewel Empowerment; this is called the Empowerment Samādhi of All Tathāgatas. Then, the heart-mantra of all Tathāgatas issued forth from his own heart, and he spoke this great vidyā-mantra:

"Vajra-ratna. As soon as this [mantra] issued from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, because of the thorough mastery of the wisdom of equality regarding all space, and because of the wondrous firmness of the Vajrasattva-samādhi, they merged into a single essence. Thus, that Holder of the Vajra endowed with such virtues became All-Light; having appeared, that light pervaded and illuminated all worlds, becoming the entire realm of space.

At that time, the entire realm of empty space, empowered by all the Tathāgatas, merged into the heart of the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, through the practice of sublime pervasiveness. From within the womb of the Vajrasattva-samādhi, which had become the entire realm of empty space, there emerged great images of vajra-jewels and so forth, equal in extent to all world-systems, abiding within the palms of the Buddha.

Then, from within that Vajra-Jewel Image, there emerged Tathāgata images as numerous as the atoms of all worlds, performing the consecrations and other rites of all Tathāgatas. Having extensively carried out the miraculous displays of the supernatural powers of all Tathāgatas throughout all worlds, they emerged from the nature of the entire realm of space and, due to the wondrous firmness of the Vajrasattva Samādhi, merged into a single entity, giving rise to the body of the Great Bodhisattva Gaganagañja, who dwelt in the heart of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana.
He spoke this verse:
"How wondrous is this sublime empowerment of mine, The supreme, unsurpassed Great Jewel Vajra!
Because all Buddhas are free from attachment, It is therefore called the Lord of the Three Realms."

At that time, the body of the Great Bodhisattva Gaganagañja descended from the heart of the World-Honored One and, within a moon disc before all the Tathāgatas, abided in accordance with the principle and again requested instruction.

At that time, the World-Honored One entered the *vajra-samādhi* of the Great Maṇi-jewel of all Tathāgatas. By means of the samādhi of the perfectly fulfilled intention of all Tathāgatas, he caused all sentient beings throughout the entire realm of existence, without exception, to obtain every benefit and purpose, as well as all forms of satisfaction and happiness, even unto the attainment of the supreme *siddhi* of the ultimate truth of all Tathāgatas. He then conferred the empowerment of the *vajra-maṇi-ratna*, the *vajra-ratna-cakra*, and the *vajra-ratna-daṃṣṭra* into the palms of the hands of the Great Bodhisattva Gaganagañja.
Then all the Tathāgatas bestowed upon him the name Vajragarbha and conferred upon him the empowerment through the rite of Vajragarbha-abhiṣeka.
At that time, the Great Bodhisattva Vajragarbha placed that vajra-maṇi jewel at the site of his own empowerment and spoke these verses:
“This is the empowerment for the entire realm of sentient beings, Bestowed by all the Honored Ones among the Great Awakened Ones.”
"Now it has been bestowed into my palm; this is the sign of the Jewel within the Jewel.

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the Great Majestic Radiance Bodhisattva Samādhi, giving rise to the Vajra-Samādhi of Jewel Empowerment. This is called the Samādhi of the Light of All Tathāgatas; then, from his own heart, the Heart of All Tathāgatas emerged, and he spoke this Great Mantra:

"VAJRA TIJA. As soon as this emerged from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that Vajradhara endowed with such virtues became a multitude of sun disks. Having appeared, they immediately entered the heart of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, and merged into a single entity. From this, the form of a vajra-sun disk emerged and rested within the palms of the Buddha.

Then, from within that mark of the vajra sun-disk, there emerged Tathāgata images equal in number to the atoms of all worlds, emitting the great radiances of all Tathāgatas and performing extensive deeds throughout all worlds by means of the miraculous play of the supernatural powers (*ṛddhi*) of all Tathāgatas. That nature of great and wondrous light, being most firm within the Vajrasattva-samādhi, merged into a single unity and gave rise to the body of the Great Bodhisattva Mahātejas, who dwelt in the heart of the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana.
He spoke this verse:
“Great indeed is the peerless, sublime light, Which universally illumines the realm of all sentient beings.
O World-Savior, Greatly Awakened Honored One, You are able to purify all who are pure.”

At that time, the body of the Great Bodhisattva Vimalamahātejas descended from the heart of the Bhagavān and dwelt appropriately within the lunar disc to the right of all Tathāgatas, again requesting instruction.

At that time, the World-Honored One entered the *vajra-samādhi* empowered by the Great Radiant Wheel of All Tathāgatas. Through the *samādhi* of the Light of All Tathāgatas, he caused all realms of sentient beings, without exception, to obtain incomparable illumination and contact, as well as every form of comfort and joy, even attaining the supreme *siddhi* of the light of the self-mind of all Tathāgatas; he then bestowed the mark of the Vajra-Sun into the palms of the hands of the Great Bodhisattva Mahātejas.
Then all the Tathāgatas bestowed upon him the name Vajraprabha and conferred upon him the empowerment through the rite of Vajraprabhābhiṣeka.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajraprabha took the form of the Vajrasūrya (Vajra-Sun) as it had been granted to him and, illuminating all the Tathāgatas with its pervasive radiance, spoke these verses:
“This is the Honored One of All Great Enlightened Ones, Who is able to shatter the darkness of all ignorance.”
"Among the suns as numerous as atoms of dust, the radiance of this sun is most supreme.

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the *samādhi* of the Great Bodhisattva Ratnaketu, giving rise to the *vajra-samādhi* of Jewel-Sustenance; this is called the *samādhi* of the Perfectly Fulfilled Wishes of All Tathāgatas. Then, the heart-mantra of all Tathāgatas emerged from his own heart, and he spoke this great mantra (*vidyā*):

"Vajra-gī-tu. As soon as this [mantra] issued from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that Vajradhara endowed with such virtues manifested various exquisite forms adorned with banners and streamers; having thus appeared, he immediately entered the heart of the Bhagavān Mahāvairocana Tathāgata, merged into a single essence, and from that emerged the form of the Vajraketu, which remained within the Buddha’s palm.

Then, from that mark of the Vajradhvaja, there emerged Tathāgata images equal in number to the atoms of all worlds, establishing the wondrous jewel banners of all Tathāgatas. Having extensively performed all manner of deeds through the miraculous play of the supernatural powers of all Buddhas throughout all worlds, that nature of the Great Jewel Banner—being wonderfully firm within the Vajrasattva-samādhi—merged into a single entity and gave rise to the body of the Great Bodhisattva Ratnadhvaja, who dwelt in the heart of the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana.
He spoke this verse:
“Great is the peerless, wondrous jewel banner! I am the Accomplisher of All Aims;
For those who desire the fulfillment of all aspirations, I shall bring all their undertakings to perfection.”

At that time, the body of the Great Bodhisattva Ratnaketu descended from the heart of the World-Honored One and dwelt appropriately within the lunar disc to the left of all Tathāgatas, once again requesting instruction.

At that time, the World-Honored One entered the Vajra Samādhi of the Establishment and Empowerment of All Tathāgatas. By means of the Samādhi of the Establishment of the Great Maṇi Banner of the Wish-Fulfilling King of All Tathāgatas, he caused all sentient beings throughout the entire realm of existence, without exception, to fulfill every aspiration and obtain all forms of comfort and happiness, even attaining the fruit of the supreme siddhi of the vast benefit and purpose of all Tathāgatas. He then placed the Vajra Banner into the palms of the hands of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ratnaketu.
Then all the Tathāgatas bestowed upon him the name Vajraprīti and conferred upon him the empowerment through the rite of Vajraprīti-abhiṣeka.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajraprīti established the perfection of generosity (*dānapāramitā*) of all the Tathāgatas by means of that Vajradhvaja and spoke these verses:
“This is the Honored One of All Great Enlightened Ones, Who can fulfill all wishes and aspirations.”
"This is named the Great Jewel Banner that Fulfills Wishes, the Dharma of the Perfection of Generosity.

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the samādhi of the Great Bodhisattva Constantly Joyful Root, giving rise to the Vajra Samādhi of the Treasure Empowerment; this is named the Samādhi of the Joy of All Tathāgatas, which is the heart of all Tathāgatas emerging from his own heart.
He spoke this great mantra: "Vajra heḥ svāhā.

As soon as it emerged from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that Vajradhara endowed with such virtues manifested the form of the Great Laughter of all the Tathāgatas. Having appeared, he entered the heart of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, and merged into a single essence. From this, the image of the Vajra-Laughter emerged and remained within the palms of the Buddha.

Thereafter, from that Vajra-Laughter image, there emerged Tathāgata images equal in number to the atoms of all worlds, performing the wondrous deeds of all Tathāgatas and extensively manifesting the miraculous play of all Tathāgatas throughout all worlds. Once these acts were completed, that nature of joy—due to its exquisite firmness within the Vajrasattva Samādhi—merged into a single unity, giving rise to the body of the Great Bodhisattva Nityapramuditendriya, who dwelt in the heart of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana.
He spoke this verse:
"How great is this Great Joyful Laughter of mine! It is the most supreme and most marvelous of all things.
It establishes the manifold benefits for all Buddhas; Therefore, it abides eternally in sublime meditative equipoise."

At that time, the body of the Great Bodhisattva Nityapramuditendriya descended from the heart of the World-Honored One and dwelt in its proper place within the lunar disc behind all the Tathāgatas, whereupon he again requested instruction.

At that time, the World-Honored One entered the *vajra-samādhi* of the wondrous empowerment of all Tathāgatas. By means of the samādhi of the wondrous birth of all Tathāgatas, he caused all sentient beings throughout the entire realm of existence, without exception, to fully perfect their supreme faculties and obtain every form of satisfaction and happiness, even attaining the fruits of the pure wisdom and supernormal powers of the faculties of all Tathāgatas. He then, with the gesture of the vajra-smile, placed [the object] into the palms of the hands of the Great Bodhisattva Ever-Joyful Faculty (*Sadāpramuditendriya*).
Then all the Tathāgatas bestowed upon him the name Vajraprīti and conferred upon him the empowerment through the Vajraprīti Empowerment Rite.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajraprīti, manifesting the form of the vajra-smile, brought great joy to all the Tathāgatas and spoke these verses:
“This is the manifestation of all the Great Awakened Honored Ones, A rare appearance brought forth from within.”
"This great joy and wisdom are well-performed; even other teachers cannot know them.
This is the Great Consecration of the Radiant Wheel, the Great Vajra-Laughter for the great benefit of sentient beings, the Great Being consecrated by all Tathāgatas.

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the samādhi of the Great Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, giving rise to the Vajra Samādhi of the Dharma-Sustaining Empowerment; this is called the Great Dharma Samādhi of all Tathāgatas. Then, from his own heart, the heart-mantra of all Tathāgatas emerged, and he spoke this great vidyā: "Vajradharma.

As soon as it emerged from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, that Vajradhara endowed with such virtues, through his thorough realization of the wisdom of equality regarding the purity of intrinsic nature, attained the radiance of the True Dharma within the Vajrasattva Samādhi. Having manifested, this light shone universally upon all worlds, merging them into one pure and wondrous Dharmadhātu.

Then that entire, vast expanse of the Dharma-realm entered the heart of the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, merging into a single essence. Pervading the full measure of all space-realms, there emerged from it the form of a great vajra-lotus, which remained within the Buddha’s palm.

Thereafter, from that vajra-lotus sign, there emerged Tathāgata images as numerous as the atoms of all worlds, performing all the samādhi-wisdoms, supernormal powers, and so forth of all Tathāgatas. Having extensively performed these through the playful display of all Buddha-siddhis throughout all worlds, that nature of Avalokiteśvara, being wondrously firm within the Vajrasattva-samādhi, merged into a single entity and gave rise to the body of the Great Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, who dwelt in the heart of the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana.
He spoke this verse:
"How great is this ultimate truth of mine! Primordially pure, it arises spontaneously.
All phenomena are like the parable of the raft; therefore, purity can be attained."

At that time, the body of the Great Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara descended from the heart of the World-Honored One and dwelt appropriately within a moon disc before all the Tathāgatas, once again requesting instruction.

At that time, the World-Honored One entered the Samādhi of the Vajra-Wisdom of All Tathāgatas’ Samādhi. By means of the pure samādhi of all Tathāgatas, he caused the entire realm of sentient beings, without exception, to achieve self-purification and the purification of others, thereby accomplishing all benefits and attaining every form of satisfaction and happiness, even unto the fruits of the Dharma-wisdom and supernormal powers of all Tathāgatas. He then bestowed the empowerment of the vajra-lotus and the wheel of the True Dharma of the Dharma-body of all Tathāgatas into the palms of the hands of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara.
Then all the Tathāgatas bestowed upon him the name Vajranetra and conferred upon him the empowerment through the rite of Vajranetra-abhiṣeka.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajranetra, because that vajra-lotus had blossomed wondrously, realized the purity of desire; and because he observed well the stainlessness of intrinsic nature, he surveyed everywhere and spoke this verse:
“This is the Honored One of All Great Enlightened Ones, Who has awakened to the true nature of passionate attachment.”
"Now it has been bestowed into my palm; this is precisely abiding in the Dharma within the Dharma.
From the *Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha-mahāyānābhisamaya-samādhi-mahākalparāja*, Fascicle Two.
The Buddha’s Teaching on the *Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha-mahāyānābhisamaya*.
The Great King of Tantras of Samādhi, Scroll Three.

Translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Imperially Appointed Grand Officer of the Court, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, Great Master of the Transmission of the Dharma, and Saṃgha of Purple Robes, Subject Shi Hu, et al., by Imperial Decree.

Section One: The Extensive Ritual of the Vajradhātu Mahāmaṇḍala, Part Three. At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the samādhi of the Great Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, giving rise to the Vajra-samādhi of the Dharma-empowerment. This is named the Great Wisdom Samādhi of All Tathāgatas; it is the heart of all Tathāgatas, which issues forth from his own heart, and he spoke this great mantra:

"Vajra-tiṣṭha. As soon as this emerged from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, that Vajradhara endowed with such virtues became the Great Sword of Wisdom. Having manifested, he entered the heart of the Bhagavān Mahāvairocana Tathāgata and merged into a single essence. From this, the form of a vajra-sword appeared and remained within the Buddha’s palm.

Then, from within that mark of the vajra-sword, there emerged Tathāgata-forms as numerous as the atoms in all worlds, giving rise to the great wisdom of all Tathāgatas and performing extensive activities throughout all worlds by means of the miraculous play of all Buddhas' supernormal powers. That nature of Mañjuśrī, being most firm within the Vajrasattva-samādhi, merged into a single entity and manifested as the body of the Great Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, abiding in the heart of the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana.
He spoke this verse:
"How great are all the Honored Ones of Great Enlightenment! I am their very name, 'Wondrous Sound.
Because that right wisdom is formless, It is therefore possible for sound to be perceived."

At that time, the body of the Great Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī descended from the heart of the World-Honored One and, abiding according to principle within the lunar disc to the right of all Tathāgatas, again requested instruction.

At that time, the World-Honored One entered the *samādhi* of the Great Wisdom Vajra of All Tathāgatas. By means of the *samādhi* of severing the fetters of all Tathāgatas, he caused all sentient beings throughout the entire realm of existence, without exception, to sever all sufferings and obtain every benefit, as well as all forms of satisfaction and happiness, even attaining the supreme *siddhi* of the perfect Great Wisdom of the Tathāgatas’ Consonant Sound. He then placed the vajra-sword into the palms of the hands of the Great Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī.
Then all the Tathāgatas bestowed upon him the name Vajramati and conferred upon him the empowerment through the rite of Vajramati-abhiṣeka.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajramati took the vajra-sword he had been granted and made the gesture of brandishing and striking it toward all the Tathāgatas, reciting this verse:
“This is the principle of Prajñāpāramitā, The sovereign of all the Great Awakened Ones.”
"It can sever all supreme enemies and extinguish all stains of sin.

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the Great Bodhisattva Samādhi of Turning the Wheel of Dharma through Arising with an Equanimous Mind, giving birth to the Vajra-Samādhi of the Dharma-Sustenance. This is called the Great Wheel Samādhi of All Tathāgatas; then, from his own heart, the Heart-Mantra of all Tathāgatas emerged, and he spoke this great vidyā-mantra:

"Vajra-he-ṭu. As soon as this [mantra] emerged from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, that very Vajradhara endowed with such virtues became the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu, equal to the maṇḍalas of all Tathāgatas. Having appeared, he immediately entered the heart of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, and merged into a single essence. From this, the form of a vajra-wheel emerged and remained within the palm of the Buddha.

Then, from within that mark of the vajra-wheel, there emerge Tathāgata-forms equal in number to the atoms of all worlds. These then give rise to an impartial mind and turn the wondrous wheel of Dharma; having extensively performed all manner of deeds through the miraculous play of the supernatural powers (*ṛddhi*) of all Buddhas across all worlds, that nature of turning the wheel of Dharma with an impartial mind—being wondrously firm within the Vajrasattva-samādhi—merges into a single entity and gives birth to the body of the Great Bodhisattva Turning the Wheel of Dharma with an Impartial Mind, who dwells in the heart of the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana.
He spoke this verse:
“Great is the wheel formed of vajra, Which is my own supreme vajra-dharma;
By merely giving rise to the mind of equality, One immediately turns the unsurpassed, wondrous wheel of Dharma.”

At that time, the body of the Great Bodhisattva Dharmacakrapravartana, having arisen with a mind of equanimity, descended from the heart of the World-Honored One and dwelt in accordance with reality within the lunar disc to the left of all Tathāgatas, once again requesting instruction.

At that time, the World-Honored One entered the *samādhi* of the Great Vajra-Wheel of All Tathāgatas. By means of the *samaya* of the Great Maṇḍala of All Tathāgatas, he caused all sentient beings throughout the entire realm of existence, without exception, to enter the wheel of non-retrogression and obtain all benefits, as well as all forms of satisfaction and happiness, even attaining the supreme signs of the most excellent *siddhi* of turning the Wheel of the True Dharma of all Tathāgatas. He then placed the vajra-wheel into the palms of both hands of the Great Bodhisattva Equal-Mindedness Turning-the-Wheel-of-Dharma.
Then all the Tathāgatas bestowed upon him the name Vajramaṇḍala and conferred upon him the empowerment through the Vajramaṇḍala Empowerment Rite.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajramaṇḍala established the non-retrogressive nature of all Tathāgatas by means of that vajra-wheel and spoke these verses:
“This is the Honored One of all Great Awakenings, The purifier of all dharmas.”
"The Vajra Non-retrogressive Great Wheel—this is what is called the Bodhimaṇḍa.

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the Samādhi of the Silent Great Bodhisattva, giving rise to the Vajra-Samādhi of the Dharma-Sustaining Empowerment. Then, from his own heart, the hearts of all Tathāgatas emerged, and he spoke this great mantra: "VAJRA-PĀŚA" (Vajra Noose).

As soon as it emerged from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, that virtuous Vajrapāṇi became the Dharma-syllables of all Tathāgatas. Having manifested, he entered the heart of the World-Honored One, Mahāvairocana Tathāgata, merging into a single essence. From this, the form of Vajra-Japa appeared and dwelt within the Buddha’s palm.

Thereafter, from that Vajra-recitation image, there emerged Tathāgata images equal in number to the atoms of all worlds, emitting the light of the Dharma of all Tathāgatas and performing extensive deeds throughout all worlds by means of the miraculous play of all Buddhas' supernormal powers. Then, because the nature of that Dharma is inherently firm and stable within the Vajrasattva Samādhi, they merged into a single entity and gave birth to the body of the Great Bodhisattva Avāca, who dwelt in the heart of the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana.
He spoke this verse:
"Great indeed is the natural great secret; I declare this to be the secret speech.
Proclaiming the gateway of the True Dharma in accordance with reality, the words spoken are free from conceptual proliferation."

At that time, the body of the Great Bodhisattva Avāca emerged from the heart of the World-Honored One, descended behind all the Tathāgatas within a lunar disc, and remained there in accordance with the principle, again requesting instruction.

At that time, the World-Honored One entered the Vajra Samādhi of the Secret Speech of All Tathāgatas. By means of the samādhi of the recitation of the speech of all Tathāgatas, he caused all sentient beings throughout the entire realm of existence, without exception, to attain the accomplishment of the secret of speech and to obtain every form of satisfaction and happiness, even up to attaining the supreme siddhi of the secret nature of the speech of all Tathāgatas. He then placed the image of Vajra Recitation into the palms of the hands of the Great Bodhisattva Avāca.
Then all the Tathāgatas bestowed upon him the name Vajravāc and conferred upon him the empowerment through the rite of Vajravāc-abhiṣeka.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajravāc engaged in discourse with all the Tathāgatas using the form of vajra-recitation and spoke this verse:
“This is the Great Awakened Honored One of All, Named the True Vajra Recitation.”
"And all those Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, are those who swiftly accomplish the Great Illumination.

This is the wisdom of the great dharmatā of the Vajra; it is the wisdom of all Tathāgatas turning the Great Wheel; it is the wisdom of all Tathāgatas following and turning the wheel of discourse and playful expression; it is the Great Wisdom Mahāsattva of all Tathāgatas.

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the samādhi of the Great Bodhisattva Skillful Action of All Tathāgatas, giving rise to the Vajra Samādhi of the Empowerment of Karma. This is called the Karma-Samādhi of All Tathāgatas; then, from his own heart, the heart-mantra of all Tathāgatas emerged, and he spoke this great vidyā-mantra:

“Vajra-karma. As soon as this emerged from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, through the wisdom of the equality of all *karmas* and by virtue of being well-versed in the *samādhi* of Vajrasattva, that very one endowed with such merit, the Holder of the Vajra, became the light of the *karma* of all Tathāgatas. Having manifested, that light pervaded all worlds and blended into the great *karma*-realm of all Tathāgatas. Then, that entire great *karma*-realm of all Tathāgatas entered the heart of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, and merged into a single essence. From this, the image of the Great *Karma*-Vajra was produced, its extent equaling the entirety of the realm of empty space, and it rested within the palms of the Buddhas.

Thereafter, from within that Great Karma-Vajra image, there emerged Tathāgata images equal in number to the atoms of all worlds, who extensively performed all supreme activities and so forth. Having widely exercised the miraculous play of all Buddhas throughout all worlds, the nature of those infinite activities of all Tathāgatas—being wondrously firm within the Vajrasattva-samādhi—merged into a single entity and gave birth to the body of the Mahābodhisattva Sarvabuddhakarmakṛt, who dwelt within the heart of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana.
He spoke this verse:
"How wondrous is the marvelous non-emptiness of all Buddhas! Though my activities are manifold, I perform the Buddha-work with effortlessness; This is precisely that which can transform vajra-karma."

At that time, the body of the Great Bodhisattva Sarvakarmakauśalya of all Tathāgatas descended from the heart of the World-Honored One and dwelt, according to principle, within the moon-disc before all the Tathāgatas, once again requesting instruction.

At that time, the World-Honored One entered the *samādhi* of the Non-empty Vajra of All Tathāgatas. By means of the vast ritual manual for all the infinite, non-empty activities of the Great Offering performed by all Tathāgatas, he caused all sentient beings throughout the entire realm of existence, without exception, to attain the accomplishment of all activities and all forms of satisfaction and happiness, even up to the supreme *siddhi* of the extraordinary power of knowledge regarding the vajra-activity nature of all Tathāgatas. He then took that *karma-vajra* scepter—the wheel of all *karmas*—and conferred the consecration of the Vajra-Karma of all Tathāgatas into the palms of the hands of the Great Bodhisattva Vajra-Śilpa-karman.
Then all the Tathāgatas bestowed upon him the name Vajraveśa and conferred upon him the consecration through the rite of Vajraveśa-abhiṣeka.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajraviśva, having placed that Karma-vajra upon his own heart, established all Tathāgatas in the nature of skillful activity and spoke these verses:
“This is the Great Awakened Honored One, Who skillfully performs the most supreme and wondrous skillful activity.
Now it has been bestowed into my palms; Within skillful activity, he establishes skillful activity.”

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the Samādhi of the Great Bodhisattva Extremely Difficult-to-Vanquish Diligence, giving rise to the Vajra-Samādhi of the Empowerment of Karma. This is called the Samādhi of the Good Protection of All Tathāgatas. Then, from his own heart, the heart-mantra of all Tathāgatas emerged, and he spoke this great vidyā-mantra: “Vajra-loccha.

As soon as it emerged from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, the virtuous Vajrapāṇi became endowed with firm armor. Having manifested, he entered the heart of the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, and merged into a single essence. From this, the image of the Great Vajra Armor was born and remained within the palm of the Buddha.

Then, from that image of Vajravarman, there emerged Tathāgata images equal in number to the atoms of all worlds, performing the vast ritual activities of the excellent protection of all Tathāgatas. Having extensively performed these deeds through the playful supernatural powers of all Buddhas, that nature of extremely invincible vigor—being wondrously firm within the Vajrasattva-samādhi—merged into a single entity and gave birth to the body of the Great Bodhisattva Extremely Invincible Vigor, who dwelt in the heart of the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana.
He spoke this verse:
“Great is this armor of my diligence; My firm body is most solidly established.
Because of its firm nature, it is fundamentally bodiless; Thus, the vajra-body performs the supreme deeds.”

At that time, the body of the Great Bodhisattva Sudurjayavīrya descended from the heart of the World-Honored One and, within the lunar disc to the right of all Tathāgatas, remained there in accordance with the principle and again requested instruction.

At that time, the World-Honored One entered the samādhi of the Solid Vajra of All Tathāgatas. Through the samādhi of the Vīryapāramitā of All Tathāgatas, he rescued and benefited the entire realm of sentient beings without exception, causing them all to obtain satisfaction and happiness, and even to attain the supreme siddhi and most excellent fruit of the wondrous vajra body of all Tathāgatas. He then placed the vajra armor into the palms of the hands of the Great Bodhisattva Mahāvīrya, who is extremely difficult to oppose.
Then all the Tathāgatas bestowed upon him the name Vajramaitrī and conferred upon him the empowerment through the rite of Vajramaitrī-abhiṣeka.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajramaitrī, donning the supreme armor against all the Tathāgatas with the vajra-armor, spoke this verse:
"This is the supreme armor of great compassion, The most excellent armor of all the Great Awakened Honored Ones."
"Steadfast diligence is the great protection of the body; this is what is called the Great Compassionate Friend.

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the Samādhi of the Great Bodhisattva Destroyer of All Māras, giving rise to the Vajra-Samādhi of the Empowerment of Karma. This is named the Samādhi of the Expedient Means of All Tathāgatas. Then, the Heart of all Tathāgatas issued forth from his own heart, and he spoke this Great Mantra:

“Vajrayakṣa” (one phrase). As soon as this emerged from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, that Vajradhara endowed with such virtue became the weapon of the Great Vajra-Teeth. Having manifested, he entered the heart of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, and merged into a single essence. From this, the image of the Vajra-Teeth was born and remained within the palms of the Buddha.

Then, from within that Vajrada image, there emerged Tathāgata images equal in number to the atoms of all worlds, performing the activities of subduing through the wrathful manifestations of all Tathāgatas. Having extensively displayed the playful supernatural powers (*ṛddhivikrīḍita*) of all Buddhas, they—whose nature is the destruction of all Māras—merged into a single entity due to the wondrous firmness of the Vajrasattva-samādhi, and gave birth to the body of the Great Bodhisattva Mahāmārapramardaka, who dwelt in the heart of the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana.
He spoke this verse:
“Great indeed is this great skillful means of mine; It is the very compassion of all Buddhas.
For the sake of the peace and benefit of sentient beings, I manifest all manner of wrathful deeds.”

At that time, the body of the Great Bodhisattva Sarvamārapramardin descended from the heart of the World-Honored One, came to rest within the lunar disc to the left of all the Tathāgatas in accordance with the principle, and again requested instruction.

At that time, the World-Honored One entered the samādhi of the Supreme Wrathful Vajra of All Tathāgatas. By means of the Samādhi of All Tathāgatas’ Ability to Subdue the Unsubduable, he bestowed great fearlessness upon the entire realm of sentient beings without exception, causing them all to attain satisfaction and happiness, and even to attain the supreme siddhi and most excellent fruit of the supernatural power of wisdom and skillful means of all Tathāgatas. He then placed the weapon of the Great Vajra Fang into the palms of the hands of the Mahāsattva Destroyer of All Māras.
Then all the Tathāgatas bestowed upon him the name Vajracaṇḍa and conferred upon him the empowerment through the rite of Vajracaṇḍa consecration.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajracaṇḍa took the weapon of the great vajra-tusk that had been granted to him and placed it in his own mouth; assuming a terrifying aspect toward all the Tathāgatas, he spoke this verse:
“This is the Honored One of All Great Awakenings, Who can subdue all those who are most difficult to subdue.”
“The great-beneficial vajra-tooth weapon is born from the mind of great compassion and skillful means.

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the Great Bodhisattva Samādhi of the Fist of All Tathāgatas, giving rise to the Vajra-Samādhi of the Empowerment of Karma. This is called the Vajra-Bond Samādhi of the Body, Speech, and Mind of All Tathāgatas; then, the heart-mantra of all Tathāgatas issued forth from his own heart, and he spoke this great vidyā-mantra:

"Vajra-santi. As soon as [this mantra] issued from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that Vajradhara endowed with such virtues became all the seals (mudrā) and bonds of all the Tathāgatas. Having manifested, he immediately entered the heart of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, and merged into a single essence. From this, the form of a vajra-bond was born and remained within the palms of the Buddhas.

Then, from within that image of the Vajra-bond (*vajrabandha*), there emerged images of Tathāgatas equal in number to the atoms of all worlds. Having universally sealed all the wisdoms of all Tathāgatas throughout all worlds and extensively performed the miraculous displays (*vikrīḍita*) of the supernatural powers (*abhijñā*) of all Tathāgatas, those natures of the wondrous bond of the Fist of All Tathāgatas—being wonderfully firm within the *vajrasattva-samādhi*—merged into a single entity and gave rise to the body of the Great Bodhisattva Sarvatathāgatamuṣṭi, who dwelt in the heart of the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana.
He spoke this verse:
"How marvelous! My wondrous and firm bond is my very own samādhi-body of firmness;
because all vows are fully accomplished therein, those who seek liberation are instead bound."

At that time, the body of the Great Bodhisattva Sarvatathāgatamuṣṭi descended from the heart of the World-Honored One, remained within a moon disc behind all the Tathāgatas in accordance with the principle, and again requested instruction.

At that time, the World-Honored One entered the Vajra Samādhi of the Binding of All Tathāgatas. By means of the binding samādhi of the seals of all Tathāgatas, he caused every single realm of sentient beings, without exception, to obtain the empowerment of all Tathāgata sages and the fulfillment of all vows, as well as all forms of satisfaction and happiness, even unto the attainment of the supreme siddhi and most excellent fruit of the Lord of Seals of the Omniscient Wisdom of all Tathāgatas. He then formed the mudrā of the vajra-bind and placed it into the palms of the hands of the Great Bodhisattva Sarvatathāgatamuṣṭi.
Then all the Tathāgatas bestowed upon him the name Vajramuṣṭi and conferred upon him the empowerment through the Vajramuṣṭi Empowerment Rite.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajramuṣṭi immediately formed the gesture of the "Exquisite Binding" by means of the Vajrabandha toward all the Tathāgatas, and spoke this verse:
"This is the secret seal-binding of all the Great Awakened Honored Ones, Which is most firm and solid."
"Because all Buddhas are swiftly accomplished, they do not transcend the Great Vajra Samādhi.

This is the Great Ritual Manual for the Worship of All Tathāgatas, the Armor of Firm Great Resolve; it is the Great Skillful Means and Immediate Wisdom of All Tathāgatas, the Mahāsattva of the Great Karma of All Tathāgatas.

At that time, the World-Honored One, Tathāgata Akṣobhya, having been consecrated by the wisdom of the World-Honored One, Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, and the wisdom of all Tathāgatas, immediately entered the samādhi of the Vajra-pāramitā and gave rise to the *vajrādhiṣṭhāna-samādhi*. This is called the Vajra-samādhi of All Tathāgatas; then, the seals (*mudrā*) of all Tathāgatas emerged from his own heart, and he spoke this great mantra:

As soon as the mantra "Sattvavajri" emerged from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, there appeared various Vajra-luminosities endowed with virtue, holding vajras. Within these vajra-luminosity gates, images of Tathāgatas equal in number to the atoms of all worlds were formed. Having been consecrated by the wisdom-seals (*jñānamudrā*) of the Vajra-pāramitās of all Tathāgatas, they again condensed into a single body and emerged from it as a great vajra-image, as vast as the entire world-system. It dwelt according to the principle within the lunar disc before the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana.
He spoke this verse:
"How great is the Honored One, the Fully Enlightened One! I am the Sattvavajra, firm and solid.
Because of this nature of solidity, I am originally without a body; therefore, the Vajra-body appears."

At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava, in order to seal the World-Honored One Mahāvairocana Tathāgata and all Tathāgatas with wisdom, entered the samādhi of the Jewel Pāramitā and gave rise to the Vajra-empowerment Samādhi; this is called the Vajra-Jewel Samādhi, which is his own seal.
Emerging from his own heart, he uttered this great mantra: "Ratnavajri.

As soon as it emerged from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, there appeared the Great Jewel Radiance, the Virtuous Vajra-holder. Within that Jewel Radiance, images of Tathāgatas equal in number to the atoms of all worlds were formed. Having pervasively sealed the wisdom of all Tathāgatas, they again condensed into a single body and emerged as a great golden vajra-jewel image, equal in magnitude to all worlds. It dwelt in its proper place within the lunar disc to the right of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana.
He spoke this verse:
“Great is the Honored One, the Perfectly Awakened One of All! I am indeed named Ratnavajra.
All those mudrās and all those aspirations— This is the firm principle of empowerment.”

At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Avalokiteśvararāja, in order to seal the wisdom of the World-Honored One Mahāvairocana Tathāgata and all Tathāgatas, entered the samādhi of the Dharma-pāramitā and gave rise to the Vajra-empowerment Samādhi. This is called the Great Dharma Samādhi; he then produced his own seal from his own heart and uttered this great mantra:

As soon as "DHARMA VAJRI" (Dharma-Vajrī) emerged from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, there appeared Padmaprabha-Śrīvajradhara. Within that Padmaprabha, he manifested images of Tathāgatas equal in number to the atoms of all worlds; having pervasively sealed the wisdom of all Tathāgatas, they again condensed into a single body. From this, there appeared a great golden vajra-lotus image, equal in magnitude to all worlds, which dwelt according to principle within the lunar disc behind the Bhagavān Mahāvairocana Tathāgata.
He spoke this verse:
"O Great One, Honored among all Perfectly Awakened Ones! The Great Dharma-Vajra is my purity;
Because it is pure by its primordial nature, It causes all defilements of desire to be stainless."
The Mahāyāna-sūtra of the King of Great Teachings on the Direct Realization of the Samādhi of the True Gathering of All Tathāgatas, Spoken by the Buddha, Scroll Three.
The Mahāyāna-sūtra of the King of Great Teachings on the Direct Realization of the Samādhi of the True Gathering of All Tathāgatas, Spoken by the Buddha, Scroll Four.

Translated by the Tripitaka Master Śīladharma (Shi Hu), Dharma-transmitting Master, conferred the purple robe and the title of Chao Feng Da Fu, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, under imperial decree.

*The Extensive Ritual Manual of the Vajradhātu Great Maṇḍala*, Part One, Section Four. At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi, for the sake of the seal of the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, and the wisdom of all Tathāgatas, immediately entered the samādhi of all pāramitās and gave rise to the vajra-adhiṣṭhāna-samādhi. This is called the karma-samādhi of all Tathāgatas. Thereupon, the self-seal emerged from his own heart, and he spoke this great mantra: [Mantra follows]

“Karma-vajri. As soon as this emerged from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, there appeared the Holder of the Vajra endowed with merit, manifesting all *karma*-lights. Within those *karma*-lights, images of Tathāgatas equal in number to the atoms of all worlds were formed.

Having universally sealed the wisdom of all Tathāgatas, they again condensed into a single entity, from which there emerged the form of the Great Vajra-karma, pervading all worlds as its measure and facing every direction; it then dwelt in accordance with the principle within the lunar disc to the left of the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana.
He spoke this verse:
"Great is the Honored One, the Fully Enlightened One! I am indeed the Vajra of manifold karma;
because through one [act] the inexhaustible is accomplished, I perform virtuous deeds within the realm of sentient beings."

This is the Dharma-gate of the Great Perfection of Wisdom for all Tathāgatas, the Great Consecration of the Vajra Nature of the Wisdom Samādhi of all Tathāgatas, and the Universal Offering to all Tathāgatas.

At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, again entered the samādhi of the Joyful Offering of All Tathāgatas, giving rise to the Vajra Samādhi, which is the Great Wisdom Consort of the Family of All Tathāgatas.
Emerging from his own heart, he uttered this great mantra: “VAJRA RĀŚI.

As soon as it emerged from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, there appeared the Great Vajra Seal-holder, the Possessor of Virtue (Guṇadhara-vajrin). Within that gateway of the Vajra Seal, he manifested images of Tathāgatas equal in number to the atoms of all worlds; these then condensed into a single body, appearing in the form of the Great Vidyārājñī Vajralāsyā. Her physical form was no different from that of Vajrasattva, endowed with various colors and shapes, exquisite grace, and adorned with all manner of ornaments. She encompassed all the Vidyārājñīs of the Vajrasattvas of the Tathāgata families and dwelt, according to the principle, within the lunar disc to the left of the Blessed One Akṣobhya Tathāgata’s maṇḍala.
He spoke this verse:
"How great is my peerless attainment, The supreme and wondrous offering to all Buddhas!
By knowing how to offer through desire and pleasure, I am thus able to transform all those offerings."

At that time, the Bhagavān again entered the *samādhi* of the Jewel-Crown Empowerment of All Tathāgatas and gave rise to the Vajra-samādhi. Thereupon, the Great Vidyārājñī of the Family of All Tathāgatas emerged from his own heart and spoke this great mantra: "VAJRA MĀLĪ.

As soon as she emerged from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, there appeared the Holder of the Vajra endowed with the qualities of the Great Jewel Seal. Within that Great Jewel Seal, he manifested images of Tathāgatas equal in number to the atoms of all worlds; these then condensed into a single body, appearing in the form of the Vidyārājñī Vajramālā. Her physical marks and ornaments were exactly as before, without any difference. She dwelt according to the principle within the lunar disc to the left of the Bhagavān Ratnasambhava Tathāgata’s maṇḍala.
He spoke this verse:
"How great is this peerless offering of mine! It is indeed called a 'jewel-offering,' for the Most Victorious King of the Three Realms has accepted my instruction and thus performed this worship."

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the Samādhi of the Exquisite Song of All Tathāgatas, giving rise to the Vajra-samādhi, which is the Great Wisdom Consort of the Family of All Tathāgatas.
Emerging from his own heart, he uttered this great mantra: “VAJRA GĪTE.

As soon as it emerged from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, there appeared the Vajradhara endowed with the virtues of the Dharma-mudrās of all the Tathāgatas. Within those Dharma-mudrās of all the Tathāgatas, he manifested images of the Tathāgatas equal in number to the atoms of all worlds; these then condensed into a single body, appearing in the form of the Great Vidyārājñī Vajragītā. She dwelt according to the principle within the lunar disc to the left of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Avalokiteśvararāja, in the maṇḍala.
He spoke this verse:
"How magnificent is this great and wondrous song! I shall make offerings to all who behold it;
through the joy arising from those offerings, all phenomena will resonate like echoes."

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the Samādhi of the Dance-Offering of All Tathāgatas, giving rise to the Vajra-samādhi; thereupon, the Great Wisdom Consort of the Family of All Tathāgatas emerged from his own heart and spoke this great mantra:

"Vajra-nṛtye (Vajra-dance)! As soon as this was uttered from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, there appeared the Holder of the Vajra endowed with the qualities of the vast ritual application of the dance-offering of all the Tathāgatas. Within that vast ritual application of the dance-offering of all the Tathāgatas, he manifested images of the Tathāgatas equal in number to the atoms of all worlds; these then merged into a single body and emerged in the form of the Great Vidyārājñī Vajranṛtyā, who took her place according to the principle within the lunar disc to the left of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi’s maṇḍala.
He spoke this verse:
"How great! This vast self-offering, performing all acts of offering extensively;
by means of the application of the vajra dance, I establish the sublime offerings for all Buddhas."

This is called the Samādhi of the Supreme Joy of All Tathāgatas, the Garland of All Tathāgatas, the Song of All Tathāgatas, the Performance of the Supreme Deeds of All Tathāgatas, and the Secret Offering of All Tathāgatas.

"Furthermore, World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, for the sake of making offerings to the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, immediately entered the Samādhi of the Great Laughter of All Tathāgatas and gave rise to the Vajra-samādhi. Thereupon, the Great Illuminating Queen Gaṇikā of all Tathāgatas emerged from his own heart and spoke this great mantra: [Mantra]"

"Vajra-dhūpe (1). As soon as this emerged from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, there appeared oceans of clouds of various fragrant offerings, adorned and pervading the entire extent of the Vajradhātu, for the sake of the virtuous Vajradharas. From within these oceans of clouds of various fragrant offerings, there emerged images of Tathāgatas equal in number to the atoms of all worlds; these then merged into a single body, appearing in the form of the Great Vidyārājñī Vajragandhā. She dwelt according to the principle within the lunar disc at the left corner of the World-Honored One’s Vajramaṇiratnaśikhara Pavilion.
He spoke this verse:
"Great indeed is this great offering of mine, The majestic Great Laughter of Vajra;
Because all sentient beings enter into it, They swiftly attain the fruit of unsurpassed enlightenment."

At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava, in order to perform an offering to the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, immediately entered the samādhi of the Jewel-Adorned Offering of All Tathāgatas and gave rise to the Vajra-samādhi. Thereupon, the Great Wisdom Queen Prajñāhārī of All Tathāgatas emerged from his own heart and spoke this great mantra:

"Vajra-puṣpe. As soon as this emerged from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, there appeared Vajradharas endowed with merit, pervading the entire extent of the realm of empty space, adorned with offerings of all flowers. From within these adornments of flower offerings, there emerged Tathāgata images equal in number to the atoms of all worlds; these then merged into a single body, appearing in the form of the Great Vidyārājñī Vajrapuṣpā. She dwelt in her proper place upon a moon disc at the left corner of the World-Honored One’s Vajramaṇiratnaśikhara Pavilion.
He spoke this verse:
“Great is this flower offering of mine, All its adornments exquisitely fashioned;
By virtue of the jewel-nature of all Tathāgatas, May all offerings be swiftly accomplished.”

At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Avalokiteśvararāja, in order to perform an offering to the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, immediately entered the samādhi of the Lamp Offering of All Tathāgatas and gave rise to the Vajra Samādhi. Thereupon, the Great Vidyārājñī Netrī of All Tathāgatas emerged from his own heart and spoke this great mantra:

"Vajra-lū-ke. As soon as this was uttered from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, there appeared the Holder of the Vajra endowed with all virtues, pervading the entire Dharma-realm with the adornment of all lamp-offerings. From within that adornment of all lamp-offerings, there emerged images of Tathāgatas equal in number to the atoms of all worlds; these then merged into a single body and manifested as the Great Vidyārājñī Vajradīpā. She took her place according to the principle within the lunar disc at the left corner of the World-Honored One’s Vajramaṇiratnaśikhara Pavilion.
He spoke this verse:
"How magnificent is this wondrous and vast offering lamp, so beautifully adorned!
Because one thereby swiftly attains radiant light, one shall immediately behold all those Buddhas."

At that time, the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi, for the purpose of making offerings to the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, entered the samādhi of the incense offering of all Tathāgatas and gave rise to the Vajra-samādhi. Thereupon, the Great Radiant Queen Sarvatathāgatānta emerged from his own heart and spoke this great mantra:

“Vajra-gandhe. As soon as this emerged from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, there appeared Vajradhara, endowed with all virtues and measuring the entirety of all worlds, adorned with all kinds of fragrant ointment offerings. From within that adornment of all fragrant ointment offerings, there issued forth images of Tathāgatas equal in number to the atoms of all worlds; these then merged into a single body and manifested as the Great Vidyārājñī Vajragandhā. She dwelt in her proper place within the lunar disc at the left corner of the World-Honored One’s Vajramaṇiratnaśikhara Pavilion.
He spoke this verse:
"Great is the offering of scented unguents, This subtle and most delightful [fragrance] of mine;
Through the pervasive application of these unguents by all Tathāgatas, It universally perfumes all pure bodies."
