This is called the Samādhi of the Great Enlightenment-Part that Pervades the Wisdom of All Tathāgatas, the Dharma-light of all Tathāgatas, and the sublime fragrance of ethical discipline, meditative concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation; it is the very activity of the commands of all Tathāgatas.

At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, again entered the samādhi of the Great Being of the Hook of All Tathāgatas’ Samādhi, giving rise to the Sattvavajra-samādhi. Thereupon, the seals of all Tathāgatas for sealing sentient beings issued forth from his own heart, and he spoke this great mantra:

“Vajraṃkuśa. As soon as this [mantra] issued from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, the Venerable Vajradhara became the assembly of vajra-mudrās of the samādhi for summoning all Tathāgatas. Having manifested, from within that assembly of vajra-mudrās of the samādhi for summoning all Tathāgatas, there emerged Tathāgata-forms equal in number to the atoms of all worlds; these then merged into a single body, giving birth to the form of the Bodhisattva Vajrāṅkuśa. He dwelt in his proper place within the moon disc at the vajra-gate of the Lord’s Vajramaṇiratnaśikhara Pavilion, performing the samādhi for summoning all Tathāgatas.
He spoke this verse:
"Great is the Honored One of All Perfectly Awakened Ones! With impartiality, you summon me with firm resolve;
because I have summoned [all] universally, the maṇḍala assembly is immediately attained."

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the Samādhi of the Great Being who Introduces all Tathāgatas, giving rise to the Vajra-samādhi. He then introduced the Seal of All Tathāgatas, *Pratīhāra*, which emerged from his own heart, and spoke this great mantra:

“Vajra-paśa. As soon as this emerged from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, the Venerable Vajradhara became the assembly of the Great Seals (*mahāmudrā*) for the introduction of all the Tathāgatas. Having appeared, from within that assembly of the Great Seals for the introduction of all the Tathāgatas, there issued forth images of the Tathāgatas equal in number to the atoms of all worlds; these then condensed into a single body, giving rise to the form of the Bodhisattva Vajrapāśa. He dwelt in his proper place within the moon disc at the jeweled gate of the Lord’s *vajramaṇiratnaśikhara-kūṭāgāra*, and thus introduced all the Tathāgatas.
He spoke this verse:
“Great is the Honored One, the Perfectly Awakened One! I am the Vajra-Noose, wondrous and firm;
Even if one enters into all atoms, I shall likewise lead them into this samādhi.”

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the Great Being Samādhi of the Samaya-Chain of All Tathāgatas, giving rise to the Vajra Samādhi. Thereupon, the Samaya-Bonds of All Tathāgatas and the Nṛtyas of All Tathāgatas emerged from his own heart, and he spoke this great mantra:

"Vajraṣṭha. As soon as this emerged from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, the Holder of the Vajra endowed with virtue manifested as the assembly of Great Mudrās of the Samaya-bond of all Tathāgatas. From within that assembly of Great Mudrās of the Samaya-bond of all Tathāgatas, there issued forth Tathāgata-forms equal in number to the atoms of all worlds; these then merged into a single body, giving rise to the form of the Bodhisattva Vajrasaṃhara. He dwelt according to the principle within the moon-disc of the Dharma-gate of the Lord’s Vajramaṇiratnaśikhara Pavilion, assuming the aspect of a wondrous bond for all Tathāgatas.
He spoke this verse:
"How great is the Honored One, the Fully Awakened One of All! I am the Vajra-Chain, wondrous and firm;
Because I bind all who seek liberation, For the benefit of sentient beings, I once again act as a bond."

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the Samādhi of the Great Being Pervading All Tathāgatas, giving rise to the Vajra-samādhi; then, from his own heart, all the seals (mudrās) of all the Tathāgatas emerged, and he spoke this great mantra:

"Vajrāveśa. As soon as this emerged from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, the Venerable Vajradhara became the assembly of the Universal Awakening Mudrās of all the Tathāgatas. Having appeared, from within that assembly of the Universal Awakening Mudrās of all the Tathāgatas, there emerged Tathāgata-forms equal in number to the atoms of all worlds; these then merged into a single body, giving rise to the Bodhisattva body of Vajraghaṇṭā. He dwelt in his proper place within the moon disc at the gate of the Karmamandala of the Lord’s Vajramaṇiratnaśikhara Pavilion, universally awakening all the Tathāgatas.
He spoke this verse:
"Great is the Honored One, the Fully Enlightened One of All! This vajra bell is my firm [commitment];
Because it is the sovereign of all, It likewise acts as their servant."

"This is called the summoning hook of all Tathāgatas, the induction of all Tathāgatas, the sublime binding of all Tathāgatas, and the loving-kindness of all Tathāgatas; such things are performed according to the commands of all Tathāgatas."

Furthermore, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, through the power of his empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*), made the gesture of snapping his fingers and universally summoned all the Tathāgatas. He spoke this heart-mantra of summoning and empowerment, which says: *vajrasamāja*.

Thereupon, within a single lava, kṣaṇa, or muhūrta, all the Tathāgatas mutually alerted one another. From throughout the ocean-like clouds of all worlds, as many Tathāgatas and assemblies of Bodhisattvas as there are atoms in all worlds, all came together to this Great Maṇḍala, the Vajra-Maṇi-Ratna-Śikhara-Kūṭāgāra, and approached the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana. Arriving there, they spoke this great mantra of universal prostration:
"Oṃ sarvatathāgatapādavandanāṃ karomi. Having thus recited this *svabhāvasiddha-mantra* as much as desired, one should universally prostrate at the feet of all the Tathāgatas.
He spoke this verse:
“Marvelous is the Great Samantabhadra of all Buddhas, The sublime object of veneration for all Bodhisattvas,
The great maṇḍala of the wheel of all Tathāgatas, In which the images of all Tathāgatas are reflected.”

When this had been said, at that time all the Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas who had assembled from the worlds of the ten directions, through the power of the empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*) of all those Tathāgatas, merged into the heart of the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana. Then, each emerging individually from the hearts of all those Tathāgatas as a host of Bodhisattvas, they surrounded the World-Honored One’s Vajra-maṇi-peak Pavilion on all sides and, dwelling together in *samādhi*, spoke these verses:
"O Great One, Honored among all Perfectly Awakened Ones, Vast, beginningless, and primordially arisen!..."
"By this, all [beings] as numerous as atoms shall together realize the single, pure Buddha-nature.

At that time, all the Tathāgatas who had gathered from all worlds throughout the ten directions, within this Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu, by means of their power of empowerment, extensively provided protection for the entire realm of sentient beings without exception, causing them all to obtain benefit and happiness, even unto the attainment of the supreme siddhi and excellent fruits of the equal wisdom and supernormal powers of all Tathāgatas.

Then all the Tathāgatas together exhorted and requested the virtuous Lord of All Tathāgatas, the Sovereign, the Self-Vajrasattva, the Great Vajradhara who is without beginning or end, by means of these one hundred and eight names of praise.
They spoke in verse: “Vajra-hero, Great Mahāsattva, You are indeed the Vajras of all Tathāgatas;
From the Vajra-beginning of the nature of Samantabhadra— I prostrate to the Noble Vajrapāṇi.”
To that King of Vajras, the Sublime and Victorious Awakening; To the Vajra Hook, who is all Tathāgatas;
To the Supreme Vajra, the Unfailing King; To the Vajra Summoner, I prostrate.
Vajra-love, the great sublime bliss, And the Vajra-arrow that subdues well;
The supreme Great Vajra of Māra’s desire— To that Vajra-bow, I prostrate.
Vajra, Excellent One, Wondrously Born, Victorious; Vajra, Utmost Joy, Great Bliss itself;
Supreme Vajra King of Delight— To that Vajra Joy, I prostrate.
Vajra-miraculous-jewel, firm and sharp, Vajra-void, great maṇi,
Vajra-prosperity, treasury of space— To that Vajragarbha, I prostrate.
The wondrous light of Vajra, blazing with great flames, The holy sun of Vajra, which is the Buddha’s radiance,
The perfect orb of Vajra, illuminating all— To the Great Vajra Light, I prostrate.
The Vajra Jewel Banner brings excellent benefit to sentient beings; the Vajra Banner-pole is wondrous joy.
The mark of the sublime jewel banner is itself the Vajra; I prostrate to that Vajra Banner.
Vajra joyful laughter, great delight; Vajra laughter, truly most rare;
Great joy, great bliss, the primordial Vajra; To the Vajra of wondrous joy, I prostrate.
The true principle of the sublime Vajra Dharma, The wondrous purity of the Vajra Lotus,
The Vajra Eye of sovereign insight— I prostrate to that Vajra Eye.
The vajra edge is the Mahāyāna Dharma; The vajra sword is the great weapon.
To the Vajra, the profound Mañjuśrī, To that Vajra Wisdom, I prostrate.
The Vajra Cause is the Vajra Mandala; the Vajra’s wondrous wheel is the Great Principle.
As taught, the Vajra arises through skillful turning; I prostrate to that Vajra Mandala.
To the supreme, wondrously luminous Vajra-speech, Which perfectly accomplishes the Vajra-recitation,
The unsurpassed siddhi of the wordless Vajra— To that Vajra-speech, I prostrate.
Sublime command of vajra activity, Well-pervading like vajra deeds,
Vajra-amsu, most vast and unerring— I prostrate to you, Vajrakarman!
Vajra Protector of Great Diligence, Vajra Armor of Great Firmness,
Supreme Hero of Utmost Invincibility— To Vajravīrya, I prostrate.
Vajra Yakṣa of great skillful means, Vajra with sharp fangs, most terrifying,
Supreme Vajra who subdues the power of Māra, Fierce Vajra, I prostrate to you!
The Greatly Powerful Fist of Wondrous Vajra, The Vajra Fist of Skillful Liberation,
The Vajra Firmness of Supreme Samādhi— To that Vajra Fist, I prostrate.
If there is one who can constantly uphold these one hundred and eight names of tranquility,
they shall achieve supreme accomplishment in all their undertakings, such as the vajra empowerment.
Thus, this supreme secret name was praised by Mahāvajradhara;
whoever constantly offers it in song shall become no different from Vajrapāṇi.
These hundred and eight names of the Vajradhara, which I have thus praised, are the Mahāyāna gateway for the realization of samādhi;
this is the dissemination of the sublime path of reasoning (naya).
I entreat you, O Noble Ones, to please proclaim the supreme self-ritual,
namely the Great Wisdom Wheel of all Buddhas, the most excellent Vajra Maṇḍala.
The Mahāyāna-abhisamaya-samādhi-mahākalparāja Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha, Revealing the Reality of All Tathāgatas, Volume Four.

Translated by the Tripitaka Master Śīlagupta, Dharma-transmitting Master, Imperially Conferred Purple Robe, Chamberlain for Ceremonial Affairs, Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and others, under Imperial Edict.

The First Part, Section Five, of the Extensive Ritual Manual of the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu. At that time, the Virtuous Vajradhara, having heard the exhortations of all the Tathāgatas, immediately entered the samādhi of the Vajra-empowerment born from the samādhi of all the Tathāgatas, and spoke this verse of the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu:
"Furthermore, I shall now proclaim The most supreme and vast maṇḍala."
Its characteristics are like those of the Vajradhātu; therefore, it is named the Vajradhātu.
One should establish the various divisions of the characteristics within the maṇḍala according to the sequence of the instructions.
First, one should perform the visualization by universally empowering [the site] with the Great Seal (mahāmudrā) of the Great Being (mahāsattva).

One should arise from the position of the previous mudrā; observing all directions according to principle, one should proceed with a dignified and uplifted demeanor while reciting the mantra of Vajrasattva.
One should take new thread that is firm and exquisite, measuring it according to the required proportions and using it skillfully;
the practitioner, holding the thread, should measure out the mandala, constructing it according to one's capacity.
The altar is square with four gates, further adorned with four corner-posts and crisscrossed by four lines, decorated with fine silks and exquisite threads.
In the various positions at its four corners, as well as at the junctions of the gates, each is inlaid with vajra-jewels;
thus, one should sequentially mark out the outer maṇḍala.
The center of the outer altar is like the form of a wheel;
next, gradually enter the central palace, well-measured by means of a vajra-line, and adorned with eight pillars set at intervals.
In that supreme vajra abode, further adorned with the five-wheeled maṇḍala,
within the wheel-maṇḍala thus established, one should install images of the Buddha according to the instructions;
around the central maṇḍala of that place, the images of the Buddha should be arranged.
The four supreme samādhi-heruka mudrās should be depicted according to their respective order.
Advancing gradually with the vajra-step, one should sequentially establish the four maṇḍalas, namely those of the four Buddhas beginning with Akṣobhya; thus all Buddha images are established.
First, draw the Akṣobhya maṇḍala, with the assembly of Vajradhara and others in perfect symmetry;
next, draw the Ratnasambhava maṇḍala, complete with the assembly of Vajragarbha and others;
next, the Amitāyus maṇḍala, with the assembly of Vajranetra and others purified.
In the Amoghasiddhi maṇḍala, one should paint Vajraviśvakarman and the others.
Within the various corners of the inner wheel-maṇḍala, one should paint the assembly of Vajra-vidyārājñīs.
At the four corners of the outer wheel-maṇḍala, one should paint the four [deities] beginning with Buddhapūjā.
Thereafter, within those four gates, one should install the four Great Vidyārājas who guard the gates.
Next, at the locations of the outer wheel-maṇḍala, one should respectively establish the Great Sattvas.
Then, according to the ritual procedures of their respective families, one should form the supreme samaya mudrās.
Once the Vajrācārya has entered, he shall open the seals universally to awaken [the disciple].
Next, he recites the Vajra Awakening Heart-mantra; the syllable *A* is the command to be taught.
Having performed self-consecration and invoked his own name, he then accomplishes the Vajra-siddhi.
Next, the Vajrācārya forms the Sattvavajra-ākarṣaṇa-mudrā;
then, snapping the fingers, he universally awakens them, invoking all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
In that very instant, all the Buddhas and Vajrasattvas assemble together.
Pervading all maṇḍalas, universally summon them all to assemble.
Thereafter, one should next form the great mudrā; thus Vajrasattva is approached.
One should recite the hundred and eight names once, praising according to the sequence of the ritual.
Having assembled, they bestow joy; all Tathāgatas are entirely steadfast.
Accomplishing the fundamental rite of Vajrasattva, they abide as great compassionate friends.
Then, at the locations of its four gates, one should perform the rites of the Vajrāṅkuśa and others, and form the supreme Mahākarmamudrās; these should be established through the method of samādhi.
Likewise, the various mudrās such as the supreme Samayasattva and Sattvavajra should be formed.
One should recite the mantra JAḤ HŪṂ BAṂ HOḤ to seek the accomplishment of the Great Sattva dharma.
Thereupon, the Buddhas and all other assemblies, together with the Great Sattvas, will gather;
by means of the ritual hook-summoning, they enter everywhere, attaining complete union and loving devotion.
Yet by performing the rite of secret offering, all the Great Selves (Mahātman) will be fully delighted;
acting for the benefit of all sentient beings according to the teachings, one is able to accomplish all feats of siddhi.
All such maṇḍalas, and all the ritual applications contained therein, are the Vajrācārya himself;
they are the various activities performed according to the instructions.
Furthermore, I shall proclaim the extensive ritual procedures for the entry of disciples into all the maṇḍalas within the Vajradhātu.
Now, first, I will explain the ritual for the disciple’s entry into the maṇḍala.

Regarding those who would enter [the mandala], they should first give rise to a mind of protection and rescue toward the entire realm of sentient beings without exception, intending to cause them all to obtain satisfaction and happiness, as well as all supreme *siddhis*.
"World-Honored One, for all those who enter this great maṇḍala, one should not discriminate between those who are worthy vessels and those who are not. Why is this?"
It means that there are sentient beings who have committed great sinful karma; if they see this great maṇḍala and enter it, they shall immediately be freed from all evil destinies.

“Bhagavān! There may be sentient beings who, while enjoying various foods, drinks, and the pleasures of the five senses, remain firmly attached to and do not relinquish worldly aims and benefits; taking these very worldly dharmas as their primary practice, they too shall be able to fulfill all their wishes and intentions simply by performing whatever they desire within this maṇḍala.”

“Bhagavān! There are some sentient beings who delight in such things as play, laughter, song, dance, food, drink, and sensual pleasures. Furthermore, because they do not understand the nature of reality (dharmatā) of this Samādhi of the Mahāyāna Manifest Realization of all Tathāgatas, they enter the maṇḍalas of other celestial classes. Seeking to fulfill all their desires, they become attached to the pleasures, delights, play, and laughter therein. Consequently, regarding the teachings on the dharmas received within the maṇḍalas of all Tathāgatas, they give rise to groundless fear and are unable to enter; instead, they develop a mind of attachment toward the paths and gates of those maṇḍalas of the evil destinies.”

For those of such a kind who are able to enter into correspondence with this Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu, even those seeking the supreme siddhi of all pleasant delights, happiness, and sublime objects of affection shall achieve accomplishment; they will immediately be able to transform those paths that lead directly into the various evil realms.

“Bhagavān! There may be sentient beings who practice the True Dharma and who, out of a longing for the supreme siddhi-fruit of the Tathāgatas’ methods of morality, concentration, and wisdom, cultivate all dharmas such as the stages of dhyāna and liberation in order to seek unsurpassed Buddha-bodhi. For those of such a kind who undergo immeasurable and boundless suffering, if they enter this Vajradhātu Great Maṇḍala, the fruit of the Tathāgata can be swiftly realized without difficulty; how much more so, then, for all other methods of accomplishment?”

Furthermore, the ritual procedure for prostration shall be proclaimed as follows: first, one should universally prostrate to all Tathāgatas of the four directions. Having first formed the vajra-añjali, one should cast one's entire body to the ground and prostrate to the Tathāgata of the eastern direction.
The Great Illumination says:

"Oṃ sarvatathāgata-pūjopasthāna-tantrān niryātaya me sarvatathāgata-vajrasattva-tiṣṭha svāhā. As before, place the vajra-palms at the heart center and prostrate with the forehead to the Tathāgata of the southern direction.
The Great Illumination says:

“Oṃ sarvatathāgatabhujaviśvagātratantra-nirjāta-mi sarvatathāgatavajraratnābhiṣiñca māṃ. As before, place the vajra-pañjali at the head and perform the oral prostration to the Tathāgata of the western direction.
The Great Illumination says:

"Oṃ sarvatathāgata-pravaratana-naya-tman-niryantraya-mi sarvatathāgata-vajra-dharma-pravarataya māṃ. As before, with the vajra-palms joined, gradually lower them from the head and place them at the heart; then, prostrate to the Tathāgata of the North.
The Great Illumination says:
"Oṃ sarvatathāgatabhūjakarmanitama-nirjātaya mi sarvatathāgatavajrakarmakuru maṃ. Then, the Vajrācārya shall have the vajra-disciple cover their face with crimson silk and form the Sattvavajra mudrā.
Recite this great vidyā-mantra:
"Samaya-sattvaṃ. Then, forming the mudrā by holding a flower garland with the two middle fingers, enter the maṇḍala.
Recite this great vidyā-mantra:
*samaya hūṃ*. Having entered the maṇḍala, one should then bestow these words of the oath:
"You have now gained entry into the maṇḍala of all Tathāgatas; you should regard me as having arisen from that vajra-wisdom."
By virtue of this vajra-wisdom, you shall attain all the siddhis of all Tathāgatas, let alone any other methods for attaining siddhis!
If there are those who have not seen the great maṇḍala, you should not explain this samaya-dharma to them.
"If one were to explain it for them, they would transgress the samādhi.
Thereupon, the Vajrācārya himself binds the Sattvavajra mudrā and places it upon the crown of the vajra-disciple's head.
Having settled [the disciple], he says these words:
"If you speak to those who should not be spoken to, this samādhi shall shatter your head like a vajra.
Next, with the water of the samādhi-mudrā, he recites this heart-mantra once as an empowerment, and then bestows it upon the disciple to drink, pronouncing this great mantra of the vow-heart:
"VAJRA-SATTVA-ŚĀNTI HŪṂ HRĪḌĀYE SAMAVASTIPTA NṚPĪḌA-TAT-KṢAṆAṂ JAYA JAYA HŪṂ NIMITTA-RUYA NIMANAYA VAJRADAKAṬA. Then, he addresses the disciple with these words of solemn admonition:

"From this day forward, you should regard me as identical to Vajrapāṇi. Whatever I do, you must also do. You must not harbor contempt or arrogance toward me; lest you instead bring calamity upon yourself and fall into the great hells after your life ends."
Furthermore, he imparts the oath and instructs the mind, saying:
“Sarva-tathāgata-śiṣya-tiṣṭha tvam | Vajrasattvam āveśaya. Then the Vajrācārya immediately binds the Sattvavajra-mudrā and recites this great mantra:

“Āḥ jvala-ta-ma-yu-vajra vajrasattva-mite mṛta aviśayāntardhaye vajra-yanam-anuttaraṃ vajrāviśaya. Then, releasing the previous Sattvavajra mudrā and again forming the wrathful fist, one should perform the rite of summoning while reciting the mantra according to one’s preference with the Vajra Speech, as in the methods of the Mahāyāna Abhisamayakalpa and other such teachings.

Upon being summoned, they arise from subtle wisdom; by means of this wisdom, they are able to intuitively awaken to the minds of others as appropriate, know events of the past and future, and attain firmness of mind. They are able to extinguish all sufferings within the teachings of all Tathāgatas and achieve freedom from all fears. They obtain the majestic empowerment of all Sattvas and all Tathāgatas, attain the manifestation and accomplishment of all *siddhis*, and experience the arising of unprecedented joy, delight, and sublime bliss.

Within that sublime bliss, one may attain the accomplishment of various samādhis, or attain the accomplishment of various dhāraṇīs, or fulfill all aspirations, or further achieve the state of all Tathāgatas; thereupon, one employs that mudrā, placing it upon one's own heart to release the disciple.
Recite this great vidyā-mantra:
"Oṃ tiṣṭha vajra dṛḍhībhava sādhaya hṛdaye me tiṣṭha sarvasattvārthaprayāsa hūṃ ha ha ha ha hoḥ. Next, have the disciple cast the flower garland he holds into the maṇḍala.
Recite this great vidyā-mantra:
"Praṭiśa-vajra-hūṃ. Then, wherever the flower falls, that is the accomplishment of the chosen deity.
Next, having tied a flower garland upon the head of the disciple, the preceptor recites this great vidyā-mantra:

“Oṃ pratisiddhi-hṛdaya-mīmāṃsā-tva mahāmala trāyamada yati namah satvaina pratyavekṣa bhavati śīghraṃ ca kṣapayati. Thereafter, the ācārya removes the face-cloth from the disciple while reciting this great vidyā-mantra:
“Oṃ vajrasattva śānti ṇe | cūḍāṭana tattvaprā | uḍāṭaya ti sarvacū | vajracūḍarodraṇa | he vajrapoṣa. Then, have the disciple gaze sequentially upon the great maṇḍala.

As soon as the disciple gazes upon the maṇḍala, they immediately receive the empowerment of the majestic power of all Tathāgatas; Vajrasattva dwells within their own heart, and they see within the maṇḍala various wheels of light and other miraculous feats. They enter the nature of the sublime empowerment of all Tathāgatas, either seeing the virtuous Great Vajradhara manifesting his actual form, or seeing the Tathāgatas and so forth.
From this point onward, all benefits and all aspirations will be accomplished exactly as desired; one shall even attain the state of Vajradhara and achieve the state of all Tathāgatas.
Having thus surveyed this great maṇḍala in its entirety, the Vajrācārya then consecrates the disciple’s crown with the fragrant water from the vajra-empowered flask, reciting this great vidyā-mantra:
“VAJRAVIŚODHA. Thereafter, the ācārya binds a garland upon the disciple using one of the mudrās, places his own insignia into both hands, and addresses him as follows:
“You have now received the vajra-abhiṣeka of all the Tathāgatas; all Buddhas have taken you under their protection, and you shall surely attain vajra-siddhi.”
Having spoken thus, he uttered this great vidyā-mantra:
“Oṃ vajratibhaktitva abhiṣiñca me vajrasamayastvam. Next, one should bestow upon the disciple the vajra-consecration name.
He spoke this great vidyā-mantra:
“Oṃ vajrasattva abhiṣiñca me vajrādhipati hi vajrādhipate. “If one bestows a Vajra-name upon a disciple, the syllable *khe* should be added and used accordingly when calling him.”
As stated above is the extensive ritual procedure for entering all maṇḍalas.
"Furthermore, ask the disciple:
'Do you delight in the wisdom that gives rise to the accomplishment (siddhi) of meaningful benefit?'"
Is it the wisdom that accomplishes the siddhi of supernatural powers?
Is it the wisdom that accomplishes the siddhi of the vidyādhara?
Or is it even the wisdom that accomplishes the supreme siddhi of all Tathāgatas?
Thereafter, according to their inclinations, one should teach them as appropriate, beginning with the instruction on the mudrās and wisdom of the *siddhi* that accomplishes the beneficial purpose.
The verse says:
“First establish the vajra-image, And visualize it as it is within the heart.”
Visualize that terrain according to its location, and at that very spot you shall behold a hidden treasure.
Draw the image of a vajra everywhere; visualize it as it should be within the sky, and wherever it falls, there you should look—there you shall behold a hidden treasure.
The vajra-image abides upon the tongue; the wise person contemplates it accordingly and in accordance with reality.
They say, "In this place there is a hidden treasure," and just as they speak, it appears immediately as the truth.
One should visualize one's own body as being entirely composed of vajra-images;
wherever one perceives these entering and settling, at that very spot one shall behold a hidden treasure.
Their heart-mantras (*hṛdaya*) are as follows:
*vajranidhi*, *ratnanidhi*, *dharmmanidhi*, and *karmmanidhi*. Next, one should instruct them in the seal-knowledge (*mudrājñāna*) for accomplishing the siddhi of vajra-ṛddhi.
The verse says:
"Once the pervasive entry of the vajra has been generated, the vajra-water takes on the form of a vajra.
By visualizing it accordingly, one will swiftly achieve accomplishment and be able to walk upon that water."
Once the vajra-pervasion has arisen, according to what is appropriate for one's own color and form, one should visualize the corresponding [deity] as it truly is;
thus, one’s own body becomes identical in color to that of the Buddha.
Having first pervaded one's own body as before, one's own body becomes identical to space;
by visualizing accordingly as desired, one immediately attains the mastery of invisibility.
The vajra-pervasion is the nature of self-arising; visualizing oneself as the vajra, one then leaps upward and ascends high, thereby able to travel through space at will.
Their heart-mantras (*hṛdaya*) are as follows:
*vajra-jvara*, *vajra-ropa*, *vajrāgasa*, *vajramaham*. Next, one should instruct them in the seal-knowledge (*mudrājñāna*) for accomplishing the siddhi of the Vajra-Vidyādhara.
The verse says:
“The image of the wondrous moon is depicted everywhere; leaping upward into the sky, one travels as one pleases.
Visualizing oneself holding a vajra in both hands, the Vajra-vidyādhara attains accomplishment.”
The pure reflection of the wondrous moon pervades everywhere; one should contemplate the great vajra-jewel as appropriate.
According to one's desire for a purified body, one shall soar upward in a single instant.
Ascending into the form of the pure moon disc, holding a vajra and a wondrous lotus in hand,
and visualizing the vajra-eye as pure, one immediately attains the accomplishment of the vidyādhara dharma.
Next, within a pure and wondrous lunar disc, one should visualize the Karma-vajra;
by swiftly performing the sublime and skillful activities of the vajra, all vidyādharas shall attain accomplishment.
Their heart-mantras are as follows:

VAJRA-DHARA (1), RATNA-DHARA (1), DHARMA-DHARA (1), KARMA-DHARA (1). Next, one should instruct [them] in the seal-knowledge (*mudrājñāna*) for the supreme accomplishment of *siddhi* of all Tathāgatas.
The verse says:
"Through the Vajra Samādhi of Skillful Action, one contemplates pervading the entire realm of space;
according to one's desire for a vajra body, one soars upward in a single instant."
Through the *sattva-viśuddhi-samādhi*, visualize the supreme [deity] in the same manner;
having attained mastery and the five supernormal powers, one swiftly achieves great wisdom.
Composed of the assembly of Vajrasattvas, Like space, it is utterly vast;
Firmly established through recollection, it is swiftly accomplished, And one’s own body immediately becomes the Holder of the Vajra.
The images of all Buddhas are composed of a multitude [of factors], free from obstructions and as vast as the realm of space;
within the meditative concentration gates of all Buddhas, therein one realizes the fruit of Buddhahood.
Their heart-mantras (cittavidyā) are as follows:

"Vajra Vajra" (one phrase), "Śodha Śodha" (one phrase), "Sattva Sattva," and "Buddha Buddha" (one phrase). Once all these accomplishments (siddhi) and wisdoms have been thus realized, [the rite is complete].
"Furthermore, the Dharma-gate of the Secret Dhāraṇī Endurance is proclaimed.
First, the *samaya-mantra* is proclaimed as follows:
*Oṃ vajrasattva-samayas tvām hṛdaye samavasthita | nirviśaṅkaḥ kuru kṣāntiṃ jñāna-mūrti-mānaya ||* Next, the words of the *samaya-admonition* are spoken:"
"You must not now transgress this samādhi of the vow-mind; do not allow yourself to incur calamity and retribution, lest after the end of this life you fall into the great hells."
Thereafter, he taught the secret mudrā-knowledge.
The verse says:
"Once the Vajra-pervasion has been generated, with the vajra-palms and subtle fingers,"
When all are gathered together and struck evenly, even mountains and stones can be made to feel reverence and love.
Through the application of the Vajra-pervasive-entry rite, the wondrous vajra-bind can destroy all things.
When those subtle fingers are joined together, even mountains and rocks can be thoroughly shaken.
By means of the previously described method of universal entry, one fully extends that vajra-bind and then opens all the fingers wide; in an instant, one can destroy hundreds of lineages.
Corresponding to the subtle and all-pervading dharmas, all fingers are equally gathered;
by performing the vajra-bind and then releasing it, one can seize away all most terrible sufferings.
"Furthermore, the secret accomplishment is proclaimed:
if a man or a woman intends to enter pervasively into the *vagi* (the speech-mantra), once they have entered it pervasively, they should imagine those bodies expanding everywhere."
The heart-mantra of that [deity] is:

*vajravāśa*, *vajraveśa*, *vajrahana*, *vajrahara*. Having bestowed this heart-mantra upon them, he then instructs them in the four types of mudrās and wisdom of the tutelary deity, and further utters these words of solemn admonition:
"To any others who do not yet know this single mudrā, you must take care never to reveal it."

Why is this? Because those sentient beings, failing to behold the great maṇḍala, haphazardly bind these mudrās and thus fail to achieve accomplishment; they immediately give rise to doubt and instead incur calamity, swiftly meeting their end and falling into the Avīci Great Hell, further descending into the evil realms.

Furthermore, he proclaimed the great seal wisdom (*mahāmudrājñāna*) for the accomplishment of the *sattva* of all Tathāgatas; this is the seal of the manifest realization of enlightenment (*abhisambodhi*) of all Tathāgatas.
The verse says:
"First, having generated the mind of wisdom, one should next visualize the vajra-moon;
one's own body is the form of all Buddhas, and one should further visualize the Vajradhātu."
As soon as this accomplishment is attained, one immediately gains wisdom, longevity, power, and vitality;
all things can be performed according to one's will, and even the fruit of Buddhahood is not difficult to obtain.
Next, the Great Seal for the accomplishment of Vajrasattva is explained.
The verse says:
“With the gesture of loftily brandishing the vajra, One assumes the sovereign posture of Vajragarva.”
Abiding in the vajras of body, speech, and mind, one is already Vajrasattva himself;
by this, one can traverse everywhere, obtain exquisite bliss as the lord of all desires,
and [attain] longevity, power, superior form, and supernormal faculties, being no different from Vajrasattva and the others.
When those vajras of body, speech, and mind are practiced according to their diagrams,
complete with all their respective emblems and mudrās, one immediately accomplishes the Great Sattva.
Furthermore, I shall now proclaim in due order the various teachings, the means of accomplishment and the dharmas to be accomplished, and the great activities of those who achieve them;
first, every day at the appropriate time, one should perform the self-consecration and other rites as required.
Once all the methods of accomplishment have been properly performed, one thereafter gains mastery according to one's desires.
Furthermore, the extensive ritual for the accomplishment of the Great Seal (Mahāmudrā) is explained.
The verse says:
"Once the Vajra-pervasion has been generated, perform the great mudrā according to the ritual manual.
Forming that mudrā as prescribed by the previous method, one should accordingly visualize the Great Sattva."
Once that Wisdom-Sattva has been seen, one should immediately visualize oneself [as him];
having performed the mudrā of summoning and universal entry, and having performed the rite of endearment, one attains accomplishment.
"The Great Heart-Mantra of that [deity] is:
VAJRA-SATTVA HOḤ. This is the heart-mantra for universal entry into the Vajra.
VAJRA-SATTVA DṚŚYA. This is the heart-mantra for the recollection of the Mahāsattva."
“Jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ. This is the heart-mantra for the Great Sattva’s summoning, entering, binding, and inspiring with love.
Furthermore, the verse says:
“This Samayasattva vaṃ enters Into that subsequent moon disc.”
Because one contemplates one’s own body as the *sattva*, one recites *samayasattvaṃ*.
By means of that *sattva-mahāmudrā*, one visualizes one’s own body as that very body;
through the sublime accomplishment of *vajra-vāk*, all mudrās can be accomplished.
If one recites the mantra JAḤ HŪṂ VAṂ HOḤ, one can immediately enter into all Buddhas;
by giving rise to a sublime resonance with a mind as kind as that of a mother, one will attain vast and supreme accomplishment.

Furthermore, I shall now explain the rite of *karma*: the supreme and unsurpassed Vajra-karma, through which one attains the wondrous *siddhi* of the Buddhas' recollection and swiftly achieves the state of the Honored One of Perfect Enlightenment.
Through the sublime accomplishment of *sattva-vajra*, one attains mastery over all mudrās;
through the accomplishment of *mahāratna-vajra*, one becomes the master of all jewels;
and through the accomplishment of *dharmavajra*, one is able to uphold all Buddha-dharmas.
Through union with the Karma-vajra mudrā, one can accomplish all the activities of the vajra assembly;
through the accomplishment of the Vajrasattva dharma by binding the Sattva-mahājñāna mudrā,
one accomplishes the rite of the vajra hook, whereby all Vajradharas can be summoned.
Through the wisdom of the Great Seal of Vajra-Supreme-Love, one is able to perfectly love all Buddhas;
through the Dharma-correspondence of "Excellent" (Sādhu) Vajra, one causes all Buddhas to rejoice;
through the Vajra-Jewel Seal according to the ritual procedure, one receives empowerment from all Buddhas.
Through union with the Dharma of Vajra-Sublime-Light, one fully attains vajra radiance;
By practicing and maintaining union with the Vajra-Banner, all aspirations are immediately fulfilled;
Through union with the Dharma of Vajra-Great-Laughter, one attains joyous laughter together with all Buddhas.
In accord with the principles of the sublime Vajra Dharma, one is able to uphold the Vajra teachings;
through union with the sharp Vajra Dharma, one attains the supreme and wondrous wisdom of all Buddhas;
by maintaining the cause of the Vajra Wheel, one is able to turn that Great Wheel of Dharma.
If one accords with the wondrous speech of Vajra, One immediately attains the accomplishment of the speech of all Buddhas;
Because of accomplishing the supreme activity of Vajra, One swiftly attains the supreme activities of Vajra;
If the armor of Vajra is donned upon the body, One attains the wondrous firmness of the Vajra-body.
Through the accomplishment of Vajrayakṣa, one becomes no different from Vajrayakṣa;
by forming the sublime vajra-fist bond, one attains the accomplishment of all mudrās;
through the accomplishment of Vajralāsyā, one immediately attains the sublime bliss of the vajra.
Through union with the method of the Vajra Jewel Garland, one receives the empowerment bestowed by all Buddhas;
through union with the method of the Vajra Sublime Song, one immediately attains the sublime vajra chanting;
through union with the method of the Vajra Circular Dance, one is universally able to make offerings to all Buddhas.
In accordance with the Vajra Incense rite, one universally bestows great delight upon the world;
In accordance with the Vajra Exquisite Flower rite, one is able to perform acts of endearment for the world;
By means of the Great Mudrā of the Vajra Lamp-light, one attains pure eyes through making offerings.
Through the sublime union with the Vajra Scent, one can eliminate all suffering and affliction;
through union with the Vajra Hook rite, one can perform the supreme activity of summoning;
and by means of union with the Vajra Noose, one causes all beings everywhere to be drawn in.
Through union with the Vajra-Chain method, one is able to endure all bonds;
by universally awakening with the Vajra-Bell, one causes all to enter and rejoice.

The Extensive Ritual Manual of the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu, Part One, Section Six: "Furthermore, I shall now expound the Dharma-gate of the Wisdom-Seal of the Vajra-Samādhi of all Tathāgatas."
The verse says:
"First form the firm Vajra-palms, meaning the ten fingers are interlaced;
this is what is called the Vajra-palms. Without altering it, one then binds the Vajra-bonds."
All mudrās of samādhi arise from the vajra-bind;
I shall now proclaim the ritual for their formation, for that vajra-knot is supreme.
Forming the firm Sattvavajra, hold the two middle fingers upright like the appearance of tusks;
with the space between the two middle fingers slightly bent, this is called the Supreme Mudrā of Akṣobhya Buddha.
The thumb and middle finger are joined in the shape of a jewel; then, bending the middle finger again, it takes the form of a lotus.
By using this seal and bending the index finger, the seals of the three Buddhas should be formed in their respective order.
I shall now, in due order, expound the most excellent Tathāgata family of the Central [Direction], including all its samādhis and supreme mudrās;
by forming these seals, all activities will be accomplished.
First, form the moon-like gesture with both hands; separate the two middle fingers like a vajra, ensuring that the surfaces of all other fingers do not touch. This is called the Sattvavajra-mudrā.
The index fingers are like hooks, with the index fingers interlaced; Then one forms the gesture of the "Excellent! finger-snap.
These four seals of Vajrasattva Are able to accomplish all multitudes of seals.
For the Jewel-Vajra mudrā, extend the thumbs; then join the tips of the index fingers together.
Without altering the previous mudrā, extend the middle, ring, and little fingers;
raise the ring fingers in the form of a banner, and then join the two little fingers together.
Rotate this very mudrā and then place it at the site of the smile.
Next, extend both thumbs and slightly bend the two index fingers;
join the faces of the two middle fingers together. This is the Vajra Sharp Sword Mudrā.
Then, with the two ring fingers and the two little fingers held upright and interlaced like a wheel,
next release the binding of the thumbs; thereafter, extend them upward from the mouth,
joining the faces of the little fingers and thumbs together— this is the *saṃhāra-karmavajra-mudrā*.
Then, with this very mudrā, raise the index fingers; next, extend them and hold them at the heart.
Bend the two index fingers like the shape of tusks, join the two little fingers and then release them.
Between the little fingers and the thumbs, bend the two index fingers so that they touch one another.
Place the two thumbs upright at the heart; then, spreading them wide again, form the garland mudrā.
With the supreme palms, scatter from the mouth, then whirl in dance and join them above the crown.
Perform the vajra-bind and bestow downward, then perform the vajra-palm and offer upward.
Join the two thumbs together, then extend them as if in the gesture of anointing;
first slightly bend one index finger, then join the two thumbs and bind them so that the thumb and index finger resemble a chain,
and finally clench the hands into the supreme vajra-fist.
Next, the accomplishment of those mudrās shall be explained; the Vajra-accomplishment is the most supreme.
First, one places one’s own mudrā at the heart; this is the Sattvavajra-samādhi.
I shall now explain their activities; the Vajra-activity is the most supreme.
The supreme mudrās of the Vajradhātu and other realms universally assemble all Tathāgatas;
within the maṇḍala, the ācārya bestows empowerment upon the disciple in an instant.
By binding the Sattvavajra mudrā, one becomes no different from Vajrapāṇi;
by binding the sublime Vajrāṅkuśa mudrā, one is able to summon all Buddhas everywhere;
through union with the sublime Vajrarāga, one can even follow the loving ones among the Perfectly Awakened Ones.
By binding the Vajra-Sādhu mudrā, one immediately receives the joy bestowed by all Buddhas;
through the sublime union of Vajra-Ānanda, all Buddhas praise one with the words "Excellent! (Sādhu!);
by binding the Ratna-Vajra mudrā, one immediately attains the sublime empowerment of all Buddhas.
By binding the sublime seal of the Vajra Sun, one becomes equal to the Buddha’s light without distinction;
by accomplishing the Vajra Banner seal, one is able to fulfill all aspirations;
through the application of the Dharma of the Great Vajra Laughter, one attains joyous laughter identical to that of all Buddhas.
By universally maintaining the yoga of the Vajra Dharma, one immediately attains non-duality with the Vajra Dharma;
because one universally maintains the sharp vajra sword, one is able to sever all afflictions;
and because one firmly binds the vajra wheel mudrā, one becomes the sovereign of all maṇḍalas.
Through union with the mudrā of Vajra-bonding, one accomplishes the supreme Vajra-speech;
through the integration of the Karma-vajra mudrā, one attains identity with the activities of Vajra-karma;
by firmly binding the Vajra-armour mudrā, one immediately obtains a body composed of vajra.
By binding the supreme mudrā of the Vajra Fang, one is able to destroy all evil māras;
by firmly binding the Vajra Fist mudrā, one is able to bring all mudrās into submission;
through Vajra Play, one attains sublime bliss; and through the Vajra Garland, one attains supreme adornment.
Through the Vajra Song, one attains majestic speech; through the Vajra Dance, one attains all offerings;
through the Vajra Incense, one attains great radiance; through the Vajra Flower, one attains exquisite dignity.
The world is purified by the Vajra Lamp; through the Vajra Incense, one attains sublime fragrance.
The Vajra Hook is able to summon universally; with the Vajra Noose, one is able to draw others in.
By means of the Vajra Chain, one is well-bound; and because of the Vajra Bell, all are thoroughly awakened.
Furthermore, the Seal of All Dharmas is proclaimed:
“Vajra-wisdom encompasses all Buddhas, Able to create the firm Vajradhātu;
I shall now explain it in successive order, Those seals of all dharmas according to the ritual manual.”
By reciting *samayas tvaṃ*, one becomes the sovereign of all mudrās;
If one recites *ānaya sarva*, one can universally summon all Buddhas;
If one chants *āhuḥ sukha*, one can cause all Buddhas to give rise to sublime affection.
When reciting "Sādhu, sādhu," all obtain "well done" and are filled with joy;
if one recites "Svāgata vaṃ," all Buddhas immediately bestow empowerment upon them;
when reciting "Rupini sudha," one obtains the light of the supreme and wondrous Dharma.
A-ri-ta-pra-bha-ti: by reciting this, one’s every wish is fulfilled;
Ha-ha-hūṃ-ha: through this sound of laughter, one attains the same joyful laughter as all the Buddhas.
If one recites *sarvakaṛi*, all that is unrighteous is purified;
when reciting *nukha-cchedana*, one is swiftly able to sever all suffering;
by reciting *buddhabodhi* in this manner, one becomes the sovereign of the maṇḍala.
By reciting *pratisaṃmodana*, one may engage in discourse with all Buddhas;
If one recites *svasti-stambhanam*, one attains mastery in all places;
*Nirvāṇa-stambhanam*: by chanting this, one is freed from fear in an instant.
If one recites *śatru-bhakṣa*, one can subdue all enemies;
if one recites *sarva-siddhi*, one fulfills all methods of accomplishment;
if one recites the words *mahārati*, one can obtain subtle and supreme bliss.
When reciting *Rūpaśubha*, one immediately possesses the marks of exquisite physical form;
when reciting *Śrī-tara-saukhyam*, one is able to obtain sublime bliss.
If one recites *sarvapuṇya*, one shall obtain the most supreme and wondrous offerings;
by reciting the words *praharaṇi*, one can generate a heart of joy and satisfaction;
when chanting the name *prāgama*, one shall accordingly attain all excellent fruits.
If one recites *sūdirya-ṅkri*, one will obtain that great and wondrous light;
when reciting *sūyantaṃ-gi*, one obtains exquisite unguents and constant purity;
with *ā-khe-jaṃ* one universally summons, and with *ā-khe-hūṃ hūṃ* one is able to lead [beings] in.
*Hīḥ*, *saḥ*, *phuṭ*, *vaṃ*, *naṃ*, *ba*, *Khaṇḍa*, *aḥ*, *aḥ*—these can stir and awaken [all].
Now I shall explain the aforementioned seals of all dharmas (*dharmamudrā*).
Regarding all methods for pure accomplishment, one should visualize that vajra upon the tongue; then all activities will be accomplished.
"Furthermore, I shall now explain the ritual procedure for forming the various *karmamudrās*:
First, form the firm *vajramuṣṭi*; with both hands extended and separated, these two become the two *vajra-mudrās*.
Thereafter, the ritual procedure for binding them shall be explained."
With the left hand held flat like a vajra-finger, the right hand is raised to form the mudrā;
this seal is named "Supreme Awakening," through which one attains the Bodhi of Buddhahood.
Akṣobhya Tathāgata performs the earth-touching mudrā; Ratnasambhava Tathāgata displays the gesture of granting boons;
the Honored One Amitāyus maintains the posture of supreme meditative concentration; Amoghasiddhi bestows fearlessness.
Furthermore, as is appropriate, I shall now expound the sequence of all the *karmamudrās*:
the Great Beings such as Vajrasattva and others perform all vajra activities accordingly;
raising the vajra with a forceful toss, the two hands again assume the gesture of holding a hook.
Thereafter, one should perform the visualization according to the method of archery; next, the "Excellent" (*sādhu*) mudrā is placed upon the heart.
With both hands in the *vajra-abhiṣeka* mudrā, one again displays the form of a lunar disc at the heart.
Holding an arrow in the left hand, one assumes the posture of shooting with the right. Then, one rotates [the hands] toward the mouth and opens them.
The two hands open like lotuses and rest on the right side; the left hand holds a sword at the heart in the gesture of striking.
Again, they rotate like a wheel of fire; from the mouth, the two vajra-hands scatter forth.
Releasing them through the vajra-dance rotation, they next move from the two cheeks to rest upon the crown of the head.
With the little fingers as armor and the thumbs as teeth, join the two vajra fists together;
next, perform the gesture of the raised vajra, and with palms joined, prostrate with a trembling heart.
First perform the binding of the garland, then scatter it with the mouth; next, perform the vajra dance while rotating.
Then, according to the ritual of the vajra-fist, one should offer incense and other offerings in due order.
This is the offering to all Buddhas; thus, the mudrās for the various offerings are distinguished according to the instructions.
Again, with the two index fingers formed like hooks, next the two little fingers like large hooks,
then again like ropes and the two [thumbs] like chains, and furthermore, the backs of the two hands pressed closely together.
Furthermore, the method for the supreme accomplishment is taught: perform the activities of Vajra with equanimity;
the assembly of Vajras becomes the wondrous Vajra, which one should visualize within one’s own heart.
Next, the activity of the Karma-mudrā is taught, wherein the Vajra-activities are manifold.
By forming the wisdom-fist mudrā therein, one is able to enter universally into the wisdom of all Buddhas;
by forming the Akṣobhya Buddha seal, one attains an unshakable and firm resolve;
and by forming the Ratnasambhava Buddha seal, one is able to encompass and sustain the deeds of others.
By binding the seal of the turning of the true Dharma wheel, one skillfully turns that great Dharma wheel;
through the seal of fearlessness, one attains supreme swiftness and is able to bestow fearlessness upon sentient beings.
By firmly binding the seal of the raised vajra, one immediately attains the bliss of Vajrasattva.
By means of the vajra hook, one can summon universally, gathering all Tathāgatas in an instant;
through the exquisite love of the vajra arrow mudrā, even the vajra retinue can be accomplished;
and by that great joy mudrā of the vajra, all Buddhas bestow the voice of "Excellent! (Sādhu).
By binding the Great Vajra-Jewel Mudrā, one is immediately able to receive empowerment from the Master;
because one universally upholds the Great Vajra-Sūrya, one becomes no different from the Vajra-Sūrya;
by erecting the Supreme and Wondrous Vajra Banner, one is immediately able to rain down a universal shower of all jewels.
By universally holding the Great Laughter of Vajra, one swiftly shares in the joyous laughter of all Buddhas;
by universally holding the Wondrous Flower of Vajra, one is immediately able to skillfully contemplate the Vajra-dharma;
by firmly binding the seal of the Sharp Sword of Vajra, one is swiftly able to sever all suffering.
By universally holding the vajra-cakra mudrā, one is able to turn that sublime wheel of Dharma;
because those Buddhas are beyond speech, the vajra-recitation is thereby accomplished.
By making offerings with the vajra-nṛtya mudrā, even the Buddhas are moved to give rise to sublime love.
By binding the seal of the adamantine armor, one attains the true nature of the vajra;
because one universally wields the sharp adamantine fangs, even that very vajra can be destroyed;
by crushing all with the adamantine fist, one skillfully achieves the perfection of all seals.
Through the Vajra Play one attains sublime bliss; through the Vajra Garland, one obtains exquisite beauty;
through the Vajra Song, one attains a sublime melodic voice; through the Vajra Dance, one gives rise to virtuous love;
through the Vajra Incense, one attains great luster and grace; through the Vajra Flower, one is moved by pure adornment.
Through the vajra lamp offering, one attains sublime light; through the vajra unguent, one obtains a fragrant body.
That vajra hook is able to summon universally, while the vajra noose is able to lead [beings] in.
By means of the vajra chain, the gates are well-bound; by means of the vajra bell, all are universally awakened and stirred.
"Furthermore, I shall now explain the ritual procedure for binding all mudrās:
First, one should bind the vajra-bond (*vajrabandha*); next, strike one’s own heart with the fingers while reciting this heart-mantra:
*vajramuṣṭi hraḥ*. Only after this may one bind all mudrās, whereby one will attain mastery over the vajras of one’s own body, speech, and mind."
"Next, bind the Vajra-Universal-Entry Mudrā and recite this heart-mantra: *vajraveśaya*.
By means of this heart-mantra, one is immediately able to enter everywhere; all become like close friends, dwelling in harmony. Thereafter, one attains the Samādhi of the Secret Seal.

Recite this Great Being’s Anusmṛti Heart-Mantra: *mahāsamayasattva hūṃ*. By means of this heart-mantra, one achieves accomplishment in all seals; this is the ritual procedure for binding all seals collectively."
"Furthermore, the ritual for the complete accomplishment is proclaimed as follows:
First, one should bind one's own mudrā; with this mudrā, one visualizes oneself as a *sattva* and recites this heart-mantra:
*Samayam hūṃ*. Having thus visualized oneself as a *sattva*, one further empowers [oneself] with this great mantra:"
*Samayasattvādiṣṭha svāhā.* Furthermore, the ritual procedures for all accomplishments (*siddhi*) are proclaimed:
"If one desires to seek the accomplishment of that purposeful benefit, one should recite this heart-mantra (*hṛdaya-mantra*):
*Artha siddhi*. By means of this heart-mantra, one attains the accomplishment of the mudrā and acquires great benefit."
Furthermore, if one wishes to seek the accomplishment of supernatural powers (*abhijñā*), one should recite this heart-mantra:
*ṛtiṣṭi* (one phrase). Furthermore, if one wishes to seek the accomplishment of a Vajra-Vidyādhara, one should recite this heart-mantra:
*vajravidyādharā* (one phrase). By means of this heart-mantra, one shall immediately attain the supreme accomplishment of a Vidyādhara according to one's desire.

"Furthermore, if one desires to seek the supreme accomplishment (*uttamasiddhi*), one should perform the ritual empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*) according to principle by means of one's own mudrā and heart-mantra (*hṛdaya-mantra*);
thus, one will attain accomplishment. Next, the general ritual procedures for all assemblies of mudrās are proclaimed:
namely, by performing the actions with firm resolve as appropriate, one will be able to attain vajra-like activities within the vajras of one's own body, speech, and mind."
If the empowerment of the mudrā being employed is slow, or if one wishes to dissolve it oneself, one should likewise make the action firm.
Recite this heart-mantra, saying: "Oṃ..."

*Bhava mahāsamayasattva āḥ.* (11) "By virtue of this heart-mantra (*hṛdaya-mantra*), even those who have transgressed against the Tathāgatas, slandered the True Dharma, committed these five deeds of immediate retribution (*pañcānantarya-karma*), or performed any other evil deeds—if they seek accomplishment through the secret seals (*guhyamudrā*) of all Tathāgatas—they shall, even in this present life, attain the solid nature of Vajrasattva. According to their aspirations, whether it be the supreme accomplishment (*uttamasiddhi*), the vajra-accomplishment, the Vajrasattva-accomplishment, or even the most excellent accomplishments of all Tathāgatas, they shall obtain every accomplishment. This is indeed the virtuous Vajrasattva of all Tathāgatas."

According to the specific context of each case, one should recite this heart-mantra: *vajra muḥ*.

Then, arising from one’s own heart, one should form the Vajraratna-mudrā and place it at the site of self-consecration; with the two index fingers, one makes the gesture of consecration, wraps the hands around the head, and again forms the binding of the garland (*mālābandha*). By means of this very mudrā, one completes the Armor-mudrā (*kavaca-mudrā*).
Recite this heart-mantra:

*Oṃ vajraratnābhiṣeka sarvamudrāṇāṃ me dṛḍhīkuru vara-granthi vaṃ*. Then, having released this armor-binding-garland mudrā, one should next clap the palms together to form the Vajra-Ānanda mudrā and recite this heart-mantra: *Vajra-toṣaya hūṃ*.
By means of this mudrā and mantra, one releases the bonds of initiation; having performed the Ānanda, one immediately attains a body as firm as a vajra, no different from Vajrasattva himself.
Furthermore, the verse says:
"By reciting the name of Vajrasattva even once, One shall obtain sublime bliss according to one's desire;
All is accomplished in the mere instant of recitation, Just as taught by Vajrapāṇi."
"This was spoken by the virtuous Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.
Furthermore, the verse says:
'Vajrasattva and the other great beings, Skillfully accomplish all matters of siddhi.'"
If one recites according to one's inclination within this, all teachings will be accomplished. Regarding secret mantras,
heart-seals (*hṛdaya-mudrā*), and vidyās— following whichever method one prefers,
whether according to the instructions or through one’s own practice— one will achieve accomplishment in all places.
Furthermore, the four kinds of secret supreme offerings are proclaimed, and they are chanted with vajra songs.
Their respective great mantras are as follows:

"Oṃ vajrasattvasaṃgraha vajraratnābhiṣiñca vajradharmagāyana vajrakarmakaro bhava. Then, if one wishes to enter the maṇḍala, first within the inner maṇḍala, one should perform the vajra-singing and vajra-dancing with these four mantras, and perform the act of offering by forming the mudrās of the four secret offerings with both palms.
Next, perform the four types of vajra offerings, such as incense and so forth, within the outer maṇḍala, each placed in its proper location.

Then, one should address all the Tathāgatas; having offered incense and other offerings according to their inclinations, further present superior flavors, various foods and drinks, and all manner of articles of pleasure. Afterwards, following the ritual procedure, lead the disciple in and bestow upon them the vajra prohibitions for the accomplishment of all the Tathāgatas:
"This is the essential nature of all Buddhas, Abiding in the hand of Vajrasattva."
"You should now always receive and uphold this firm samaya of Vajrasattva.
Then, he bestows this great vidyā-mantra: Oṃ sarvatathāgata-siddhi-vajra-samayas tiṣṭha | iṣṭārthadhāraṇāya me | vajrasattva hi hi hi hi hūṃ || Thereafter, he addresses the disciple, saying:
"At all times, you must not reveal this secret dharma-gate to others.
Thereupon, he bestowed the samaya-mantra appropriate for him.
Thereafter, at all times, one should enter the maṇḍala as appropriate, present various offerings according to one's capacity, and address all Tathāgatas.
Once the ritual actions are completed, one should form the Sattvavajra mudrā and release it sequentially from bottom to top.
Recite this heart-mantra:

"Oṃ kṛto va sarvasattvārthasiddhida yathānugaccha saccidvanno buddhaviśayaṃ punarāgamanāya tu vajrasattva muḥ. With this heart-mantra, one should act thus within all maṇḍalas, and likewise release the samaya-vijaya-mudrā as appropriate.

2. The Section on the Extensive Ritual of the Vajra-Guhyamandala. Second. At that time, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, entered the *samādhi* called the Vajra-Sustaining Emanation of the Vajra-Dhāraṇī of All Tathāgatas.

Within this samādhi, from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, there appeared the sublime form and appearance of the virtuous Vajrapāṇi, the Great Vajradhara, as well as the Vajra-dhāraṇī-samādhi-mudrā of the Universal Blazing Treasury.

Once the assembly of all noble and holy beings has appeared, and all the Vajra-Dhāraṇī wisdom of the Buddhas and Tathāgatas of all worlds has been fully accomplished, the images of the Wisdom-Seals (jñāna-mudrā) of all Tathāgatas are manifested. Therein, the ritual application of the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu of all Tathāgatas is established, and [the deities] abide resting upon a pure lunar disc.
He spoke this verse:
"How great is the unsurpassed bodhicitta! May all sentient beings be filled with joy;
In order to cause them to submit peacefully and fearlessly, I manifest here in the form of a vidyārājñī."

At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, again entered the samādhi of the empowerment of the Vajradhātu through the Samādhi of the Wisdom-Seal of All Tathāgatas, and spoke this supreme heart-mantra:

“Oṃ vajra dhātveśvari hūṃ vajriṇi. Then, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, immediately entered the samādhi of the empowerment of the Maṇḍala of the Wisdom-Seal of the Vajrasattva of All Tathāgatas, and spoke this supreme heart-mantra:

“Oṃ vajravajriṇi hūṃ. At that time, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava, entered the samādhi empowered by the maṇḍala of the wisdom-seal of the Vajra-Jewel of all Tathāgatas, and spoke this supreme heart-mantra:

“Oṃ ratnavajriṇi hūṃ. At that time, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amitāyus, entered the samādhi empowered by the maṇḍala of the wisdom-seal of the Vajra-Dharma of all Tathāgatas, and spoke this supreme heart-mantra:

“Oṃ dharmavajri hūṃ. At that time, the World-Honored One, Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi, entered the samādhi of the empowerment of the Maṇḍala of the Wisdom-Seal of the Vajra-Karma of All Tathāgatas, and spoke this supreme heart-mantra:

“Oṃ karmavajri hūṃ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi spoke these four great vidyās of the Great Dhāraṇī-Samaya-Seal of All Tathāgatas: “Oṃ vajrasattvayogisamaye hūṃ. This vidyā is Samantabhadra.
"Oṃ jvālāvajraghoṣa hūṃ. This mantra is the hook of the Tathāgata.
"Oṃ jñānavajrarāgarāge hūṃ. This vidyā-mantra is itself desire-joy."
"Oṃ jvālāvajradhātu śrī hūṃ. This mantra is indeed 'Great Well Done' (Sādhu)."
"These are called the Vajra Dhāraṇī-gates.
Furthermore, the four vidyās are as follows: 'Oṃ vajra-ghurya ratna-samaye hūṃ. This vidyā is Ratnottama."
"Oṃ vajra-guhya-pravi hūṃ. This mantra is the Jewel Radiance."
"Oṃ vajratvagarbhe hūṃ. This vidyā-mantra is the Victorious Banner and Garland."
"Oṃ jyotihara-svadhāriṇi hūṃ. This mantra is the Great Laughter."
"These are called the gateways of the Jewel Dhāraṇī.
Furthermore, the four vidyās are as follows:
'Oṃ vajradharmaguhya-samaye hūṃ. This vidyā is the arising of the Vajra Cloud."
"Oṃ vajra-kuśalya hūṃ. This mantra is the ādhāraṇī."
“Oṃ vajra-guhya-maṇḍale hūṃ. This mantra is the wheel of all.
"Oṃ vajra-guhya-ja-pasamayī hūṃ. This mantra is that which transforms the great trichiliocosm."
"These are called the gateways to the dhāraṇī of the Dharma.
Furthermore, the four vidyās are as follows: 'Oṃ vajrayakṣa-karma-samaye hūṃ. This vidyā is the supreme accomplishment."
"Oṃ vajra-ghuṭa-kavaca hūṃ. This mantra is the protection of all."
"Oṃ vajra-guhya-ṇeṣṭara-dharīṇi hūṃ. This mantra is the Subduer of Majestic Splendor.
"Oṃ vajra-guhya-muṣṭi hūṃ. This mantra is the seal of the dhāraṇī.
"These are called the gateways to the collective *dhāraṇīs*.
At that time, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva Mahāsattva further spoke these four great vidyās of the Vajra-secret Samaya-mudrā of all Tathāgatas: "Oṃ..."
Oṃ vajrasattva hūṃ. Oṃ.
