The Second Part of the Second Section of the Extensive Ritual Manual for the Vajra Secret Maṇḍala. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, endowed with virtue, again spoke these verses on the secret great maṇḍala:
"I shall now, in due order, expound The supreme Vajra Maṇḍala."
Its characteristics are identical to that Vajradhātu; this is called the Vajra Secret.
In accordance with the method of the Great Maṇḍala, all maṇḍalas should likewise be drawn.
Within all maṇḍalas, according to the ritual rules, one should draw all the Buddha-mudrās.
Seated with legs crossed in the posture of meditative equipoise, this is named the Sovereign of the Vajradhātu;
with vajra-crossed legs and vajra-mark, this is the Vajra of the Vajra Family.
The vajra-jewel paryaṅka posture is thus called self-consecration;
the vajra-lotus paryaṅka posture is said to be the sustaining of life;
the karma-vajra paryaṅka posture is the method of the skillful-karma vajra.
One should draw the positions of lotuses everywhere, and furthermore, draw the marks of circular halos;
within the seats, one should draw vajra-clubs, as well as vajra-hooks standing upright.
One should draw two vajra-marks joined together, with both hands forming the "well done" (sādhu) mudrā.
Furthermore, one should paint the Jewel Heap with blazing flames; the seal of the sun’s orb is likewise.
The Victorious Banner is surrounded by intense light; the rows of teeth are in the form of a vajra-smile.
Within the vajra, one should paint the mark of a lotus; the sharp sword is likewise surrounded by blazing flames.
Furthermore, one should paint the great wheel of vajra-fire, and paint the tongue-mark complete with blazing flames;
everywhere, one should paint vajra-pestles, and one should paint the appearance of the vajra-armour;
according to the ritual, one should next paint the vajra-fangs, and the two hand-mudrās of the fists should be painted as appropriate.
One should paint the Sattvas, Vajras, and so forth, according to the ritual procedures explained for the great maṇḍala.
One must paint all their respective mudrās and insignia; within the maṇḍala of Vajralāsyā and the others, one should paint them according to the ritual rules.
Within the outer maṇḍala, one should likewise paint all the specific insignia of each respective family.
The same applies to Bodhisattva Maitreya and the others; they should all be depicted according to their respective preferences.
Furthermore, I shall now proclaim the ritual for entering the Vajra Secret Maṇḍala.

"The Vajrācārya, having first bound the Sattvavajra-mudrā himself, should enter the maṇḍala according to the instructions and perform a circumambulation to the right. He should present the mudrā he has bound to the Honored One Vajrapāṇi and recite his own heart-mantra at the four gates of the altar as prescribed."
Having performed the dissolution, one again binds the Vajrāṅkuśa-karmamudrā.

Having performed the ritual activities as taught in the instructions, one should then proceed toward and exit the maṇḍala; subsequently, one causes the vajra-disciples to enter the Vajradhātu-mahāmaṇḍala according to its ritual procedures in due order. Once they have entered, they then release their fists according to the dharma.
Next, one should bestow the secret accomplishment of the vajra insignia and instruct in the methods such as the wisdom of the vajra secret mudrā.
Furthermore, within this context, one should instruct in the wisdom of the vajra secret body-mudrā:
"Abiding within the pure moon maṇḍala, Visualize the vajra performing its vigorous dance."
The fingers and palms of the hands and feet all tremble; even the Vajra-vidyārājñī gives rise to love.
Bending the arms like the mudrā of holding a hook, visualize the vajra upon the head.
Striking the palms together to produce a resonant sound, visualize the vajra-hook as the act of summoning.
Furthermore, one should perform the rite of shooting arrows: assuming the posture of heroic exertion (*pragṛhīta*), shoot [the arrow] into the heart;
by thus slaying those various evil māras as appropriate, one shall personally attain the Vajra of Sublime Joy.
Furthermore, one should perform the binding by fastening it upon the arm, extending from one's own heart throughout the entire body;
through union with that application of the Vajra-dharma, one will personally receive the constant protection of all Buddhas.
Then he spoke these heart-mantras (*hṛdaya-mantra*) as follows:
VAJRA RĀGA HOḤ (1) VAJRĀṄKUŚA JAḤ (1) MĀRAMĀRAYA PHAṬ (1) BANDHALOCANA (1) Furthermore, the instruction on the wisdom-seal (*mudrā*) of the secret gaze of the Vajra:
"The gazes of all Vajras produce sublime love; That is to say, the joyful opening of the lotus-eyes."
Because one gazes upon the consort with this vision, one is immediately able to attain her constant and compliant love.
Furthermore, with extremely fierce and flickering eyes, the lashes of the eyes manifest the sign of illumination and summoning;
this is called the "Glorious Gaze," by which all those in the world are summoned.
Furthermore, with a frowning brow and a destructive mien, he can manifest the power of wrath in an instant;
this is called the Universal Holder’s Wrathful Gaze, which subdues even the three times.
Furthermore, one should fix the eyes with firm and loving-kindness, Like the mountain stones of Mount Sumeru;
This is called the gaze of loving-kindness, Which can destroy pestilential poisons and malevolent spirits.
Then he spoke these heart-mantras (*hṛdaya-mantra*):
VAJRA-DṚṢṬI-MAṬA (1) NĪ-PADA-DṚṢṬI-KUŚI-JAṄ (2) GURU-DHA-DṚṢṬI-HĪ (3) DṚTA-DṚ-DṚṢṬI-TRAṬA (4) Furthermore, the instruction on the knowledge of the mudrā of the Vajra Secret Speech:
When one utters "HU HU HU HU," in an instant one attains the state beyond speech.
Causing all sentient beings to give rise to wholesome love, they attain adamantine speech that is entirely luminous and radiant.
When these syllables *jaḥ jaḥ jaḥ jaḥ* are recited, all sounds and speech become luminous and radiant;
one is universally able to summon all worlds and immediately becomes no different from Vajrapāṇi.
HŪṂ HŪṂ HŪṂ HŪṂ! Because they are all-pervading holders, the words of all the wrathful ones become brilliantly clear;
they slay all malevolent sentient beings, who are as numerous as the stones upon the mountains of Mount Sumeru.
When these syllables—ṢAṂ ṢAṂ ṢAṂ ṢAṂ—are recited, all subtle and wondrous speech becomes utterly radiant and clear;
they are able to universally protect all worlds, and one immediately attains a vajra body identical to that of the Buddha.
Then he spoke these heart-mantras (*hṛdaya-mantra*):
VAJRA HŪṂ (1) | VAJRA JAḤ (1) | VAJRA HŪṂ (1) | VAJRA ĀḤ (1). Furthermore, the instruction on the wisdom of the Vajra Secret Heart-Seal (*mudrā*) is as follows:
"One should visualize oneself as being fully endowed with all the [divine] marks."
One’s own self is Vajrapāṇi; one attains the sublime love born of all those Buddhas.
One should visualize one's own body as it truly is, complete with all its marks;
one’s own self is Vajragarbha, who is able to summon Vajrapāṇi.
One should visualize oneself accordingly, complete with all the marks;
one's own body is the Vajra Eye, which destroys the evils of Māra through the True Dharmas.
One should visualize oneself accordingly, complete with all the various marks;
one's own body is the Skillful Vajra, receiving the constant protection of all the Vajras.
Then he spoke these heart-mantras as follows:
VAJRA PA...
Nivāśa-mānaya sarva-mṛtaṃ.
Vajragarbha vajra.
Bhaṇiḥ kṣetraḥ (or Bhaṇiḥ-kṣetra)
MĀKṢĀYA HŪṂ.
2. VAJRA-NITTRA (Vajra-nittra)
Sarvadāṃ (1) māḥ.
RAḤ HŪṂ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ | VAJRAVIŚODHANI SARVA...
Vajra āḥ. Furthermore, the instruction on the wisdom of the Vajra Secret Seal:
"Because the Sattva-vajra is omnipresent, one should visualize oneself within one's own heart."
Perform the universal visualization of the vajra-gaze, universally awakening all worlds.
Because one universally upholds the Great Jewel Vajra, visualize oneself within one's own heart;
perform the universal visualization of the light-gaze, summoning all and causing them to be drawn in with love.
Because the sublime Dharma is the pervasive vajra, one visualizes oneself within one's own heart;
casting a wrathful gaze everywhere, one slays all the evil māras of the world.
Because he universally upholds the Karma-vajra, he visualizes his own body within his own heart;
casting eyes of loving-kindness, he gazes everywhere, providing excellent protection for all the world.
Then he spoke these heart-mantras (*hṛdaya-mantra*):

VAJRA-GUHYA-SAMAYA ĀḤ VAJRA-GUHYA-SAMAYA HŪṂ VAJRA-GUHYA-SAMAYA HOḤ VAJRA-GUHYA-SAMAYA HAṂ Furthermore, the ritual procedure for binding the Great Secret Seal (*mahāmudrā*) of the Vajra is taught as follows:
“The seal produced from the vajra-palms Is called the Great Secret.”
I shall now explain the ritual for forming the seals of those great mudrās in their proper sequence:
Interlock the two thumbs with one another, then bend the tips of the index fingers so that they touch;
extend the two middle fingers upward—this is the seal of the Sovereign of the Vajradhātu.
This very middle finger forms the vajra-mudrā; furthermore, the middle finger takes the shape of a jewel, while the middle and ring fingers form a lotus;
extending the palm, these four mudrās should be performed in sequence.
The two index fingers are like vajras; the two thumbs are both tucked away.
The snapping of the fingers and the index fingers form the jewel [mudrā];
then again, with the index fingers in the form of jewel-light, the two ring fingers are held upright like jewels. One then turns this seal toward the mouth.
Again, extend and spread all the fingers, erect the two thumbs so they remain in the center, and extend the fingers like the appearance of a wheel; then, with this mudrā, release it from the mouth.
Extending the thumbs like vajras, with the two index fingers extended and held in the middle,
opening the two thumbs again like tusks, then drawing them back into the palms to form the fist-seal;
this is the Vajra Secret Dharma, which arises from that vajra-binding.
Furthermore, regarding the secret insignia of the Dharma: visualize the internal mind as being naturally united;
the secret of Karma likewise abides therein, and the insignia of Karma should be manifested.
"Now I shall explain the sequence of the Dharma-mudrās, namely the various seeds of the supreme secret:

'One should form the secret mudrā with both hands; as taught, one should distinguish the karma-mudrās, up to the samaya, dharma, and victory mudrās; that which is accomplished by both hands is likewise so.'"

Next, the ritual for accomplishment shall be proclaimed: by reciting "Samayasattva," if one binds one's own mudrā, one will immediately achieve success and obtain the supreme, wondrous bliss of all desires.
Whether single or manifold, these secret mudrās should not be bound at any other time.
Whether accomplishing great deeds or in secret practice, the wise should act in harmony as is appropriate.
Always dwelling within this state, the vajra retinue arises spontaneously;
the practitioner, with firm and sublime loving-kindness, should never abandon it for as long as life endures.
Furthermore, the proclamation of all the activities for forming mudrās and so forth:
"Once the Vajra-pervasion has arisen, whether one forms or releases various mudrās for oneself or another therein, one should recite this heart-mantra accordingly:"
“Vajra hūṃ bandha. Next, the ritual procedure for releasing the mudrās is explained:
“The sequence of all mudrās, which arise from their respective origins, should be released at those same respective locations while reciting this heart-mantra:”
"Oṃ vajra muḥ. Next, the ritual procedure for the firm protection of the body is explained:
"Form the precious vajra-firm fist; with the two index fingers, form the armor mudrā.
Release it sequentially from the heart to the crown of the head, while reciting the following heart-mantra as appropriate:"
“Oṃ dṛḍhavajrakaṣaca tr̥ṭ. Next, the ritual for the *samaya-bandha* (binding of the pledge) is explained:
Having thoroughly loosened [the bonds] everywhere as appropriate, one should form the firm protection-of-the-body mudrā.
With palms joined at the level of the waist, perform the striking gesture; then recite this heart-mantra:
Recite the Vajra Secret Verses as you wish; skillfully perform all the rites of the mandala.
When one accords with the samādhi within this, one can achieve the most supreme of accomplishments.

3. The Section on the Extensive Ritual for the Vajrajñāna-Dharmamaṇḍala, Part Three. At that time, the venerable Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi again entered the samādhi of the empowerment of the maṇḍala of the subtle vajra-jñāna-mudrā of all Tathāgatas, and spoke this supreme heart-mantra:

“Oṃ suṣṭhu karmavajra-jñānasamayā hūṃ. At that time, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, entered the samādhi of the empowerment of the maṇḍala of the subtle vajra-wisdom seal of the Vajrasattva of all Tathāgatas, and spoke this supreme heart-mantra:

“Oṃ vajrasattvasūkṣmamudrānyasanasamayā hūṃ. At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava, entered the samādhi of empowerment for the maṇḍala of the subtle wisdom-vajra seal of all Tathāgatas’ vajra-jewels, and spoke this supreme heart-mantra:

"Oṃ vajraratna sūkṣma-jñāna-samaya hūṃ. At that time, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amitāyus, entered the samādhi of the empowerment of the maṇḍala of the subtle vajra-wisdom seal of the vajra-dharma of all Tathāgatas, and spoke this supreme heart-mantra:

“Oṃ vajradharma sucakṣa-mā-jñāna-samaya hūṃ. At that time, the Bhagavān Amoghasiddhi Tathāgata entered the samādhi of the empowerment of the subtle wisdom-seal maṇḍala of the vajra-activity of all Tathāgatas, and spoke this supreme heart-mantra:

"Oṃ vajrakarma sucakṣma jñānasamayā hūṃ. At that time, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, entered the samādhi of the subtle wisdom-vajra of all Tathāgatas. Within this samādhi, from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, there emerged the subtle wisdom-vajra radiance of the virtuous Vajradhara.

Having appeared, he universally illuminated all worlds; having become firmly established within the assembly of all Tathāgatas and within the samādhi and samāpatti of the subtle vajra-wisdom of all Tathāgatas, he again became a single mass. Having thoroughly observed with the sublime vajra-body of samādhi-wisdom, he merged into a single entity and gave rise to the wisdom-body of a Tathāgata, which dwelt within the heart of the Bhagavān Mahāvairocana Tathāgata in accordance with the principle.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, endowed with virtue, entered the wisdom-mind of all Tathāgatas.
Having thus entered, he spoke this Vajra Great Mantra of the Subtle Wisdom Samādhi of All Tathāgatas:

"Kṣamavajra. When this great mantra was spoken, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, endowed with virtue, emerged from the hearts of all Tathāgatas. By means of a body that was the empowered image of the subtle wisdom-vajra of all Tathāgatas, he stood upon the tips of the noses of all Tathāgatas and spoke this verse:
“Great indeed is the Honored One, the Fully Enlightened One of All! I am the subtle and wondrous Vajra, vast and expansive.
Because of this vast and subtle nature, I am able to pervade the entire triple world.”

When the virtuous Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi had spoken thus, he immediately, by means of the subtle mark of vajra-wisdom, extended [it] throughout the bodies of all Tathāgatas from the tips of their noses.

Having thus extended and pervaded, it further permeates the entire dharma-realm and merges with the realm of space. Because this subtle mark of vajra-wisdom extends and pervades throughout the entirety of the realm of space, it abides accordingly within the bodies of the reflected images empowered by the wisdom-vajras of all Tathāgatas.

Thus, this reflected body, in a single instant, merges into the wisdom-vajra of all Tathāgatas; having observed the vajra-dharmatā, one abides accordingly within the samādhi of the subtle wisdom-vajra of all Tathāgatas and all Tathāgatas.
Thereupon, from the vajras of all Tathāgatas, he spoke this heart-mantra of the samādhi-wisdom of all Tathāgatas:

*vajranābhitathāgata hūṃ*. When this heart-mantra was spoken, the virtuous Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi again entered the subtle wisdom of his own mind and merged with the bodies of all Tathāgatas.
Having entered thus, one forms the image of a vajra within one’s own mind and abides in accordance with the principle.
At that time, all the Tathāgatas spoke these heart-mantras of the four great wisdoms, such as the Sattvavajra: "Vajra-tama-ka. This is the wisdom-mudrā of Vajrasattva.
"Hrīḥ nāvaraṃ kuśa. This is the wisdom-seal (*jñānamudrā*) of the empowerment of the assembly of all Tathāgatas.
“Tiṣṭha rāgavajrapravīśahrīḥ. This is the Wisdom-Seal (jñānamudrā) of the Delight of All Tathāgatas.
"ĀḤ VAJRA-ṬUṢṬI. This is the Great Joy Wisdom Seal (*mahā-pramoda-jñāna-mudrā*).
These are called the gateways of the great vajra meditative absorption (*mahā-vajra-samādhi*) of all Tathāgatas.
At that time, the virtuous Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi again entered the subtle wisdom of the heart of all Tathāgatas, merging it with his own mind.
Having thus entered, one abides within one’s own mind in accordance with the principle, by means of the body of the reflected image empowered by the vajra.
Regarding this very mark of the vajra-reflected image, the mantra of the four minds is proclaimed as:
*vajraratnatmadhṛk* (Vajra-ratna-ātma-dhṛk). This is the empowerment-wisdom seal (*abhiṣeka-jñāna-mudrā*) of all Tathāgatas.
VAJRA-SŪRYA-ṬIṢṬHA (1). This is the wisdom-seal (jñāna-mudrā) for the adornment of the Great Radiance Maṇḍala.
“Vajratvaja-gara vaṃ. This is the Wisdom Seal (jñānamudrā) that fulfills the aspirations of all Tathāgatas.
"Hrīḥ naya-vajra ha sa. This is the wisdom-seal (jñāna-mudrā) that gives rise to the great joy of all Tathāgatas.
"These are called the gateways of the precious samādhis of all Tathāgatas.
At that time, the virtuous Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi again entered his own subtle and wondrous wisdom, merging it with his own mind.
Having entered in this manner, one abides according to principle with a body that is an image empowered by vajra.
Regarding this very characteristic of the vajra-image, the mantra of the four minds is stated as:
*vajrapadmatma-ka*. This is the seal (*mudrā*) of the wisdom of the equality of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-samatājñāna*).
"Hrīḥ navara kuśa. This is the wisdom seal (jñānamudrā) of all Tathāgatas."
Tiṣṭha vajra-cakra-hṛdaya-praviśa. This is the entry into the Great Wheel Wisdom Seal (mahācakra-jñāna-mudrā).
"Vajra-jihvāgra-hrīḍaya. This is the wisdom-seal (*jñāna-mudrā*) of all Tathāgatas’ Dharma-speech, which is free from conceptual proliferation (*niṣprapañca*)."
"These are called the gateways of the dhāraṇī of the Dharma of all Tathāgatas.
At that time, the virtuous Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi again entered the subtle wisdom of the vajra from the vajra-heart of his own mind, merging with the vajra-heart.
Having thus entered, he further abides through the empowerment of the body of the extremely subtle vajra-image, and speaks these four heart-mantras of the extremely subtle vajra-image and so forth:
"Sarva-vajra-tama-ka. This is the skillful-action wisdom-seal (*karmajñānamudrā*) of all Tathāgatas.
"Hrīḥ navavajra-gavaja. This is the Wisdom Seal of the Most Difficult-to-Vanquish Vow.
“Tiṣṭha vajrayakṣa hṛdaya. This is the wisdom-seal (jñānamudrā) that destroys all demonic realms.
“Vajramuṣṭi hrīḥ naya. This is the wisdom-seal (jñānamudrā) of binding for all Tathāgatas.
"These are called the gateways to the samādhis of the ritual activity (*karma*) of all Tathāgatas.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, endowed with virtue, again extended his subtle and wondrous marks of wisdom and merged them with the bodies of all Tathāgatas.

Having emerged from this, he immediately manifests the body of the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, further assuming the forms of great bodhisattvas such as Vajrasattva; each having placed their respective insignia upon their own heart, they then establish the ritual applications corresponding to the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu, abiding in reliance upon the meditative absorption (*samādhi*) of the pure moon maṇḍala within their own hearts.

Furthermore, the virtuous Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, desiring to accomplish all the matters of the samādhi-wisdom and supernormal powers of all Tathāgatas, spoke this subtle wisdom maṇḍala of vajra-wisdom:
"I shall now explain in sequence The supreme and wondrous moon maṇḍala, Whose characteristics are like those of the Vajradhātu; Because it is the subtle vajra, it is thus proclaimed."
In accordance with the ritual of the Great Maṇḍala, one should establish the Great Sattva as taught;
within the Vajra altar, one should paint the forms of the Buddhas—thus is the Buddha Maṇḍala established.
Throughout the maṇḍala, one should draw the Great Sattva;
placing the self-seal upon the heart as taught, one should assume the posture of samādhi, with both hands forming the vajra-bond.
Furthermore, the ritual procedures for the invocation and other rites of the subtle Vajra Dharma Maṇḍala are proclaimed.

That is to say, having performed all the rituals for entry and so forth within the great maṇḍala according to the corresponding methods, one should then bestow the insignia of great wisdom, which should be employed according to the activities to be performed by one's own mind.
"Furthermore, the method for teaching the wisdom of the Great Seal (Mahāmudrā):
Having gradually emerged from the tongue and the palate, Next, fix the visualization upon the tip of the nose;
When the subtle touch of vajra-bliss arises, The mind immediately abides in meditative equipoise (samāhita)."
Within the subtle vajra touch of bliss, from this arises a supreme mark;
because this mark is vast and all-pervasive, the mind is likewise vast and pervades all.
Expanding according to the mind’s delight, that vastness immediately pervades the three realms.
Furthermore, one should gradually contract [the visualization] in reverse, withdrawing it even to the tip of the nose;
thereafter, all that exists should be constantly visualized as the sublime meditative equipoise (*samāpatti*).
Firmly establishing what has been performed throughout everything, the wisdom of *samādhi* is thus established.
Then he spoke these heart-mantras (*hṛdaya-mantra*):
“If one arouses a mind of loving-kindness toward sentient beings, One should likewise arouse it with great firmness;
Because it accords with the vastness of the mind, All sentient beings are also vast.”
Because it is conjoined with the vastness of loving-kindness, the compassion that arises is likewise so;
conjoined with the benefit of all sentient beings, all one's activities are entirely vast.

The intrinsic nature is luminous and pervades all; Primordially pure, equal to space, whether it be dharmas or non-dharmas therein, Contemplating them all as universally pure, one rejoices in their entirety.
All those who are extremely wicked are not vessels for the Buddha’s bodhi;
yet, observing them with a mind of great equanimity, he likewise embraces them all.
Then he spoke these heart-mantras as follows:
MAHĀ MĪ TRĪ SAPPHARA | MAHĀ KARUṆA SAPPHARA | SARVA ŚUDDHA-PRA-MODA SAPPHARA | SARVA-SATTVA-SAMĀDĀPAYA || Furthermore, the instruction on the wisdom of recollecting all the Tathāgatas is given.
Whether in the midst of space or in any other direction, one should harmonize with the subtle vajra;
whether sitting or rising within the midst of dignified conduct, one should constantly visualize the reflection of the vajra.
In all places it is likewise so; the subtle vajra is ever in union.
Thus, the mind-vajra of all bodhisattvas should visualize it as eternally abiding in sublime meditative equipoise.
One should constantly visualize that great image of Vajrapāṇi in all places,
in accordance with the subtle vajra-dharma, following the sequence as it has been taught.
Visualize the Buddha’s image pervading all, Complete with every one of his marks;
Following the sequence as it has been taught, One should practice meditative absorption accordingly.
Then he spoke these heart-mantras (*hṛdaya-mantra*):
“Because of union with the subtle vajra, one should immediately visualize one’s own body;
within the reflection of a moon appearing from one’s own body, one should visualize the pure bodhicitta.”
Furthermore, within a pure and wondrous lunar disc, one should visualize oneself as appropriate;
one's own body is the Vajra-form, identical in nature to the thought of Sattvavajra.
In union with the subtle Vajra-dharma, one should visualize oneself accordingly;
within one's own body is the Sattva-vajra mind, which is no different from the conception of the Sattva-vajra.
One should visualize oneself accordingly, complete with all the marks;
one's own body is the very image of the Buddha, and one should visualize the enlightenment of all Buddhas.
Then he spoke these heart-mantras (*hṛdaya-mantra*):
*Samantabhadra viśa sattvavajra viśa vajrasattvasamādhi-nyāna viśa tathāgatodghaṭṭam.* Furthermore, he taught the secret seal-wisdom (*guhyamudrājñāna*) of the *dharmatā* of all Tathāgatas:
"I am equal to all Buddhas; By reciting once this Vajra Secret Speech,"
The vajra and lotus joined in union, causing all sentient beings to share in sublime love.
I am indeed identical to the Great Vajra; by once uttering the secret vajra words, the vajra and lotus joined in union, one will certainly summon all the world.
I am indeed identical to the Vajra Dharma; by reciting once the secret vajra speech, the two aspects of the vajra and lotus are joined together, universally subduing all throughout the world.
I am identical to the Skillful Vajra; by once uttering the secret vajra speech and joining the two signs of the vajra and lotus, one can accomplish all activities.
Furthermore, the instruction on the wisdom-seal of the empowerment of the Wisdom-Vajra of all Tathāgatas:
"In harmony with the subtle Vajra-dharma, Visualize the Vajra abiding within the heart;
One’s own body is the very image of the Buddha— By means of this visualization, one becomes a Buddha."
"Furthermore, the instruction on the wisdom of the Vajrasattva Samādhi Mudrā:
'Because of the union with the subtle vajra, The mind-vajra is equal to those multitudes;
One should contemplate oneself as Vajrasattva and the like, Which can bestow all self-accomplishments.'"
"Furthermore, the instruction on the knowledge of the samādhi and samaya-mudrās of the entire Tathāgata family:
'From that vajra-binding arise the samādhi and samaya-vijaya-mudrās;
the sixteen mahāsattvas should be applied in their proper order; their binding mudrās shall now be explained.'"

Regarding what are called the *paryaṅka-mudrā* (cross-legged posture), the *ucchrita-vega-mudrā* (raised momentum), the *iṣu-vartana-mudrā* (arrow-twisting), and the *hṛdaya-sthita-mudrā* (abiding at the heart): [these are performed] at the forehead, between the shoulders, on the shoulder, and at the site of the smile;
they hold the *mukha-dvāra-hṛdaya* (heart of the mouth-gate), the *khaḍga-hṛdaya* (sword-heart), and the *praphulla* (blooming);
they radiate from the mouth to the crown of the head, the chest, the face, the thumbs, the front of the heart, and so forth.
Furthermore, the sequence for teaching the Supreme Dharma-Mudrā is as follows:

*ṭa ke* (one syllable), *gara gara* (two syllables), *mṭha* (one mora), *akara* (two syllables), *traṃ traṃ* (two syllables), *aṃ aṃ* (one syllable), *daṃ daṃ* (one syllable), *traṭa* (one syllable), *triṭa* (one syllable), *briṭa* (one syllable), *kuśa* (one syllable), *ha ha* (one syllable), *va va* (one syllable), *baṃ baṃ* (one syllable), *phaṭ* (one mora), *kara sa* (two syllables). Furthermore, the instruction on the Supreme Dharma-Karma is given.
Regarding what is called "the performance of all desires," one should, in accordance with the dharma of samādhi, form the subtle Vajra-Wisdom Fist, which is produced by the union of both hands.
The Mahāyāna-abhisamaya-samādhi-śrī-mahātantra-rāja, Spoken by the Buddha, Entitled “The True Gathering of All Tathāgatas,” Fascicle Seven.
The Mahāyāna-abhisamaya-samādhi-śrī-mahātantra-rāja, Spoken by the Buddha,
Entitled “The True Gathering of All Tathāgatas,” Fascicle Eight.

Chapter Four: The Extensive Ritual Manual of the Vajrakarma Maṇḍala. At that time, the virtuous Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi again entered the *samādhi* of the Vajra-empowerment of the pervasive *karma* of the extensive ritual manual for the unsurpassed offerings of all Tathāgatas, and spoke this supreme heart-mantra (*hṛdaya-mantra*) as follows:

“Oṃ sarvatathāgata-vajradhātvanuttarapūjāspharaṇa-karmasamaye hūṃ. At that time, the Blessed One, Akṣobhya Tathāgata, entered the samādhi of the vajra empowerment known as the Extensive Ritual of the Supreme Offering of All Tathāgatas’ Vajrasattva, Pervasive Karma, and spoke this supreme heart-mantra:

“Oṃ sarvatathāgata-vajrasattva-anuttarapūjā-spharaṇa-karmasamaye hūṃ. At that time, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava, entered the vajra-empowerment samādhi of the pervasive ritual of the supreme offering of the vajra-jewel of all Tathāgatas, and spoke this supreme heart-mantra:

“Oṃ sarvatathāgata-vajra-ratnābhiṣeka-karmaspharaṇasamaye hūṃ. At that time, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amitāyus, entered the vajra-adhiṣṭhāna-samādhi of the extensive ritual procedure for the supreme offering of the Vajradharma of all Tathāgatas, which pervades the pervasive karma, and spoke this supreme heart-mantra:

“Oṃ sarvatathāgatavajradharmānudārapūjāspharaṇakarmasamaye hūṃ. At that time, the Bhagavān Amoghasiddhi Tathāgata entered the samādhi of the vajra empowerment of the pervasive karma of the ritual procedure for the vast and supreme offering of the vajra-karma of all Tathāgatas, and spoke this supreme mantra of his own heart: “Oṃ sarva...”
Tathāgata-vajra (one phrase) [tathāgata-vajra] (two syllables)
Karmānudārābhogaḥ
Spharaṇa-karma.

*Samaye Hūṃ.* At that time, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, again entered the Vajra-samādhi of the Samaya of Karma, which is the vast ritual procedure for making offerings to all Tathāgatas, pervading and extending throughout the entire Dharmadhātu. Within this samādhi, from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, there appeared the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Guṇavat-vajrapāṇi. Because he pervades and extends throughout the entire Dharmadhātu and enters into all realms of space, he manifested as a vast ocean-like cloud of all manner of wondrous offerings and adornments, circulating throughout the ritual procedures for all worthy sages.

These noble and holy ones, streaming forth from the ocean-like clouds that pervade all worlds, have gathered within the great maṇḍala of the assembly of all Tathāgatas. From the unsurpassed great bodhicitta of all Tathāgatas, they give rise to the wisdom of the *anurāga-jñāna* (wisdom of loving interest) of the families of all Tathāgatas, thereby accomplishing the supreme and most excellent conduct of Samantabhadra. They proceed to the site of great enlightenment (*mahābodhimaṇḍa*), subdue the hosts of Māras, and manifest perfect awakening through the equality of all Tathāgatas. Born from the great maṇḍala of all Tathāgatas, they universally turn the supreme wheel of the True Dharma throughout the three realms, extensively performing all manner of beneficial deeds for the entire realm of sentient beings without exception, and manifesting the miraculous displays of the supernatural powers of all Buddhas.

Then, those clouds and oceans of offerings to all the worthy sages and holy ones, having each bound their respective root mudrās and performed the offerings according to what is taught in the ritual manuals of all Tathāgatas, took their places, relying upon the moon disk corresponding to the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu.
He spoke this verse:
“Great indeed are the Buddhas whom I worship; I act as the transformer of all offerings.
Because the nature of the Buddhas is vast and great, All the Buddhas’ acts of giving are thereby accomplished.”
At that time, the virtuous Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi further proclaimed the extensive ritual manual for the rites of worship and so forth of all Tathāgatas:
"The great mantra of the Vajrakarma Maṇḍala is: Oṃ sarvatathāgata-sarvatama-nirya-tanapūjā-spharaṇa-karmavajri āḥ. This is the supreme bliss of all Tathāgatas."
"Oṃ sarvatathāgata-sarvatattva-niryātana-karṣaṇa-prajñāraṇa-karmagṛhīḥ jaḥ. This is the hook-summoning of all Tathāgatas."
"Oṃ sarvatathāgata-sarvatama-nirjāta-anurāgaṇa-praspharaṇa-karmavānī hūṃ hoḥ. This is the delight of all the Tathāgatas."
“Oṃ sarvatathāgata-sarvatama-niryātana-sādhu-kāra-prayoga-spharaṇa-graha-dṛṣṭyaḥ. This is the universal joy of all Tathāgatas.
"These are called the Great Offerings to all Tathāgatas.
Furthermore, the great mantra is as follows: Oṃ namas sarvatathāgatānāṃ gayāviśiṣṭa-garbhita-vyūha-vajra-maṇi oṃ. This is the Great Sovereign."
"Oṃ namo sarvatathāgatebhyaḥ surativyūhavajra-tejini-jvala-hi. This is the Great Radiance."
"Oṃ namaḥ sarvatathāgatāśāparipūraṇajñānamahitejovajrateja-gṛhīta svāhā. This is the Great Jewel Rain.
“Oṃ namaḥ sarvatathāgatebhyo mahāpṛthivīpramokṣakarī vajrahāsye haḥ. This is the Great Joy.”
"These are called the empowerment offerings for all Tathāgatas.
Furthermore, the Great Mantra is: Oṃ sarvatathāgatavajradharmatāsamādhi-viṣṭo-nami mahādharmaguhya-hrīḥ. This is the Song of Great Wisdom."
"Oṃ sarvatathāgata-prajñāpāramitā-nirhāra-siddhanumite mahāguśanugye taṃ. This is the Great Sound."
"Oṃ sarvatathāgata-cakrākṣara-parivartita sarvasūtrendradhāraṇī-mayi sarvamaṇḍale hūṃ. This is the universal entry into all maṇḍalas."
"Oṃ sarvatathāgata-sandhā-vyūha-buddhasaṃgīti-vigrahya-siddhanu-mi vajra-vajri vaṃ. This is the practice of the mantra-words (mantrapada)."
"These are called the Dharma-offering of all Tathāgatas.
Furthermore, the Great Illumination (mahāvidyā) is as follows: 'Oṃ sarvatathāgatadūṣyamālābharaṇapravarjitagṛhṇa gṛhṇa. This is the Great Hero."
“Oṃ sarvatathāgata puṣpaprasara-spharaṇapūjā-karomi giri-giri. This is the Great Enlightenment Portion.
"Oṃ sarvatathāgatālokagarbharaspharaṇapūjā-karomi | vara vara || This is the Great Illuminating Mantra."
"Oṃ sarvatathāgata-gandhasamudra-spharaṇa-prayogakarmīṇi kuru kuru. This is the Great Perfume."
"These are called the ritual offerings of all Tathāgatas.
Furthermore, the Vajra-Action Maṇḍala is proclaimed, which refers to the performance of all offerings to all Tathāgatas without exception."
"I shall now, in due order, expound the supreme Karma Maṇḍala;
its characteristics are like those of the Vajradhātu, for it is the activity of the Vajra."
In accordance with the rites of the Great Maṇḍala, one should arrange the images of the Buddhas therein;
conjoined with Vajrasattva and the others, the seals (mudrās) of those noble ones should be drawn according to the ritual rules.

Next, the ritual procedures for entering the Vajrakarma Maṇḍala and so forth are explained; that is to say, one should enter accordingly according to the ritual applications of the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu.
Having thus entered, he says to the disciple:

"This is the Samādhi of Making Offerings to All Tathāgatas; you should daily constantly make offerings to the sixteen great beings, yet you must also perform various activities according to your ability."

Having spoken thus, he removed the face-cloth from his disciple and immediately had him gaze upon the maṇḍala within; he then conferred upon him the insignia of the specific karmic family, whereby even all the Tathāgatas shall offer him worship, let alone others!
"Furthermore, the instruction for accomplishing the offering mudrā of the great bodhicitta is as follows:
'Arising from the firm bodhicitta, I visualize myself as all the Buddhas;
By means of this playful offering, I immediately attain the supreme, wondrous bliss of all Buddhas.'"
Born from the firm bodhicitta, I visualize all the Buddhas;
by offering this precious garland, I universally make offerings and receive empowerment.
Born from the firm bodhicitta, I perform this visualization of all Buddhas;
through the offering of songs and sublime music, may I obtain exquisite love by means of universal offering.
Born from the firm bodhicitta, I visualize all the Buddhas;
through this offering of circumambulatory dance, even the Buddhas themselves receive my worship.
Then he spoke these great mantras as follows:

*Buddha-tamaṃ hūṃ* (1) *Buddha-mabhisecaya mi* (1) *Buddha-stuti-kāruṇi mi* (1) *Buddha-pūjā-kāruṇi mi* (1) Furthermore, the instruction on the wisdom-seal (*mudrā*) for making offerings to all Buddhas:
One should perform the gesture of prostration corresponding to the supreme body, speech, and mind-vajras.
By making this offering to all Buddhas, one will certainly attain their eternal faith and veneration.
That great mass of merit of all those Buddhas arises from the vajra of body, speech, and mind;
because I offer it with sympathetic joy, I shall thereby swiftly attain Buddhahood.
This body, speech, and mind, the essence of the vajra— I offer this subtle and wondrous body;
Among all the offerings to the Buddhas, I make this offering as my worship.
All supreme and virtuous deeds, arising from the vajra of body, speech, and mind—
by dedicating these as offerings, one attains equality with all Buddhas, without distinction.
Then he spoke these great mantras:
*praṇamāmi* (1), *anumanye* (2), *buddhapūjā* (3), *mālīna* (4). Furthermore, the instruction on the seal and wisdom of the Dharma-offering (*dharmapūjāmudrājñāna*) is as follows:
“The intrinsic nature of all phenomena is entirely luminous; their intrinsic nature is primordially pure.”
By means of making such offerings of Dharma, one immediately attains the supreme and wondrous bliss of all Buddhas;
once the conventional designations and verbal expressions of the gate of marks have been established, all dharmas are then fully assembled.
It is said that by means of such gates of the Dharma-seal, one is able to sever all suffering;
such dharmas pervade all things, and within the causal state, this very dharma is the Tathāgata.
By making offerings with the wheel of the True Dharma, one becomes a holder of the Dharma through such offering.
Within the intrinsic nature of all phenomena, All taught dharmas are like echoes;
By making offerings through these very dharmas, One can swiftly attain the voice of perfect enlightenment.
Then he spoke these great mantras:
*sarvaśuddha* (1), *samantabhadra* (2), *dharmakṣetra* (3), *niṣprapañca* (4). Furthermore, the instruction on the wisdom of the Samādhi-mudrā:
Within the vajras of body, speech, and mind, one’s own body is like the size of a minute mote of dust.
Visualizing the forms and marks of the vajra-image, one can swiftly attain the vajra-body.
Within that vajra of body, speech, and mind, one's own body is like a mote of dust;
by contemplating it as pervading all Buddhas, one can swiftly attain the sublime Dharma-body.

Within the vajras of his body, speech, and mind, one visualizes one's own body as being the size of a minute atom, contemplating it as the body of Vajrasattva; thus, one becomes inseparable from Vajrasattva.
Within the vajras of his body, speech, and mind, one should visualize one’s own body as being the size of a minute atom, appearing as the very image of the Buddha;
thus, one will swiftly attain the true essence of Buddhahood.
Then he spoke these great mantras: *vajra-gaya* *dharma-gaya* *sattva-gaya* *buddha-gaya* Furthermore, the instruction on the secret mudrā-knowledge:
When all those bodies are completely unified, spontaneous sublime bliss constitutes the offering.
By making this offering, one can swiftly attain a state no different from Vajrasattva.
Because it accords with the union of true and sublime passion, wherever it is directed, pleasurable touch arises.
By making this offering to all Buddhas, one attains a state no different from the Vajra-Jewel.
Firm and stable joy and bliss constantly succeed one another; wherever they touch and in whatever way they respond, supreme bliss arises.
By offering this to all Buddhas, one attains the vajra-dharma, which is equal and without distinction.
The vajra and lotus mudrās joined together, with pervasive sublime bliss in union—
by offering this as a gift, one attains equality with the Vajrakarma and others.
Then he spoke these great mantras:
*RĀTI VAJRA* (1) *RĀGA VAJRA* (1) *PRITI VAJRA* (1) *KĀMA VAJRA* (1) Furthermore, the instruction on the wisdom of the Great Seal of the Ritual of Offering to all Tathāgatas is as follows:
Namely, the heart, both flanks, and the back; The two breasts, the two shoulders, the throat, and the forehead.
From both ears, the crown of the head, down to the waist—thus, one should perform the sixteen locations according to the rite.
Furthermore, the instruction on the wisdom of the *samaya-mudrā* for the ritual of making offerings to all Tathāgatas is as follows:
"That which is called the firm binding of the vajra-bond is itself the method for the correspondence with the Great Seal (*mahāmudrā*)."
"Arrange the mind and all other locations according to the original ritual, and offer worship to the Buddhas.
Furthermore, [I shall explain] the wisdom of the mudrās for the ritual of making offerings to all Tathāgatas."
That is to say:

"Oṃ kṛyāya svāhā tīraṃ haṃ kroṃ śaṃ hūṃ he śaṇa si saṃ. Next, the *karmamudrā* is explained: according to the ritual procedure and in its proper sequence, one should form the *karmamuṣṭi* (action-fist) with both hands and thereby accomplish all the various mudrās.

Chapter Five: The Great Ritual Manual for the Realization of Samādhi. At that time, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, through the power of the empowerment of all Tathāgatas, proclaimed the great ritual manual of the family of all Tathāgatas arising from the family of all Tathāgatas—the vast application of the Dharma that encompasses all matters of accomplishment—and spoke the Great Mantra of the Seals of All Tathāgatas:

“Oṃ sarvatathāgatamūrti vaṃ. At that time, through the empowerment of all Tathāgatas, the World-Honored One Akṣobhya Tathāgata proclaimed the great ritual manual of the family of all Tathāgatas born from the family of all Tathāgatas, the vast Dharma application that encompasses all matters of accomplishment, and the great vidyā-mantra of the seal of all Tathāgatas:

"Oṃ vajrasattva muṣṭi āḥ. At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava, through the empowerment of all Tathāgatas, proclaimed the Great Ritual Manual of the Family of All Tathāgatas, which arises from the Family of All Tathāgatas. This is the Great Dharma Application that encompasses all matters of accomplishment, the Great Mantra of the Seal of All Tathāgatas: [The mantra follows]... "Oṃ vajrasattva muṣṭi āḥ. At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava, through the empowerment of all Tathāgatas, proclaimed the Great Ritual Manual of the Family of All Tathāgatas, which arises from the Family of All Tathāgatas. This is the Great Dharma Application that encompasses all matters of accomplishment, the Great Mantra of the Seal of All Tathāgatas:

"Oṃ vajraratnamuṣṭi traṃ. At that time, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amitāyus, through the power of the empowerment of all Tathāgatas, proclaimed the great ritual manual of the family of all Tathāgatas born from the family of all Tathāgatas—the vast dharma-activity that encompasses all matters of accomplishment—and the great vidyā-mantra of the seal of all Tathāgatas, which says:

“Oṃ vajradharma muṣṭi khaṃ. At that time, the Bhagavān Amoghasiddhi Tathāgata, through the empowerment of all Tathāgatas, proclaimed the Great Ritual Manual of the Family of All Tathāgatas born from the Family of All Tathāgatas, which encompasses all matters of accomplishment through extensive Dharma applications. He spoke the Great Vidyā-mantra of the Seal of All Tathāgatas:

"Oṃ vajrakarma muṣṭi haḥ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, endowed with virtue, through his own empowerment and by the power of the empowerment of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, proclaimed the great ritual manual of the family of all Tathāgatas born from the families of all Tathāgatas—the vast Dharma application that encompasses all matters of accomplishment, the four-seal maṇḍala of the Vajra-siddhi:
"I shall now explain in succession The supreme four-seal maṇḍala, Whose characteristics are like those of the Vajradhātu; It is taught here because it is the Vajra-siddhi."
According to the ritual application of the Great Maṇḍala, the wise one should cast the lines as appropriate;
according to the rite, he should install the images of the Buddhas and so forth, and paint the maṇḍala of the four mudrās.
Within a pure and exquisite lunar disc, he should paint the vajra-mudrā and the others according to the rite.
Next, the ritual procedures for summoning and other rites within the Vajrasiddhi Four-Seal Maṇḍala are explained:
having entered the maṇḍala after performing the appropriate rites according to the dharma, one should admonish the disciples, saying:
"You must take care never to reveal or instruct this secret gateway to others."

Why is this? It is because there are sentient beings who possess various evil views and further commit sinful deeds, lacking skillful means and unable to comprehend the myriad sublime activities. Due to their inferior diligence, even though they have performed [the rites] within the maṇḍalas of all the Tathāgata families, they instead give rise to thoughts of fear and are unable to enter.

Within this Vajra-Siddhi Maṇḍala, the Maṇḍala of the Mudrās of All Tathāgatas, and the True Maṇḍala of the Samaya of the Family of All Tathāgatas, they were unable to extensively bring about the salvation, benefit, and happiness of the entire realm of sentient beings without exception, nor could they establish the signs and phenomena of the supreme accomplishment of the Vajra of all Tathāgatas.

Therefore, you must not fail to give rise to pure faith in these secret samaya-mudrās of all the Tathāgata families; otherwise, this will lead to your ruin and the premature end of your life, causing you to fall into the three evil realms.

Having spoken thus, he immediately removed the face-cloth from his disciple and had him gaze upon the maṇḍala within; thereafter, he explained for him the samaya of the mudrās of the family of all Tathāgatas:
"Whichever mudrās one binds, According to the corresponding great lords, One should recite the heart-mantra according to the rite, And visualize oneself likewise as taught."
If one is endowed with such wisdom, one shall immediately attain the supreme accomplishment of a Mahāsattva;
all mudrās in all places are as taught by Vajrapāṇi.
"Furthermore, I shall explain the secret dharma of all mudrās:
'Restraining and subduing one's own sense faculties, one should next grasp the vajra-fist.
If anyone comes into contact with this mudrā, they will instantly give rise to sublime passion.'"
"Furthermore, he taught the dharmatā of all mudrās:
'The methods employed by the subtle vajra— Within these, one should bind the wisdom-mudrā (jñāna-mudrā).
If the ritual procedure is thus applied correctly, This is the sublime method of loving attraction through the wisdom-mudrā.'"
"Furthermore, I shall explain all the methods of the *mudrā-karmas*:
Whether it be song, dance, or food and drink, Whatever practices and joyful dharmas there may be,
If these are offered to the Buddhas and the Noble Ones, This is the sublime principle of the *karma-mudrā* of love."
Furthermore, the instruction on the secret seal-knowledge for the accomplishment of all maṇḍalas:
"First, one should stabilize oneself, sitting upon a seat in profound stillness and silence, remaining unmoving like a stūpa;
one should then visualize oneself as the Vajradhātu."
Next, bind the firm Vajra-bond; with both hands, extend the middle fingers like fangs, while the little fingers and thumbs face upward.
This is the Samādhi of the Supreme Samādhi mudrā, the subtle and wondrous application of the supreme Vajra Dharma.
Within this, one should visualize the sublime meditative equipoise (samāhita).
The subtle and wondrous Vajra Maṇḍala is the principle of mastery over samādhi.
One should form the vajra mudrā with both hands, grasping the two firm vajras;
binding the little fingers and the index fingers together is the supreme maṇḍala mudrā of the Vajra Body.

"Then, having bound the four great mudrās as performed by Vajrasattva and others, according to the extensive ritual applications within the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu, all the four-mudrā ritual applications for the Akṣobhya Tathāgata Maṇḍala and all other maṇḍalas shall be executed; furthermore, they should be drawn according to the Vajrasiddhi Four-Mudrā Maṇḍala, each employing the specific mudrās of its own family, whereby one immediately attains the accomplishment of all that is to be done."

If one paints various paṭa images, first paint the surface of the paṭa with the color of empty space; then, according to the ritual rules, paint all the locations and arrange that maṇḍala as instructed, whereby one shall attain the accomplishment of all activities.

From this point forward, according to one's own inclination, one may enter the great maṇḍala to perform the rites of accomplishment, or begin the practice within a single day, or again over four days, or sixteen days, as appropriate for the task to be performed.

Even if one has committed the five crimes of immediate retribution, whatever they may desire—whether it be all manner of cherished food, drink, enjoyments, activities, or deeds that bring about various forms of happiness—they shall obtain them.
If one seeks accomplishment, even within a single year one may attain the most supreme accomplishment; this is what the virtuous Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi has taught.

At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, again entered the vajra-samādhi of the supreme accomplishment-trance of all Tathāgatas. Within this samādhi, from his own heart, he brought forth the hearts of all Tathāgatas and spoke this great vidyā-mantra of the Mahāyāna realization-trance of all Tathāgatas:

“Vajrasattva. Then, the virtuous Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, for the sake of extensively rescuing, benefiting, and bringing happiness to the entire realm of sentient beings without exception, and even to the point of causing them to attain the unsurpassed accomplishment of all Tathāgatas, spoke this maṇḍala of the Mahāyāna realization-trance:
“I shall now, in due order, expound The supreme maṇḍala of Sattva.”
Its appearance is like the Vajradhātu; thus it is called Vajrasattva.
Following the ritual application of the Great Maṇḍala, one should mark out the outer maṇḍala in due order.
Within a pure and exquisite lunar disc, one should arrange the form of Vajrasattva.
"Then, as taught in the instructions, the ritual procedures for summoning, causing entry, and so forth herein are all born from the wisdom of all Tathāgatas.
Having performed them according to the Dharma, one should admonish the disciple, saying:
'If there are those who have not seen the samādhi and cannot fully comprehend these secret teachings, you must not explain them to them.'"
"If one were to explain it [otherwise], it would cause extreme ruin and bring about the premature end of their life; do not let them fall into the various evil destinies.
Furthermore, he taught the wisdom-seal (*jñāna-mudrā*) for the accomplishment of the supreme *siddhi* of Vajrasattva:
"Abiding within the full-moon maṇḍala, all are subsumed within the Great Seal (*mahāmudrā*)."
Vajrasattva is one’s own body; by visualizing him accordingly, one will swiftly achieve accomplishment.
Furthermore, the instruction on the secret samaya-mudrā wisdom of all maṇḍalas is as follows:
“One should know that there is nothing separate within the three realms; to perceive desire as something to be abandoned is itself a transgression.”
Therefore, the nature of defilement and purity is truly eternal; herein, the knower has no further task.
Then, the Great Vidyā is proclaimed:

*Mahā-samaya-hana-phaṭ* (one syllable). Thereafter, he bestows the samaya-heart-mantra, as well as the extensive ritual manual for the maṇḍala of the family of all Tathāgatas and the samaya-restraints.

"Furthermore, regarding the methods for accomplishment such as the four great mudrās of Vajrasattva and so forth, as well as such painted images (paṭa) and all other sacred icons according to one's inclination."
By performing according to the ritual, one shall attain the accomplishment of all that is sought; this is all based upon the extensive ritual manual of the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu.

At that time, all the Tathāgatas gathered once more like clouds and, in praise of the virtuous Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva Mahāsattva—the sovereign lord of all Tathāgatas, the supreme master of the Great Bodhicitta, and the Vajradhātu—spoke these words:
"Excellent, excellent!"
He then spoke this mantra of Vajra Joy: "Oṃ. Furthermore, the verse says:
"Excellent, O Vajra Great Hero! Excellent, O Vajra Great Jewel!"
The wondrous Dharma of the Vajra is good and inconceivable; Excellent, O Vajra-karma assembly!
You have skillfully proclaimed this true Dharma, This unsurpassed and vast Vajrayāna, The secret gateway of all Tathāgatas, Subsumed within the Mahāyāna’s dharma of direct realization.
If one hears the name of Vajrasattva, one shall yet attain all supreme accomplishments;
if one performs the rite with a pure mind, one immediately attains the supreme, wondrous bliss of all Buddhas.
All the corresponding Vajra dharmas are the sublime bliss among all sensual pleasures;
for those seeking accomplishment, they shall obtain inexhaustible and undying bliss in this very life.
The Mahāyāna-abhisamaya-samādhi-mahātantra-rāja, the King of Great Teachings for the Manifest Realization of the True Gathering of All Tathāgatas, Spoken by the Buddha, Scroll Eight.
The Mahāyāna-abhisamaya-samādhi-mahātantra-rāja, the King of Great Teachings for the Manifest Realization of the True Gathering of All Tathāgatas, Spoken by the Buddha, Scroll Nine.

Translated by the Tripitaka Master Śīladharma, Dharma-transmitting Master, Imperially Conferred Purple Robe, Court Attendant for Honoring the Emperor and Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and others, under Imperial Decree.

Part Six: The Extensive Ritual Manual of the Trailokyavijaya Maṇḍala, Part One. At that time, the World-Honored Ones, all Tathāgatas, again assembled like clouds and praised the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, the Great Universal Wheel-Turning King, with one hundred and eight names.
The verse says:
“Vajrasattva, the Great Vajra, Wondrous Vajra Honored One, the Excellent One!
Vajra Consecration, Vajra Radiance, Victorious Vajra Banner—to you I prostrate.”
To the Great Sublime Dharma of Hevajra, who wields the great vajra-sword,
the supreme king of all maṇḍalas, and who is free from conceptual proliferation, I prostrate.
Vajrakarma, the great protector; the fierce Yakṣa, the great subduer;
the firm Great Seal, the Vajra Fist—I prostrate to all mudrās.
The wondrous bodhicitta, the Great Bodhi; The pure and wondrously awakened Tathāgatas;
The gateway of great wisdom arising from vajra-knowledge— To this supreme Mahāyāna, I prostrate.
All purposes and all true meanings, The great heroic meaning pervading all;
O Sovereign who acts everywhere, the All-Knowing One, I prostrate to you who manifest everything.
Vajra-body, wondrous and supreme Vajra, Vajra-vīrya, Lord of Vajras,
Born from the true meaning of the Great Samaya, Mahāsattva, I pay homage to you.
Vajra Great Hook, Great Sublime Desire, Supreme Sublime Bliss, Great Sublime Light, Vajra Radiance,
Manifesting Radiance, I prostrate to the Buddha’s Great Illumination.
Victorious Vajra Lord, supreme among vajras; Supreme Great Mantra, Honored One among men;
Foremost Vajra, Greatly Victorious Supreme One; I prostrate to the Infinite Great Mantra.
Great Vajradhātu, Great Secret; Vajra Secret, Wondrous Secret Mind;
Vajra Subtle and Wondrous Great Dhyāna; To the Vajra Activity, I prostrate.

The Buddha, the supreme among the vajra-siddhas, the supreme among Buddhas; He who has awakened to the great wisdom of the Bodhi of the three Buddhas, The supreme wisdom of all Buddhas, the Great Universal Enlightenment— I prostrate to him who is self-awakened and awakens others.
To the one who makes offerings to the Buddha with the great offering, The one who offers the sublime offering of the *sattva*,
The great accomplishment of vast skillful means— I prostrate to the Vajra Accomplishment.
The great wisdom-body of all Tathāgatas, The supreme eloquence of all Tathāgatas,
The great loving-kindness of all Tathāgatas— To the Vajra of Vajras, I prostrate.
I prostrate with my head to the one who carries out the Buddha’s decree, the Victorious Lord of Buddhas; to the supreme birth of all the sons of the Buddha;
to the All-Illuminating Honored One, the Supreme Teacher; to the one who is both tranquil and majestic.
The great reality of all Tathāgatas, The ultimate limit of all phenomena and the great principle,
The wisdom of all pāramitās— To the ultimate truth, I prostrate.
The vast and supreme conduct of Samantabhadra, the most excellent among all, the wisdom of equality,
who subdues all māras and brings down the hosts of māras— I prostrate to you who have attained universal penetration.

The great wisdom of all Buddhas is primordial great wisdom; O Vajra Great Wisdom, you who are well-disciplined, The courageous vajra of the manifold vajra bodies— I prostrate and take refuge in Vajrapāṇi!
That which was spoken by you, O Vajrasattva, Is this very adamantine mind of vajra.
By this, you have attained the state where all those Tathāgatas pay homage, make offerings, and revere you with total faith.
Through the power of your sovereignty, you have realized perfect enlightenment and can manifest as the Father of the World for all beings.
You have attained the source from which all goodness arises and serve as the foundation upon which all Tathāgatas rely.
With these most excellent words of praise, extolling you with a heart of filial love,
if one praises your venerable self through song, they shall become no different from those who hold the Vajra.
I now entreat you, O Holy Lord, who skillfully performs the wondrous acts of love of all Buddhas, for the vast benefit of all sentient beings: please teach the dharmas born from your own family.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, endowed with virtue and the supreme sovereign of all Tathāgatas, having heard the exhortations of all the Tathāgatas, placed his vajra upon his own heart and addressed all the Tathāgatas, saying:
"World-Honored Tathāgatas, this is not within my sphere of practice."
The Tathāgatas asked,
"What is the cause of this? Vajrapāṇi replied:
“World-Honored Tathāgata!
There are malevolent sentient beings such as Maheśvara and others whom even all the Tathāgatas cannot subdue; how then could I possibly subdue them now?”

At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, through the empowerment of all Tathāgatas, entered the vajra-samādhi of the great skillful means wisdom of all Tathāgatas. Within this samādhi, all those Tathāgatas pervaded the entirety of the realm of empty space like particles of dust, extending everywhere and interpenetrating one another, reaching even to the summit of Mount Sumeru and within that great jeweled pavilion with its peak of vajra-maṇi gems.
Then all the Tathāgatas gathered once more; having observed everywhere, they entered the heart of the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, from within his auspicious and supreme marks.

At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, through the empowerment of his own heart as the heart of all Tathāgatas, and by virtue of the equality of all vajras, extensively sought to rescue, protect, benefit, and bring happiness to all sentient beings throughout the entire realm of beings without exception, so that they might attain the supreme siddhis. Desiring to subdue all who are evil, he thoroughly observed with the samādhi-wisdom of the great compassionate skillful means of all Tathāgatas; he then entered the Vajra Samādhi of the Wrathful Samādhi of Great Compassionate Skillful Means of all Tathāgatas. Within this samādhi, in a single kṣaṇa, emerging from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, he proclaimed the secret heart-mantra of the Vajra Samādhi of the Heart of All Tathāgatas, saying:

When this heart-mantra "HŪṂ" was spoken, from the vajra in the hand of the Vajrapāṇi, there emerged the venerable Vajradhara, his entire body a treasury of blazing light, with furrowed brows, a knitted face, wide eyes, and sharp fangs; possessing a great wrathful aspect, he held various weapons such as a vajra-hook, a sharp sword, and a noose.
Furthermore, a mass of vajra-flame light radiated forth before him, and the form of Vajrapāṇi was adorned with countless, wondrous colors and marks.

Having thus manifested, for the sake of subduing all evil beings throughout all worlds, he dwelt within the moon disc corresponding to the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu surrounding the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, and spoke these verses:
“Great is the skillful means of sublime subduing; Possessing great skillful means, it is even greater than the great.”
“If one transforms sentient beings through skillful means, manifesting a wrathful body, one remains untainted.

At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, having universally contemplated the dharmatā of all Tathāgatas as being free from conceptual proliferation, entered the *samādhi* of the Vajra Empowerment of the Great Wrathful Vajra Samaya of All Tathāgatas, and spoke this supreme great vidyā-mantra of the heart-essence of all Tathāgatas, the Great Wisdom of the Vajra of All Tathāgatas:

"Oṃ suṃbha niḥsuṃbha hūṃ | gṛhṇa gṛhṇa hūṃ | gṛhṇāpaya hūṃ | ānaya hoḥ | bhagavan vajra hūṃ phaṭ. When this great mantra was spoken, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, endowed with all virtues, emerged once more from the hearts of all Tathāgatas. He extended throughout the ocean-like clouds of all worlds, reaching even unto the assemblies of all Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas, universally bestowing empowerment and summoning them all to enter the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajra Samādhi.

Having thus entered, he gathered all the samādhis and further condensed them into a single entity, forming the body of the Great Vajra Wrathful One. Abiding within the heart of the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, he spoke this verse:
“O, how great is the unsurpassed bodhicitta! Universally virtuous and pure by nature, If it brings sentient beings to subdual, Then from wrath itself arises sublime love.”

At that time, the body of the Great Vajra Wrathful One descended from the heart of the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, and took his stand within the moon disk before all the Tathāgatas, remaining there to once again request instructions.

At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata of All Tathāgatas, entered the Samādhi of the Vajra Hook-Summoning of All Tathāgatas and spoke the heart-mantra of the self-mind for the hook-summoning of all Tathāgatas, saying:

“HŪṂ CAKRĪ JAḤ. When this heart-mantra was spoken, it spread and pervaded the ocean-like clouds of all worlds, reaching as far as Maheśvara, the sovereign of the three realms, until every world was completely exhausted without exception.

That assembly gathered together and surrounded him; because of the summoning by the vajra-hook of the samādhi of all Tathāgatas, they were all summoned to arrive at the Vajra-maṇi-jewel-peak pavilion on the summit of Mount Sumeru, where they remained, encircling the Buddha’s assembly on all sides.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, endowed with virtue, brandished a vajra at his heart and cast it playfully; having surveyed the entire great assembly throughout the three realms, he spoke these words:
"O you noble ones!
"You must act in accordance with my instructions to protect and uphold all the teachings of the Tathāgatas.
Then Maheśvara said, "How am I to act now?"
Vajrapāṇi said: "You should take refuge in the Triple Gem—the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha;
this is your practice. O noble ones!"
"If one practices in this way, one shall attain the knowledge of all-knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*).

At that time, Maheśvara, the sovereign lord of the three realms of this world, because he was the supreme ruler of those three realms, gave rise to an air of haughty pride and manifested a wrathful aspect, speaking these words:

"You, Vajrapāṇi, Great Yakṣa King! I am the greatest and most autonomous lord of the three realms; among all *bhūtas*, whether in their formation or destruction, I have attained sovereignty. I am the Great Deva among devas; why should I follow the instructions and commands of you, a Yakṣa King?"
At that time, the virtuous Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi playfully hurled his vajra and further issued this command:
"You, Maheśvara, most wicked of sentient beings, must now swiftly enter the great maṇḍala within my samādhi and abide according to the instructions."
At that time, Maheśvara addressed the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, saying:
"World-Honored One!
How is it that this Great Being has received instructions from me, Maheśvara?"
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, addressed the assembly of devas, including Maheśvara and the others, saying:
"You should take refuge in the Three Jewels and practice in accordance with what is set forth within the samaya precepts."

If it be otherwise, this Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva, the Great Yakṣa King, manifesting a form of violent wrath and extreme ferocity, shall not allow that supreme vajra to emit flames of fire and utterly destroy these three realms.

At that time, Maheśvara, the Lord of the Three Realms, by virtue of his sovereign wisdom as the ruler of the three realms, manifested for the virtuous Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi a form of great terror, extreme malice, wrath, and immense ferocity; emitting great blazing flames and a great, evil laughter, he appeared together with his own retinue and spoke these words: "Vajrapāṇi!
"Now I am the supreme lord of the three realms; I grant you this instruction that you must follow according to my practice.
At that time, the virtuous Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi again brandished his vajra, smiling with a joyful countenance, and spoke these words:

"You are born of the kaṭapūtanas; you take human flesh, corpses, ash, and various impurities as food; your beds, seats, and attire are entirely perverse and wretched. Since your conduct is such as this, how can I be made to share in your teachings and practices?"
Then Maheśvara assumed a state of great wrath and, by his own power, spoke these words:
"Since you are thus, I too shall protect my own teaching and act according to the instructions within my own samādhi."
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, the Great Wrathful King endowed with virtue, addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!

This Maheśvara, relying on the power of his own wisdom as a wealthy sovereign, is arrogant and self-willed; therefore, he does not give rise to faith or take refuge in the pure teachings of all Tathāgatas. How should I now act according to my capacity?"
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this Great Vajra Samaya Mantra of the Emergence of the Heart of All Tathāgatas:
"Oṃ niḥsvabhāva-vajra hūṃ phaṭ. Then, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi also spoke his own Vajra Heart Mantra: "Hūṃ.

When he spoke this Heart Mantra, Maheśvara and all the others who had gathered from throughout the triple world covered their faces, fell to the ground in a state of confusion and distress, and cried out in pain as they sought refuge and protection from the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi.
When Maheśvara and the others had thus fallen to the ground, their consciousnesses ceased to function and they were on the verge of death.
At that time, the World-Honored One, knowing these events, addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, saying: "Vajrapāṇi!"
You should now, by means of your own practice, bestow fearlessness upon all beings throughout the entire triple world, so that these people do not all lose their lives.
Then, having heard these words of the Bhagavān, Vajrapāṇi, the Great Wrathful King, addressed the assembly of Maheśvara and the others, saying:
"If you wish to preserve your lives, you must take refuge in the Triple Gem—the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha—and act in accordance with my instructions."
Maheśvara said: "If I were to take refuge in the Triple Gem of the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṃgha, I would still not know any of the instructions contained within your teachings."
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, addressed Maheśvara, saying:

"You should now know that this Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra Vajrapāṇi—supreme sovereign of all Tathāgatas, father of all Tathāgatas, executor of the commands of all Tathāgatas, and most excellent son of all Tathāgatas—has received the empowerment of the Great Wrathful King for the sake of subduing all sentient beings."
Why is this? Because even all the Tathāgatas are unable to pacify or restrain you and the other extremely wicked beings, such as Maheśvara and the rest.
"Therefore, so that all sentient beings with evil karma may be fully tamed and established in samādhi, you should now abide in samādhi according to my instructions."
Maheśvara said: “World-Honored One!
I can no longer sustain my life; I pray that you will save me. I shall follow whatever instructions you have bestowed upon me.”
The Buddha addressed the Great Lord Maheśvara, saying:
“If you can take refuge in the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, he shall be your true protector; there is no other protector.”
At that time, the entire assembly gathered from throughout the triple world all turned toward the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi and, with one voice, uttered cries of distress, saying: "Vajrapāṇi!
"May you protect me! May you protect me!
Now, in the midst of this suffering of death, I pray only that you will take me under your care.
At that time, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi addressed that assembly, saying:

"You evil ones! If you act according to my teaching within my instruction, do not cause this great vajra of mine to emit fiery light, becoming a single mass of vast, blazing flames that burns everything to ashes."
Then that assembly said:

"You are born from the hearts of all Tathāgatas as Samantabhadra; you are serene, well-disciplined, and bring benefit to all sentient beings, universally bestowing fearlessness. Why do you not grant us benefit?"
Then Vajrapāṇi, the Great Wrathful King, addressed that assembly, saying:

"O noble ones, although I am endowed with the mind of Samantabhadra, yet by the command of all the Tathāgatas, since you extremely wicked sentient beings have given rise to a sinful mind and do not abide in the samādhi of the Tathāgatas, I shall act as their subduer to bring them to purification."
Then that assembly said, "We all likewise abide in samādhi. At that time,

the virtuous Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, the Great Wrathful King, setting aside Maheśvara for a moment, comforted the other hosts of devas and caused them to arise, and spoke this Great Mantra of the Heart of All Tathāgatas, the Vajra-Arising:

When this great mantra—*vajrodṛḍha*—was spoken, with the exception of Maheśvara, all the remaining hosts of the three realms along with their retinues, as well as those who had previously fallen to the ground in a state of confusion and distress, immediately found their hearts comforted. They attained a touch of sublime bliss, were freed from fear, and their body hair stood on end with joy. Gazing up at the virtuous Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva, they were able to rise together.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, saying: "Great Being!
Why does this Maheśvara, Lord of the Three Realms, not rise from the ground? Is it not possible that his life is about to perish?"
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi immediately proclaimed the Great Vidya-mantra for Protecting Life, saying:
"Vajra-yu. As he spoke this vidyā-mantra, Maheśvara attempted to rise from the ground; though he exerted all his strength, he was ultimately unable to do so. He then addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"Who now serves as your teacher for you to take refuge in?

The Buddha said, "I am not your teacher for whom you should take refuge; that Great Being Vajrapāṇi is the one to whom you should go for refuge. Why do you not now rely upon his instructions and act accordingly?"
Maheśvara said: "World-Honored One!
If you are not my teacher and refuge, who else can protect and deliver all sentient beings of evil?"
The Buddha said:
"As for the one who provides protection, that is Vajrapāṇi himself;
it is not within my power. Maheśvara said:
"Why is that? the Buddha said, "Because that Vajrapāṇi is the supreme sovereign of all Tathāgatas."

Maheśvara said: "I do not understand the meaning of what the Buddha has spoken. Since the Buddha Tathāgata is the sovereign of the three realms, how is it that the Great Being Vajrapāṇi is further superior?"
"Why am I ultimately unable to clarify this meaning?
At that time, the virtuous Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi again addressed Maheśvara, saying:
"You evil being, for what reason do you not act in accordance with my instructions?"
At that time, having heard these words spoken by Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva, Maheśvara again manifested a violent, wrathful, and extremely fierce appearance, and spoke thus:
"I would rather face death than ever practice according to your teachings."
Then, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, the Great Wrathful King, manifested from his own heart the form of the wrathful Vajrānkuśa and spoke this great mantra:

“Oṃ prana gṛsna vajra hūṃ. At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, raised the sole of his foot and likewise manifested the form of the wrathful Vajrānkuśa, blazing with flames all around, with furrowed brows and sharp fangs; his great face was terrifying as he stood before the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi and again requested instructions.
At that time, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, for the sake of purifying Maheśvara, spoke this great vidyā-mantra:

“Oṃ bhañja grasa grasa ya | sarvavajradhara nocara | krandakrandaya vajra hūṃ jaḥ. Having spoken this great vidyā-mantra, Maheśvara and the Queen Umā fell prostrate upon the ground, rising again upon their two feet with their bodies naked and their forms hideous; all who beheld them broke into laughter.
At that time, he summoned forth the wrathful images manifested from the soles of his feet, and they all stood before Vajrapāṇi at his heels.
Then, the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva Mahāsattva addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!..."
"How shall this most violent and wicked god and his queen be restrained?
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this great mantra:

"Oṃ vajra krama huḥ. Having spoken this great mantra, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi raised his left foot and stepped upon Maheśvara, and his right foot stepped upon the queen Umā; pressing them between his thighs, he spoke this great mantra:
"Oṃ vajraviśa hana ya traṃ traḥ. When this great mantra was spoken, Maheśvara, being oppressed by it, raised his own thousand hands and struck his own thousand faces.
At that time, all the celestial hosts outside the Maṇiratnaśikhara Pavilion raised their voices together and proclaimed these words:
"Now our sovereign, Maheśvara, has been subdued by the Great Being Vajrapāṇi."
At that time, for the sake of Maheśvara, the World-Honored One gave rise to a supreme and great heart of compassion and spoke this Heart-Mantra of the Compassionate Protection of all Buddhas:
"Oṃ buddhamaitrī vajra rakṣa haṃ. When he spoke this Heart-Mantra, Maheśvara immediately entered samādhi; having entered samādhi, all his sufferings were stilled.

Furthermore, because his feet and heart were touched by the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, he immediately attained the supreme siddhi, the sublime empowerment, as well as samādhi, liberation, dhāraṇī, supernatural powers, wisdom, and so forth.

Having thus entered the gate of the samādhi, liberation, and dhāraṇī of all Tathāgatas, the body of that Mahādeva emerged from the heart of the feet of Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva and traveled downward through worlds equal in number to the atoms of thirty-two Gaṅgā-sands, arriving at a world named Vaśamañcana. There, a Buddha had appeared in the world, titled the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Vaśamiśrānirguṣa.
Then Maheśvara appeared in his true form and, before that Buddha, spoke these verses:
“Great indeed is the Honored One, the Fully Awakened One! The great wisdom of all Buddhas is unsurpassed.
If a dharma falls within the realm of words and phrases, Even nirvāṇa is but a provisional designation.”
Having spoken these verses, he returned to his original place.
Furthermore, the virtuous Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi addressed Nārāyaṇa and all the other lords of the triple world, saying: "O noble ones!
"You should all enter the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajra Samādhi of all Tathāgatas, and you must all protect and uphold all the samādhis of all Tathāgatas."
Nārāyaṇa and the others replied,
"As you have commanded us, we shall carry it out.
At that time, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi addressed the entire assembly throughout the three realms, saying:
"I now accept you, O noble ones; you should further take refuge in the Triple Gem, receive the samaya precepts, and abide correctly within my samādhi."
Then that assembly said:
"We have all abided according to your instructions; however, this samādhi of yours is unknown to us.
At that time, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi immediately bestowed upon them the method for his own samādhi:
“Once the great bodhicitta has arisen, perform the supreme ritual procedures in their proper sequence;
act according to the power of great wisdom as is appropriate, and you shall dwell well in samādhi.”
