At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, endowed with virtue, having summoned the celestial hosts into the maṇḍala according to the instructions, [proceeded as follows].
Having caused everyone to universally behold the mandala according to the sequence of ritual applications of the Great Maṇḍala,
he then conferred upon them the vajra-jewel empowerment and the insignia.
In order to extensively bring benefit and happiness to sentient beings, all the Tathāgatas conferred upon the lords of the triple world the names of the Vajra Empowerment.
Their names were as follows: Maheśvara was named Krodhavajra; Nārāyaṇa was named Māyāvajra; Kumāra was named Vajraghaṇṭā; Brahmā was named Maunavajra; and Śakra was named Vajrāyudha.
These five are the Vidyārājas of the Vajra Consecration.

Furthermore, there is the host of celestial lords who fly through the air: the one named Amṛtakuṇḍalin is called Vajrakuṇḍalin; Candradeva is called Vajraprabha; Mahājayabhadra is called Vajradaṇḍa; and Bhṛṅgiriṭi is called Vajrabhṛṅgiriṭi. These four are the Wrathful Lords of the Vajra Consecration.

Furthermore, there were the hosts of celestial lords who traverse the void, whose names were: Mātṛmāta, known as Vajraśūṇḍa; Amṛtakara, known as Vajramālā; Varada, known as Vajrapriyadhara; and Jaya, known as Jayavajra. These four were the masters of the *gaṇas* for the Vajra-Abhiṣeka.

Furthermore, there are the hosts of terrestrial celestial lords, whose names are: the one named Śrīvajramātā Sarā, known as the Guardian of the Treasury; Vajravāyu, known as the Wind Deity; Vajrāgni, known as the Fire Deity; and Kuvira, known as the Greatly Fierce Vajra. These four are the masters of the *nuda* (subduing) rites of vajra consecration.

Furthermore, there are the hosts of principal deities dwelling in the waters, namely: Vāraha, known as Vajrāṅkuśa; Yāma, known as Vajrakāla; Bhṛtīvijūlika, known as Vajrapināka; and Varuṇa, known as Nāgavajra. These four are the lords of the Vajrābhiṣekacitaka.

Furthermore, all those queens and mother-goddess hosts who are the mistresses of the three realms, having been conferred the vajra-jewel initiation and the vajra empowerment of the insignia of their respective families, were all established by all the Tathāgatas for the sake of benefit and happiness with vajra-initiation names. Their names are as follows: the queen Umādevī is named Krodhavajrajvālā; the queen Rūpyavarṇadevī is named Vajrasuvarṇadevī; the queen Śaścidhevī is named Vajrakumāridevī; the queen Brahmāṇī is named Vajraśānti; and the queen Śakradevī is named Vajramuṣṭi. These five are the vidyā-consorts of the vajra-initiation.

Furthermore, there are the hosts of the Sky-faring Mother Goddesses (*mātṛkā*), whose names are: the Mother Goddess Amṛtā, titled Vajrāmṛtā; the Mother Goddess Rūhiṇī, titled Vajraprabhā; the Mother Goddess Daṇḍadhārī, titled Vajrāgnidaṇḍā; and the Mother Goddess Jātaharī, titled Vajramaṇimekhalā. These four are the wrathful Mother Goddesses of Vajra Consecration (*vajrābhiṣeka*).

Furthermore, there are the hosts of the Mothers who traverse the sky, whose names are as follows: the Mother Mālinī is named Vajraguhyā; the Mother Grasanī is named Vajragrasanī; the Mother Vaśanā is named Vajreśvarī; and the Mother Nartakī is named Vajravatsalā. These four are the Gaṇikā Mothers of the Vajra Consecration.

Furthermore, there are the various Mother Goddesses (*mātṛkā*) dwelling on earth, whose names are as follows: the Mother Goddess of Tranquility named Vajrī-Dūtī; the Mother Goddess of Wind named Kṣipravajrā; the Mother Goddess of Fire named Jvalanavajrā; and the Mother Goddess of Kuverī named Vajratīkṣṇā. These four are the Mother Goddesses who are the vajra-consecrated female messengers (*vajrābhiṣekadūtī*).

Furthermore, there are the water-dwelling Mātṛ goddesses, whose names are: Varāyī, known as Vajramukhī; Jvālāmukhī, known as Vajrakālī; Cinnānasā, known as Vajrapūtana; and the water-mother goddess, known as Vajramakari. These four are the Mātṛ goddesses of the Vajra-Abhiṣeka-cakra.

At that time, the virtuous Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, for the sake of all those hosts of devas who had entered the maṇḍala, instructed them in all the mudrās of the great wisdom of the Buddhas and bestowed upon them the heart-mantra of the Vajra-samaya vow:
“This great vajra, the adamantine scepter, Is empowered by all the Buddhas.
Should anyone transgress this samaya, Their own lineage shall swiftly be destroyed like ashes.”
The Great Illumination says:
“Oṃ hana samaya hūṃ phaṭ. Next, bestow the Great Seal for Gathering the Mind:
“With both hands, one should form the Vajra Mudrā; interlace the two index fingers like hooks.”
Just like the posture of one stringing a flower garland or nocking an arrow, whatever task you undertake shall accord with your will;
place this seal before your heart, and once placed, all matters will be accomplished.
Do not transgress this samādhi, lest you bring ruin upon your body and life.
Firmly forming the vajra-bind once more, bend the two index fingers and curl them around;
then join the two thumbs together and press the two middle fingers against one another.
This is the secret mudrā of the Great Binding Samādhi of the Vajra Great Vidyādhara.
"You must not break this samādhi; one who breaks it incurs the offense of transgression.
With both hands, you should form the Vajra-mudrā: first, interlace the two little fingers;
then, bend the backs of the two thumbs and insert them within; finally, rotate it and place it upon the head."
This mudrā of samādhi of the Great Being is called the Vajra-Vidyādhara-baṃdha;
when performing the wrathful gaze, it should be placed before him accordingly.
One should firmly bind the Vajra-protection; forming the Vajra-bond, one should press them together.
This is the Samādhi-mudrā of the Earth-goer, which manifests as a protector for all sentient beings.
If one wishes to perform an act of rescue and protection, one should join the hands in the Wrathful Bond.
To protect all sentient beings according to their wishes, one should place this mudrā upon their backs.

First, form the vajra-mudrā with both hands; then, pressing the left hand’s vajra index finger against [the back] in the manner of drawing a bowstring, and finally forming the little fingers like a lock, the mudrā is accomplished.
If any matter of anger should arise, one should employ this samādhi;
by placing this mudrā before the object as appropriate, one will immediately attain all supreme accomplishments.
First, bind the two hands in the vajra-bond; next, firmly join the two index fingers, with the middle fingers and thumbs meeting face-to-face. This is the Vajrāsanī mudrā.
Rotate this seal to the forehead; having placed it there, perform the summoning as appropriate.
If one wishes to rescue and restore life, place this mudrā before that person.
Next, the Samādhi of Gathering the Mind Throughout the Entire Triple World is explained.

Regarding the Great Mantras used for the aforementioned mudrās, they are as follows: "Oṃ vāridūta vaśyākarṣaya hūṃ jaḥ. This is also the mantra for summoning the Mother Goddess with the Garland-Tying Vajra Mudrā.
"HŪṂ VAJRA-GHRĪṆĀ-JĀPĀ-SAMAYA HŪṂ. This is the great vidyā-mantra of the goddess Ākāśagarbha."

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, endowed with virtue, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
I have already subdued all who are evil, and all Tathāgatas have established my name for the consecration.”
Excellent, World-Honored One!
Grant me further instructions regarding this maṇḍala constructed by these wicked ones;
how should I proceed?
At that time, having heard these words, the World-Honored One spoke this Great Vidyā-mantra:

“Oṃ vajrasumbhani sumbha hūṃ phaṭ. Then, for the sake of extensively rescuing, liberating, benefiting, and gladdening all sentient beings, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this Great Vidyā-mantra for summoning all maṇḍalas:
“Oṃ vajrasamayakarṣaya sarvamaṇḍalam | vajradharasatya mām ākarṣaya hūṃ phaṭ. Regarding the mudrās to be employed with this Great Vidyā-mantra:
"Form the two hands as a vajra-hook; this mudrā is rotated at the heart.
Then, with the two index fingers curved outward like hooks, one performs the supreme summoning of the maṇḍala."
When this seal-mantra was spoken, the entire assembly of all maṇḍalas was summoned and gathered at the summit of Mount Sumeru, where they remained encircling it.
At that time, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi addressed all those in the assembly of maṇḍalas, saying:
"O Noble Ones! You should practice the vow of never killing; I shall sustain you through samādhi."
At that time, the sentient beings within the outer maṇḍala spoke thus: "O Great Being!
We are all evil sentient beings who sustain our lives by eating meat. According to the instructions of the Great Being, how shall our lives be sustained?"
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this mantra of the extremely fierce Vajra-Wrathful One:

"Oṃ ṣṭa-vajra-krodha hana daha bhasma vikīraya vikirasarva-ṣṭa-samayamudrāṃ mañjara mañjara marīna marīna kana kana parā-mardaya vajra-samaya hūṃ phaṭ. The mudrās to be employed for this great vidyā-mantra are as follows:
"Join the vajra-anger fingers upright, then interlace all the fingernails;
with the finger-faces joined together firmly, this mudrā can subdue all who are evil."

When this seal-mantra was spoken, all the extremely malevolent assemblies of the maṇḍala gathered into a single mass, manifesting various signs of dissolution and dispersal, and the samādhis of their respective families were likewise broken.

The minds of these sentient beings were as if scorched and boiled; under extreme oppression, they uttered great cries of lamentation and distress, and with palms joined before the virtuous Vajradhara, they addressed him, saying: "O Great Being!
"May you rescue and protect me! May you rescue and protect me!
My life is about to end; do not abandon me!
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, endowed with virtue, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
As for these extremely wicked members of the maṇḍala assembly, how should I further cause them to act?
We pray only that the World-Honored One grant us your instructions.”

“Oṃ niḥsambhava hana daha paca kṛtaṇa māraya hūṃ phaṭ. Then, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi also spoke this vajra-ferocious vidyā-mantra: “Oṃ...”

At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, saying: "Vajrapāṇi!

“Oṃ vajra-pratīkṣa-hana hṛdayam ākarṣaya āḥ jaḥ hūṃ vaṣaṭ mā saritena mṛtyate tannaḥ hṛn niṣkramitu samaya hūṃ jaḥ. The mudrā to be employed for this vidyā-mantra is as follows:
"Form the vajra-bond by joining the two hands together; with the two arms held firmly at the heart, the surfaces of all the fingers are like vajras, and one strikes them against one's own armpits."
"By means of this seal and mantra, one can seize all sentient beings as *hrīṇaya* to be consumed as food.
When the *ḍākinīs* and other malevolent possessors heard this great vidyā-mantra, they clapped their hands, made a rattling sound, and fled in terror back to their own abodes.
At that time, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!

By virtue of being empowered by all the Tathāgatas, I shall universally subdue all who are evil. I only pray that the World-Honored One will further grant me instructions: how should all those possessing the spirits of disease, such as those with malarial fevers, be subdued?"
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this great vidyā-mantra:
"Oṃ hūṃ phaṭ. Then, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi also spoke this great vidyā-mantra for summoning all spirits such as those of malarial fever:

"Oṃ vajrasamayājñaya sarvaduṣṭajvarādīn āveśaya hūṃ phaṭ. When this vidyā-mantra was spoken, all those spirits who hold diseases, such as those of malarial fever, were summoned and came to dwell, surrounding the outer maṇḍala on the summit of Mount Sumeru.
At that time, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi addressed them, saying:
"You should practice never again to harm or disturb any sentient beings; you shall receive the precepts of subjugation."
The spirits of malaria and other such ailments spoke thus:
"O Great Being! We spirits subsist by absorbing the vital essence of humans; we shall act according to your instructions."
"How can I possibly practice it?
At that time, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi then proclaimed for him the Great Mantra of the Wisdom-Seal of Purifying One’s Own Karma, saying:
"Oṃ vajrakarma viśodhaya sarvavaraṇāni buddhasatyenādhiṣṭhāya hūṃ. The mudrā to be employed for this great mantra is as follows:

"Form the vajra-palms with both hands firm; next, bend those two index fingers, while the remaining fingers are all extended upward and interlaced. This mudrā, when rotated, destroys the evil destinies."
“Once these mudrās have been displayed accordingly, you yakṣas of malarial fever and other spirits must quickly disperse; if you do not, your lives shall surely be destroyed.”
Then, having received these instructions, the various spirits returned to their respective abodes as directed.
At that time, the virtuous Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva Mahāsattva addressed the Tathāgatas, saying:

"In order to universally purify and extinguish all karmic obstructions, I have brought forth various great mantras from my own heart. I pray that the Tathāgatas will further instruct me on how to purify those evil destinies, such as the hells."
At that time, all the Tathāgatas spoke this great vidyā-mantra:
“Oṃ kṣapa-vajra svāhā. Then, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi also spoke the great vidyā-mantras for summoning the hosts of the evil realms, such as the Raurava hell and others:

"Oṃ sarvavyākarṣaṇa viśodhanavajrasamayā hūṃ phaṭ. When this great mantra was spoken, all the various classes of beings within the evil realms, such as the Raurava and Mahāraurava hells, were summoned and arrived, surrounding the outer maṇḍala on the summit of Mount Sumeru.
At that time, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi addressed all the sentient beings within those three evil realms, saying:

"I now take you all under my protection; you must all take refuge in the Triple Gem and receive the samaya precepts. I shall explain for you the great vidyā-mantra and mudrā that liberate one from all evil realms."
Then that assembly, with one voice and in unison, addressed him thus:
"O Great Being! We pray that you will protect and deliver us!"
"Our minds are tormented by the urgency of our perilous suffering; we now take refuge in the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, just as you have instructed.
Then, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the great vidyā-mantra for destroying all evil destinies, saying:

“Oṃ vajrapāṇi viṣabhūta jaha | sarvapāpamardana pramokṣaya | sarvapāpagatiṃ śodhaya | sarvatathāgatavajrasamayatraṭ |” The mudrā to be employed for this great vidyā-mantra is as follows: With both hands, firmly form the vajra-bond (*vajrabandha*); then, join the two middle fingers face-to-face.
The other fingers enter within without touching the face; this mudrā is named "Destroying the Evil Realms."

"When reciting that great mantra while forming this mudrā, it signifies that all sentient beings within the three evil realms have entered the outer maṇḍala and abide therein according to the principle."

When these sentient beings had seen such secret mudrās from the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, their respective karmas leading to the three evil destinies were immediately extinguished; they all emerged from the heels of the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, and those places of the evil destinies were also completely purified.
At that time, the virtuous Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi again addressed the Tathāgatas, saying:
"World-Honored Tathāgatas!

For the sake of extensively saving, benefiting, and bringing peace and happiness to the entire realm of sentient beings without exception, and even to the point of causing them to attain the supreme siddhi of all Tathāgatas—by virtue of attaining the fruit of supreme siddhi—they shall receive the vajra-accomplishment bestowed by all the Tathāgatas."

All of this has been established through the majestic spiritual power of all the Tathāgatas; yet, I now further request instruction from all the Tathāgatas: regarding those among the human realm who abide in the Dharma, how should they practice?
At that time, all the Tathāgatas spoke this great vidyā-mantra: "Oṃ vajra..."

At that time, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, having heard the instructions and commands of all the Tathāgatas, for the sake of extensively saving and liberating the realm of all sentient beings, so that they may attain all supreme happiness and the most excellent accomplishments, up to the fruits of the wisdom and supernormal powers of all the Tathāgatas, spoke this Supreme Great Maṇḍala of the Three Realms Born from the Vajra-Samaya of All Tathāgatas:
"I shall now explain in sequence The vast and supreme maṇḍala, Whose characteristics are like the Vajradhātu, The most excellent among all accomplishments."
This is called the most supreme maṇḍala of the three realms, born from the vajra-samādhi;
it is the gateway through which the bodhi of all Buddhas proceeds, capable of destroying all that is evil.
Then he spoke the great mantra for casting the lines and binding the boundary:
"The mandala is square with four gates, Adorned with four pavilions and various ornaments;
The four lines cast for measurement are equal without deviation, Beautifully decorated with silk banners and strings of pearls."
Regarding all four corners of that maṇḍala, as well as the junctions of its various gates, they are adorned with vajra-jewels;
these are distributed in sequence throughout the boundaries of the outer maṇḍala.
The wise one skillfully discerns within it a magnificent adornment of vajra-jewels and the like;
with four sides, four gates, and eight pillars between them, the inlaid pavilions are exceptionally wondrous.
One should establish the supreme vajra pillar, adorned with five maṇḍalas;
within the maṇḍala, one should draw the lines according to the ritual, making them complete with the five colors as they are drawn.
Then he spoke the great vidyā-mantra for using the marking-line:

“Once the divisions within have been established, the practitioner, abiding in a state of meditative equipoise, should open the gates of the maṇḍala according to the ritual while maintaining focused attention; thus those four vajra-gates are opened.”
He then spoke the Great Mantra for employing the Gate of Generosity (*dāna-mukha*), saying:
"All images of the Buddhas of the four directions Should be installed according to their respective quarters and the ritual law;
Whether made of gold, silver, or clay bricks, The construction of the Buddha-thrones should be performed as taught."
He then spoke the great mantra for universally summoning all Tathāgatas, saying:
"One should place [the symbols] before the Buddhas of the eastern direction, A vajra within a mass of flames;
likewise in the south, west, and north, Are the jewels, the lotus, and the karmic implements."
Next, the mantras and mudrās for arranging the Vajrasamaya are taught as follows:
"Having performed the vajra-stride and emerged, the wise one should likewise, before that Buddha,
draw the supreme mandala of Vajrahūṃkāra according to the ritual rules as appropriate."
Then he spoke this Vajrapada Great Mantra:

"Oṃ vajravedikrama hūṃ. Having thus emerged from all maṇḍala realms, such as the Vajradhātu and others, according to the ritual procedure, one proceeds everywhere without obstruction, according to one's desire.

Section Three on Evil: Furthermore, there is the extensive ritual application for entering the Great Maṇḍala of the Supreme Victor of the Three Realms, also known as Trailokyavijaya.
First, the Vajrācārya should personally bind the Vajra-ferocious Tiri-tiri mudrā and enter the maṇḍala.
Having thus entered, he should then address all the Tathāgatas, saying:
"World-Honored Tathāgatas!..."
I shall perform the rites of wrathful subjugation and magnetizing: those who should be subdued, I shall subdue; those who should be gathered, I shall gather.
I pray only that the World-Honored One grant me his instructions; how should I proceed as is appropriate?

Having spoken these words, he immediately placed the Vajra-Āveśa-Tir-tir seal—which he had bound—upon his own heart according to the instructions, and extensively performed the activities of the Vajrāṅkuśa and so forth.

Having performed this, one again binds the *samaya-mudrā* of the assembly; thereupon, one immediately attains the empowerment established by the majestic spiritual power of all Tathāgatas, and next performs the four kinds of secret offerings.
Having performed these, he further offers incense and other articles of worship.
Next, the ritual procedure for leading the vajra-disciple into the maṇḍala is proclaimed.
That is to say, the Vajrācārya causes the disciple to bind the Vajrakrodha Tiri-tiri mudrā which he himself has bound, and imparts this great vidyā-mantra:
“Oṃ kṛṣṇavajrasamaya hūṃ vaṃ. Then, having bound [the disciple] with blue silk and wrapped his head with blue cloth, and having covered his face with blue cloth, he is led into the maṇḍala.
He is given this great vidyā-mantra: “Oṃ vajrasamayapra-veśaya mi. Having entered, he then forms the Vajra-pervasive-entry samādhi-mudrā and is given this pervasive-entry arising vidyā-mantra:
“Oṃ vajrāveśa aḥ. Having performed this rite of pervasion, by virtue of this entry, he immediately receives the empowerment bestowed by all the Tathāgatas.

In a single instant, one is able to comprehend matters of the past, future, and present; one is not obstructed by the evils of Māra, and furthermore attains the power of invisibility such that others cannot see them.
Thus, by attaining union with the Trailokyavijaya rite, one is able to tame and gather all sentient beings according to their needs.
One can perform all the activities of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, and furthermore, can constantly accomplish all matters of siddhi.
Thereafter, one should bestow upon them the Great Mantra of the Vow-mind.
Next, having removed their face-cloth for them, one should cause them to behold the entire great maṇḍala.
As soon as those disciples see the maṇḍala, they are able to extinguish all stains of sin and are well able to subdue all things throughout the three periods of time.

Because this corresponds to the practice of Trailokyavijaya, one is able to summon all the hosts of deities, including Maheśvara and others; furthermore, one performs such acts as awakening, binding, subjugation, and magnetizing. One obtains the empowerment of the spiritual power (*adhiṣṭhāna*) of all Tathāgatas, is constantly protected by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, and additionally receives from Vajrapāṇi the methods for bestowing accomplishments (*siddhi*).
However, one confers initiation by means of the Vajra Initiation ritual; that is, one places a vajra-sword into the recipient’s hand and further bestows this great vidyā-mantra:
“Oṃ vajrapāṇi vajrakarma kuru bhava. Thereafter, one is designated as one who has received the Vajra Initiation.
Furthermore, he bestowed this great vidyā-mantra:

“Oṃ vajra-krodha-tva-ma-viśca mina ma viśika ga hī vajra nāma. This means that whatever names correspond to their respective functions are all in harmony with the sound *hī*. Thereafter, for the sake of explaining the verse on the arising of great wisdom, he said:
“One should draw the vajra-image everywhere, Endowed with great flaming light, placed within the heart.”
In union with the Vajra Wrathful Dharma, one can awaken all the worlds.
Placing the vajra-jewel mark upon the forehead, and likewise painting it everywhere as appropriate,
through union with the Vajra Wrathful Dharma, all sentient beings will be filled with reverence and affection.
The Vajra-Lotus is placed at the throat, possessing great light of blazing flames;
through union with the Vajra-Aggressive Dharma, all sentient beings are completely subdued.
Placing the skillful-action vajra upon the crown, possessing great light of blazing flames,
and in accordance with the Vajra Wrathful Dharma, one is able to protect all the world.
Furthermore, the Heart Mantra of the Wisdom Seal (*jñānamudrā*) is proclaimed as follows:

That vajra hook should be drawn everywhere; one should tread upon it with the soles of one's own feet as appropriate, and likewise pass over it from the birth-gate; thus, one will certainly summon the hosts of devas.
That vajra hook should be drawn everywhere, arising equally from the birth-gate;

therein, the ritual action is performed according to the prescribed rite, whereby this most excellent [deity] is summoned as appropriate.

one shall destroy the very life-force of whichever malevolent beings are to be subdued, according to their respective natures.
With the intent to destroy all evils, one should dwell in the vajra-mind and observe with clarity;
one should recite the mantra of the syllable HŪṂ for all [beings], manifesting the seal of one's own wisdom before oneself.
According to the inclinations of sentient beings to be tamed, the very arising of the intention constitutes the seal.
The manifest seal seals manifest phenomena; all activities can be accomplished. These vidyā-mantras are:

*Ṭaki* (one syllable), *Ṭaki jaḥ* (one syllable), *Ṭaki hūṃ* (one syllable), *Ṭaki phaṭ* (one syllable). Each of these seals is entirely consistent with the four types of ritual actions (*karma*) and their four corresponding seals and mantras.
"Furthermore, the instruction on the secret wisdom of the wrathful mudrā:
'All parts of the body are joined together; applying the syllable HŪṂ according to the ritual method, the lotus and vajra are conjoined;
thus the life-force of the one one wishes to destroy is ruined.'"
The lips and teeth are joined according to the ritual method;
within the practice corresponding to the syllable HŪṂ, the lotus and vajra are conjoined, facing one another as is appropriate for each.
If one relies on the method associated with the syllable HŪṂ, one obtains the experience of bliss and present nourishment;
through the union of the lotus and the vajra, one immediately attains the equality of both suffering and bliss.
If one relies on the practice corresponding to the syllable HŪṂ, all parts of the body are pressed together;
when the lotus and vajra join, those various parts of the body likewise unite.
The heart-mantras for these are as follows:
HŪṂ AḤ; HŪṂ JAḤ; HŪṂ HOḤ; HŪṂ HAṂ. Furthermore, the instruction on the wisdom of the Great Seal of the Reality of the Samaya of the Mahāmaṇḍala of Trailokyavijaya is as follows:
"Through union with the Dharma of the Vajradhātu, one attains accomplishment in the Buddha-smṛti-samādhi."
If for the sake of benefiting sentient beings, one shall certainly attain Buddhahood as appropriate.
Maheśvara and Queen Umā—according to the method, draw them upon the ground;
by practicing in accordance with what has been drawn, one attains the accomplishment of the Sattva-mudrā.
By binding this secret mudrā in its center, one can immediately subdue those of the three times;
one will swiftly achieve the supreme vidyā, no different from the form of Trailokyavijaya.
In the center of the blazing maṇḍala, one should practice according to the prescribed drawings;
with the vajras of body, speech, and mind, one should bind the various mudrās of the sattvas.

I shall now explain that rite of action (*karmavidhi*); the Vajra-karma is supreme because it accomplishes the samādhi of mindfulness of the Buddha, whereby one swiftly attains buddhahood as appropriate.
If one binds the Great Seal of Trailokyavijaya, one immediately becomes the Noble Deity Trailokyavijaya;
with the vajra-life pervading all conduct, one is no different from the form of Trailokyavijaya itself.
The Supreme King of Vajra Empowerment, sovereign over all phenomena in the world,
the Great Wrathful One of Karma-Vajra, who skillfully accomplishes all vajra activities.
The Great Firmness of the Wrathful Sattva, the Wrathful Supreme Hook that can summon all;
the Wrathful Great Love from which wondrous love arises; the Excellent Wrath who bestows joy;
the Frowning One who skillfully subdues all; and the Wrathful Solar Orb of Wondrous Radiance.
The Wrathful Jewel Banner seizes away what is not beneficial; The Great Laughter Wrathful One destroys all evils;
The Wondrous Dharma Wrathful One subverts what is not the Dharma; The Vajra Sharp Sword cuts through everything;
The Right Cause Wrathful One crushes the wheel of suffering; The Secret Speech Wrathful One shatters improper speech.
The Karma-krodha accomplishes virtuous deeds; the Vajra-krodha provides protection and defense.
The Tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭra-krodha subdues and devours adversaries; the Jñānamuṣṭi-krodha bestows siddhi.
Furthermore, the ritual procedure for forming the Vajrasamādhi-mudrā is proclaimed:
"Born from the two hands as vajras, this is called the Supreme Samādhi;
I shall now explain the ritual for its formation as appropriate, wherein the wrathful binding is supreme."

The two arms joined together like a vajra, the little fingers hooked and bound together, and the two index fingers forming the *mudrā* of the *kṣepaka*; this is called the Great Seal of Trailokyavijaya.
With the index fingers not touching the face, slightly curved like the shape of a jewel;
then the middle fingers are held upright like lotuses, with the tips of the middle and index fingers meeting;
then the two index fingers are joined like a vajra, and finally the two [index] fingers are bent like a hook.
Without altering the previous mudrā, they are again placed side by side; one should then form the gesture of snapping the fingers.
The mudrā of the Frowning Honored One has the fists placed side by side, with the index fingers positioned at the heart like a sun disk;
next, extend the arms and place them upon the crown of the head, with the index fingers pointing toward the mouth as if in a smile.
Furthermore, with the fingertips joined together, form the right fist in the manner of grasping a sword;
extend the middle finger upward in the form of a wheel. With both fists directed toward the mouth for the Vajra-speech, the index and middle fingers should be like vajras.
Furthermore, with the two index fingers like great fangs, the two vajra-fists placed back-to-back,
and joined in the manner of the Vajralāsyā mudrā;
that seal is gathered by the syllable HŪṂ, and all those dharma-seals are likewise gathered through their correspondence with the syllable HŪṂ.
Furthermore, the Vajrasamādhi-mudrās are proclaimed as follows:
The syllable *HŪṂ* is the Wisdom-Vajra; The syllable *TRAḤ* is Vajragarbha;
The syllable *HRĪḤ* is Vajrasena; The syllable *AḤ* is the Vajrakarma of the Assembly.
Furthermore, the sequence of the Dharma seals (*dharmamudrā*) is as follows:

*HŪṂ*, *HOḤ*, *TĀLAṂ* (one syllable), *DHĀṂ*, *HI*, *HI*, *NI*, *HAḤ*, *TIKCU* (two-syllable conjunct), *TI*, *HŪṂ*, *GRAṂ* (one syllable), *KRĪ* (one syllable), *VAṂ*, *NRI* (one syllable), *AḤ*. These Dharma seals are the skillful means for accomplishing the assembly of Vajra Wrathful Deities (*vajrakrodha*).
"Furthermore, the various *karmamudrās* of the Vajrasamādhi are proclaimed:
'Both hands should form the wrathful fists, In accordance with the "Vajra Raised High" and other [mudrās];
The sequence of all *karmamudrās* Is as explained in the Mahāvajrakula.'"

According to what is appropriate for each, the various mudrās and their respective karmic retinues on the left and right are installed in their places according to the ritual; thus, all those mudrās are brought into perfect harmony.
"This is the so-called Extensive Ritual of All Mudrās.

Part Six of the Extensive Ritual Manual for the Trailokyavijaya Maṇḍala, Continued: "Furthermore, the general mudrās to be employed within the Trailokyavijaya Great Maṇḍala are now proclaimed: [The text continues with the descriptions of the mudrās. "
"All mudrās of Trailokyavijaya, Which are the supreme Vajra-samādhi,
And the mantras and vidyās of the Vajra-hūṃ syllable, Can bestow all accomplishments in an instant."
The little fingers are hooked and the two hands are joined; the two vajra-fists move from above to below.
This is called the Supreme Seal of the Samādhi Hook, which instantly summons all beings.
The most supreme and honored among all vidyās is the mantra-vidyā of Trailokyavijaya;
it causes universal respect and affection to arise and skillfully accomplishes all victorious activities.
With both vajra fingers upright, joined tightly and held in meditative equipoise—
this mudrā is named Vajrotthāpana, which causes all who have died to regain their lives.
First, extend the two vajra index fingers; next, form the vajra-bind mudrā;
finally, rotate it and place it upon the crown of the head. This increases one's lifespan and brings about peace and happiness.
With both hands, one should form the vajra-bond (*vajrabandha*); extending the two thumbs, insert them within the bond.
Keeping the index fingers firm and slightly bent, one should place the feet together in the posture of summoning (*ākarṣaṇa*).
To subjugate [an opponent], step upon him with the left foot. Following the ritual procedure, one should arrange the image of that being accordingly.
By entering into union with the Trailokyavijaya mudrā, one attains accomplishment within half a month.

One should form the Vajra mudrā with both hands; this mudrā is to be struck together here, striking the bodies of those sentient beings who are to be subdued, causing them all to be universally awakened by the impact.
One should form the vajra-mudrā with both hands; then, interlacing the two index fingers, this mudrā serves as armor for oneself and others, providing protection at all times.
With palms level, one should form the vajra-bond; with thumbs tightly clenched like a vajra, conceal the mudrā while generating a wrathful mind, and thus attain the great siddhi of the Vajra Family.
Forming the firm Sattvavajra, join the two thumbs together with the middle fingers;
extend the little fingers like a vajra-gate—this mudrā subsumes the Sharp Samādhi.

With both hands, one should form the vajra-mudrā; by bending the two index fingers and hooking them together, one assumes the posture of nocking an arrow as appropriate. This is the supreme method for summoning all the devas.
One should firmly form the vajra-bind; bend the two index fingers so they touch, and press the thumbs against the space between the middle fingers—this is the mudrā of the Samādhi of Flight.
One should first form the vajra-mudrā with both hands; then, interlace the two little fingers and place the backs of the two index fingers together.
By rotating [the hands], this also constitutes the flying mudrā.
The steadfast one should perform the vajra-protection; pressing together with the vajra-bind, this is called the earth-walking samādhi-mudrā, by which all that is done is never transgressed.

With both hands, one should form the vajra-mudrā; the left vajra-index finger is pressed close [to the palm], then the index fingers are opened wide. This is able to summon the hosts dwelling upon the earth.
One should form the vajra-bond with both hands, making the two index fingers firm and tight;
with the middle and thumbs like a vajra—this mudrā can destroy all evil beings.

The two hands should form the Vajra-mudrā; placing this mudrā at the heart and gathering [the fingers] evenly, when pressing them together with the wrathful fists, one can destroy the various maṇḍala rites of heterodox outsiders.
With the left hand, the vajra-finger is tucked in; with the right, the index finger is slightly bent.
Then, with wrathful intensity, it is opened wide on all sides; even Mount Sumeru itself could be destroyed by it.
With the left hand, the vajra-finger is tucked within; with the right hand, the index finger is slightly bent.
Arousing a mind of wrath, one summons all [beings] completely; all the seizing grahas will be drawn into loving devotion.
Joining the two vajra-bonds, place both arms firmly at the heart;
placing the two index fingers between the two armpits, one hooks the hearts of those evil ones and destroys them.
Again, with the two index fingers facing each other, generate a wrathful intent and press them together;
then, with the two thumbs, pinch the two roots, hooking and summoning [the spirits] to destroy all malarial fevers.
Firmly form the vajra-palms; next, bend those two index fingers, and finally join the two thumbs together. This mudrā can destroy all evil realms.
First, interlace the two index fingers; then, insert the vajra-mudrā within them.
By raising the mudrā, one can ascend in an instant, and even those who have fallen may be raised up.
Again, form the firm Vajra-bond; next, join the two middle fingers face-to-face, while the remaining four fingers do not touch their faces internally. This mudrā destroys all sins in an instant.
Furthermore, the mudrās to be employed in the rituals of the maṇḍala of all Tathāgatas are proclaimed as follows:
"One should first employ the [mudrā] for drawing the maṇḍala; next, one should bind the Vajra-Wisdom-Fist Mudrā.
Subsequently, when holding the thread, the mudrā used is the same; this is taught as the mudrā for drawing the lines of the altar."
Extend the two index fingers and join them together.
Both hands should form the Vajra-mudrā; this mudrā, empowered with the five colors, can summon all when one gazes with radiant light.
With both vajra-fingers extended upward, then firmly joined together with palms facing up, one forms the gesture of wrathful striking;
this is the supreme mudrā for opening the gate of the maṇḍala.
Furthermore, the methods for accomplishing all mudrās of the Vajra families are proclaimed:
"Having performed the vajra-stride, skillfully uttering the vajra-anger speech,
with an angry gaze and an angry countenance, all activities will be accomplished."

Chapter Seven: The Extensive Ritual Manual for the Maṇḍala of the Wrathful Secret Mudrās. At that time, the venerable Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi again entered the vajra-adhiṣṭhāna samādhi born from the samādhi of the dhāraṇī of all vajras, and proclaimed the supreme vidyā-mantra of his own family, saying:

"Oṃ sarvavajrīvajramate ānaya sarvavajrasattva hūṃ jaḥ. When this great mantra was spoken, an image of Vajrapāṇi emerged from the heart of the virtuous Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi. All his physical characteristics were identical to those of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, and there was no difference between them. Having manifested as the noble being of the Secret Samādhi Seal of Vajra Wrath, he accomplished all the activities of the Tathāgatas throughout all worlds.

Furthermore, for the sake of accomplishing the secret consort of the virtuous Vajrasattva and all matters of concealment and manifestation, once the images of the vajra seals of body, speech, and mind have been perfected, they abide according to principle within the moon disk corresponding to the Great Maṇḍala of the Bhagavān Mahāvairocana Trailokyavijaya.
He spoke this verse:

"How great are all the Honored Ones of Perfect Enlightenment! Possessing secret, supreme great wisdom, they act as Vajra Consorts as appropriate, in order to bring about the cause of the Tathāgata’s sublime bliss."
Then, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva Mahāsattva again spoke these verses on the secret maṇḍala of the vajra-samādhi of the family’s samaya-mudrā:
"I shall now, in due order, expound The supreme Vajra Maṇḍala, Whose characteristics are like those of the Vajradhātu; It is taught as the wrathful secret."
Relying on the ritual application of the Great Maṇḍala, one should delineate all the maṇḍalas according to the instructions;
having established the five maṇḍalas according to the dharma, one should arrange the secret mudrās in their respective places.
In the center of the Vajra Maṇḍala, one should arrange the forms of the Buddhas according to the ritual rules, as well as the assembly of wrathful deities in samādhi;
the wise practitioner should draw them accordingly in accordance with the Dharma.
Advancing gradually with the vajra-step, one should arrange the Vajrapāṇi maṇḍala;
within it, one should first draw a vajrāṅkuśa and a vajra all around,
and further, in that center, draw blazing light according to the sequence as described.
Holding a vajra and a vajra-hook, with a vajra-arrow and the gesture of snapping the fingers,
one advances gradually with the vajra-step and lays out the second maṇḍala to the south.
According to the ritual, one draws the Jewel Vajra Honored One and installs him within the great wheel.
Vajra-bhṛkuṭī is the Jewel-marked One; Vajrasūrya and Ratnaketu likewise.
The rows of teeth are like vajras; these should be depicted encircling him.
Advancing gradually with the vajra-step, one should lay out the third maṇḍala in the west.
Therein, one should draw and install the subtle Vajrapadma;
within that lotus, amidst blazing flames, one should further depict the lotus, the sword, and the vajra-wheel.
That Vajra Tongue should likewise be depicted accordingly around its perimeter.
Advancing gradually with the vajra-step, one should lay out the fourth maṇḍala in the north;
according to the ritual, draw a vajra in the center, and around it, also draw vajras and light rays.
On its four sides, one should further paint the blazing, dense, and great flaming light, the Vajra of Skillful Action, and the armor;
the Vajra-toothed Fist should be painted in their proper sequence.
At the corners of the maṇḍala and in the outer areas, they should be depicted according to the ritual rules as appropriate;
I shall now explain in sequence those supreme mudrās and great vidyās.

Next, the root vidyā-mantra for the secret vajra-offering to the noble ones at the corners of the maṇḍala is stated:
*Vajra hūṃ kaṇi*, *Vajra hūṃ koṃ*, *Vajra hūṃ tiṃ*, *Vajra hūṃ sittiṃ*. Next, the vidyā-mantras for the outer-corner offerings of song and music to the noble ones are stated:

“Vajra-te-te (one phrase), vajra-ṭha (one phrase), vajra-dha-do (one phrase), vajra-tuṃ-dha (one phrase). Next, the great vidyā-mantra for making offerings to the noble ones to protect the gates is spoken as follows:

"Vajra jaḥ jaḥ" (one phrase). "Vajra hūṃ hūṃ" (one phrase). "Vajra vaṃ vaṃ" (one phrase). "Vajra aḥ aḥ" (one phrase). Furthermore, regarding the ritual procedures for entering this secret maṇḍala of the Vajra Family, all such dharmic applications are identical to the ritual for entering the Great Maṇḍala of Trailokyavijaya.

Once the Vajrācārya has thus entered, he shall immediately perform the rite of offering to the manifest Vajradhara by means of the Vajra-secret Vajrakula samaya-mudrā, the pratimudrā, the kṣudramudrā, and the jñānamudrā.

What are called the various activities such as whirling dances are precisely those: whirling dance, facing dance, small dance, and wisdom dance; these constitute the activity-seal wisdom (*karmamudrājñāna*).

First, having praised and extolled all the Tathāgatas with the heart-mantra of the Vajradhātu-parigraha and the vajra-song, the Vajrācārya should then reveal the Sattvavajra-mudrā. Subsequently, he should lead those who are to enter the application-mudrā into its presence:

"According to the method of the Vajranṛtya, With the two hands in the form of wrathful fingers, One should, according to the rite, at the center of one's own heart, Form the Great Mudrā of Trailokyavijaya."
Then, performing the whirling dance according to the ritual manual,
one universally summons all the Tathāgatas with that vajra-anger hook, assuming the posture of a skilled archer raising the vajra-arrow.
By virtue of skillfully shooting with the vajra-arrow, one immediately attains the accomplishment of Vajra-joy;
next, one should release the mudrā as described, joining the palms in a binding gesture and striking them together.
By performing this great ritual of offering in this manner, one shall attain the joy of Vajrapāṇi;
through the cause of that Noble One’s joy, all desired aims will be accomplished in an instant.
The mantras for these samādhi-mudrās are as follows:
SIDDHYA VAJRA (1) ĀNAYA VAJRA (1) RĀGAYA VAJRA (1) SAṂTOṢAYA VAJRA (1) Next, one should perform the offering of the ritual of the counter-dance (*pratipraṇartana*):
Just like the form of the Vajra-whirl dance, One should hold the left hand with the fist of the right hand.
Rotate it back and place it before the forehead; next, the index finger should be placed at the mouth.
Rotate again to form the solar disc mudrā; this rotating seal can summon all universally.
Next, one should erect the vajra-banner and manifest the vajra-laughter with a joyful smile.
Through such a great ritual of offering, one can cause kings and the multitudes to give rise to reverence,
affection, and the bestowal of majestic light, or to grant wealth and treasures, or to feel joy.
The mantras for these mudrās are as follows:
Furthermore, regarding the manner of the whirling dance: join the two fists closely together, place the index fingers at the heart center, and prostrate with a mind filled with awe and trembling.
Next, one should again perform the gesture of whirling dance; the Vajra-Sharp-Sword Honored One can sever [all bonds].
This whirling gesture is further like a wheel; this is the form of the Revolving Wheel Maṇḍala.
With the sublime song of vajra speech, One makes offering to the holy lord Vajrapāṇi;
Through such a ritual for the great Dharma offering, All things shall ultimately attain accomplishment.
The mantra for these minor seals is as follows:
Next, extend the vajra-anger fingers; then, again raising them upward, join the palms together;
thereafter, rotate them and place them between the crown of the head; finally, let the index fingers rest at the opening of the mouth.
Employing the Vajrakarma according to the ritual, one performs all activities within the supreme maṇḍala;
having displayed the ritual of the corresponding dance, one subsequently re-establishes [the deities] within one's own heart.
According to the ritual sequence, one should perform the whirling dance; binding [the hands] constitutes the Vajra Protection.
Joining the two hands as Vajra Fangs, the two vajra-fists are pressed closely together.
Through such rites of worship for the Great Dharma, one can accomplish all *karma* rituals;
regarding these four types of worship rites, the release of the mudrās should be performed according to the original teachings as appropriate.
The great mantras of these wisdom-mudrās (*jñāna-mudrā*) are as follows:
*Nṛtya-vajra*, *Locana-vajra*, *Kanakavajra*, *Padminī-vajra*. Furthermore, the instruction for the wisdom-mudrā of the Wrathful Vajra (*krodha-vajra*) is as follows:
"Holding that vajra with both hands, generate a wrathful intent and perform destruction."
Whosoever desires to cause destruction—such-and-such a person by name—may their heart be shattered with the vajra held in hand;
with the lower lip pressed against the teeth in close union, whosoever desires to cause destruction should be coerced and subdued.
If there be any who transgress these commands, their cranial vault shall swiftly be split asunder.

With the great gaze of Vajra-wrath, as the two eyes blink and move in accordance with the occasion, one should look upon whoever is to be destroyed; that person’s two eyes will then be utterly destroyed.
Through the union with the form of Vajra-krodha, one visualizes oneself within one’s own heart;
by pressing together with the vajra-bind, the minds of those evil ones are instantly destroyed.
These great vidyās are as follows:

HŪṂ VAJRA-SEPHAṬA; HŪṂ MUKHA-VAJRA CA; HŪṂ VAJRA-NĪTRA CA; HŪṂ MANU-VAJRA CA. Furthermore, the secret seal-knowledge (*mudrājñāna*) of the Great Vajra Family is taught. Among these, one should first form the Great Seal (*mahāmudrā*):
"Arrange the vajra-fury fists, with the little fingers of both hands interlocked."
Place the left hand with the three prongs turned back; this is called the Great Seal of Trailokyavijaya.
Extend the index finger of the left hand and raise it upward;
subsequently, rotate it in the same manner, returning once more to the position of the Vajra on the left side.
Place the palms together in the vajra-bond; with a wrathful intention, conceal them while firmly extending the thumbs like vajras—this is the wrathful *tiri-tiri* mudrā.
Forming a fist, first bend the two index fingers; then again, bring the two fingers together in the shape of a hook.
The faces of the two index fingers are like vajras. Then, snap the two index fingers together;
the faces of the two index fingers are like vajras. Within the heart, further display the mark of the solar disc.
Raising the two index fingers, place them at the crown of the head; rotate them back to the position of the smile.
Keeping the two index fingers upright and closely joined, form the posture of two fists as if grasping swords.
Joining the two index fingers like a wheel, raise the two thumbs toward the mouth and scatter them.
Next, one should extend both index fingers; then, wrap the two ring fingers around the thumbs.
With both hands positioned at the corners of the mouth like fangs, form the mudrā of tightly clenched fists.
"Thus is the sequence for the differentiation of the Great Seal (Mahāmudrā).
Next, bind the Secret Samaya Seal of the Vajra Family:
'That which arises from the secret fist—this is said to be all samayas.'"
I shall now explain the ritual for forming that bond, which is the supreme and unsurpassed Vajra-bond.
First, place both fists at the heart; next, place both fists at the two flanks;
summoning and holding the arrow, keep them all to the left; finally, rise from the heart and disperse.
Next, rotate the Jewel of the Frowning Lord; thereafter, one should form the sign of the solar disc.
Extending the arms, they should likewise be placed upon the crown of the head; rotating them back, they are then set at the position of the smile.

Place both fists well toward the mouth; next, hold the gesture of brandishing and striking with a sharp sword, followed by the gesture of casting down the wheel; finally, again place both fists toward the mouth and open them.
The body maṇḍala is most supreme at the crown; next are the two shoulders, then the heart, and again the two flanks.
One should likewise perform the vajra-protection, with the clenched fists firmly pressed together in the form of fangs.
The various mudrās of the outer maṇḍala are bound with their respective insignia in due order;
these are the samaya-vajra-bands, and the vajra-fists are likewise.
Furthermore, the *dharmamudrās* of the Vajra Family are proclaimed as follows:

The sequence of all *karmamudrās* Is performed according to the rite of the vajra-fist.
"Install them in their respective places according to the instructions as appropriate; gazing with wrath is the Wrathful Method.
Thus spoke the Buddha in the *Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha-mahāyānābhisamaya-samādhi-mahātantrarāja*, Fascicle Twelve.

"I shall now, in due order, expound The supreme and unsurpassed Dharma Maṇḍala."
Its appearance is like the Vajradhātu; this is called the Wisdom of Wrath.

According to the ritual application of the Great Maṇḍala, one should delineate all the maṇḍalas as taught, with the Wisdom-Vajra as the central division; therein, one should paint the image of the Buddha.
Next, one should further draw the respective mudrās all around that Buddha;
thereafter, proceeding gradually with the vajra-step, one should arrange the four maṇḍalas according to the ritual method.
All the venerable deities, such as Trailokyavijaya and others, should be established according to the sequence of the instructions;
likewise, around their perimeter, one should also arrange the host of Vajra-Wrathful Ones as appropriate.

"Once this subtle wisdom maṇḍala of the Vajra Family has been extensively laid out according to the instructions for each detail, one should enter the maṇḍala in accordance with the ritual rules as appropriate."
Having entered, he bestowed the oath and instructions upon his disciples, saying:
"You have received the empowerment of the vajra-anger of all Tathāgatas and of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi."

Through your virtuous conduct, you shall act as a savior for the entire realm of sentient beings without exception, even unto the attainment of the supreme siddhi and the most excellent fruits of the vast benefit and bliss of all Tathāgatas.
You should now know that this Vajra Wrath is capable of subduing all sentient beings and causing them all to become pure; how much more so, then, those who are evil within this world!

Having spoken these words, he immediately removed the face-cloth and then had him observe the various maṇḍalas. Once he had observed them, he conferred upon him the vajra according to the ritual procedure. Next, he should instruct him in the subtle wisdom-method of the Vajra Wrathful One:
"Formed from the firm and subtle vajra, Gathered through union with the syllable *HŪṂ*, If this method of the syllable *HŪṂ* is applied, The lives of all those who are evil shall be destroyed."
Forming the subtle vajra with firm stability, one gradually expands the ritual procedure as taught;
through this correspondence with the gradually expanding dharma, all those enemies and adversaries are utterly destroyed.
The subtle and wondrous applications of all vajra dharmas are gathered through union with the Vajra Hūṃ syllable;
through gradual expansion in accordance with the wrathful dharma, all those who are evil are subdued.
Furthermore, the method of gradual reduction is likewise: the practitioner may proceed until all things are gradually reduced without exception, according to their desire;
furthermore, they cause those who are evil to return to their own lives.
These great mantras are as follows:
"All malevolent sentient beings and adversaries, May they all together achieve the Great Solidity;
If one accords with a vast and expansive mind of loving-kindness, All vast adversaries will be utterly destroyed."
Because of the encounter with vast enmity, compassion arises from this;
if one is fully endowed with that compassion, all evildoers will be destroyed.
Whether phenomena or non-phenomena in the world, their intrinsic nature is fundamentally pure;
visualizing sentient beings in this way, one destroys them all through the method of the syllable HŪṂ.
All those most wicked sentient beings, who are not vessels for the Buddha’s bodhi—
so that they may be purified, destroy them all through the method of the syllable HŪṂ.
"These great mantras are as follows:

'The Vajra-image should be painted everywhere; if there is anyone who breaks it, one should direct one's intention toward them, and they shall immediately fall into that person's house, and that evil one shall destroy their clan.'"
Furthermore, relying on that subtle and wondrous Dharma, one should visualize the Mind-Vajra as appropriate;
likewise, one should visualize the form of the Great Bodhisattva, whereby the wicked are destroyed within their own clan.
Those in the world who turn their backs on the Dharma and commit transgressions— whether men or women, all are alike—
when one visualizes the form of Vajrapāṇi, those faults and failings are all destroyed.
Visualize the image of the Buddha according to the ritual, complete with all its marks and in accordance with the practice;
having performed the visualization, those who walk in ways that oppose the Dharma, whether they hold power in the world or not, shall be destroyed.
"These great mantras are as follows:
'By employing the subtle vajra according to the ritual, one should visualize it within one's own body;
one's own body is the reflection of the moon, capable of shattering whatever one desires to destroy.'"
Visualize yourself according to the ritual method as a vajra within a moon disk;
when the intention of wrath arises to destroy [the enemy], one should instantly destroy their clan accordingly.
One should visualize oneself accordingly; one's own body is Vajrapāṇi.
Whichever direction one wishes to destroy, that direction will be swiftly destroyed before long.
One should visualize oneself accordingly; one's own body is the very image of the Buddha.
If one wishes to destroy those who oppose the Dharma, that person shall be destroyed before long.
These great vidyās are as follows:

When performing the rite of encircling with the syllable HŪṂ, whatever evildoers there may be shall be destroyed.
Because of the union of the subtle vajra, the sublime Dharma is accomplished within a single inhalation;
by employing the resonance of that syllable HŪṂ, even the three times can be shattered.
In union with the subtle Vajra Dharma, one should cast a wrathful gaze with vajra-eyes;
when observing an evildoer accordingly, that person shall immediately lose their sight or face death.
Having gained entry through the secret gate, one should give rise to the intention and perform the ritual applications as appropriate;
by means of the mind’s hook-summoning and other corresponding practices, even the Lord Yama will conceive of respectful love.

Chapter Nine: The Extensive Ritual Manual for the Vajra Family Karma Maṇḍala. At that time, the Bhagavān, all the Tathāgatas, entered the samādhi called "The Empowerment Arising from the Vajra-Karma Samaya" and spoke this great mantra:
Oṃ sarvatathāgatagatimīśvari hūṃ. Then, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi again spoke this supreme great mantra of his own family:

“Oṃ sarvatathāgatadharmadhātu-spharaṇa-mahāpūjākarma-vitistara-samaye trilokavijaya-kāre sarvaduṣṭanirmocani hūṃ. Then, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajragarbha further spoke this supreme vidyā-mantra of his own family:
“Oṃ sarvatathāgatāgryadhātusamavasaraṇa mahāpūjākarmavisaratasamayai hūṃ. Then, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajranetra again spoke this supreme vidyā-mantra of his own family:
“Oṃ sarvatathāgatadharmadhātu-spharaṇa-mahāpūjākarma-vithi-visphāra-samaye hūṃ. Then, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajraviśvakarman again spoke this supreme great mantra of his own family:

“Oṃ sarvatathāgata-sarvalokadhātu-vivardha-mahāpūjākarma-vitativisphāra-samaye hūṃ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi again, through the extensive ritual procedure for offering to his own family, caused the noble deities to emerge from his own heart; he then universally summoned all Tathāgatas throughout all worlds to perform acts of love and sublime joy, accomplishing all ritual applications for *karmasiddhi* and all the miraculous activities of the Tathāgatas.

Having performed the extensive ritual activities, he dwelt in reliance upon the moon disk corresponding to the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu of the Bhagavān Mahāvairocana Tathāgata, and spoke these verses on the vast ritual procedure for the Karma-maṇḍala of the Vajrakarma-samaya:
"I shall now sequentially expound The supreme Karma-maṇḍala, Whose characteristics are like those of the Vajradhātu; This is named the Dharma of Karma-vajra."
Relying on the ritual application of the Great Maṇḍala, one should successively mark out five maṇḍalas;
in the center, one should arrange them according to the dharma, and the Buddha images should be arrayed as prescribed by the teaching.
Next, surrounding that Buddha, one should arrange the images of the supreme samādhis;
advancing gradually with the vajra-step, one should sequentially lay out the four maṇḍalas.
In each direction, one should install the four Vajra-honored ones, distributing them according to what is taught in the instructions;
furthermore, all around them, one should install the Great Sattvas in accordance with the ritual manual.
Furthermore, the mantra of the action seal (*karmamudrā*) for proclaiming the action maṇḍala (*karmamaṇḍala*) is as follows: Oṃ vajra...

The Ninth Part of the Extensive Ritual Manual for the Karma Maṇḍala of the Vajra Family, Continued: "Furthermore, regarding the teaching on the mudrās and wisdoms for pacifying rites (*śāntika*) and so forth, as in the preceding methods:
'Using auspicious wood for fuel together with honey, Abiding in equanimity and concentrating the mind, perform the homa. "
In accordance with the Vajra Wrathful Rite, one casts sesame seeds to destroy all misdeeds.
Again, using the aforementioned firewood for homa, one kindles a great, blazing fire according to the ritual rules.
When constantly casting non-glutinous rice while performing the rite, one will certainly achieve increase within that dwelling.
Auspicious wood is used as fuel along with honey; when the practitioner performs the rite, the fire blazes intensely.
With *darbha* grass and coral branches, combined with clarified butter, one increases their lifespan.
Again, use the aforementioned firewood to perform homa; according to the ritual, raise the fire until it blazes intensely.
Combining grass, coral branches, and oil, cast them into the flames as required; having performed this, one will be constantly protected.
"The mantras for these homas are as follows:
Using wood from thorny trees that is gnarled and crooked, together with thorns, kindle a blazing fire;
maintaining the mind of Vajra-Krodha while performing the homa, one will be able to summon [the deity]."
Furthermore, using the aforementioned firewood to perform homa, with a wrathful mind kindling a blazing flame, one casts red flowers and fruits into the hearth;
this will cause all in the world to feel respect and affection.
Using auspicious wood as fuel according to the rite, raise the fire with a wrathful mind until it blazes;
casting iron fragments like dust into the furnace, one gains the constant protection of the Vajra Honored One.
Again, using the aforementioned firewood for homa, with an equanimous and concentrated mind, raise the fire until it blazes fiercely;
by casting bitter fruits into the hearth, one can destroy all evils in an instant.
"These great mantras are as follows:
'Using sour wood as fuel according to the ritual, kindle a blazing fire with a wrathful mind;
by performing homa with sour-flavored flowers and fruits, one immediately accomplishes the supreme rite of subjugation through love.'"
Furthermore, using the aforementioned fuel to perform homa, one should kindle the fire with a concentrated mind until it blazes intensely;
by casting kāmaphala fruits into the hearth, the rite of kāmarūpa is immediately accomplished.
According to the ritual, employ the same fuel as before; with a wrathful mind, kindle the fire until its flames blaze forth.
Visualize grasping the formless flowers of the wilderness; by casting them away as you wish, you shall immediately attain the method for invisibility.
Furthermore, using the aforementioned firewood according to the ritual rules, one should concentrate the mind and raise the fire until it blazes.
Visualizing rows of flowers in the sky, as soon as one casts them [into the fire], one will be able to travel through the air.
"These great mantras are as follows:
'Using firewood from wood that is bitter and hard, one kindles a blazing flame by concentrating the mind;
with a wrathful intent, one burns the vajra-flower, acting in accordance with the Vajra commands.'"
Furthermore, using the previously mentioned firewood according to the ritual, one kindles a blazing fire with a wrathful mind;
then, taking flower garlands as they are obtained and casting them into the hearth, one causes the [deities] to act entirely in accordance with the instructions.
With the fierce intention that auspicious wood serves as fuel, one gathers the mind and raises the fire until it blazes;
casting the garland of Vajrapāṇi, one accomplishes the task according to his instructions.
Again, use the aforementioned fuel to perform homa; with a wrathful mind, kindle the fire until its flames blaze fiercely.
Perform the ritual with one's robes and cast them into the hearth; in an instant, cause that person to comply with the command.

"These great vidyās are as follows: *HŪṂ VAJRA-VYAṄKARA YE SVAHĀ*. *HŪṂ CAURĪ VAJRA-VYAṄKARA YE SVAHĀ*. *HŪṂ VAJRA-PĀNĪ VYAṄKARA YE SVAHĀ*. *HŪṂ BUDHA-VYAṄKARA YE SVAHĀ*. Furthermore, the instruction on the secret karma-mudrā wisdom is as follows:
"For those who perform the rites according to their own preferences, one should employ *añjana* at the birth-gate."
Having prepared the ritual substances and placed them therein, one generates affection through the attainment of pleasurable contact.
Applying realgar to the birth-gate and performing the vajra-bind while striking,
one practices the union according to the four types of signs and thereby attains the four types of siddhi.
Placing the ox-gall at the gate of birth, one presses it with the secret fist;
immediately, blazing flames arise from that very spot, and one becomes no different from Vajrapāṇi.
Saffron is applied to the birth-gate; there, one performs the Sattvavajra rite.
With it concealed within, blazing intensely, one becomes no different from Vajradhara.

The great vidyās for these are as follows: Oṃ ghurya rativajra vaśakara siṃca hūṃ. Oṃ ghurya vajra siṃca hūṃ. Oṃ vajradhara ghurya siṃca hūṃ. Oṃ vajra ghurya siṃca hūṃ. Furthermore, the instruction on the wisdom of the Great Seal (mahāmudrā) of the Vajra Family’s ritual activity (karmamudrā):
“Perform the vajra activities according to the rite; All the great seals (mahāmudrās) are applied in their proper order.”
In accordance with the Vajra Wrathful Dharma, one should skillfully employ the vajra-fist mudrā.
The supreme samaya-mudrā is likewise; one should follow the finger-technique of Trailokyavijaya.
All dharma-mudrās are used in the same way, as are the various syllables such as Oṃ.
The sequence of those various *karmamudrās* is performed according to the ritual by means of the *karmamuṣṭi*;
through union with the Vajrakarma method, all accomplishments (*siddhi*) are rendered pure.

10. The Tenth Section: The Extensive Ritual Manual of the Great Vajra Family At that time, the Bhagavān again entered the samādhi called “The Empowerment of the Vajra-Samaya Seal of All Tathāgatas” and proclaimed the supreme vidyā-mantra of his own family:
“Oṃ sarvatathāgatavajrasamayai hūṃ. Then, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the mantra of the Vajra-Samaya Seal of his own family:
“Oṃ vajrimaṭha. Then, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajragarbha proclaimed the mantra of the Ratna-Samaya Seal of his own family:
"HŪṂ BRAHMAKUṬI VAJRI ṬHA. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajranetra proclaimed the mantra of the samaya-seal of his own family:
"HŪṂ PADMAVAJRI NṚ ṬHA. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajraviśvakarman proclaimed the mantra of the karma-samaya-seal of his own family:
"HŪṂ VAJRAKARMAGṚHṆA KṚTA. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi further proclaimed the maṇḍala of the four mudrās of Trailokyavijaya:
"I shall now explain in sequence the supreme maṇḍala of the four mudrās;
its characteristics are like those of the Vajradhātu, for it is the Vajra Wrathful One."
Relying on the ritual application of the Great Maṇḍala, one should thus mark out all the maṇḍalas;
according to what is appropriate for Trailokyavijaya and the others, the images of the Buddhas should be drawn around the perimeter.

"Having performed all the extensive rituals for the rites of summoning and so forth within the maṇḍalas of the four mudrās according to the methods of that Great Maṇḍala, the practitioner should enter the maṇḍala of the four mudrās in accordance with the prescribed rules."
Having entered, he was instructed in the wisdom of the secret mudrās:
"Draw the four mudrās yourself according to the ritual, The maṇḍala of the pure dharmatā;
Communicating with those who are in harmony, One will always achieve all that is undertaken."
One should personally draw the four seals according to the ritual, the maṇḍala of the pure dharmatā;
by means of gazing at it while engaged in the speech of sublime passion, accomplishment is attained.
One should personally draw the four mudrās according to the ritual;
when the one whose wondrous marks correspond [to the deity] revolves within the maṇḍala of the pure dharmatā, one immediately attains the accomplishment of the matter of sublime bliss.
One should personally draw the four mudrās according to the ritual;
when the maṇḍala of the pure dharmatā is joined with the bliss of sublime loving speech, one immediately attains all supreme siddhis.
These are the mantras of the seals of the pure *dharmatā*:

Oṃ sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhāna-dharma-tejaḥ hūṃ. (1) Oṃ vajravidyādharī-ṭaṃ jaḥ. (1) Oṃ sarvabuddhamukhe hūṃ. (1) Oṃ sarvabuddhakāyavākcittasamaya-vajri jaḥ. (1) Furthermore, the instruction on the secret-of-secrets seal-wisdom within the four-seal maṇḍala:
"Once one has entered this maṇḍala, all the exquisite pleasures of the five desires can be accomplished;
when the time comes for union with another according to the dharma, one immediately attains the matter of supreme siddhi."
"This great vidyā-mantra is: *Hūṃ vajraga* (1).

Then, as taught in the instructions, having duly bestowed the extensive ritual procedures for the four samaya-mudrās—such as the vajra, jewel, lotus, and trident seals—one should, by means of these four seal-methods, perform vajra songs and music, and sing the playful melodies of Vajrasattva as an offering to all the noble ones. Next, with the mudrās, counter-mudrās, minor mudrās, and wisdom-mudrās, one performs the act of worship through the presence of universal dancing. By virtue of this offering of dance, one immediately attains the accomplishment of the activity of the dance-offering:
"One should rely on the method of the Vajra Dance; Then, with the two hands, using the wrathful fingers..."
According to the ritual, one should form the Great Seal of Trailokyavijaya within one's own heart;

the Vajra Dance is performed in the same manner. One should hold the right fist with the left hand, rotate it, and then place it before the forehead; next, the index finger should be placed at the mouth.
Furthermore, understand the mudrā of the whirling dance: join the two fists closely together, place the index fingers at the heart center, and prostrate with a mind filled with awe and trepidation.
Next, extend the vajra-anger fingers, then again raise them upward with the palms joined;
subsequently, rotate them and place them between the crown of the head, while the index fingers remain at the opening of the mouth.
"This is called the Maṇḍala of the Four Seals.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi again spoke this great vidyā-mantra of the Vajra-anger of his own family:
"HŪṂ. Furthermore, he spoke of this maṇḍala:
"I shall now explain in sequence the supreme external maṇḍala,
whose characteristics are like those of the Vajradhātu; one should know that this is Trailokyavijaya,
and according to the ritual application of the Great Maṇḍala, the external maṇḍala should be drawn in its entirety."
In that [mandala], one should draw according to the ritual procedure: within a lunar disc, arrange a vajra;

this vajra is Trailokyavijaya. Holding the great mudrā according to the rite, perform the majestic and wondrous stride of the Vajra with physical characteristics corresponding to those described in the teachings.
"Having extensively performed all the ritual procedures required for all external and secret maṇḍalas, next I shall explain the secret seal and wisdom of Vajra Trailokyavijaya:
'Once one has entered this maṇḍala, Binding it firmly with the wrathful fingers,
When performing the rite within the birth-gate, All activities will be successfully accomplished.'"
The mantra for seeking accomplishment is:
*HŪṂ VAJRA-SAMAYA KṚTVAḤ*. Furthermore, the instruction on the secret accomplishment mudrā and wisdom of Vajra Trailokyavijaya is as follows:
"Once one has properly entered this maṇḍala, One should place the supreme great mudrā."
When the Vajra and the syllable HŪṂ are united, one is able to skillfully accomplish all activities.
The mantra for that accomplishment is:
HŪṂ VAJRA-SAMAYA HŪṂ. According to what has been taught, the ritual procedure for forming the seals (mudrās) is performed in accordance with the instructions of the four seals.

Thereafter, from this, all matters of accomplishment arise; according to the respective maṇḍalas, such as these painted banners and images, whoever draws various forms should universally employ this method of accomplishment for them all.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi addressed all the Tathāgatas, saying:
"World-Honored Ones, all Tathāgatas!

I pray that you empower me so that the ritual applications performed within this family of mine may bring about beneficial deeds for all sentient beings according to their desires, causing them all universally to attain all accomplishments."
At that time, all the World-Honored Tathāgatas, desiring to establish this Great Ritual Manual of Trailokyavijaya, gathered once more like clouds and spoke these words of praise:
“Excellent, O Vajrasattva! Excellent, O Great Vajraratna!”
Excellent! The wondrous Dharma-gate of Vajra; Excellent!
One who can skillfully proclaim this True Dharma, The unsurpassed Vajra Secret Vehicle.
“The secret gateways of all Tathāgatas are subsumed within the Mahāyāna dharma of direct realization.

Chapter Eleven: The Extensive Ritual Manual for the Great Maṇḍala of the Wheel of the Three Times. At that time, the Blessed One, having thus fully known the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, all spoke these words: “Vajrapāṇi!”
You should now act in accordance with the commands of all Tathāgatas.
Since that Maheśvara has been subdued, he has long pressed his heart under your feet; you should now lift your foot and release him.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi addressed all the Tathāgatas, saying:
“I have first received from all the Tathāgatas the wrathful empowerment to subdue all evil beings; why now do you command me to release him?”

At that time, in order to restore the life-force of Maheśvara, the supreme sovereign who pervades and controls the three times, all the Tathāgatas brought forth from the hearts of all Tathāgatas this great vidyā-mantra:
"Oṃ vajrasattva hūṃ jaḥ. This vidyā-seal is as follows: "One should form the secret hook with firm resolve; extend all the fingers outward."
"By placing this mudrā joined together upon the crown of the head, one can cause even the dead to regain their lives.
When these mudrās and mantras were spoken, the Tathāgata Vajrasamādhi-nirghoṣa from the world-system of Vajrasamuccaya in the nadir suddenly emerged from the body of Maheśvara and spoke this verse:
"How marvelous! All Honored Ones of Perfect Enlightenment, The Great Wisdom of all Buddhas is unsurpassed!"
"It can cause the consciousness of deceased sentient beings to depart and return, thereby restoring their lives.
At that time, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva Mahāsattva spoke this Great Mantra of Raising the Foot: "Oṃ vajramukha. This is the mantra-seal:
"Form the vajra-anger finger-seal with the thumbs joined; keeping the tips of the fingers from touching, hold them firmly.
Rotate them until they form two vajras, rising gradually from below to the crown of the head."
When these seal-mantras were spoken, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi immediately raised the sole of his foot, and from that point, Maheśvara arose and his life was restored.

At that time, having been restored to life through the majestic spiritual power established by that Tathāgata, Maheśvara shall receive empowerment in that world; he will then perform deeds for the benefit of all sentient beings within that realm and likewise subdue those sentient beings who are malevolent.

At that time, from the center of the foot of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, there emerged a great mantra called Candrāṅga; this is the wisdom-seal (jñānamudrā) of all Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas.
The Great Mantra says:
“Oṃ vajratārisamantabhadra-kīlini mahā-vajriṇi hūṃ. This mantra-seal is as follows: “Firmly form the vajra-bond;
Extend both the little fingers and the thumbs upright.”
"Raising this seal while dwelling in equanimity and gathering the mind—this is called the Moonlight Seal.
When this seal-mantra is uttered, the Tathāgata Candrottara appears from the heart of the feet of the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi.
Once he had thus appeared, Maheśvara raised his head and placed it at the feet of the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi; the Bodhisattva then consecrated him with the half-moon mark upon his crown.
Having received the empowerment, he then took his place appropriately at the left side of the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi.

Thereafter, all the Tathāgatas placed a vajra-javelin into the two palms of Maheśvara and commanded him to act as an assistant to the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi; furthermore, they conferred upon him the empowerment of the Supreme Vidyā-vajra, thereby establishing his name as the Bodhisattva Vajravidyottama.

Part Two of the Eleventh Section: The Extensive Ritual Manual for the Great Maṇḍala of the Wheel of the Three Times. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrottama-vidyā, taking the great vajra-scepter he had received, whirled it like a wheel and performed the ritual service of a wondrous dance, speaking these verses:
“O Great One, Honored among all Perfectly Awakened Ones! The Great Bodhicitta is unsurpassed.”
"When the feet of the Exalted One’s supreme form touch [me], by this I shall attain Buddhahood.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi arose from the Vajra-Wrath Samādhi and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"I first received the great vajra of all Tathāgatas with my own hands, and furthermore, the empowerment rite of Vajrapāṇi was bestowed upon me.

At that time, Maheśvara and the others were all situated within the external sections of the various vajra families; now that this Trailokyavijaya Great Maṇḍala has been established, just as I have performed it, by virtue of this cause, these sentient beings shall all attain non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*."
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, spoke this Great Cakra-mantra of the Crown of All Tathāgatas:

"Oṃ vajrasattvaniṣaṇṇa hūṃ phaṭ. When this mantra was spoken, from the crowns of all the Tathāgatas there appeared the image of the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi endowed with virtue; from within that image, furthermore, countless rays of light of various colors emerged, illuminating the entire world-system.

Having shone forth, it returns and merges into the crown of the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi; thereafter, it becomes a mass of light from the uṣṇīṣa of all Tathāgatas. From within that mass of light, this great mantra of the Uṣṇīṣa of all Tathāgatas emerges, which says:

“Oṃ namo sarvatathāgatotsṛṣṭa-juśrī-nāvalokite hūṃ | jvala raṭa gaṭa gaṭa | vinarda vinarda | chinna | pinna hūṃ phaṭ. Then, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this heart-mantra of the messenger of his own family:
"Oṃ niḥsvabhāva-vajra hūṃ phaṭ. Furthermore, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi again spoke this great vidyā-mantra of his own heart:
"Oṃ ṭakki jaḥ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajragarbha spoke this supreme vidyā-mantra of his own family:
"Oṃ vajra-ratna-tama jvalaya hūṃ phaṭ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajranetra spoke this supreme vidyā-mantra of his own family:
"Oṃ sarvabuddha-vajrapadma-śodhaya sarvavidyud-dharmāḥ hūṃ phaṭ. Then, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajraviśvakarman spoke this supreme vidyā-mantra of his own family: "Oṃ vajra..."
Kṛtama vajra.
