sarvakarmāṇi me [kuru] svāhā.

PHAṬ (half-syllable) SVĀHĀ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrottamaprabhā, in order to pay homage and offer worship at the feet of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, spoke this heart-mantra:

“OṂ SUṂBA NIṂBA VAJRA VIDYOTATMA HŪṂ PHAṬ. At that time, the Wrathful Vidyārāja Vajraśūla, in order to pay homage and offer worship at the feet of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, spoke this heart-mantra:
“VAJRAŚŪLA. At that time, the Vidyārāja Māyāvajra spoke this heart-mantra:
“Oṃ vajramāyānṛśaya sarva hūṃ phaṭ. At that time, the Vidyārāja Vajraghaṇṭa spoke this heart-mantra: “Oṃ vajra-kaṇṭha raṇa raṇa hūṃ phaṭ.
At that time, the Vidyārāja Tūṣṇīmbhava-vajra spoke this heart-mantra: “Oṃ vajramohana mahāpradā hūṃ phaṭ. At that time, the Vidyārāja Vajrāyudha spoke this heart-mantra:
"Oṃ vajrayudhānāmaka hūṃ phaṭ. Such are the hosts of vidyārājas.
At that time, Vajrasena Nāḍī, the Vajra Wrathful King, in order to pay homage and make offerings at the feet of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, spoke this heart-mantra of his own:

"Oṃ vajra-kuṇḍali mahā-vajra-krodha-gṛhṇa hana daha paca vidhvaṃsaya vajriṇam-ūrdhvapāda-sphālaya pinahṛdayaṃ vajra-krodha hūṃ phaṭ. At that time, Vajraprabha, the Vajra Wrathful King, spoke this heart-mantra:
“Oṃ vajraprabhā-mārāya sāmakuṇḍa hūṃ phaṭ. At that time, the Vajra-staff Vajrakrodharāja spoke this heart-mantra:
“Oṃ vajradaṇḍa tāḍaya sarvaduṣṭān mahākuṇḍa hūṃ phaṭ. At that time, the Vajra-bhīṣaṇa Vajrakrodharāja spoke this heart-mantra:
"Oṃ vajrabhīkaraviśaya sarvaduṣṭān vimardaya hūṃ phaṭ. Such are the hosts of Vajra Wrathful Kings.
At that time, the great māra-lord Vajraśṛṅkhalā, in order to pay homage and offer worship at the feet of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, spoke this heart-mantra:
“Oṃ vajraśṛṅkhala mahāgaṇapati lokaya sarvaduṣṭān vyūha vajradara jñānapralaye hūṃ phaṭ. Then, the great māra-lord Vajramālā spoke his own heart-mantra:
“Oṃ vajramāragāṇapate māra graśaya praveśaya praveśaya bandhaya bandhaya vaśīkuru māraya hūṃ phaṭ. At that time, Vajrānurāgaṇamahāmārapati spoke this heart-mantra:
“Oṃ vajravajraśi mahāgaṇapataye vajraśikuru hūṃ phaṭ. At that time, the supreme Vajra Great Lord of Māras spoke this heart-mantra:
“Oṃ vajravidyāvidyaṅkuru mahāgaṇapati hūṃ phaṭ. Such were the hosts of great lords of Māras.
At that time, the Vajra-musala Vajrapāśa messenger, in order to pay homage and offer worship at the feet of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, spoke this heart-mantra:
"Oṃ vajramusala kuṭṭa kuṭṭa sarvaduṣṭān vajranudata hūṃ phaṭ. At that time, the Vajravāyu Vajrapāśa messenger spoke his own heart-mantra:
“Oṃ vajrānala mahāveganaya sarvaduṣṭān hūṃ phaṭ. Then, the Vajra Fire Vajradūta spoke this heart-mantra:
“Oṃ vajrānala-mahānuda jvālāya sarvavatsiṃha kuru | Sarva-duṣṭān hūṃ phaṭ. At that time, the Vajrapaiśāca Vajradūta spoke this heart-mantra:

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this Great Mantra of the Samādhi for Summoning All Vajra Families:
“Oṃ vairaṅkuśākarṣaya hūṃ. Next, the mantra for summoning is taught: “Oṃ vajrapāśakṛta hūṃ. Next, the samaya-mantra is taught: “Oṃ vajrasphoṭa vaṃ. Next, the karma-mantra is taught:
"Oṃ vajrakarma sādya kṛtvaḥ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this Great Maṇḍala of the All-Vajra Family:
"I shall now explain in sequence the supreme, unsurpassed Great Maṇḍala, whose form is like a Dharma-wheel altar;
one should strike out the various maṇḍalas according to the prescribed order."
The Great Illumination for Casting the Lines states:

"One should employ [the lines] within the maṇḍala; using *khadira* wood to fashion the stakes, one should double the length of the lines according to the ritual procedure, and having done so, cast the positions of the altar according to their respective measurements."
The mantra for the ritual stake is as follows:
"Four lines are joined together according to the rite; one should then strike out the perimeter of that wheel-maṇḍala in sequence.
Gradually draw out the outer boundary, making it twice the size of the previous one."
Alternatively, one may perform three times as much as appropriate; following this sequence, one should strike out the outer maṇḍala.
According to the original ritual manual, the various corner sections should be struck with their boundaries measured according to the correct proportions.
"This is the ritual procedure for casting the lines:
'Thereafter, according to the lines to be cast, using five colors that are pure and perfect,
form the great vajra-fist with the left hand, and mark the boundaries of the mandala with colored powder in sequence as desired.'"
The *Five-Colored Great Illumination* states:

"Once the altar has been completed according to the ritual rules, the Ācārya, abiding in a state of meditative equipoise (*samāhita-citta*), should next focus his attention on opening the gates of the mandala; thus, those four vajra-gates shall be opened."
The Opening of the Door and the Great Illumination state:
"According to the ritual, use either gold or silver; or fashion [the images] by modeling or painting upon banners.
They should be installed and arranged in the four directions as appropriate; the forms of the four Buddhas must accord with the instructions."
The Great Vidyā of all Buddhas says:
"Furthermore, on the four sides of that Buddha, one should paint the four great secret beings;
in the center, one should place the noble lord Vajrapāṇi, manifesting the wrathful form of Trailokyavijaya."
The Great Mantras of the Four Great Beings state:
"When descending the line, one should maintain focused mindfulness; one must not enter or exit beyond the prescribed limits.
One should proceed in sequence with the vajra-step, for all those mandala boundaries follow the ritual law."
The Vajrapada Great Mantra says:
"Advancing gradually with the vajra-step, one should lay out the first maṇḍala in the east;
according to the sequence and the ritual rules, one should install the four vidyārājas, Māyā and the others."
"These great mantras are as follows:
Advancing gradually with the vajra-step, one should arrange the second maṇḍala in the south,
placing the Vajrakrodha and the four, such as Jāṅgulī, in their proper order."
"These great mantras are as follows:
Advancing gradually with the vajra-step, one should lay out the third maṇḍala to the west;
there, the four Vajramuṣalas and the others, the Vajradūtas, are arranged in their proper order."
"These great mantras are as follows:
Advancing gradually with the vajra-step, one should lay out the fourth maṇḍala in the north;
the four servants, such as Vajrāṅkuśī and the others, should be installed there according to the sequence of the instructions."
"These great mantras are as follows:
Advancing gradually with the vajra-step, one should draw [the deities] at the four gates according to the ritual;
the Vajra-Ṣaṇmukha and other lords of māras should be arranged in their proper sequence."
"These great vidyās are as follows:
Advancing gradually with the vajra-step, one should arrange the divisions of the outer maṇḍala;
all the Mātṛkās should be painted around the perimeter, arrayed in their respective positions according to the sequence of the instructions."
Within all four vajra gates, as previously taught by the noble protectors of the gates, I shall now explain the ritual for that supreme maṇḍala;
each detail shall be exactly as prescribed in the ritual manuals.

"Once all the rites, such as summoning and so forth, within this Great Maṇḍala of the Wheel of the Three Times have been performed according to the original teachings, the Vajrācārya should personally bind the Vajra-ferocious *Tiri-tiri* mudrā and say to the disciple:

'I have now arisen from the wisdom of that Vajra-samādhi; you must not rashly explain this samādhi-dharma to others. Do not cause yourself to incur calamity and ruin your life, lest after death you fall into the great hells.'"

Having spoken thus, he further conferred upon him the Great Mantra of the Vow-mind (*samayacittamahāvidyā*). Subsequently, he manifested it by means of the *vajrakrodha-tirītirī* mudrā and spoke these words:

"If there should be anyone who transgresses this bond of the samaya, this Vajra-Krodha Samaya shall arise from the crown of their head and destroy their body; therefore, you must act according to the ritual."

Translated by the Tripitaka Master Śīlagupta, Dharma-transmitting Master and Imperially Conferred Purple-Robed Śramaṇa, together with others, under imperial decree during the Song Dynasty. The Remainder of the Eleventh Section: The Extensive Ritual Manual for the Great Maṇḍala of the Wheel of the Three Times.

"At that time, the Vajrācārya should bind the Vajradhara-karma-mudrā. The great vidyā-mantra of this mudrā is: Oṃ sarvatathāgatavajradhara-ṭkṛ-hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. Next, the characteristics of the mudrā are explained: [Insert description of mudrā here]."
"Interlock the little fingers and the thumbs; place the two vajra hands again upon them.
This is called the Karma-samaya-mudrā, which skillfully accomplishes all supreme karmas."
"Then, with the vajra-water, one should confer the empowerment upon the disciple.

The great mantra (*mahāvidyā*) is: *Oṃ vajravighnaga viśodhaya vajradharatvāya samayagala gala*. Then, having covered the disciple’s face with a silk cloth, lead the disciple into the maṇḍala and confer this great mantra."
"Oṃ praviśa vajra-praveśaya vajrāviśa vajrādhiṣṭha vajra hūṃ. Having entered the maṇḍala, one should next cast a flower according to the ritual procedure.
He bestowed this great vidyā-mantra, saying:
“Oṃ pratisaṃsthitivajra hūṃ. Then, according to the place where the flower falls, that is the accomplishment of one’s chosen deity (iṣṭadevatā).
Next, one should remove the face-cloth from the disciple and, following the proper sequence, cause them to behold the maṇḍala within.
Furthermore, one should confer the oath of secrecy, saying: "You must not casually explain this samādhi to others."

Why is this? Because there are certain individuals of wrong views who lack faith; how could they know that these Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, possess great wisdom that is not in vain, nor can they receive this Vajrapāṇi initiation-samādhi within the Tathāgata Vajra Family, but instead place their faith and inclination only in other deities?

Having bestowed the oath and instructions, he next conferred upon him the empowerment of the vajra insignia and garland; thereafter, placing the ritual vajra (karmavajra) into his hand, he established him with a vajra name.
Then, according to the ritual procedure of that Vajrasamādhi Great Maṇḍala, one should provide instruction on the formation of the Great Seal (Mahāmudrā):
"Form the vajra-bind firmly with both hands; Next, extend the two index fingers, And bend their first joints so that the two tips meet; This is the Crown Wheel Seal of the Mahāsattva."
Joining them again, form the vajra-bond; extend the two index fingers inward between the middle fingers.
This is called the *Tejorāśi-uṣṇīṣa-mudrā*, which is the supreme samādhi of the Buddha Tejorāśi.
With both hands, one should form the vajra-mudrā: joining the little fingers and thumbs together, then inserting the thumbs into the binding [of the other fingers].
This is called the mudrā of the supreme vidyā, for it is accomplished by the supreme vidyā;
thereafter, one should skillfully perform the binding of the various mudrās.
Placing the index fingers at rest as in the two gates, this is called the Heart-Binding Seal (*hṛdayabandhana-mudrā*).

Then, inserting the ring fingers into the center, one should properly rotate all the fingers according to the ritual procedure of the Vajra-Jewel. Having rotated them, they return to rest within the mouth.
Then, forming the gesture of looking upward once more, rotate it in succession and rest it at the heart;
this is called the Four-Flower Mudrā, which is the supreme vidyā of the Lotus.
From this, it rises again from the crown of the head; revolving upon the body, it forms the supreme wheel-seal (*cakramudrā*).
This is called the Vajra-karmakarma-mudrā; it brings about the excellent accomplishment of Vajra-activity (*vajrakarman*).
Firmly forming the Sattva-vajra, the little fingers are joined together like a vajra.
This is called the Heart-Seal of All Buddhas.
This seal can accomplish all matters.
Join the little fingers and thumbs of both hands together; the middle finger of the left hand forms the shape of a fork.
This is one prong from among the three-pronged [vajra].
It is the supreme vidyā-mudrā of Vajra; this mudrā is itself the vajra-prong.
All the mudrās shall be proclaimed in sequence, performed by Māyāvajra and the others.
"Such are the seals (*mudrā*) of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas:
'Firmly form the vajra-bond (*vajrabandha*) with both hands; the left hand, acting as a vajra, is pressed close [to the right].
This is called the Vajra-fist (*vajramuṣṭi*), employed within all the Vajra families (*vajrakula*')."
The two hands should be formed into the vajra gesture; according to the ritual, one should arrange the various insignia.
Among all the vajra families, this mudrā is able to summon swiftly.
With the backs of the two index fingers extended and spread, and the two thumbs held downward, place the *Oṃ* seal upon the crown of the head; the arrangement of the *Vajra* seal is likewise.
"Such are the great seals (mahāmudrā) of the Vajra-vidyārājas.
Furthermore, extend the two auspicious hands; likewise, the two hands are turned back-to-back.
Again, form fists with the half-arms, and finally rotate them so they rest at the mouth."
"These are the great mudrās of the Vajra Wrathful Kings.
Place the thumb of the left hand well-settled; likewise, perform the binding of the garland according to the ritual method.
The right hand again assumes the gesture of bestowing wealth, while the index finger forms a fist as the sword mudrā."
"Such are the seals of the great Vajra Māra lords:
'The left hand is like grasping a musala; extending the arm to form the seal is likewise so.
The right hand manifests blazing light; forming a vajra-fist, one then vibrates it.'"
"Such are the mudrās of the Vajra Messengers.
Forming a face with upraised countenance and sharp fangs, holding a staff in the manner of striking to harm,
forming the mudrā by bending the arms as appropriate, and making the left and right hands perform the gesture of seizing."
"Such are the mudrās of the Vajra Servants.
Regarding the various mudrās within the maṇḍala: the left hand in all cases is like that of Vajrapāṇi;
as all the mudrās are proclaimed in their proper sequence, thus the *karmas* are successfully accomplished."
All the mudrās of the Great Beings are accomplished within one's own body;
by visualizing oneself as such, one immediately attains the supreme accomplishment of the mudrā.
The Great Being’s Uṣṇīṣa-mudrā is the great protection; the Light-Gathering Great Seal bestows accomplishment.
The Trailokyavijaya Seal performs all deeds; all hooks for summoning emerge from the heart.
“Such are the seals of the Buddhas.
By means of the seals of all Buddhas, one attains all *siddhis*. The Vajra is the supreme vidyā, most excellent;
that great seal of the Vajra-khaṭvāṅga can effectively bestow all accomplishments.”
Māyāvajra brings excellent accomplishment; the vajra bell can universally awaken all.
He who holds the staff is perfectly tranquil; the vajra weapon shatters with vajra power.
With most supreme blazing flames, he subdues all evils; with supreme and virtuous radiance, he destroys everything.
The Victorious Staff likewise strikes down harm; with eyes of dread, it creates all terrors.

It is the most supreme subduer and slayer; the Victorious Garland skillfully performs all ritual acts (*karmas*), able to accomplish whatever is desired through reverence and love. It is the most supreme, thoroughly crushing and subjugating all things.
Mūsala destroys all evils; that *pattā* seal can bind them well.
Most supreme and blazing, it subdues all evils. The yakṣa who seizes all evil ones, with sharp fangs devouring everything—Vajra-kara shatters all evils.
"The one who creates all obstacles is the supreme obstructer; the one who seizes everything is the supreme plunderer. Chapter Twelve:

The Section on the Extensive Ritual of the Vajra Maṇḍala of the All-Vajra Family. At that time, the Bhagavān again entered the samādhi called "The Empowerment Born from the Vajra-Dhāraṇī of All Tathāgatas," and spoke this supreme vidyā-mantra of his own family:
"Oṃ vajrasavitri svāhā. Then, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this supreme vidyā-mantra of his own family:
"Oṃ vajradhāri hūṃ. Vajravikrāmiṇi hūṃ phaṭ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajragarbha spoke this supreme vidyā-mantra of his own family:
"Oṃ vajraratnavaśitī svāhā. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajranetra spoke this supreme vidyā-mantra of his own family:
"Oṃ vajrapadma nīte hūṃ phaṭ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrakarmā spoke this supreme vidyā-mantra of his own family:
"Oṃ vajrakarma kṛ hūṃ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrāgraprajñā spoke this supreme vidyā-mantra of his own family:
"Oṃ vajraśūra gṛi svāhā. At that time, Māyāvajraprajñā-rāja spoke this mantra of his own mudrā:
"Oṃ vajra-cakri oṃ. Thus spoke the Vidyārāja Vajraghaṇṭā. He spoke this mahāvidyā: "Vajra-khaḍgi hūṃ. Thus spoke the Vidyārāja Tūṣṇīṃvajra.
He spoke this mahāvidyā: "Oṃ vajra-daṇḍa ghe ghe hūṃ. Thus spoke the Vidyārāja Vajrāyudha. He spoke this mahāvidyā:
“Oṃ vajri hūṃ. Such are the mantras of the samaya-mudrās of the Vajra-Vidyārājas.
At that time, the Vajrakrodharāja Vajrasena proclaimed this mantra of his own samaya-mudrā: “Oṃ jvala vajri hūṃ. The Krodharāja Vajraprabha proclaimed this great mantra:
"Oṃ vajrasāme hūṃ. This is the great mantra spoken by the Wrathful King Vajradaṇḍa: "Oṃ vajradaṇḍe hūṃ.
This is the great mantra spoken by the Wrathful King Vajrabhīṣaṇa: "Oṃ vajraviśane hūṃ. Such are the samaya seals and mantras of these Vajra Wrathful Kings.
At that time, the great mārapati Vajraśṛṅkhalā spoke this mantra of his own samaya-mudrā:
“Oṃ vajraśṛṅkhalā hūṃ. The great mārapati Vajramālā spoke this mahāvidyā: “Oṃ vajramālā hūṃ. The great mārapati Vajrarāga spoke this mahāvidyā:
"Oṃ vajravakṣi hūṃ. This great mantra was spoken by the most supreme Vajra Great Lord of Māras:
"Oṃ vajrāparājite hūṃ. Such are the mantras of the samaya seals of the Vajra Great Lords of Māras.
At that time, the Vajra-musala Vajrapāśa spoke this mantra of his own samaya-seal:
"Oṃ vajramusara gṛhe hūṃ. The Vajra-vāyu Vajrapāśa spoke this great mantra: "Oṃ vajrapati. The Vajra-tejas Vajrapāśa spoke this great mantra:
"Oṃ vajrajvāli hūṃ. This is the great vidyā-mantra spoken by the Vajrapairava Vajradūta:
"Oṃ vajraghore hī. Such are the samaya-mudrās and mantras of these Vajradūtas.
At that time, the Vajra-servant Vajrāṅkuśa spoke this mantra of his own samaya-mudrā:
"Oṃ vajra-aṅkuśi hūṃ. The Vajra-servant Vajraghola spoke this great mantra: "Oṃ vajra-gholani hūṃ. The Vajra-servant Vajravinaṭaka spoke this great mantra:
"Oṃ vajravijñāni hūṃ. Thus spoke the Dragon Vajra Vajrapreṣya, reciting this great mantra:
"Oṃ vajraharaṇi hūṃ. Such are the samaya-mudrās and mantras of the Vajrapreṣyas.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi spoke these verses on the maṇḍala of the entire Vajra Family:
"I shall now, in due order, expound the most supreme Vajra Maṇḍala.
Its form is square with four gates; one should mark out its outer boundary lines accordingly."
According to the ritual, establish the position of the central palace; the rule for the eastern gate is likewise.

Within that, following the sequence of the ritual procedure, one should install the Buddha images as appropriate, arranging the Vajrahūṃkāra and other deities; these four great beings surround the Buddha.
In front of the maṇḍala, one should, according to the ritual, draw the vajra-mudrā everywhere.
Furthermore, on its various left and right sides, one should draw the mudrās of each respective family according to the ritual.
The Vajraśuṇḍa and other lords of māras should serve as the guardians of the four gates.
Bhūtī, Śrī, and Sarasvatī, along with Vāgīśvarī and the others—these four should reside in the inner corners;
in the outer corners, one should follow the ritual procedures and paint everywhere the seals (mudrās) of the sages and noble ones as described before.
Furthermore, within the outer maṇḍala, one should paint the forms of the deities and so forth according to the ritual rules;
the sequence of the altar and all its ritual procedures are exactly as described in the Extensive Ritual Manual.

"Within this Vajra Maṇḍala, perform whatever rites you desire according to the ritual procedures. Having performed the samaya-karmas of this family, such as the vajrāṅkuśa and others, the Vajrācārya shall then personally bind the Vajradhara mudrā and say to the disciple:
'You must not proclaim this Dharma before those who have not entered the samaya and do not perceive the Dharma by means of this samaya-mudrā; do not cause the destruction of the secret samaya.'"
Having spoken thus, he then takes that *karmavajra* scepter and places it upon the *vajradhara-mudrā*, and according to the ritual procedure of the root text, leads the disciple into the maṇḍala.

Having entered, one should immediately cast the *karmavajra*; wherever the vajra falls, one attains the wisdom-seal (*jñānamudrā*) of the Samaya of the Principal Deity and achieves the rite of magnetizing (*vaśīkaraṇa*). By virtue of this cause, all ritual actions (*karmakriyā*) will be fully accomplished.
Thereafter, having removed the face-cloths from his disciples and caused them all to behold the maṇḍala, he spoke these words regarding the secret samaya-mudrā:

"Now, this samaya-mudrā can constantly accomplish all desired karmas of veneration and love; all beings shall regard it as a mother, a son, a wife, or a daughter, and will all come to follow it with compliance."
Next, he conferred upon him this great vidyā-mantra, saying:

"Oṃ sarvagāmini sarvavaśīkaraṇa-ghurghure vajriṇi hūṃ phaṭ. This great vidyā-mantra, if recited once, causes all those who are beloved to come and show respect and affection; whatever one does according to one's will becomes free from faults; one obtains all enjoyments as desired and achieves accomplishment, thereafter attaining a pure mental nature and generating the supreme intention; one is able to observe all seals of omniscience (*sarvajñamudrā*) and further perform all activities—thus spoke the virtuous Vajradhara.
"Next, one should instruct them in the mudrā of that samādhi:
'Place the fingers of the Samaya-Angry Fist upon the crown; bind them firmly at the heart.
Spread the face, eyebrows, and mouth-aperture; then place both hands again upon the crown.'"
Binding the left hand with the vajra-pointing gesture, form the triple-pronged mudrā and press it close;
by forming this seal according to the ritual procedure, one attains the accomplishment of the supreme vidyā.
Within all the Vajra families, the left vajra index finger is always held in [the gesture of] grasping;

I shall now explain the ritual for binding those mudrās. According to the rules of the various samādhi-dharmas, the index fingers are pressed together like the form of a wheel; the same applies to the mudrā of the vajra bell.
The mudrā of the syllable Oṃ is identical to this; the mudrā of the Lion-Ear Gathering of Weapons is likewise.
Such are the mudrās of the Vajra-Vidyārājas.
The gathering of the Blazing Flame mudrā is also thus; the gathering of the Vajra-Light mudrā is likewise.
The mudrās for the staff and the fist are gathered as before; finally, the mudrā is rotated at the edge of the mouth.
"Such are the mudrās of the Vajra Wrathful Kings.
Those are the mudrās of the *pāśa* (lasso) and the garland, as well as the hook-signs of the Vajra Subjugation and others."
Place that most excellent seal at the crown; these are the four lords of Māras who guard the gates.
Such are the seals of the great Vajra lords of Māras.
Next, one should bend the arms into the form of a wheel, with the backs of both hands turned according to the ritual procedure.
The mudrā of Liberation has blazing flames; the mudrā of Slaying is placed at the mouth.
Such are the mudrās of the Vajra Messengers.
Inserting the two fingers within and placing them at the opening of the mouth, pressing them close together, one forms the gesture of striking.
Wrapping the arms to form the mudrā as appropriate, one performs the mudrā of the fierce and malevolent form for seizing and plundering.
"These are the mudrās of the Vajra Servants.

Chapter Thirteen: The Extensive Ritual Manual for the Samaya Maṇḍala of All Vajra Families. At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the *samādhi* called "The Vajra Empowerment Born from the Dharma-Samaya of All Tathāgatas," and spoke this supreme vidyā-mantra of his own family:
"Oṃ vajravidhu. Then, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this vidyā-mantra of the samaya of his own dharma:
“Oṃ chana chana hūṃ phaṭ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajragarbha spoke this great vidyā-mantra of his own dharma-samādhi:
“Oṃ hara hara hūṃ phaṭ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajranetra spoke this great vidyā-mantra of his own dharma-samādhi:
“Oṃ mara mara hūṃ phaṭ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajraviśvakarman spoke this great vidyā-mantra of his own dharma-samādhi:
“Oṃ kuru kuru hūṃ phaṭ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrottamaprajñā spoke this Great Mantra of the Samaya of his own Dharma:
“Oṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ. The Great Mantras of the four Vajra-vidyārājas, Māyāvajra and the others, are as follows:
"Oṃ cina cina hūṃ phaṭ. "Oṃ aviśa aviśa hūṃ phaṭ. "Oṃ buribu vaśa hūṃ phaṭ. "Oṃ cina cina hūṃ phaṭ. These are the great vidyā-mantras of the four wrathful Vajra Kings.
"Oṃ nama-nama hūṃ phaṭ. "Oṃ maraya maraya hūṃ phaṭ. "Oṃ gādaya gādaya hūṃ phaṭ. "Oṃ vāya vāya hūṃ phaṭ. These are the great vidyās of the four vajra-mahāmārīs.
“Oṃ mana mana hūṃ phaṭ. “Oṃ bandha bandha hūṃ phaṭ. “Oṃ vaśībhava hūṃ phaṭ. “Oṃ jaya jaya hūṃ phaṭ. These are the great mantras of the four Vajra Messengers.
"Oṃ vyūha-vyūha hūṃ phaṭ. "Oṃ guṅguṅ hūṃ phaṭ. "Oṃ jvala-jvala hūṃ phaṭ. "Oṃ kana-kana hūṃ phaṭ. These are the great mantras of the four Vajra Servants.

“Oṃ caṇa caṇa hūṃ phaṭ. “Oṃ mara mara hūṃ phaṭ. “Oṃ gṛhṇa gṛhṇa hūṃ phaṭ. “Oṃ bhuva bhuva hūṃ phaṭ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this verse concerning the Samaya Maṇḍala of all the Vajra Families:
“I shall now, in due order, expound The Great Dharma Samaya Maṇḍala.”
Its appearance is like the wheel of the three times; this maṇḍala is to be drawn in this manner.

Within it, everything follows the proper sequence: the Buddhas and the Vajradharas and other honored ones, according to the ritual of that dharma-maṇḍala, are to be depicted everywhere with their respective heart-symbols.
"Within this Dharma-samaya-maṇḍala, having performed the rites according to the instructions as taught,
that Vajrācārya shall, with a vajra-bell, form the Vajradhara mudrā together with it, and lead the disciple into the maṇḍala according to the ritual rules, saying to the disciple:
'If there should be anyone who has not entered this samaya and does not know the teachings of this family, do not rashly explain this Dharma to them.'"
Having bestowed the oath-instructions, one should immediately ring the bell and further bestow this verse of the Vow-heart, saying:
“Following this sound of the great wisdom bell as it rings, All that is performed shall be decisively accomplished as appropriate;
And this vajra of ritual action (karmavajra), That which is to be destroyed shall likewise be decisively so.”
If one does not respect the ācārya, the Vajra companions will not be friends;
when the wicked turn back toward one with a compassionate mind, this is what constitutes the path of saṃsāra.
Having spoken these verses, he then removed the face-cloth from his disciples.
Next, he proceeded to reveal the wisdom of the Dharma-samādhi-mudrā:
"The Buddhas and the Honored Ones such as Vajradhara, As described in the Dharma Maṇḍala,"
The cause of peace for all sentient beings, This is the supreme vidyā of Vajra.
If this world is like an illusion, So too is suffering like the sound of a bell;
The cause that pacifies all sufferings— This unsurpassed vajra weapon.

The supreme wrathful one who subdues sentient beings, whose excellent light decisively shatters [all things], wields the invincible vajra-staff that strikes down harm; he terrifies all those with wrong views.
Against the arrogant enemy, there is no victor; he binds them with the invincible vajra-garland.
The one who is honored by the world and beloved by those he desires; the unsurpassed conqueror of Māra, who destroys enmity;
the unsurpassed subduer who excels at crushing [the wicked]; the all-pervading Vajra-Wind that turns according to [his will];
the supreme Great Radiance, the Vajra-Fire; the unsurpassed enjoyer who excels the most greedy.
The great tusk is pure and able to summon; it can restore life to all who have died.
Among those feared, none surpass Vajrin; among all things that provide flavor, none surpass water.

“Oṃ vajramakari gra-sagra sa śīghraṃ śīghraṃ praveśaya pātālaṃ bhañjaya vajramakaradhāriṇi hūṃ phaṭ. Then, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this verse concerning the entire Vajra-family Karma-maṇḍala:
“I shall now, in due order, expound the most supreme Karma-maṇḍala.”
Relying upon the ritual procedures of that vajra maṇḍala, one should delineate this maṇḍala as appropriate.
In the initial position of all maṇḍalas, first install the image of the Buddha therein;
then, within the rows to his left and right, arrange the various mahāsattvas according to the ritual rules.
In the center, paint the supreme vidyā of Vajra, and likewise paint his vidyā-consort.
The secret [deities] such as Vajralāsyā and the others, along with the dancing offerings, should all be depicted for the Honored One.
Within that, the successive order of the noble ones (āryas) should all be executed according to the rules of the wheel-maṇḍala;
the self-seals (svamudrā), the corresponding seals (pratimudrā), and the dances should be drawn in their respective order as previously described.
The four offerings, such as Vajra-incense, and the method of the Vajra-whirl dance,
should be performed according to the previously explained ritual in the four corners and the intervals between the four gates.

“Within this *karmamaṇḍala*, having performed all the ritual methods such as summoning (*ākarṣaṇa*) according to the rules, the Vajrācārya shall, as taught, form the *karmasamaya-mudrā* and address the disciple as follows:
‘If there are those who have not seen the teachings of this family (*kula*), you must not explain this secret *samaya* of the ritual to them; do not allow yourselves to incur misfortune and blame.’”
Having spoken these words, the Vajrācārya again binds the self-karma-vajradhara-samaya-mudrā, casts a wrathful gaze, and utters this great vidyā-mantra:

“Oṃ vajradharīya veśaya bandhaya gṛhṇāpaya sarvakarmāṇi stambhaya hūṃ phaṭ | Hūṃ ā | Ra ra ra ra vajri. Thereafter, according to the ritual procedure, one should lead the disciple into the maṇḍala; then, as appropriate, one should perform the various acts of offering, including the wondrous circular dance (maṇḍala-nṛtya), by means of the mudrās and their corresponding counterparts.
From this point onward, his body, speech, and mind, as well as all activities he undertakes, will achieve accomplishment.
Thereafter, the face-veil of the disciple shall be removed, and he should be instructed in the mudrā-knowledge of the ritual dance:
"The Buddhas and the Vajradharas and other Honored Ones, Through the supreme samādhi of the two palms joined together."
The vajra-play and other offerings are the supreme vidyā of the vajra;
all those vidyās are likewise so. According to what has been taught, in their proper sequence, the performance of the dance serves as the supreme offering, making offerings to the karma-maṇḍala.
The ritual applications of all phenomena are the vajra dance; the instruction on the Great Seal (mahāmudrā) is likewise.
Through the union of the two hands in the supreme samādhi, one attains liberation by facing the seal manifest before one.
Performing the activity of manifest whirling dance, one makes offerings to all the Great Victorious Lords, such as Mahāvajradhara and others; thus, all definitive *karmas* are accomplished.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, in order to establish all sentient beings within the Vajra Family so that they might abide on the stage of non-retrogression, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
“I uphold the secret dharma of all Tathāgatas; having already received empowerment and the Tathāgata’s instructions, what, then, is this secret?
At that time, the World-Honored One entered the *samādhi* of the Secret Vajra of All Tathāgatas and spoke these verses on the secret of all Tathāgatas:
“Whatever ritual procedures for all phenomena exist according to their requirements, they all emerge from the intrinsic nature of sentient beings.”
"This arises from acting for the benefit of sentient beings; thus, all actions such as desire and the like are purified.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this secret dharma of his own:
"For the sake of benefiting all sentient beings, taking the Buddha’s teachings as the true cause,"
"By means of this, one slays all sentient beings; herein there is neither sin nor defilement.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajragarbha spoke the secret dharma of his own jewel:
"For the sake of benefiting all sentient beings, one immediately enters into union with the Buddha-body itself."
"By this, one destroys the minds of others; herein there is neither fault nor defilement.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajranetra spoke this secret dharma of his own *karma*:
"The nature of desire is true bliss, peerless and beyond compare; it is the common practice of all Buddhas."
"Acting in accordance with what is desired to benefit sentient beings—those who practice in this way obtain supreme merit.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajraviśvakarman spoke this secret dharma of his own activity:
"For the sake of benefiting all sentient beings, taking the Buddha’s teachings as the true cause,"
"All activities will be accomplished everywhere, And he shall obtain vast and manifold supreme merit.
Then, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, in order to praise the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, spoke these verses:
"Excellent is the Vajrasattva! Excellent is the Great Vajraratna!"
Excellent is the wondrous Dharma-gate of Vajra! Excellent is the supreme Karmavajra!
You have excellently proclaimed this True Dharma, The unsurpassed Vajra Secret Vehicle, The secret door of all Tathāgatas, Subsumed within the Mahāyāna’s dharma of direct realization.

Chapter Fifteen: The Section on the Extensive Ritual of the Great Maṇḍala for Subduing All Worlds. At that time, all the Tathāgatas again gathered like clouds in order to exhort the virtuous Vajradhara, the Lord of All Dharmas, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara. They spoke these one hundred and eight names in verse, saying:
“Lotus-Sattva, Great Lotus, World-Lord King, Great Sovereign, ... (the rest of the verses follow) ...”
To the Victorious Hero Avalokiteśvararāja, I prostrate and take refuge in the Vajra Dharma.
To the Supreme Dharma King, the Greatly Pure One, the Great-Minded, Most Exalted Heroic King,
the Great Padmasambhava with a lotus body— to the Lotus Honored One, I prostrate and take refuge.
Born from the lotus, with the light of the wondrous lotus, Pure as a lotus, the one most excellently pure;
With a body of wondrous lotuses, the vajra-lotus, I take refuge in the Lotus One, the Lord of Lotuses.
Victorious great radiance, master of great skillful action, Vast and excellent metaphor, great and supreme body,
Possessing great valor and great fearlessness— I bow my head and take refuge in the Great Hero.
Knowing the minds of sentient beings and the Mahāyāna Dharma, Corresponding with the Dharma and the Great Forefather,
Bringing about the pacification of calamities, purity, benefit, and the birth of tranquility— I bow my head and take refuge in the exquisite blossom of awakening.
The Dharma is the true meaning; it upholds the True Dharma, acts as the pure Dharma, and performs the wholesome Dharma.
It is the supreme, wondrous Dharma, the Great Dharma-gate. I bow my head and take refuge in the Wheel of the True Dharma.
Bodhi-mahāsattva, Subhūṣaṇavīra, Sattvavara, Dharmamahāsattva,
Sarvottama-subhavīra-bhaṭṭāraka— homage to you, Vīravara-mahāsattva!
O Sovereign of Supreme Mastery in Contemplation, Universal Observer, Great and Victorious Lord,
Light of the World who benefits all beings— I bow my head and take refuge in the World-Sovereign.
The worldly syllables are the great syllables; the supreme syllable is the metaphor for all syllables.
Among all syllables, it is the syllable within syllables; I bow my head and take refuge in the wheel of syllables.
The Lotus-Handed One possesses vast and great hands; he who bestows universal peace and security is the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Great Honored One.
I prostrate and take refuge in the majestic power of the Buddha.
The Buddha’s wondrous marks and great marks, The vajra-marked one of auspicious signs,
The supreme and wondrous light of the Great Dharma— I bow my head and take refuge in the World’s Radiance.
To the Glorious Lotus Victorious Lord, to the Venerable Dharma-Śrī-Vijaya,
the Supreme Great Brahmā, the Honored One among Brahmās— to the Son of Brahmā, I prostrate and take refuge.
Supreme Lamp of the Dharma, Lamp of Lamps, Who emits the radiance of lamps that shines everywhere,
Venerable One of Radiant Splendor, Great Illuminator— I bow my head and take refuge in the Buddha of radiant marks.
Having attained the supreme awakening of the Buddha’s consecration, you are the great awakened wisdom for all the sons of the Buddhas;
you are the supreme crown-wheel of the great awakened consecration. I bow my head and take refuge in the Awakened One among the awakened.
Having already perfected the Buddha-eye, which is the Great Eye, you further possess the Dharma-eye for great observation;
sovereign of all samādhi and wisdom, I prostrate and take refuge in the Vajra-eye.
If anyone, with their whole body, pays respectful homage to this hymn of one hundred and eight names,
or contemplates it, or recites it, that person shall attain sovereignty over the world.
Now I entreat you, O Fearless One: Great Muni, please speak well of the excellent activities of the Dharma-maṇḍala, the wondrous correspondences arising from its own family.

At that time, having heard the words of exhortation from all the Tathāgatas, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Noble Avalokiteśvara immediately stood before the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni. Placing a vajra-lotus at his own heart, he spoke these verses:
“O Great One, most supreme and utterly pure! This wondrous vajra-lotus of mine Is like a son born from a great progenitor of the world;
It is the excellent empowerment of the dharma of this family.”

At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, entered the *samādhi* of the empowerment of the lotus born from the *vajra-dharma-samaya* of all Tathāgatas, and spoke this *dharma-samaya* of all Tathāgatas. Then, the heart-mantra of all Tathāgatas emerged from his own heart, and he spoke this heart-mantra:
"Hrīḥ. When he spoke this heart-mantra, the appearance of a lotus emerged from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, possessing countless colors and exquisite radiance.

That light universally illumined all worlds; having thoroughly purified them through the wisdom of the pure dharmas such as desire and so forth, the light then returned and entered the heart of the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara.
At that time, the World-Honored One, all the Tathāgatas together, spoke this supreme great vidyā-mantra of the samādhi of their own family:
“Oṃ vajra-patnī-tama-hrīḥ. At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this supreme great vidyā-mantra of his own family:
“Oṃ vajra hūṃ phaṭ. At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajragarbha spoke this supreme great vidyā-mantra of his own family:
"Oṃ vajra-ratna-tattva-tra. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajranetra spoke this supreme vidyā-mantra of his own family:
"Oṃ vajra-vinaya-tattva-hrīḥ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrakarmā spoke this supreme vidyā-mantra of his own family:

"Oṃ vajraviśuddhatmaka. At that time, the Noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara entered the samādhi called "Manifesting All Forms" and spoke this great mantra for subduing all worlds and one's own mind: "Oṃ hūṃ hrīḥ hoḥ.

When this heart-mantra was spoken, from the heart of the Noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara there appeared the Venerable Vajradhara, possessing the same marks as the Noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara. He sat upon a lotus, formed the lotus mudrā, was fully adorned with various exquisite colors and features, and manifested as the fused embodiment of all Tathāgatas and Great Beings.

Once these images of great bodhisattvas had thus appeared, they manifested their own physical forms throughout all worlds, extensively taming all sentient beings as was appropriate for each, reaching the entire realm of sentient beings without exception.

Having performed these various activities, he returned once more to the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajra Realm. There, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, dwelt in reliance upon the lunar disc that surrounded him, and spoke this verse:
“O, how great are all the Honored Ones of Perfect Enlightenment! Compassion and skillful means are their sovereign lords.
If those in any of the evil realms are tamed, They shall immediately achieve the fruit of the celestial realms.”

At that time, the noble and virtuous Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, having emerged from his own family, in order to accomplish the fruit of the supernatural knowledge of the vajra-dharmatā—the supreme siddhi of the manifest fearlessness of all Tathāgatas and all Bodhisattvas—spoke these verses on the Great Maṇḍala for Subduing All Worlds:
"I shall now explain in sequence the supreme and unsurpassed Great Maṇḍala, whose characteristics are like those of the Vajradhātu; this is called 'Subduing the World.'"
The altar is square with four gates, And four pavilions, most exquisite;
With four lines drawn according to the rules of harmony, Adorned with silken fabrics and strings of pearls.
In the various corners of that maṇḍala, as well as at the junctions of the gates,
one should adorn them with vajra-jewels set inlaid; according to the ritual, one should mark the boundaries of the outer maṇḍala,
and next, one should divide the central palace site, measuring out the four directions according to the instructions.
In the corner spaces of the gates of the second tiered altar, one should arrange lotus patterns;
divide them according to the rite using eight pillars, and lotuses with eight petals should be painted in succession.
In the center of those lotus filaments, one should place an image of the Buddha in accordance with the instructions.
"One should recite the mantra for consecrating the image according to the fundamental teaching:
'Around the Buddha, one should further draw four insignia within lotuses:
the vajra, the jewel, and the lotus; the multicolored lotus is the fourth.'"
"These great mantras are as follows:
Advancing gradually with the vajra-step, one should lay out the maṇḍala according to the ritual method in the east;
in its center, one should place the supreme lord Avalokiteśvara, endowed with all excellent colors and marks."
To the left and right of that Honored One, draw according to the ritual the Great Beings such as Vajroddhṛta;
all the Buddhas and other Great Beings should each be depicted holding the lotus gesture.
"These great vidyās are as follows:
Advancing gradually with the vajra-step, one should lay out the second maṇḍala to the south;
therein, one should paint the deity of the respective family, with an image of the Tathāgata within his crown."
To the left and right of that Honored One, one should paint all the great beings, such as Bhṛkuṭī and others,
each holding a lotus flower as their emblem, arranged in sequence according to what has been taught.
"These great vidyās are as follows:
Advancing gradually with the vajra-step, one should lay out the third maṇḍala in the west;
there, the great beings of the respective families should all be depicted seated upon lotus thrones in their proper order."
The Honored One’s attendants should be painted all around him, according to the sequence as described;
the Great Beings such as Padmaprabha and others should be arranged in accordance with the ritual order.
"These great vidyās are as follows:
Advancing gradually with the vajra-step, one should lay out the fourth maṇḍala to the north;
there, according to the ritual procedure, one should draw a four-faced lotus marked with the sign of a lotus trident."
In the positions to the left and right of that Honored One, one should paint deities such as Vajranṛtya;
each holds a lotus flower as their emblem. These great beings should be painted according to the instructions.
"These great mantras are as follows:
Advancing gradually with the vajra-step, one should arrange the various corners of the maṇḍala;
according to the ritual procedures such as the Vajralāsyā, one should paint the deities such as Padmalāsyā."
"These great vidyā-mantras are as follows:
'Advancing gradually with the vajra-step, one should arrange the divisions of the outer maṇḍala;
all four, including the lotus and incense, should be painted according to the ritual for making offerings to the noble ones.'"
"The mantras and mudrās for these offerings are as follows:
Next, within the four gates of the lotus, one should paint the four lords of Māra according to the ritual rules;
their heart-mudrās should be drawn in sequence, painted everywhere exactly as described in the teachings."
"These great mantras are as follows: Oṃ hāya-kṛi."
Vāmahe padme.

"That which is now being performed is the secret of the self-familial Lotus-Sattva; you must not rashly reveal this secret dharma to others, lest it bring about calamity and retribution."
"At the dissolution of the body and the end of life, one will fall into the great hell.
Then, have them form the samaya-mudrā and bestow this vidyā-mantra:
"Oṃ vajrapadmasamayastvaṃ. Next, have them don white garments and cover their faces with white silk; then, according to the ritual procedure, lead them into the maṇḍala and bestow this vidyā-mantra:
"Oṃ padmasamaya hūṃ. Next, having performed the *karma* as prescribed by the teachings, the face-cloth is removed.
The Ācārya takes a lotus and bestows it upon the disciple, giving this great vidyā-mantra: "Oṃ padmahasta padmadharmadhara pravaraye ti.
The disciple asks: "What is that lotus-dharmatā?"
Then the Ācārya replied in verse:
“The nature of this lotus is the very nature of desire, yet that seed-nature is fundamentally unstained.
Contemplating all things as causes of purity, one sees that the nature of sin is likewise fundamentally unstained.”
"This is the very nature of the Lotus (*padma-dharmatā*).
Thereafter, instruct them in the seal-knowledge (*mudrājñāna*) of the Lotus Family:
'Visualize the form of a lotus within the heart; contemplate the lotus appearing within the heart.'"
If even the auspicious love-attainment of Padmaśrī can be accomplished, how could that which others desire not be achieved?
Visualize the image of the Buddha upon your forehead.
By continuously contemplating according to the ritual, through the firm cause of that visualization, one swiftly attains the empowerment of union (*yoga*).
Visualize the image of the Buddha residing within the mouth; next, visualize it appearing at the tip of the tongue.
The Great Vidyārājñī of Eloquence of one’s own family is thus ever-present within the mouth.
By means of equalizing and gathering the mind, one should skillfully arrange it; visualize a lotus appearing within the crown-cakra.
Because of visualizing the lotus appearing in the crown, even those who soar through the sky will feel reverence and love.
"These great vidyās are as follows:

*Padma śrī-yaśas-mānaya hūṃ* (1); *Padma viśvagaprayaścā vaṃ* (2); *Padma sarasvatyai śuddhaye hūṃ* (3); *Padmor-dhvāṅgavakṣaku ru jaḥ* (4). Such are the seals and wisdoms of the Lotus Family (*padmakula*)."

when the Lotus Chain mudrā is bound, the desired objective will immediately increase and flourish.

"These great mantras are as follows:

through the meditative absorption of the Lotus Sattva, one becomes the supreme sovereign of the Lotus Wrathful One.
The accomplishment of Vajra Avalokiteśvara, the supreme purity of passion through the lotus,
attaining Buddhahood through the mastery of the Buddha, and the excellent accomplishment of the Vajra Lotus.
Through mastery over desire, one accomplishes sublime love; Vajra-sādhu bestows joy;
Bhṛkuṭī is wrathful yet tranquil; Padma-prabhā shines with wondrous light.
Lotus-Moon of Sublime Radiance, Vajra-Laughter of Wondrous Joy,
Supreme Accomplishment, Noble Tārā, Bestowing Great Benefit and Virtue with the Lotus-Sword.
Nīlakaṇṭha universally summons; the Great Honored One clad in white is well-accomplished;
he who freely accomplishes the lotus dance, the fearless Honored One, well bestows fearlessness.
With fierce fangs, she subdues the wicked; with the lotus-fist, she bestows accomplishment upon the practitioner.
Through Vajra-lāsyā, one attains sublime bliss; through Vajra-mālā, one bestows great wealth.
Through Vajra-gītā, one obtains wondrous sound; through Vajra-nṛtyā, one achieves sublime joy.
Exquisite fragrances, nourishing unguents, and floral adornments; With scented ointments, sublime incense, lamps, and visual offerings, one can skillfully summon the Lord Hayagrīva.
The Amoghapāśa is excellent for veneration and love; the Padma-śṛṅkhalā constitutes a great binding, while the Vajraghaṇṭā can universally awaken all.
"Furthermore, the instruction on the wisdom of the samādhi-mudrā within the Lotus Family is as follows:
'Join the two hands in the vajra-bind, With the two thumbs extended and joined inwardly;
This mudrā is named the Dharma-samādhi, Capable of bestowing the true Dharma of all Buddhas. "

Joining the two hands in the vajra-bind, with the thumbs, ring fingers, and middle fingers extended upward—this is called the Buddha’s Supreme Vidyā-mudrā; this mudrā is able to bestow the fruit of Buddhahood.
Form the vajra-bind with both hands joined; join the two middle fingers like a vajra.
This is the supreme vidyā-mudrā of Vajra; by means of this mudrā, one can accomplish the Vajra-honored One.
This very middle finger, shaped like a jewel, can bestow the accomplishment of the Vajra-jewel;
when the middle finger is tightly bent according to the ritual procedure, it can bestow the siddhi of the Lotus.
Joining the two hands in the vajra-palms gesture, one skillfully performs the various activities (*karma*) of the Vajra-multitude.
When the Dharma-vajra mudrā is joined, all samādhis are accomplished in an instant.
Forming the vajra-bind (*vajrabandha*) with the index fingers raised, this seal can bestow the accomplishment of the Buddhas.
I shall now proclaim in sequence, according to the Dharma, those most supreme seals of the great beings:
join the two hands in the vajra-palms; likewise, extend the middle fingers upright;
open the little fingers and the thumbs of each hand separately—this is called the seal of the multicolored lotus.
Then, hooking the two thumbs together, next bend the first joints of the two index fingers;
place the vajra crowns of the middle fingers upon the crown of the head—this is called the Buddha-Crown Mudrā.
Firmly form the *vajrabandha* with both hands, aligning the two thumbs pointing downward;
then, slightly bending the two index fingers, lift them upward to form the Samādhi Mudrā.
All fingers are held upright and joined together; the middle fingers are pressed close like a vajra;
the two thumbs are spread apart like two gates—this is called the Seal of Amoghasiddhi.
Firmly forming the vajra-bind with both hands, one then raises this very bind upward;
next, extending the thumbs, one forms the lotus—this is called the Lotus Buddha-Vijaya Mudrā.
First, place the two thumbs like vajras; the index fingers are like hooks or swords.
Insert the second fingers within to form the opening gesture; the middle and ring fingers are tightly bent, while all other fingers are held upright and joined together.
Next, with the index fingers grasping the [other] index fingers, perform the hook-summoning gesture of the Lotus Arrow seal.
Then, with palms joined, form the upward-facing gesture; by binding them, the "Excellent" (Sādhu) seal is completed.
This seal can perform great excellence, and is therefore named the Lotus Excellent Seal.
Firmly join the two palms together, bend the two index fingers toward the mouth, and then extend both little fingers; this is called the Lotus Frowning Brow Mudrā.
Firmly forming the vajra-bind with both hands, extend all the fingers at the heart;
as all the fingers are like a wheel of sublime light, this is called the Lotus Sunlight Seal (*padmasūryaprabhāmudrā*).
Firmly join the two palms together; next, form the two index fingers like a jewel.
Extending the arms gradually toward the crown of the head—this is called the Lotus Jewel Banner Mudrā.
Form the vajra-bond and place it upon the crown of the head; extend the index fingers toward the mouth and smile.
Because a smile appears upon one's own face, one immediately assumes the form of the Eleven-faced Honored One.
Joining the hands in the Lotus Samādhi gesture, stand the two thumbs upright and side by side.
This is named the Honored One Padmatārā; her supreme mudrā bestows all accomplishments.
This very mudrā of Padmatārā forms a lotus-sword with the index fingers bound;
through this Padma-khaḍga mudrā, the sword is established according to the Dharma of Tārā.
Firmly interlocked and curved inward like a great lotus, next apply the two thumbs according to the ritual;
finally, bend the index fingers like a great conch shell to form the Vajrabandha Wheel Mudrā.
Firmly form the vajra-palms with both hands; the right hand forms the *oṃ* seal in a coiled manner, while the thumb of the left hand is positioned as if holding a rosary.
Join the two vajra-palms together, with the left and right sides separated according to the ritual procedure.
Whirling and turning, one performs a free and spontaneous dance; in the posture of dancing, one places the Mother upon the lotus at the crown.
Firmly forming the vajra-palms with both hands, the tips of the fingers are likewise opened according to the Dharma.
Having completed the rotation, it becomes a lotus; according to the ritual, one settles the mind and makes it firm.
Firmly join both hands in the *vajra-palms* gesture; for the Secret Yakṣa, employ it according to the ritual.
Extend the fingers and palms as appropriate, with the appearance of swallowing a lotus toward the mouth.
Firmly join both hands in the *vajra-fist* gesture, concealing and gathering them by placing the backs of the two thumbs against each other.
According to the ritual, bend [the fingers] into the middle of the middle finger; this is called the Great Seal of the Lotus Fist.
Following the application of the Vajradhātu Dharma, with the vajra-palms held upright, one forms the seal of the supreme samaya-bond for all the most excellent offerings and vidyā-queens.
Firmly form the vajra-bind with both hands; next, join the two index fingers together, and finally, joining them again, bend them forward. This is called the seal of the Victorious Lord Hayagrīva.
Join the two lotus-palms together; next, interlace the two index fingers.
This is called the Supreme Seal of the Unfailing Lasso (*Amoghapāśa*).
With the index fingers and thumbs joined behind like a chain, join the two lotus-palms according to the method of the Vajra Awakening.
Press the two thumbs together; insert the little fingers and ring fingers inside.
Furthermore, the mantra for the Lotus Family’s Dharma-Wisdom Seal (*dharmajñānamudrā*) is proclaimed as follows:
*khe hṛ bhrī khe śrī śiṇi khe gati kṛ viti le sṭiri a*. Next, one should form the lotus-fist with both hands; this is the sequence for all the *karma*-seals.

16. The Chapter on the Extensive Ritual of the Lotus Secret Seal Maṇḍala, the Sixteenth. At that time, the Bhagavān again entered the samādhi called "The Empowerment Arising from the Lotus Dhāraṇī of the Dharma of All Tathāgatas," and spoke this supreme vidyā-mantra of his own family:
"Oṃ sarvatathāgatadharmasamaye hūṃ. Then, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this supreme vidyā-mantra of his own family:
"Oṃ vajrasamaye hūṃ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajragarbha spoke this supreme vidyā-mantra of his own family:
"Oṃ maṇiratna samaye hūṃ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajranetra spoke this supreme vidyā-mantra of his own family:
"Oṃ padma samaye hūṃ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajraviśvakarman spoke this supreme vidyā-mantra of his own family:
"Oṃ karmasamaye hūṃ. At that time, the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara spoke this verse concerning the maṇḍala of the samaya-mudrā of his own family:
"I shall now explain in sequence the supreme samaya-mudrā maṇḍala;
its characteristics are like those of the Vajradhātu, and it is named the Lotus Secret Dharma."
According to the ritual application of the Great Maṇḍala, one should mark out this maṇḍala in due order;
therein, one should draw exquisite lotus flowers everywhere, as well as the Sovereign of the Vajradhātu.
To their left and right, as appropriate, one should draw the mudrās of the supreme samādhis as previously described;
all the deities such as Dharmavajra and the others should be depicted according to the ritual, in union with their respective vidyās.
"These great vidyās are as follows:
'Advancing gradually with the vajra-step, one should lay out the supreme maṇḍala of various colors;
therein one should paint the Lord Padma, surrounded further by many lotuses.'"
To their left and right, one should duly arrange the lotus mudrās in sequence;
the lotus insignia should be painted likewise, for these are the self-seals of those noble deities.
"These great mantras are as follows:
Advancing gradually with the vajra-step, one lays out the second maṇḍala to the south;
there, according to the ritual, one paints the Buddha Abhiṣekavajra, upon whose crown is a great lotus."
To its left and right, one should act according to the ritual;
as previously described, they should be arranged in sequence, complete with lotus insignia, and there one should place the mudrā of the most excellent samādhi.
"These great vidyās are as follows:
Advancing gradually with the vajra-step, one should lay out the third maṇḍala in the west;
therein, one should paint a sublime lotus flower and, according to the ritual, arrange the lotus mudrā."
To its left and right, one should act according to the ritual;
following the sequence previously described, one should completely provide the lotus insignia and, as instructed, draw lotus seats in their entirety.
"These great vidyās are as follows:
Advancing gradually with the vajra-step, one should lay out the fourth maṇḍala in the north;
within the lotus, one should further paint a lotus, endowed with the radiant light of the Jvālāmālinī family."
To their left and right, one should act according to the ritual;
following the sequence as previously described, the lotus insignia should likewise be drawn, with each deity placed within its own lotus.
"These great vidyās are as follows:
'Advancing gradually with the vajra-step, one should arrange and draw everywhere the offerings to the Buddha,
the various mudrā-deities such as the lotus-hook and others, and the lotus insignias in their proper sequence.'"
The great vidyā-mantra for this lotus offering to the Honored One is: Oṃ padma.

"Having performed the extensive rituals for summoning and so forth within this samaya-mudrā maṇḍala according to the dharma, the Lotus Ācārya shall, according to the dharma, lead the Lotus disciple into the maṇḍala and confer the words of the oath: "
"You must not rashly explain this secret dharma to others; do not cause them to fall into hell in this present life and undergo various sufferings.
Having said this, he further addressed his disciple, saying:
"You should observe this maṇḍala and see what kind of radiant signs appear within it."
"Hereafter, I shall bestow upon you whichever dharma-gate of accomplishment is appropriate.
If you see white light, I shall then bestow upon you the wisdom-dharma of the supreme siddhi;
if you see yellow light, I shall then bestow upon you the wisdom-dharma of accomplishing meaningful benefit."
If you see red light, I shall then bestow upon you the wisdom-method of attraction;
if you see black light, I shall then bestow upon you the wisdom-method of subjugation;
if you see the appearance of multicolored light, I shall then bestow upon you the wisdom-method of all-accomplishing activity.

Having thus instructed so that the disciple understands, one then removes the face-cloth from the disciple; thereafter, according to their spiritual capacity (*indriya*), one should teach them the methods such as the *mudrā-jñāna* (wisdom of the seal) born of wisdom.

"As previously described, within all these maṇḍalas, such as the Vajradhātu and others, one should, according to the capacities of the disciples, select them accordingly as stated above, and then provide them with the respective instructions on mudrās and wisdom (*jñāna*) as appropriate."

The Sixteenth Part, Continued: The Extensive Ritual Manual of the Maṇḍala of the Secret Seal of the Lotus. "Furthermore, herein one should first instruct upon the seal-knowledge (*mudrājñāna*) for accomplishing the supreme siddhi.
The verse says:
"Visualize the Great Being Avalokiteśvara in all his forms as being none other than yourself;
through that visualization by means of the gateway of the Great Seal (mahāmudrā), one immediately attains the method of the supreme siddhi."
The Buddha’s Consecration Jewel Great Samādhi: Abiding in a state of meditative equipoise, perform it with firm resolve;
Visualize accordingly that you are the deity itself, And you shall attain the dharma of the most supreme siddhi.

The Great Being Padma belongs to the Lotus Family; by visualizing him as one's own self as appropriate, the method for supreme siddhi will naturally be accomplished, and one shall immediately attain firm and sublime meditative equipoise (samādhi).
Amoghasiddhi accomplishes the *karma*, spontaneously perfecting the seals (*mudrā*) that are bound;
by following the ritual procedures for whatever is sought, one swiftly attains the method of the supreme *siddhi*.
"These great vidyās are as follows:
Oṃ padmasattva hūṃ svāhā. Oṃ buddhavijaya hūṃ svāhā. Oṃ dharmasamādhi raḥ svāhā. Oṃ amoghasiddhi hūṃ svāhā. Next, one should be instructed in the mudrā and jñāna for accomplishing benefit:
One should visualize oneself accordingly, With various exquisite jewels within the mouth."
Through mastery in skillful action, the Great Seal is accomplished; what is performed once yields a thousandfold return.
Visualize yourself accordingly, taking a portion of that precious refined gold;
the supreme Great Samādhi is firmly established, and what is performed once yields a thousandfold return.
One should visualize oneself accordingly, with a sublime wish-fulfilling jewel in one's mouth;
as the venerable Avalokiteśvara is oneself, whatever is performed yields a thousandfold return.
One should visualize oneself accordingly, taking up all manner of precious jewels;
by forming the two hands into the *karmamudrā*, whatever is performed will yield a thousandfold return for every single effort.
"These great vidyās are as follows:

Oṃ padma-hilanyā-gṛhṇa hūṃ jaḥ. Oṃ padma-spharaṇa-praṇa hūṃ jaḥ. Oṃ padma-mukta-praṇa hūṃ jaḥ. Oṃ padma-sarva-ratna-praṇa hūṃ jaḥ. Next, one should instruct in the knowledge of the mudrā of attraction (vaśīkaraṇa):"
"Through the great mudrā of mastery over skillful action, one should visualize oneself accordingly;
by holding the wondrous lotus manifest before one, one shall thereby attain the power of attraction as appropriate."
Holding a firm red lotus is the seal (mudrā) of the Great Samaya;
by visualizing it upon one's own body as appropriate, one gains the love and devotion of all who are virtuous and beloved.
One should visualize oneself accordingly, and likewise hold a lotus;
with the vajra-gaze directed everywhere, all the world will be filled with devotion and love.
Employing the *karma-mudrā* according to the ritual, and holding the lotus according to its original rite,
when those two hands are moved and turned, one gains the loving devotion of all who are virtuous and beloved.
These great vidyās are as follows:
Oṃ vighnu-vaiśravaṇa-padma-hā; oṃ samaya-padma-hā; oṃ yuga-padma-hā; oṃ karma-padma-hā. Next, one should be instructed in the mudrā and wisdom of subjugation:
"One should visualize oneself as the Great Seal (mahāmudrā) of the Sovereign of Skillful Action, according to the appropriate [deity]."
When the manifest lotus is severed, that which is to be subdued is extinguished in an instant.
Firmly grasping the wondrous lotus, the seal of the supreme samādhi is just like this;
if one performs the firm destruction, that which is to be subdued perishes according to its name.
The mudrā of samādhi is joined in an exquisite manner, and holding a lotus is likewise;
when the held lotus is severed, that one who was subdued perishes accordingly.
Employing the *karmamudrā* according to the ritual, hold the lotus as prescribed by the original rite;
when one visualizes it manifesting in a wrathful form that destroys, the life of those to be subdued shall perish.
"The great vidyā-mantras are as follows: Oṃ mahā..."

Vaiṣṇavī kṛta phaṭ phaṭ. Third,
the secret seal-knowledge (*mudrājñāna*) for teaching the samādhi:
"Visualize the Lotus-Surata; when the vajra rests upon the lotus and the supreme union of the vajra and lotus occurs, Surata is purified and accomplishment is attained."
Visualize the Lotus Bhadramatī; upon the lotus is the jewel of Buddha-wisdom.
When the crown of great Buddha-wisdom is perfected as Bhadramatī, one should visualize her according to the rite for the accomplishment of the dharma.
Visualize the Lotus Bhadraḥ; with one's own lotus upon the lotus, when the lotus and the lotus are excellently joined, the pure Bhadraḥ attains accomplishment.

Visualize the Lotus Bhadra; when the skillful wisdom-vajra rests upon the lotus and the wisdom-vajra and lotus are excellently joined, one immediately attains the rite for the accomplishment of skillful action.
"These vidyās are as follows:"

“Oṃ vajrapadmasaṃyoga sādya hṛīḥ. Oṃ buddhamakuṭasaṃyoga sādya śrīḥ. Oṃ padmapadma saṃyoga sādya te. Oṃ viśvapadma saṃyoga sādya siddhi. Furthermore, the instruction on the secret great mudrā of the Padmakula is as follows:

"Pressing the fingers together to form the añjali, with the two [middle] fingers in the form of Vajra-krodha, the index fingers like a jewel and like a lotus; the vajrabandha is performed in the same manner."
Joining the two hands in the vajra-bond, raise the two middle fingers upright like tusks;
bend the left index finger as appropriate—this is called the Seal of Śākyamuni.
Place the Dharma-vajra mudrā at the heart; rotate it and place it back upon the forehead.
Place the Samādhi mudrā between the ribs, and subsequently rotate it toward the crown of the head.

Next, bind the seal of the Lord of the Vajradhātu: form the lotus gesture like a stūpa shape, with the middle fingers joined according to the original ritual; this is called the Buddha-Excellence Lotus Seal.
The thumb is like a vajra, and the index finger has the appearance of a sword and a hook;
this is named Padma-vajradhara, a secret mudrā according to the fundamental teaching.

One should then release these two thumbs; again, with the index fingers grasping the index fingers, the Seal of Sublime Love (*Mitrā-mudrā*) takes the form of an entwined coil, and snapping the fingers for "Excellent! (*Sādhu*) is likewise performed.
Firmly forming the vajra-bond with both hands, extend the two thumbs and insert them within the bond;
slightly bend the two index fingers like a gate—this is the Lotus Seal of the Honored One Bhṛkuṭī.
Then one should place this at the heart; again, form the appearance of the radiance of the solar disc.
Then, forming the bind as before, like a banner, one should subsequently extend the two hands toward the head and back.
Firmly forming the vajra-bind with both palms, bend the upper joints of those two index fingers.
Hold the lotus and sword as appropriate; with the index fingers, form the bound-lotus union.
Firmly form the vajra-bind with both hands, inserting the left thumb into the bind.
Raise the right thumb to assume the gesture of holding a staff, while the tips of all the fingers rise to form the lotus seal.
Then these same fingers are slightly bent; the little fingers and the two lotus-fingers are joined together.
The right hand should be as if holding a rosary; the right thumb and index finger are joined, and both hands firmly form the *vajrabandha*.
The little fingers and the two lotus-fingers are joined together.
Form the Lotus-Eye with the two index fingers extended, and rotate them in the proper sequence as appropriate.
Firmly form the Vajra-Bandh with both hands; join the two little fingers in the manner of a lotus.
Slightly bend the two index fingers and press them against the palms, while the two thumbs form the gesture of armor.
Then, with these two thumbs like tusks, again raise the thumbs and insert them into the binding;
these mudrās in their proper sequence have been proclaimed by me, and the mudrā of supreme samādhi is the most excellent.
With both hands joined together in the vajra-bond, the two index fingers are joined like lotus petals;
then, the two thumbs are interlaced within them—this is called the Mudrā of Secret Sovereignty.
This very same unaltered vajra-bind, with the little fingers and middle fingers joined together,
and the two thumbs like a vajra-gate, has the image of the Tathāgata within the crown.
This very same Vajra-bond, unchanged, with the thumbs and lotuses joined together;
having performed it, one then disperses them at the mouth-opening, placing the Samādhi-mudrā at both flanks.
This very same unaltered vajra-bind, with the fingers joined evenly toward the mouth,
held firm and dense according to the original ritual, has the two index fingers joined like a vajra.
This very same unaltered vajra-bind, with the index fingers joined like two lotuses,
the two thumbs hooked together as appropriate, and the two middle fingers bent and held together.
This very same unaltered Vajra-bond has the two thumbs joined in the form of a vajra;
the two index fingers are like a sword-hook, and the two little fingers are joined in the lotus gesture.
Then, forming the gesture of encircling once more, one holds the tips of the index and thumb fingers together;
when the left index finger is raised, it performs the firm and skillful rite of summoning.
Having first performed the binding of the palms together, join the index fingers and thumbs;
according to the ritual, snap the fingers to grant "well done"—this is the Lotus Joyful Mahāsattva Mudrā.
This very same unaltered vajra-bind, with the tips of all fingers joined face-to-face and the two thumbs pressed closely together, with the two index fingers raised and well-positioned,
this solar-disc gesture is placed at the heart; the lotus-banner gesture is placed upon the crown of the head.
Rotating the smiling faces toward one another’s mouths, this is the established Lotus Smile.

With palms joined, one should perform the Vajra-bond; according to that rite, using the Vajra-method, with the little fingers and thumbs as prescribed by the ritual manual, this is called the Tārā Bhagavatī Samādhi.
This very same unaltered vajra-binding, with the two index fingers grasping a lotus-flower sword,
and the palms likewise forming wheels— thus too is the mudrā for recitation.
Without altering this very vajra-binding, extend the two index fingers apart;
then, forming the binding again toward the heart, this is called the mudrā of the secret protection.
This very same unaltered vajra-bind, with the little fingers joined like two lotuses,
the index fingers firmly pressed together and slightly bent, and the two thumbs opened like the tips of tusks—
employing this fist-method as such, with the two thumbs pressed face-to-face.
This great fist of the Lotus Secret is the most excellent samādhi, well-distinguished.
One should know that the other mudrās, such as the Lotus Lāsyā and so forth, all involve joining the palms to form the vajra-bond; by means of this bond, all the mudrās are accomplished.
Furthermore, the instruction on the secret seal-knowledge (*mudrājñāna*) of the Lotus Method is as follows:

*Hraḥ* (1), *Ghraḥ* (1), *Praḥ* (1), *Haḥ*, *Saraḥ* (1), *Saḥ*, *Naḥ*, *Haḥ*, *Gaḥ*, *Vaḥ*, *Kraḥ* (1), *Dhaḥ*, *Vaḥ*, *Rāṣṭra* (1), *Muḥ*. Regarding the sequence of all *karma*-seals, one forms fists with both hands according to the ritual rules.

Chapter Seventeen: The Extensive Ritual Manual for the Wisdom Maṇḍala At that time, the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called "The Empowerment of the Lotus Born from the Dharma-Wisdom Samādhi of All Tathāgatas," and spoke this supreme vidyā-mantra of his own family:
"Oṃ dharma-samādhi-jñāna tathāgata hūṃ. Then, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this supreme vidyā-mantra born of his own family:

"Oṃ vajraratnamakuṭi hūṃ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajranetra spoke this great mantra of his own seal:
"Oṃ dharmapadme te. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajraviśvakarman spoke this great mantra of his own seal:
"Oṃ sarvamukhe hūṃ. At that time, the Noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara spoke these verses on the maṇḍala of the four seals:
"I shall now, in due order, expound the supreme maṇḍala of the four seals;
its characteristics are like those of the Vajradhātu, no different from the Great Maṇḍala."
In the center of the maṇḍala of the four seals, one should arrange the image of the Buddha according to the ritual rules;
in all the surrounding positions encircling that deity, one should paint the vajra, lotus, and other symbols.
"Having performed all the rites of summoning and so forth within this maṇḍala according to the extensive ritual procedures, lead the disciple into the maṇḍala as prescribed and say to them:
'You must not speak of this secret dharma to others indiscriminately; do not cause them to undergo extreme suffering or meet with an untimely death.'"
"Then, the teaching on the dharma for generating wisdom is as follows:
'Holding a wondrous lotus flower with both hands, single-mindedly grasping its exquisite fragrance;
with this sublime fragrance making universal offerings, having offered thus, one swiftly attains the accomplishment of Buddhahood.'"

Within the jeweled crown is the form of a Buddha; having established it with a mind in sublime meditative equipoise, for the sake of becoming a cause for the world’s veneration and affection, he manifests a lofty and exalted appearance while moving in accordance [with the ritual].
Having performed the visualization of the great image of the lotus within the *samādhi* of the mind,
one should sit according to the instructions and the ritual procedure, mentally slaying all the evil māras.
Having established lotuses at all four gates according to the ritual, hold them in one's hands;
once they are grasped, perform the act of universal awakening, and then, as taught, perform the rite of circumambulation.
The vidyā-mantras are as follows: Oṃ khadba.

one should instruct in the method of the secret mudrā-knowledge:
