through this mudrā, even dharmas difficult to accomplish will be attained in a single kṣaṇa."
"The great mantra of this samādhi is:
Oṃ sadhaya padma rāgasamaya āḥ. Next, one should be taught how to bind all the mudrās of this family, such as the Great Seal (mahāmudrā) and so forth."
At that time, the Noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara spoke this great vidyā-mantra for subduing all the world:

“Oṃ sarvārthasiddhānaya mahāsattvākāśigarbha vaiśravaṇa piśācasaṃdarśaya mama sarvasiddhyapracāra hūṃ. Having spoken this great vidyā-mantra, he then spoke these verses on the maṇḍala for subduing all the world:
"I shall now explain in succession the maṇḍala for subduing the world;
according to the ritual applications of the Great Maṇḍala, the outer maṇḍala should be drawn in its entirety."
In the central position of that [mandala], one should place a lotus flower; likewise, one should draw them all around according to the ritual rules.
All these lotuses are in full bloom, and these flowers further possess various colors.
"All the ritual applications, such as the procedures for introduction and so forth, within this maṇḍala, are exactly as described in the Extensive Ritual.
Next, the method for the wisdom that subdues all worlds shall be taught:
'Once this maṇḍala has been drawn in its entirety, one should know that it effectively subdues the world.'"
Visualize according to the ritual that the Mahāmudrā is accomplished, identical and no different from the Honored One of Skillful Action (Viśvakarman).
Next, the instruction on the secret seal-wisdom (*mudrājñāna*) for subduing the world is as follows:
"Visualize all colors within *samādhi*, with a mind in sublime meditative equipoise (*samāhita*)."
"When the lotus and vajra are joined, the maṇḍala rite attains accomplishment.

Thereafter, one is instructed in the binding of the great mudrās and other mudrā signs; all the methods for accomplishment herein, such as those involving painted images and maṇḍalas, are performed according to the ritual procedures for accomplishment based on the single-mudrā maṇḍala."
At that time, all the Tathāgatas again gathered like clouds and together praised the Noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, reciting these verses:
“Excellent, O Vajrasattva! Excellent, O Great Vajraratna! Excellent, O Vajradharmamukha! Excellent, O Supreme Vajrakarma!”
One who is able to skillfully proclaim this sublime Dharma— the unsurpassed Vajra Secret Vehicle,
the secret gateway of all Tathāgatas, subsumed within the Mahāyāna dharma of direct realization— [is a true teacher].

Chapter Nineteen: The Extensive Ritual Manual of the Great Maṇḍala of Sarvārthasiddhi At that time, all the Tathāgatas gathered once again like clouds and, having together offered praise to the Vajradhara, the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha—who had already received the jewel-consecration of all the Tathāgatas—they made this request by means of one hundred and eight names, speaking in verse:
“Ākāśagarbha, who benefits sentient beings, Mahāsattva of great radiance, Great Jewel and most excellent treasure— We prostrate and take refuge in the Vajra-Jewel.”
The Lord of Great Jewels who has received empowerment, vast, pure, and most excellent;
the body of pure wisdom and great jewels—to you, the Jewel among Jewels, I bow my head and take refuge.
Space arises from space; all space is the great space.
That very realm of space possesses all vows; I bow my head and take refuge in these supreme vows.
The hair-treasure mark born from among treasures, Is the Buddha’s hair-mark, the wondrous Tathāgata;
To all that is most sublime and every treasure, I bow my head and take refuge in that which is made of jewels.
Sublime jewel, supreme jewel, jewel of further jewels and valor, And likewise the jewel of all Tathāgatas,
the most supreme jewel of great empty space— I prostrate and take refuge in you who are equal to space.
Exquisitely adorned and most magnificent, Possessing all marks of adornment and wondrous beauty,
You who bring pure benefit and purify sentient beings— I bow my head and take refuge in your practice of giving.
The most supreme, pure, and wondrous Dharma-jewel, And the Tathāgata, who is likewise the Jewel of the Saṃgha;
To the Great Consecrated One who benefits the world, I bow my head and take refuge in the Ultimate Truth.

Generosity, vast generosity, and supreme generosity; you who are skilled in relinquishing, excellent in relinquishing, and capable of relinquishing—having extensively benefited all sentient beings, I bow my head to you, the one of great benefit and sublime welfare.
The Great Majestic Radiance of the Wish-Fulfilling Jewel King, the principle of the perfection of generosity—this is the great heroism of the Tathāgata;
I bow my head and take refuge in all the Awakened Ones.
This is the great treasure of the Tathāgata; this is the great radiance of the Tathāgata;
this is the great jewel-banner of the Tathāgata. I bow my head and take refuge in the one with the mark of the Great Laugh.
The Tathāgata, the supreme consecration, the self-consecrated one, the Great Honored One;
the most excellent and wondrous one in the world, the Honored One of the world—to the Sun of the World, I bow my head and take refuge.
The most supreme among the supreme jewels, adorned with all manner of precious things;
for the sake of the jewel-world and the great world, I bow my head and take refuge in the one named Jewel.
To Subhūṣaṇavīra and Ratnottama, Maṇivajra and Maṇiguṇa,
To the one who shines with the light of supreme jewels, I bow my head and take refuge in all jewels.
Great-bodied one, jewel-staff, Lord of Jewels, You who can fulfill all vows and aspirations,
Who have attained the perfection of all desires— I bow my head and take refuge in you, the mass of all jewels.
Possessing great majestic power that reaches to the very limit of the Peak of Existence, Capable of bestowing all aspirations through great vows,
Endowed with every form of great auspiciousness— I bow my head and take refuge in Vajragarbha.
Those who have already received the empowerment of all Buddhas— O Śāntamuni,
if anyone praises and upholds these one hundred and eight names of yours, they shall, in that very instant, extinguish all their sins.
I now entreat you, O Lord of Jewels, to excellently expound the treasury of your own precious wealth—
the supreme consecration of all Buddhas, which gives birth to the secret family of reality.

At that time, having heard the words of exhortation from all the Tathāgatas, the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha spoke this great vidyā-mantra of the empowerment of all Tathāgatas: “Oṃ vajraratna hūṃ.

Then the World-Honored One, the Great Vairocana Tathāgata, spoke this supreme vidyā-mantra of the maṇi-ratna samādhi: “Oṃ sarvatathāgataśāpaparivāraṇa mahāratna hūṃ. Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this supreme vidyā-mantra born of his own family:
“Oṃ vajraratna hūṃ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajragarbha spoke this supreme vidyā-mantra of his own family:
“Oṃ maṇi hūṃ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajranetra spoke this supreme vidyā-mantra born from his own family:
“Oṃ padma hrīḥ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajraviśvakarman spoke this supreme vidyā-mantra of his own family:
“Oṃ viśvaratna hūṃ. At that time, the Noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha entered the samādhi called “The Jewel of the Empowerment of All Tathāgatas.”

Having thus entered, from the heart of that Tathāgata there appeared the mark of a vajra-maṇi jewel, its vast radiance universally illuminating all worlds. Having performed the empowerment for all sentient beings through the empowerment-rite of all Tathāgatas, it again condensed into a single entity. That light then returned and entered the heart of the virtuous Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gaganagañja. Thereupon, from the heart of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gaganagañja, there emerged the virtuous Vajrapāṇi, whose body was entirely endowed with a treasury of blazing light and adorned with exquisite ornaments such as multi-colored vajra-mahāmaṇi jewels and empowerment jewels; he held the insignia and mudrā of the great vajra-pure maṇi jewel.

Having manifested such a body of a great bodhisattva, he extensively rained down great treasures and other things for all sentient beings in all worlds, thereby producing every kind of benefit and welfare.

Having caused all beings to rejoice, his manifested body returned once more to abide within the moon disk corresponding to the Great Vajradhātu Maṇḍala surrounding the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana. There, he remained and spoke this verse:
“O Great One, Honored among All Perfectly Awakened Ones, Treasury of all true jewels!
Within this Vajra Jewel Family of yours, You bring forth all worldly benefits.”

The Nineteenth Chapter, Continued: The Extensive Ritual Manual for the Great Maṇḍala of the Accomplishment of All Rites. At that time, the Noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha, having emerged from his own family, fulfilled all the supreme vows of all the Tathāgatas and spoke these verses on the Great Maṇḍala of the Accomplishment of All Meanings:
"I shall now, in due order, expound The unsurpassed, supreme Great Maṇḍala."
Its appearance is like the Vajradhātu; this is called the Accomplishment of All Aims.
The mandala is square with four gates, adorned with four pavilions.
Measured with four lines according to the ritual procedure, it is extensively decorated with pearl necklaces, silken streamers, and colorful fabrics.
In the various corner sections of that maṇḍala, as well as at the junctions of the gates, one should inlay vajra-jewels within them;
the lines of the outer maṇḍala are to be drawn accordingly.
Within the center of the maṇḍala, perform the rites according to the dharma;
a palace formed of the wondrous jewels of vajra, with eight pillars as excellent as the original ritual, laid out by measuring and marking according to the instructions.
The five maṇḍalas are exquisitely adorned, brilliantly illuminated by the blazing radiance of various jewels.
Surrounded on all sides by self-seals, one should install the Buddha image therein according to the ritual.
These great mantras are as follows:
"The Vajra-step emerges from the east and gradually spreads, forming the maṇḍala that fulfills all aspirations."
Within that [maṇḍala], one should paint Vajragarbha; the bestowal of jewels and the fulfillment of vows should be according to the instructions.

In all the surrounding positions of that Honored One, one should paint various jewel-seals (ratnamudrā) everywhere, and likewise paint the Great Beings (mahāsattva) according to their original rites, following the sequence as explained in the teachings.
These vidyās are as follows:
"Advancing gradually with the vajra-step, one should lay out the jewel-garland maṇḍala to the south;
therein, according to the ritual, one should correctly draw the supreme deity holding the jewel-garland."

This Honored One is surrounded by all the various positions; as taught in the scriptures, they should be drawn in successive order, with all the Great Beings fully adorned, each holding a jewel as their distinctive emblem.
"These great vidyā-mantras are as follows:
'By gradually spreading the vajra-steps, one should draw the maṇḍala of the wondrous jewel lotus therein according to the rite;
one should hold the Honored One of the wondrous jewel lotus.'"
Surrounding this Honored One in all positions, one should paint the various Mahāsattvas, fully adorned;
holding their precious insignia according to their original protocols, following the sequence as it has been taught.
"These great mantras are as follows:
'Advancing gradually with the vajra-step, one should array the Jewel-Rain Maṇḍala in the north;
therein, according to the ritual, one should paint the central deity, manifesting the appearance of raining down all kinds of jewels.'"
Surrounding this Honored One in all positions, one should paint the great beings according to their original rites,
each holding their respective precious insignia and their hand gestures in due order.
"These great vidyās are as follows:
Advancing gradually with the vajra-step, one should arrange the various corners of the maṇḍala and draw the four deities,
such as Ratnavilāsinī and the others, according to the sequence taught in the instructions."
"These great mantras are as follows:
Advancing gradually with the vajra-step, one should arrange the most excellent outer maṇḍala;
in the four corners of the outer maṇḍala, one should draw the four deities, such as the Incense Offering and so forth."
"These vidyās are as follows:
'The four gates of the maṇḍala should be painted according to the ritual with the noble protectors of the gates;
within each respective gate, the vidyās of the hook, the noose, the chain, and the bell are as follows:'"

PHAḤ ŚAḤ HŪṂ. "OṂ MAṆIPARĀMRAHĪTA HŪṂ."
The single syllable *VAM*: "Oṃ maṇiratna vai..."

The single phrase for abandoning evil: "All the *ācāryas* of the Jewel Family belonging to this great maṇḍala, having entered the maṇḍala as prescribed by the teachings and first performed protection for their own bodies according to the extensive ritual manual, shall then take the consecrated water from the Jewel flask and bestow the initiation upon the disciple of the Jewel Family.

They shall cause that disciple to form the *vajramaṇi-samaya-mudrā* and impart this great vidyā-mantra: 'Oṃ vajramaṇisamaya vaṃ. Next, they shall take a colored silk cloth and cover the disciple's face so that he cannot look out, and lead the disciple into the maṇḍala while imparting this great vidyā-mantra:"
"Oṃ hūṃ praviśa maṇirājaguhya. Having entered, he says to the disciple: 'You must not casually explain this secret dharma to others;
lest you fall into the great hells and suffer the pains of poverty throughout all your future births, failing to attain liberation.'"
Having spoken these words, he manifested the samādhi and further taught them the Mahāyāna Dharma-gate of the Samādhi of Direct Realization.
Thereafter, the Vajrācārya Ratna uttered vajra-words, looking toward the sky and asking:
"Where shall there be a vast treasure-trove?"
"How can this be attained?
At that time, the virtuous Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gaganagañja explained it all for him.
As he spoke these words, he removed the face-cloths from his disciples and allowed them all to behold the great maṇḍala.

Next, he shall further be taught the Samādhi of the Empowerment of All Tathāgatas; finally, when the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata, appears before him, the practitioner should make offerings according to his capacity, whereupon all the activities he undertakes will be accomplished.
Next, one should be instructed in the verse on the Wisdom Seal (*jñānamudrā*), which says:
“Whichever Great Seal of Vajragarbha is bound according to the ritual by means of a mind in sublime meditative equipoise (*samādhi*),
if one wishes to excavate a hidden treasure (*nidhi*) at any location, one shall see that treasure immediately at that very spot.”
If one binds the most supreme seal of samādhi, wherever that treasure-trove may be located,
as soon as the forms of these seals are joined and pressed together, that treasure-trove will spontaneously surge forth.
One should visualize the samādhi of the Honored Vajragarbha with a mind in sublime meditative equipoise;
wherever one knows there is a hidden treasure according to one's will, that very place shall be where the treasure resides.
If one forms the seal accomplished through the ritual procedure (*karmavastu*) and abides in the *vajragarbha-samādhi*,
when this seal universally awakens all, hidden treasures shall be seen in every place.
"These great mantras are as follows:
'When the great mudrā is joined according to the ritual, and this seal is wrapped around the body,
wherever a treasure store may be located, one should know that it is manifested from one's own samādhi.'"
If one binds the most supreme samādhi-mudrā, one should perform the awakening and clear revelation;
wherever treasures may be located, all the adornments of great jewels shall be obtained.
If one binds the samādhi mudrā, the Wisdom itself speaks upon being awakened;
by declaring that a treasure-trove exists in a certain place, one obtains all the adornments of great jewels.
If one binds the great seal-mudrā of the ritual action (*karmamudrā*) through the practice of the awakening samādhi,
when the two hands are bound together with one another, hidden treasures will appear wherever they may be.
"These great mantras are as follows:
'If one binds the Great Seal according to the ritual, even if doubt arises in accordance with that,
when one understands it through wisdom as being like the mind, a treasure-trove will naturally appear in that place.'"
Wherever a doubt arises, one should immediately bind the seal of the supreme samādhi;
when this seal is subsequently released, a hidden treasure will manifest at that very spot.
Bind the samādhi-mudrā according to the ritual; wherever doubt arises, one will attain certainty.
When the time comes that it is known to have arisen from wisdom, there shall always be hidden treasures in every place.
If a hidden treasure should arise in a place of doubt, one should form the *karmamudrā* at that spot;
when the mudrā is formed according to the instructions, the hidden treasure will clearly manifest.
"These great mantras are as follows:
'When the great mudrās of one's own family are joined together, and one seeks out various hidden treasures (terma) while traveling,
if one awakens according to the ritual at a particular place, then a hidden treasure shall manifest at that very spot.'"
Bind that supreme samādhi mudrā and seek out the various hidden treasures (nidhāna) wherever you go;
when the mudrā is firmly established at a location, a hidden treasure will manifest there.
Having bound that samādhi mudrā, one should seek out all hidden treasures (nidhāna) while traveling;
wherever wisdom arises, there the treasure will manifest.
Forming the seal accomplished through that ritual action (*karma*), one should search for hidden treasures (*nidhi*) wherever one goes;
wherever the ritual action seal wavers, there a hidden treasure will manifest.
The great vidyās are as follows:
Oṃ mahāmaṇiratna parīkṣa viśa. Oṃ ratnasamaya dṛḍha dṛśaya. Oṃ ratnaparikṣa jñāna viśa. Oṃ maṇigraha pramocaya. Next, one should be instructed in the secret mudrā-vidyā:
"Joining the lotus and the vajra, One seeks out all hidden treasures (nidhi) according to the practice."
When one visualizes the Great Seal (Mahāmudrā) according to the ritual, one will universally awaken to and obtain the hidden treasures (nidhi).
By binding that supreme samaya-mudrā, even the beloved ones will likewise be won over.
Wherever the mudrā is firmly established, there the hidden treasures shall manifest.
The lotus and vajra joined together, seeking all hidden treasures (terma) wherever one goes;
when visualizing the wisdom seal (jñānamudrā) according to the ritual method, the treasures shall manifest at that very moment.
Form the *karmamudrā* according to the ritual: join the lotus and the vajra.
When that mudrā shines brilliantly wherever it is placed, treasures will manifest in that very spot.
"These vidyā-mantras are as follows:

Oṃ mahāmaṇisamudgaviśa | Oṃ samayasamudganiḍhūmivāva | Oṃ nityajñānaviśa viśasamudga | Oṃ sarvakarmasaṃbhṛtasamudga | Thereafter, one should instruct in all the mudrās and jñāna-dharmas within the Mahāratnakula."
Regarding what was previously taught as that method of the Great Seal Wisdom (*mahāmudrājñāna*):
"In the center of the Maṇḍala of the Sublime Moon, practice according to the drawn forms;
when one meditates upon the Great Seal according to the ritual, all supreme benefits will be accomplished."
Next, the functions of all the great mudrās are explained:
"By binding the Buddha-mudrā, one attains Buddhahood; the Vajragarbha-mudrā brings excellent accomplishment;
the Supreme Jewel Hook-mudrā can summon everywhere; that Jewel Love-mudrā always bestows excellent love."
The Ratnamudrā of Joy is ever-joyful; through the Ratnavilokita, one gathers great wealth.
The Ratnamālāmudrā performs excellent consecration; the Ratnārcismudrā bestows majestic splendor.
The Ratnadhvajamudrā grants whatever is desired; the Ratnahāsāmudrā is able to accomplish beneficial aims.
The Dharma-Jewel Seal constantly bestows the sublime Dharma; through supreme renunciation, one shall obtain the highest benefit.
The Jewel-Sword Seal produces great sharpness and utility; the Jewel-Wheel Seal serves as the sovereign lord.
The Sublime Jewel-Speech Seal is the gateway to accomplishment; it can turn forth a great mass of wealth like a rain of jewels.
The Jewel Offering Mudrā performs excellent offerings; The Jewel Armor Mudrā provides firm protection;
The Jewel Tusk Mudrā gathers all precious wealth; The Jewel Fist Mudrā accomplishes all siddhis.
"Next, the method for the wisdom of the samaya-mudrā within this great maṇḍala is explained:
'That mudrā formed from the vajra-jewel can bestow the empowerment of all mudrās;
when one binds the Great Vajra-Jewel Mudrā, all vajra-jewel activities are accomplished.'"
With the two hands performing the vajra-activity, one attains the great wealth of the Vajradhara Lord;
this very thumb, like a vajra, rests at the heart and is able to bestow all manner of precious jewels.
Binding the index fingers tightly forms the Jewel-binding; one obtains the bestowing of wealth from the Honored One Avalokiteśvara.
With the two hands forming the Great Jewel Banner of Skillful Action, one is able to bestow the Vajra-karma Jewel.
Raising the two index fingers and bending them back, join the two thumbs like a vajra;
this is called the Supreme Jewel of the Vajradhātu, and by this seal, one attains the Buddha-jewel.
This which is taught is the Vajraratnamudrā; it is the mudrā of the Honored One Vajragarbha.
By binding this mudrā according to the ritual, one obtains the Great Vajraratna.
Join the two hands in the mudrā of the precious vajra; extend the two middle fingers upward like tusks.
Forming this seal according to the rite in the center, one obtains the great empowerment for both oneself and others.
Then, with these same middle and ring fingers, as well as the little fingers, join them tightly together according to the rite.
This is called the Heart Seal of Avalokiteśvara; this seal is able to bestow all manner of wealth and treasures.

According to the ritual application of the Vajra-Ratna, join the index fingers, thumbs, and little fingers together, with the two middle fingers likewise joined, while the ring fingers are extended upward like tusks.
With both hands firmly forming the vajra-bind, bend the two index fingers into the shape of a jewel;
extend the thumbs with their faces as prescribed by the original ritual. Placing this at the heart, one can bestow all accomplishments.
Join the two hands in the vajra-bond gesture; join the two middle fingers so they resemble a jewel.
This mudrā is named the Jewel Banner; it can bestow great maṇi jewels.
To employ this same gesture as a hook, bend the two index fingers and join them together.
This mudrā summons all wealth; the maṇi-jewel hook is likewise. Again, from this, one assumes the posture of heroic power:

grasping the right index finger with the left index finger like an arrow, one summons and shoots according to the original ritual procedure, thereby summoning worldly objects of veneration and affection.
Then, again, perform the "Excellent" (Sādhu) mudrā: join the index finger and the thumb together;
while not altering the joined thumb, likewise join the tips of all the other fingers together as well.
Furthermore, bind the two thumbs within and form the two index fingers like eyes;
this mudrā is named the Precious Gaze. Having gazed with it, one can gather all manner of wealth and profit.
Then, joining the faces of these two thumbs together, form the mudrā and place it at the heart;
this is called the Garland of the Accomplishment of All Meanings, and this mudrā can bestow self-consecration.
Place both hands in the *ratnāloka* (Jewel Light) gesture with the palms resting at the heart; this seal can bestow great majestic light.
Extend the ring fingers and place them at the crown of the head; this is called the Seal of the Vast and Supreme Banner (*viśāla-vijaya-dhvaja-mudrā*).
Then, again assuming the gesture of great laughter, one performs a playful circumambulation according to the ritual;
this mudrā is named the Great Jewel Laughter, and the gesture of laughter can attract all wealth and profit.
The tips of the fingers are like precious lotuses; through the dharma of samādhi, all wealth is gathered.
By binding these index fingers within, this mudrā can bestow a great accumulation of riches.
Aligning the two thumbs and pointing them downward, stand the two index fingers upright in the shape of jewels.
This sword mudrā gathers all wealth; it is the great, swift blade that valiantly subdues the world.
Forming the supreme vajra-bond wheel, join the two thumbs together and insert them within the bond;
the two index fingers are then formed like jewels. This is called the mudrā of the Universal Bestowal of the Turning Wheel.
Then, joining the faces of these fingers together, this mudrā is held level and upright;
because they are joined in this manner, the Vāg-mudrā is accomplished, whereby one gathers all wealth and profit through one's own teaching.
One should form the Great Vajra Jewel Seal; this seal can rain down all manner of jewel-showers.
When the fingers are spread apart according to the rite, it rains down all kinds of wealth and treasures everywhere in the four directions.
One should form the Great Vajra Jewel Seal; at the crown of the head, one should perform the gesture of whirling dance.
When making offerings as prescribed by the teaching, one should universally offer all kinds of precious jewels.
Forming the seal of the Accomplishment of All Meanings, join the hands at the neck according to the ritual;
this is called the Jewel-Binding Seal, which serves as armor for excellent protection.

This very seal of all-accomplishment, with the gesture of devouring placed at the mouth, is said to be the Jewel Tusk according to the original ritual; it strikes terror and gathers all wealth and profit.
With both hands firmly forming vajra-fists, bend the two index fingers according to the rite;
holding the two thumbs like a gate, this jewel-fist mudrā bestows accomplishment.
The mudrās for making offerings to the various supreme samādhis all rely upon the methods of the Vajradhātu mudrās;
according to the ritual procedures of the Jewel Dharma as they have been taught, these supreme samādhi mudrās are thus distinguished.
The two middle fingers should be formed like a jewel; one should distinguish them well in this manner.
All ritual procedures, such as the single hook and others, will bring all *karmas* to fulfillment.
Furthermore, the wisdom of the various Dharma-mudrās of this Great Jewel Family (*Mahāratnakula*) is proclaimed as follows:

*traḥ*, *graḥ*, *triḥ*, *hrīḥ*, *śrīḥ*, *e*, *raḥ*, *haḥ*, *de*, *de*, *kriḥ*, *vaḥ*, *riḥ*, *caḥ*, *jyaḥ*, *aḥ*. Now, within this family, one should form the Jewel Fist (*ratnamuṣṭi*), by which all *karmamudrās* are accomplished.

Chapter Twenty: The Extensive Ritual Manual for the Maṇḍala of the Jewel Secret Seal. At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the Samādhi of the Birth of the Jewel Empowerment through the Totality of the Dhāraṇīs of All Tathāgatas’ Empowerment, and spoke this Great Mantra of His Own Seal:
“Oṃ vajraratna sūdi pe hūṃ. Then, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this Great Mantra of His Own Seal, which gives birth to his own family:
“Oṃ vajra-viśva-karmāra-viśvakarma-samaye hūṃ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajragarbha spoke this great mantra of his own seal:
“Oṃ vajra-ratna-viśva-ge hūṃ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajranetra spoke this great mantra of his own seal:
“Oṃ vajra-dharma-viśvakarma-m. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrakarmakara spoke this great mantra of his own seal:
“Oṃ ratnaviśvagabhojya-samaye hūṃ. At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha spoke this verse concerning the maṇḍala of the samaya-seal of his own family:
“I shall now explain in sequence the supreme maṇḍala of one’s own seal;
its characteristics are like those of the Vajradhātu. This is called the Jewel Secret.”
Relying on the ritual application of the Great Maṇḍala, one should mark out the various maṇḍalas in their proper sequence;
therein, according to the original rite, one should draw the mudrās of the Buddhas everywhere throughout.
In front of the Vajradhātu, one should further paint [the deities] seated in the precious cross-legged posture according to the ritual rules:
in the south, the Jewel-Garland; in the west, the Jewel-Lotus; and in the north, the Jewel and those surrounded by jewels.
These vidyās are as follows:
“The Vajra-step emerges from the east and spreads forth;
in the center of the Sarvasiddhi-maṇḍala, one should draw the Vajraratna according to the ritual, as well as the Great Vajramani.”
In all those surrounding positions, one should draw various mudrās joined with jewels;
according to their sequence and in accordance with the ritual protocol, the Jewel Ācārya should draw them everywhere.
"These great mantras are as follows:
Advancing gradually with the vajra-step, one should lay out the second maṇḍala to the south;
therein, one should paint a precious jewel, and paint two eyes, complete and perfect."
In all those surrounding positions, according to the sequence taught in the instructions,
draw the jewel insignia in their entirety and completeness, and everywhere draw the primary mudrās.
"These great vidyās are as follows:
Advancing gradually with the vajra-step, one should lay out the third maṇḍala in the west;
therein, according to the ritual procedure, one should draw precious lotuses all around."
In all those surrounding positions, according to the sequence taught in the instructions,
draw the jewel insignia in their entirety and completeness, and draw the fundamental mudrās throughout.
"These great mantras are as follows:
'Advancing with the vajra-step toward the north, one should draw the fourth supreme maṇḍala;
in its center, depict the sign of the rain of jewels according to the ritual, fully complete with vajras and jewels.'"
Around the perimeter, further draw the karma-mudrā; each and every one must be exactly as described in the teachings.
Draw the precious insignia according to the ritual procedure, following the proper sequence for all their respective positions.
"These great vidyā-mantras are as follows: Oṃ ratna..."

HŪṂ (one syllable). Having performed all the ritual applications within this precious secret maṇḍala according to what is taught in the instructions, one leads the disciples of the respective family into the maṇḍala and says to them:

"If there are those who know other teachings, you must not hastily explain this secret dharma to them; do not cause them to undergo the suffering of great poverty, nor to fall into the hells after the end of their lives."
"Then, for their sake, he taught the Dharma born from the wisdom of the Jewel Samādhi:
'Entering the Vajraratna Samādhi, one visualizes a vajra-jewel being drawn in space;
placing that jewel between one's own brows, once the visualization is complete, one becomes a sovereign. "
When you bind the mudrā of the supreme samādhi, visualize a vajra-jewel being drawn in the sky;
placing that jewel upon the site of empowerment, through this visualization, you immediately obtain the jewel empowerment.
Entering the samādhi of the Great Dharma Jewel, one visualizes a vajra-jewel being drawn in space;
by placing it according to the rite upon the site of the Wisdom Jewel, and having so visualized, one becomes a great Lord of Dharma.
According to the ritual, one should bind the karma-mudrā;
visualize a vajra-jewel being drawn in the sky, and place that jewel within one's own position. Having visualized this, one attains the status of the Karma-lord.
"These great mantras are as follows:
'One should visualize the binding of that great mudrā, with the Great Vajra Jewel appearing within the heart;
having visualized that jewel according to the original ritual, one immediately attains the supreme empowerment method.'"
With a mind in sublime meditative equipoise, one should visualize a vajra-jewel at the space between the eyebrows;
by forming the jewel-vajra mudrā according to the ritual, one will attain mastery wherever one dwells.
Entering the Vajraratna Samādhi, visualize the vajra-jewel at the tip of the tongue;
contemplating with a mind of truth according to the original ritual, one immediately attains the rank of the Dharma King through empowerment.
With a mind of sublime meditative equipoise, one should visualize a vajra-jewel at the crown of the head;
by forming the karma-mudrā according to the ritual procedure, one immediately accomplishes the activities of the Sovereign.
"These great mantras are as follows:
Having visualized and painted the image upon the cloth according to the ritual, one’s own body is the Vajraratna;
by meditating on the Great Seal (*mahāmudrā*) as taught, one immediately attains the state of a sovereign siddha."
Having painted the image on the banner according to the ritual manual, it is itself the unsurpassed Vajra Jewel;
by visualizing the Lord Sattvavajra, one immediately attains mastery over all samādhis.
Having painted the mandala cloth image according to the ritual manual, one’s own body is itself the Vajra-jewel;
by visualizing the mudrā of thought according to the instructions, one will certainly become a lord among dharmas.
Having painted the image on the cloth according to the ritual manual, it is itself the unsurpassed vajra-jewel;
by visualizing the accomplishment of the karma-mudrā, one immediately attains supreme mastery over karma.
These great mantras are as follows:
"Whatever gold or silver jewels there may be, Visualize them as becoming vajra-jewels;
The same applies to those made of other jewels. By visualizing them appearing in the heart, one receives empowerment."
Whatever gold or other jewels there may be, they are none other than the unsurpassed vajra-jewel;
by visualizing them according to the ritual method appearing between the eyebrows, one immediately obtains the great wealth and treasures of a king.
Whatever gold, jewels, or other precious things there may be, visualize them as the Vajraratna;
by visualizing them according to the rite within one's mouth, once this visualization is complete, one attains mastery over speech.
Whatever gold or other jewels there may be, visualize them as the Vajraratna;
by visualizing them according to the rite upon the crown of the head, one immediately attains the status of the Lord of All Karmas.

"These great mantras are as follows: Oṃ vajraratna hṛdaya parāṇa hūṃ. (1) Oṃ vajraratna viśoka mahārtha-praṇata. (2) Oṃ vajraratna vajrasādhi. (3) Oṃ vajraratna mahākarmapate. (4) Next, the secret mudrā-knowledge method of the Ratnakula Samaya is taught: "
"Visualize the great vajra-jewel according to the ritual; that jewel is the gateway of birth.
Having entered, one shall achieve the Great Seal (Mahāmudrā); by visualizing accordingly, one will obtain accomplishment."
The mudrā of the seal of the most supreme samādhi treasure—this supreme samādhi is the very gateway of birth.
Once that seal is bound, one accomplishes the dharma and receives empowerment in all places.
According to the ritual, bind the Great Vajra-ratna; visualize the dharma-mudrā as it should be.
That jewel is the gateway of birth; having visualized it, one shall attain supreme accomplishment.
Bind the Jewel Seal of Karma according to the ritual; that seal is itself the gateway of birth.
Having bound it as taught, one immediately accomplishes the unsurpassed, supreme mudrā of Karma.
The vidyās for these are as follows:
Oṃ mahā-siddhi; oṃ samaya-viśvagha-siddhi; oṃ dharma-siddhi; oṃ karma-siddhi. Next, the great mudrās for all within this maṇḍala are explained:
Form the "jewel-vajra-fang" with the index fingers; the middle, ring, and little fingers [are joined].
Joining and extending them according to the original rite, one attains supreme accomplishment by placing them upon the crown of the head.
Joining the two palms in the vajra-bind, hooking the two index fingers together,
with the thumbs and ring fingers like a vajra, one receives empowerment by rotating them at the space between the eyebrows.
Relying on the ritual application of that Jewel-Vajra, join the upper joints of the index fingers like a gateway;
by rotating this mudrā, one shall obtain the supreme empowerment rite.
Relying upon the ritual application of that Dharma-vajra, one should join the thumbs and index fingers and rotate them toward the space between the eyebrows;
thus, one immediately obtains the sublime empowerment of the Great Dharma.
Joining the two hands in the Karma-vajra mudrā, rotate them according to the rite between the eyebrows;
this immediately forms the garland of all consecrations, and having placed it there, one shall obtain the great consecration.
The Samādhi of the Supreme Seal of the Birth of Jewels arises from the Vajradhātu;
by forming it like the jewel-mark and placing it between the eyebrows, one immediately attains the great empowerment.
Hook the two thumbs together; next, join the two index fingers, and let the index fingers form a jewel-gate.
By forming this mudrā, one attains the Great Vajra Jewel.
Joining the two palms in the vajra-bind, then again extending them fully in the jewel-fist,
with the two middle fingers shaped like jewels— one thereby attains the empowerment of the Jewel Garland.
Joining the two palms in the vajra-bind, form the shape of a jewel with the two middle fingers;
extending the index and ring fingers while keeping them apart, one forms the lotus gesture and attains accomplishment.
Furthermore, form the shape of a jewel with the two middle fingers, while all the other fingers are raised upward;
if one visualizes the method for the Jewel Seal in this manner, one will immediately obtain an assembly of excellent and wondrous retinues.
Join the two palms together in the vajra-bond; join the middle fingers and thumbs together, while the ring fingers and little fingers are each extended upward.
Placing this seal at the mouth, one shall obtain jewels.
Then, with this index finger like a vajra, one forms the hook gesture with the index finger;
the index finger grasps the index finger in the shape of an arrow, and finally, with palms joined, one bestows joy.

Furthermore, form the shape of a jewel with the two middle fingers; make the two index fingers slightly bent, and place the two ring fingers inside like a gate. Then, cover [the hands] inwardly with the two thumbs;
this is the solar disc (*sūryamaṇḍala*), which is rotated clockwise. Extending the arms, one places them back upon the crown of the head.
Forming precious necklaces and excellent banners and pennants, they subsequently join together and scatter from the place of the smile.
With both hands joined in the *vajrabandha*, the thumbs and ring fingers facing upward, one should visualize this mudrā as having the form of a lotus;
furthermore, the two middle fingers are like precious [jewels].
This same little finger in the *varada* (boon-granting) gesture forms the seal for the application of the Vajra-sword;
this same seal is then transformed into the Vajra-wheel, which subsequently disperses from the edge of the mouth.
Forming the vajra-tooth mudrā with the thumbs while extending all the other fingers, one should place this seal at the crown of the head;
it will immediately cause a rain of all manner of precious jewels to fall.
This is the application of the Vajra Jewel Dharma: settle the mind upon the jewel-mark and guard it well;
form the thumb like the shape of a jewel tusk, while the middle fingers are joined to form a fist.
"Furthermore, the general teaching on the methods for the Samādhi-Seal Wisdom (*samayamudrājñāna*) is as follows:
'All these great seals (*mahāmudrā*) are joined together by means of the Vajra-Bond (*vajrabandha*);
through the secret and most secret sequence they are accomplished, and one shall attain fourfold accomplishment.'"
As taught in the Vajra Secret, one should not form mudrās at improper times;
I shall now further explain the gateway of the Dharma-mudrās, and their sequence should be as follows.

Abiding in samādhi, one should paint according to the ritual instructions the image of Vajragarbha on a banner-cloth and so forth;

Abiding in samādhi, one should paint according to the ritual instructions the images of Vajragarbha and others upon a cloth;
through meditative absorption, one seeks the various karmas, thereby obtaining the speech of the deity and the accomplishment of activities.
"These great mantras are as follows:
'Whether in the sky or in other directions, one should visualize with a mind of sublime meditative equipoise that noble Great Being Ākāśagarbha;

Whether in the sky or in any other direction, one should visualize with a mind of sublime meditative equipoise that noble Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha; thus, the wondrous jewels sought will be produced.
Whether in the sky or in other directions, one should visualize with a mind of sublime meditative absorption the Honored Great Being Ākāśagarbha;
thus, the sought-after True Dharma will be attained in its entirety.
Whether in the sky or in any other direction, one should visualize with a mind of sublime meditative equipoise that noble Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha;

"These great mantras are as follows:
'Visualize Vajragarbha within the mind, and contemplate him with a mind in sublime meditative equipoise;

Visualize Vajragarbha painted upon the forehead, likewise contemplating him clearly according to the ritual;

Visualize Vajragarbha appearing within the mouth, likewise contemplating it clearly according to the ritual method;
if one visualizes the mouth opening, one will attain the speech-empowerment bestowed by the deity.

Visualize Vajragarbha appearing within the crown of the head; by arranging [the visualization] according to the ritual and contemplating it with focused attention, if light should manifest from the crown, one will immediately attain the power to travel through the air.
"These great mantras are as follows:
'One should visualize the Great Seal of Vajragarbha with a mind in sublime meditative equipoise;
by praying for the gateway to the attainment of accomplishments, one shall immediately achieve the *elī* jewel-siddhi.'"

The Samādhi Seal of the Honored One Ākāśagarbha: Binding it according to the Dharma with a mind of sublime samādhi, I pray that you grant me the gateway of requested empowerment; Thereby one immediately attains the Mīli-ratna empowerment.
One should visualize the samādhi of the Honored Vajragarbha with a mind of sublime meditative equipoise;
by praying, "Grant me the gateway to the sought-after True Dharma," one immediately attains the sublime Dharma of the *cīrī* jewel.

The supreme *karmamudrā* of Gaganagañja, when bound according to the ritual with a mind of sublime meditative equipoise, shall grant all sought-after jewels; thus one attains the accomplishment of the *kīli* jewel.
"These great vidyās are as follows:

Whether in the void or in other directions, one will always attain the supreme methods of accomplishment.
By uniting the lotus and the vajra, visualize them as the Vajragarbha;
by visualizing them painted with exquisite beauty according to the ritual, one immediately receives the empowerment bestowed by the deity.
The lotus and vajra are joined together; visualize them as the Vajragarbha.
That which is beloved will become well-loved, and all the world will be filled with respect and affection.
The lotus and vajra joined together— visualizing this as the Vajragarbha,

Chapter Twenty-Two: The Extensive Ritual Manual for the Karma Maṇḍala. At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the samādhi called "The Empowerment Born from the Consecration Karma of All Tathāgatas," and spoke this supreme vidyā-mantra of his own family:
“Oṃ sarvatathāgataguhyavijaye hūṃ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this supreme vidyā-mantra of the arising of the karma of his own family:

Regarding the single phrase for abandoning evil: "All ritual applications within this maṇḍala must be performed according to the extensive procedures. Having acted thus, one should lead the disciples of the respective family into the maṇḍala in accordance with the dharma.

Once they have entered, one should say to them: 'You must not casually explain this secret dharma to others; do not cause the establishment of such heavy karmic obstructions that you might swiftly meet your end.'"
Then, he taught the verse on the wisdom of the Jewel *Karma-mudrā*,
saying: “The great seal (*mahāmudrā*) of Vajragarbha, Bound according to the rite with a mind of sublime meditative equipoise (*samādhi*),
This seal universally performs all offerings, And one thereby attains the loving-kindness of all Buddhas.”
By correctly forming once the mudrā of all supreme samādhis, the essence of samādhi,
one makes offerings to all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and immediately attains the precious empowerment of one’s own family.
One should visualize the samādhi of the Vajragarbha Honored One with a mind of sublime meditative equipoise;
making offerings to all the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, one becomes supreme in subduing the world.
With the samādhi of the Vajragarbha Honored One, one should form the seal accomplished through karma;
by making offerings to all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, one attains all benefits and purposes in an instant.
“The great mantras are as follows:
Oṃ ratnapūjā-vāk-kuru. Oṃ ratnapūjā-samaya-viśodhaya. Oṃ ratnapūjā-dharmanāśaya-pati. Oṃ ratnapūjā-karma-sarva-ṛddhi-nidhana. Next, the secret mudrā-karmajñāna-dharma is explained:”
“By uniting the lotus and the vajra, through the samādhi of the Honored One Vajragarbha,
one makes offerings to all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and attains the love and respect of all the world.”
"Then, as previously described, one immediately attains the supreme accomplishment of the Great Seal Wisdom (*mahāmudrājñānasiddhi*).
Next, the method for the Samaya Seal Wisdom (*samayamudrājñānadharma*) is taught:
'Joining the great vajra-jewels together, they should be arrayed according to their respective positions.'"
In accordance with the Vajra-activity rites, one should proceed according to the sequence taught in the instructions.
Next, the wisdom of the mudrās of this family is explained:

*Ṭaḥ* (one syllable), *Jaḥ*, *Gaḥ*, *Dhaḥ*, *Tanaḥ*; *Jaḥ*, *Tuḥ*, *Smaḥ*, *Rimaḥ*; *Kṣaṇaḥ*; *Tuḥ*, *Shaḥ*, *Rimaḥ*; *Kṣa*, *Kṣa*, *Ti*. One should form the Vajra-ratna with both hands; thus are formed all the karma-mudrās of this family.

23. The Section on the Vast Doctrine of Appropriate Expedient Means for the Ritual Procedures of the True Gathering of All Tathāgatas, Part One of Twenty-Three. At that time, the Bhagavān again entered the *ratnamudrā-samādhi* and spoke this supreme vidyā-mantra of his own family:
"Oṃ vajra-ratne traṃ. Then, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this vidyā-mantra of his own seal:
"Oṃ vajramāle hūṃ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajragarbha spoke this great vidyā-mantra of his own seal:
"Oṃ maṇiratne hūṃ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajranetra spoke this great vidyā-mantra of his own seal:
"Oṃ dharmaratne hūṃ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajraviśvakarman spoke this great vidyā-mantra of his own seal:
"Oṃ viśvamūrti ṭṭhi. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha spoke this verse concerning the four-seal maṇḍala of his own Jewel Family:
"I shall now, in due order, expound The supreme four-seal maṇḍala;
Following the ritual procedures of the previous four-seal altar, I shall distinguish the characteristics of this altar accordingly."
"Then, having entered the maṇḍala as prescribed by the instructions, one says to the disciple:
'You must take care never to speak of this dharma and so forth rashly.
Next, one provides the instruction on the method for the arising of wisdom:"
"Joining the great vajra-jewel mudrā, abiding in the Vajraratna-samādhi,
and placing the seal upon the forehead, one immediately attains all methods of accomplishment."
This great vidyā-mantra is as follows:
“Oṃ vajraratna sarvaviśoka sarvasiddhodyami prayaccha rā rā rā rā hūṃ traḥ. Next, the method for the secret mudrā is explained and demonstrated:
“Whether it be those beloved by the world or those who are exceptionally dear, whether male or female, it is likewise so.”
Forming the seal by joining the hands at the forehead, one immediately attains the accomplishment of the secret dharma.
This mantra of accomplishment is as follows:

Oṃ vajraratna-satkṛtya dhāraya pratyakṣīkuru kṣaṇam abhiṣiñca he hā hā hā hātra. Then, according to the instructions as taught, one should perform the binding of those four types of mudrās and likewise effect those four types of accomplishments.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Gaganagañja further spoke this great mantra for the accomplishment of all purposes (*sarvārthasādhana*):
“Oṃ vajramaṇidhara sarvatrātistambhi prayaścāhuḥ | bhagavān vajraratna hūṃ ||” Next, he spoke this verse concerning the maṇḍala:
“I shall now further proclaim the supreme and unsurpassed great maṇḍala.”
Relying upon the maṇḍala of the Accomplishment of All Aims, one should draw it completely according to the ritual procedures as previously described.
Next, the secret wisdom-mudrā wisdom method is taught:
"By not abandoning any of the objects of the five desires, such as form and so forth, one experiences all forms of bliss."
By offering this to the Buddha, the World-Honored One, one immediately achieves success in all ritual procedures.

Regarding the dharmas of the four kinds of mudrās and wisdom: having painted them according to the rules within the left lunar maṇḍala using such items as the aforementioned scroll-painting and the seals of the Mahāsattvas, one should perform the activities for the accomplishment of whatever is sought.
At that time, all the Tathāgatas gathered once more like clouds and together praised the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gaganagañja, speaking these verses:
“Excellent, O Vajrasattva! Excellent, O Great Vajraratna! Excellent, O Vajra Dharma-gate! Excellent, O Supreme Vajrakarma!”
One is able to skillfully proclaim this sublime Dharma, the unsurpassed Vajra Secret Vehicle,
the secret gateway of all Tathāgatas, which is subsumed within the Mahāyāna dharma of direct realization.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the vast doctrinal system of the Great Reality Dharma of all the families:
"In this regard, one should first explain in general the doctrinal system for the supreme accomplishment of the Great Mudrā. The verse says:
'All the great mudrās of the Tathāgatas, When bound, pervade the entire realm of space.'"
The images of all Buddhas are established and formed, entering from the heart and becoming vast.
If there is anyone who, in this present life, seeks the supreme dharma of peace,
there is nothing superior to this method of accomplishment, other than the attainment of Buddhahood itself.
Next, the teaching on the supreme accomplishment of the various mudrās of the Tathāgata family is explained.
The verse on the Great Seal (Mahāmudrā) says:
“The Great Seal is joined according to the ritual method; this is what the Honored Great Being has taught.”
I follow all the traces of the teachings, visualizing through the methods of the Great Being.
If there are those who, in this present life, desire to seek the supreme and virtuous fruit of a bodhisattva,
and for whom no other means exists besides their own person to accomplish the task— for them, this method of accomplishment is unsurpassed.
The *Sādhana-vidhi for the Supreme Accomplishment of the Samaya-mudrā*:
"Just as in the *sādhana* of Vajradhara, I likewise perform this visualization;
there is no Buddha or Bodhisattva external to this. This *sādhana* is superior to all others."
The *Dharmamudrā-paramasiddhi-tantra*:
"All speech that is pure by nature is what is taught as all phenomena;
there is nothing outside of this for accomplishing buddhahood, and no means of accomplishment superior to it."
The *Karmamudrā-uttamasiddhi-tantra*: "All things are pure in every respect, and all activities are likewise pure.
Apart from the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, there is nothing else; this method of accomplishment surpasses all others."
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the instructional principles for the supreme accomplishment of this own family (*kula*):
"First, the instructional principles for the supreme accomplishment of the Great Seal (*mahāmudrā*):
'For the benefit of all sentient beings, the Buddha-wisdom has established various skillful means of accomplishment.'"
By meditating according to the ritual, one becomes the Great Seal (Mahāmudrā) and attains Buddhahood in this very life.
Regarding the "Instructional Principle for the Supreme Accomplishment of the Samaya Seal":
"Just as in the Vajradhara Sadhana, I likewise perform this visualization."
The Great Seal (Mahāmudrā) is accomplished according to the ritual method; in an instant, one attains the stage of a Bodhisattva.
Regarding the instructional principle for the supreme accomplishment of the Dharma Seal (Dharmamudrā):
"All phenomena are fundamentally without letters; therein, conceptual proliferation (prapañca) does not exist."
This teaching is the supreme Dharma-gate; Through meditative visualization, one attains the stage of a Bodhisattva.
The Ritual Seal (Karmamudrā) of Supreme Accomplishment:
"Whatever activities are performed, Whether they be pure or impure within this [practice],"
"By offering all of this to the Buddha, the World-Honored One, one attains the rank of a bodhisattva in a single instant.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the supreme siddhi-tantra of the Lotus Family:
"First, the supreme siddhi-tantra of the Great Seal (mahāmudrā) is explained:"
“The nature of the dharma of greed is fundamentally pure; external phenomena ultimately do not exist.
Within this, even the dharma of being free from greed does not exist—this is what is accomplished within the Mahāyāna.”
The *Sādhana-vidhi for the Supreme Accomplishment of the Samaya-mudrā*:

"The practice consists of the mind of great compassion; Through the application of the firm method of samādhi, In accordance with the vast teachings as they were taught, One attains the rank of a Bodhisattva in a single instant."
The Dharma Seal of the Supreme Accomplishment Teachings:
“The nature of desire is primordially pure; This teaching first proclaims this.
Through the perfection of desire, one attains fulfillment, And in an instant, achieves the rank of a Bodhisattva.”
The *Karmamudrā-paramasiddhi-tantra*: "Whatever is seen or heard, and likewise whatever is perceived or known—
may I and all sentient beings always bring them entirely to the end of suffering."
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the teaching on the supreme accomplishment of the Ratnakula:
"First, the teaching on the supreme accomplishment of the Great Seal (mahāmudrā) is spoken:
'I have been consecrated by all the Buddhas; therefore, I have attained the state of Vajragarbha.'"
And this visualization, being universally devoid of intrinsic nature, Enables one to attain the rank of a Bodhisattva in a single instant.
The Instructional Principle for the Supreme Accomplishment of the Samādhi Seal:
"May all sentient beings attain this, So that all their wishes and desires are completely fulfilled."
Equal and without distinction from the Honored One Ākāśagarbha, one attains the stage of a bodhisattva in a single instant.
Regarding the supreme teaching and principle for the accomplishment of the Dharma Seal:
"Having completely relinquished one’s own body, one should then joyfully bestow precious wealth."
The adornment of speech through the seal of preaching the Dharma allows one to attain the rank of a bodhisattva in this very life.
Regarding the instructional principles for the supreme accomplishment of the *karma-mudrā*:
"If one wishes to benefit those who are poor, the production of wealth and jewels is supreme."
Beyond the diligent seeking of the Bodhisattva, there is nothing else; that method of accomplishment surpasses all others.
"The above constitutes the various mudrās of all the families, which attain the vast scriptural principles of the supreme accomplishment of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas."
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the instructional principles for the accomplishment of the samādhis of all families:
"First, the instructional principles for the accomplishment of the samādhis of all Tathāgatas are explained in general:
'If one is conjoined with the state of passionate attachment, that very passion is itself purified.'"
This is the Great Seal Gate (Mahāmudrā) of all Buddhas; it is called the Wisdom Samādhi.
Regarding the *Tathāgatakula-samayasiddhi-tantra*:
"If one does not abandon the cravings of desire, that itself is the sublime principle of samādhi."
This is the gate of purity of the Tathāgata family; even the Buddhas do not dare to transgress it.
Regarding the "Vajra Family Samādhi Accomplishment Doctrine":
"The Buddhas originally possess no wrathful mind; they manifest wrath for the sake of benefiting sentient beings."
In this Dharma-gate of the Great Vajra Family, there is no transgression of samādhi.
Regarding the "Teachings on the Accomplishment of Samādhi in the Lotus Family":
"By means of that wisdom of intrinsic purity, one should perform whatever tasks are to be done as appropriate."
In this Dharma-gate of the Great Lotus Family, there is no one who transgresses the samādhi.
Regarding the "Teaching on the Accomplishment of the Samādhi of the Jewel Family":
"Whether things are few or many in nature, the same applies to the dharmas according to whatever one desires."
The daily practice of unerring activities is itself the bestowal of samādhi.
"The above constitutes the doctrinal principles for the samādhis of all families."
Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva Mahāsattva proclaimed the instructional principles for the accomplishment of the dharmas of all families:
"First, the instructional principles for the accomplishment of the dharmas of all Tathāgatas are explained in general:
'In this regard, there is no dharma that the Buddha can speak; once there is nothing to speak, it is the very nature of things (dharmatā), the syllable.'"
This is the Great Seal Gate of the Buddha-dharma; it is the supreme dharma of great wisdom.
Regarding the "Teachings on the Accomplishment of the Tathāgata Family Dharma":
"The purity of passionate attachment is unsurpassed; herein, one constantly bestows the bliss of all dharmas."
This is the sublime Dharma-gate of the Tathāgata family, the supreme activity for the accomplishment of karma.
Regarding the instructional principles for the accomplishment of the Vajra Family’s dharmas:
"The pure meaning of the Buddhas’ commands, and likewise their benefit in delivering sentient beings."
"From within the absence of anger, wrathful fury arises; by destroying all evil māras, one attains accomplishment.
The *Sādhana-nyāya* for the Lotus Family:
'The lotus dwells in defilement yet remains undefiled; likewise, the nature of desire is without attachment.'"
This teaching states: "If one knows that external objects do not exist, even if one commits various transgressions, there will be no defilement.
The *Ratnakula-dharmasiddhi-tantra* says:
"In the practice of impartial giving, there is no [grasping at] phenomena; the same is said regarding the conduct of reality."
There is nothing outside this Dharma of the Jewel Family that can surpass those methods of accomplishment.
Thus concludes the doctrinal principles for the accomplishment of the Dharmas of all the Families.

The Twenty-third Part, Section Two: The Vast Doctrine of Expedient Means Corresponding to the Ritual Procedures for the True Gathering of All Tathāgatas. Furthermore, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the doctrine for the accomplishment of the *karma* of all families:
"First, the general doctrine for the accomplishment of the *karma* of the Tathāgatas is stated in verse:"
"All sentient beings shall all attain Buddhahood, Or likewise become Bodhisattvas;
According to the ritual procedures as taught, One can bestow the supreme accomplishment of *karma*."
The *Tathāgatakula-karmasiddhi-tantra* states:
“Having arranged the four kinds of supreme offerings, And likewise the four kinds of corresponding rites,
One should perform the ritual procedures according to the four seasons To accomplish the activities of *karma-siddhi*.”
The Ritual for the Accomplishment of Karma in the Vajra Family:
"To destroy malevolent sentient beings, One should perform even those acts that follow unwholesome dharmas.
This ritual procedure of karma in the Vajra Family Is able to grant all supreme accomplishments."
*The Ritual Manual for the Accomplishment of Karma in the Lotus Family:* "To all who are terrified,
grant fearlessness; As the Dharma taught in the scriptures likewise says,
This ritual manual for the karma of the Lotus Family Can bestow the accomplishments of all Buddhas."
The *Ratnakula-karmasiddhi-tantra*: "By bestowing the jewel initiation according to the ritual, All supreme aspirations are fulfilled;
So it is for all Buddhas and all sentient beings, Accomplishing every activity of karma."
“The above constitutes the instructional principles for the accomplishment of the *karmas* of all families.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the instructional principles for the accomplishment of the wisdom of the *dharmatā* of all families:
“First, the general instructional principles for the accomplishment of the wisdom of the Tathāgata’s *dharmatā* are as follows:”
"In the *Vajrasattva-samādhi*, the *dharmatā* of all Buddhas abides;
by means of this very wisdom, one becomes a Buddha-Bhagavān—apart from this, no other Buddha can be found."
The *Tathāgatakuladharmatājñānasiddhinaya*:
“By visualizing the Great Seal (*mahāmudrā*) according to the ritual method, one can accomplish all matters of siddhi;
this is the dharma-gate of the Tathāgata family, which bestows the supreme accomplishment of that dharmatā.”
The *Vajrakula-dharmatājñāna-siddhi-tantra*:
"By binding the supreme mudrā of samādhi according to the ritual, one can accomplish all karmic activities;
by relying on the fundamental ritual of that great mudrā, one immediately attains the supreme Vajra accomplishment."
The *Padminī-kula-dharmatā-jñāna-siddhi-tantra*:
"Whatever dharma-mudrās are the fundamental applications, When the dharma-mudrā is turned according to the ritual procedure,
This is the sublime gateway of accomplishment, Which is the vajra-dharma of dharmatā."
The *Ratnakula Dharmatājñānasiddhi-tantra*:
"By means of the ritual application of that *karmamudrā*, place the *karma-vajra* at the heart;
by visualizing in this manner, the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) is accomplished, and one immediately attains all supreme activities (*karma*)."
"The above constitutes the instructional principle for the accomplishment of the wisdom-seals (*jñāna-mudrā*) of the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) of all families.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the instructional principle for the accomplishment of the wisdom-seals of all families:
"First, the general instructional principle for the accomplishment of the Tathāgata’s wisdom-seal is as follows:"

"The samādhi of Vajrasattva, through the supreme application of the pure moon-vajra dharma, should be known to manifest according to various forms and signs; likewise, it manifests according to signs within the world."
One should know that the supreme wisdom within purity is pure; its characteristic is white and radiant.
Within defilement, it manifests as a wrathful body, appearing in accordance with various forms and characteristics.
The *Tathāgatakulajñānamudrāsiddhitantra*: "By joining according to the Great Seal (*mahāmudrā*), the sublime radiance of the moon maṇḍala,
if one understands it in accordance with its own function, one likewise knows the intentions of the entire world."
The *Vajrakula-jñāna-mudrā-siddhi-tantra*:
"Whether in the sky or in other directions, wherever the wrathful maṇḍala appears,
if one contemplates it with such characteristics, that very intention will be fully understood."
The *Padminī-kula-jñāna-mudrā-siddhi-tantra*:
"Visualize subtle syllables arranged in rows, appearing within the expanse of space;
know them in succession according to their various forms and characteristics, as those very signs manifest from the mind."
The *Ratnakula-jñānamudrā-siddhi-tantra*:

"One should thoroughly examine all worlds; if they possess such characteristics of resistance and obstruction, one should likewise observe them as having those very characteristics, until the mind of the world is fully understood."
Because this mind is thus conjoined with such [objects], within it there is both going and coming;
if there is movement within what is produced, the perceived signs likewise appear accordingly.
All individual sentient beings, with minds of meditative equipoise, universally visualize;
what each perceives is likewise so, and they fully awaken to all such mental states.
"This is the Vajradhara Dharma-gate taught by the Buddha.
The above constitutes the instructional principles for the accomplishment of the Wisdom-Seals (jñāna-mudrā) of all families.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the instructional principles for the wisdom of the accomplishments of all families:
First, the general explanation of the scriptural principles for the Tathāgata’s accomplishment of wisdom is stated as follows:
“Through the application of the sublime dharma empowered by the Great Being, one should visualize one’s own body as the very image of the Buddha.
If one accords with this wisdom in such a manner, one shall immediately attain the supreme accomplishment of Buddhahood.”
The *Tathāgatakulasaṃpattijñānopadeśa*:
"Whether in the sky or in other directions, A maṇḍala of yellow-white light appears;
Within it, the body of the Great Being with his own mudrā Is clearly and brilliantly visible."
The *Vajrakula-siddhi-jñāna-naya*: "If such images appear, one should accordingly visualize them as black;
this is the supreme door of accomplishment for the Vajra Family, through which all that is desired is swiftly attained as wished."
The *Sādhanajñānanirdeśa* of the Padmakula:
“That very sky of wondrous blue, Within which the form of a lotus appears— This is the mudrā and vidyā of the Great Padmakula; It accomplishes and gives birth to such dharmas.”
The Jewel Family’s Wisdom of Accomplishment Scripture:
Whether in the sky or in other directions, That very space is pure and stainless;
From it, garlands of light gradually emerge and expand. Having seen this, one swiftly attains the methods of accomplishment.

The great beings such as Vajrasattva, with the wondrous radiance of the moon maṇḍala, manifest their holy bodies according to the directions as appropriate; at the time of accomplishment, they arise from their own physical forms.
“Thus above is the teaching on the wisdom of accomplishment for all families.
Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva Mahāsattva proclaimed the teaching on the accomplishment of the wisdom of supernatural powers for all families:
‘First, the general teaching on the accomplishment of the Tathāgata’s wisdom of supernatural powers is as follows:’”
"In the *Vajrasattva-samādhi*, one should visualize the manifestation of all the bodies of the Tathāgatas;
likewise, one should visualize all the Bodhisattvas and so forth, and the appearance of their various bodies is also thus."
The *Tathāgatakula-ṛddhijñānasiddhi-tantra*: “The Great Mudrā of Vajrasattva,
Bound according to the rite with a mind of sublime meditative equipoise (*samādhi*),
When one practices accomplishment by means of this method, One immediately attains the five types of supernormal powers (*abhijñā*).”
Regarding the supernormal knowledge of the divine eye (*divyacakṣurabhijñā*) and so forth:
"When the Great Seal (*mahāmudrā*) is joined according to the ritual method, the visual consciousness arises therein;
at whatever time one observes with it, even that which is extremely distant can be seen."
"This is the Dharma-gate of Vajrasattva spoken by the Buddha:
'By joining the Great Seal according to the ritual method, the auditory consciousness arises therein;
all matters follow one's thoughts, and one can hear even from the furthest reaches.'"
"This is the Dharma-gate of Vajrasattva spoken by the Buddha:
'When the Great Seal is joined according to the ritual method, the mental consciousness arises therein;
whenever one contemplates it in accordance with the various sentient beings, one is able to fully know their minds and intentions.'"
When the great mudrā is joined according to the ritual, if one can observe the signs— whether of oneself or another—
one will know that person’s mind, and all events from past lives will manifest.
"This is the gate of the Vajra-hand methods taught by the Buddha:
'By joining the Great Seal according to the ritual, one may perform miraculous feats as desired;
whether in this place or in all directions, they can all be manifested through a mind of sublime meditative equipoise.'"
"This is the Dharma-gate of the Great Bodhicitta taught by the Buddha.
The *Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Vajra Family’s Supernatural Wisdom*:
'All the supreme mudrās of Trailokyavijaya should be bound according to the ritual, with the mind in sublime meditative equipoise.'"
When one practices accomplishment based on this dharma, one immediately attains the five kinds of supernormal powers (*abhijñā*).
Manifesting all those wrathful activities according to the sequence taught in the instructions,
and through the application of methods such as the divine eye and wisdom, one accomplishes all supernormal powers in an instant.
"This is the Dharma-gate of Vajrasattva spoken by the Buddha.
The *Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Supernatural Wisdom of the Lotus Family*:
'The supreme mudrā for subduing the world should be joined with a mind of sublime meditative equipoise.'"
When one practices accomplishment based on this dharma, one immediately attains the five kinds of supernormal powers (*abhijñā*).
According to the methods of passionate attachment as they are taught, and following the sequence of the instructions, one likewise accords with the dharmas such as the divine eye and wisdom;
thus, one is able to accomplish the matters of supernormal power.
"This is the Dharma-gate of Avalokiteśvara spoken by the Buddha.
The *Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Wisdom of Supernatural Powers of the Ratna Family*:
'That seal of Sarvārthasiddhi, one should bind according to the ritual with a mind of sublime meditative equipoise.'"
When one practices accomplishment based on this dharma, one immediately attains the five kinds of supernormal powers (*abhijñā*).
One performs all offerings to the Buddhas, following the sequence as taught;
through the application of dharmas such as the divine eye and wisdom, one is able to perceive the five kinds of supernormal powers.
“This is the Dharma-gate of Ākāśagarbha as taught by the Buddha.
The above constitutes the instructional principles for the accomplishment of the supernormal knowledges (*abhijñā*) of the various families.
Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva Mahāsattva proclaimed the instructional principles for the accomplishment of the true pledges (*samaya*) of the various families:
"First, the general explanation of the Tathāgata’s true precepts for accomplishing the principles of the teachings is as follows:
'Once one has correctly followed the truth as it is, One should utter words of solemn pledge according to the instructions;
This is the great, true, and well-guarded ritual, By which one swiftly attains the fruit of Buddhahood.'"
“This is the Dharma-gate of awakened wisdom taught by the Buddha.
Regarding the *Tathāgatakula-tattvasamaya-siddhi-naya*:
‘Now, this samādhi-dharma of the pledge was born from the Tathāgata family.’”
The vajra-reality gate of excellent protection; through this, one swiftly attains supreme accomplishment.
This is the Dharma-gate of the Vajradhara taught by the Buddha.
The *Vajrakula-tattva-samaya-siddhi-śāstra*:
“The Vajradhara’s swift vow and injunction: once performed, none shall dare transgress it.
This gate of the true samādhi well-protects; according to one's desire, supreme accomplishment is attained.”
“This is the Vajradhara-dharmaparyāya spoken by the Buddha.
Regarding the *Siddhi-tantra* on the True Samaya of the Lotus Family:
‘Once the samaya rites of the royal law have been performed, the supreme and most excellent of the Great Lotus Family [is attained].’”

The gate of the true samādhi that well protects, Through which one attains supreme accomplishment according to one's desires. "This is the Dharma-gate of the Vajra Dharma taught by the Buddha. The *Ratnakula-tattva-samaya-siddhi-naya*: The gate of the true samādhi that well protects, Through which one attains supreme accomplishment according to one's desires.
"This is the Dharma-gate of the Jewel Family taught by the Buddha. The *Ratnakula-tattva-samaya-siddhi-naya*:
"Having performed the excellent vows and precepts as offered to all Buddhas, none dare to transgress them;
this is the supreme, true, and well-guarded gateway, through which one obtains the great empowerment."
“This is the Dharma-gate for making offerings to the Buddha as taught by the Buddha.
The above constitutes the principles of the teaching for the accomplishment of the true pledges of all families.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the principles of the teaching for the accomplishment of the true samādhis of all families:
"First, the general teaching on the principle of the true accomplishment of the Tathāgata’s samādhi is stated as follows:
'Reciting "Samayas tvam," all mudrās emerge from within one's own family;
by binding them firmly according to the ritual procedure, there is no rite to be performed that will not be accomplished.'"
"This is the Dharma-gate of the True Reality of the Great Samādhi spoken by this Buddha.
Regarding the *Tattvasiddhi-śāstra* of the Samādhi of the Tathāgata Family: 'By reciting *sūradasatvaṃ*, all mudrās are accomplished.'"
"Because that which is bound by oneself is accomplished, this is the true speech of the Great Being.
This is the Dharma-gate of the True Reality of the Great Samaya spoken by the Buddha."
The *Vajrakula-samaya-tattva-siddhi-naya*:
"When one utters the syllable HŪṂ once according to the ritual, all mudrās follow their proper sequence;
therein, through the gateway of self and other mudrās, one binds them for oneself and likewise causes others to bind them."
The *Lotus Family Samādhi-Truthful-Accomplishment-Śāstra*:
"When reciting 'Sarvadhātu,' whether for oneself or for others, the birth-gates and so forth are joined in accordance with the practice; one does not abandon this at any time or place."
The *Ratnakula-samaya-tattva-siddhi-naya*:
"By performing the accomplishment of the syllable Oṃ in this manner, all mudrās are accomplished in their proper sequence;
likewise, all that is supreme in the world is spontaneously accomplished as this sublime offering."
“Thus concludes the *tantra* of the true accomplishment of the samādhis of all families.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *tantra* of the accomplishment of the mudrās of all families:
“First, the general *tantra* for the accomplishment of the Tathāgata mudrās is as follows:”
"The Buddha-seal is joined in accordance with the Dharma; One should contemplate the Tathāgata, And swiftly accomplish the gateway to *siddhi*, Abiding eternally in the Bodhi of all Buddhas."
The *Tathāgatakulamudrāsiddhitantra*:
"Having bound the Great Seal (*mahāmudrā*) of Vajrasattva according to the ritual, one should perform visualization before Vajrasattva; thus, one will swiftly attain that supreme *siddhi*."
The Vajra Family Seal Accomplishment Doctrine:
“Having bound that supreme samaya-mudrā, In the vajrasattva-samādhi, one should visualize the venerable Vajrasattva within; Thus, one attains the method of twofold accomplishment.”
The Ritual for Accomplishing the Mudrā of the Lotus Family:
"Having bound the mudrā produced by that dharma, one should visualize the noble Lord Avalokiteśvara within the samādhi of the Honored One Avalokiteśvara; thus, one attains a twofold accomplishment."
The *Ratnakula-mudrā-siddhi-tantra*:
"By joining the *karmamudrā* according to the ritual, One enters the samādhi of the Honored One Vajragarbha;
Visualizing the holy deity Vajragarbha within, One attains the method of twofold accomplishment."
"The above constitutes the ritual principles for the accomplishment of the seals (*mudrā*) of all families.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the ritual principles for all the methods of accomplishment of the various families:
"First, the general explanation of the ritual principles for all the methods of accomplishment of the Tathāgatas:"
"One should dwell before the Buddha oneself, And practice the visualization of the Buddha-remembrance samādhi;
By universally binding all mudrās to completion, One attains that method of accomplishment in an instant."
"This is the Dharma-gate of awakened wisdom taught by the Buddha.
Regarding the ritual procedures and principles for all accomplishments of the Tathāgata family:
'If one performs the accomplishment of all mudrās, one should perform this visualization according to whatever one desires.'"
Through union with the method of Vajra-recitation, one can accomplish all supreme siddhis.
This is the Dharma-gate of Vajrasattva spoken by the Buddha.
The Ritual Manual for All Accomplishments of the Vajra Family:
"The vajra image is one's own body; with a mind in sublime meditative equipoise, one should perform visualization.
If all mudrās are bound and perfected, accomplishment will be attained in an instant."
"This is the Dharma-gate of the Firmness of All Tathāgatas, spoken by the Buddha.
Regarding the ritual applications and principles for all accomplishments of the Lotus Family:
'The lotus image is one's own body; according to the rite, one should visualize it as one's own body.'"
The gateway to the accomplishment of the adornments of all wisdoms; this is the ritual application of the Great Lotus Family.
This is the Dharma-gate of Avalokiteśvara spoken by the Buddha.
The scriptural principles for the ritual applications of all accomplishments of the Jewel Family:
"Visualize yourself according to the ritual manual, appearing as a mass of radiant flames from mani-jewels;
this is the gateway to the accomplishment of all offerings, the sublime application of the Great Ratna Family."
“This is the Dharma-gate of Ākāśagarbha spoken by the Buddha.
The above constitutes the principles and applications for the rites of accomplishment of all the families.
