Having offered oneself as service and worship, one should recite these four great vidyās as follows: "Oṃ sarvatathāgatapūjopasthānāya... (1)
*Ātman-niryātaya me | Sarvatathāgatavajrasattva-tiṣṭha svāhā || Oṃ sarvatathāgata-prayojanavigrahāya ||*
*Atma-nir-yātaya mi sarva-tathāgata-vajra-ratna-viśodhaya.* *Oṃ sarva-tathāgata-pūjā-pravartanāya.*
Ātman-nir-yātaya me | Sarva-tathāgata-vajra-dharma-pravartaya māṃ || "Oṃ sarva-tathāgata-pūjā-karmani... (1)
Ātman-niryātaya me | Sarvatathāgatavajrakarmakuru me || 4 "Subsequently, one may enjoy all desired foods and drinks according to one's will without any restriction;

however, for the sake of seeking the accomplishment of one's own mind, one should contemplate with focused attention the image of the Buddha within one's own body. Then, reciting the heart-mantra (*hṛdaya*) with *vajra*-speech according to one's desire for eight hundred times, one will swiftly attain accomplishment as requested."
"This is the Dharma-gate of Vajrasattva spoken by the Buddha.
If one wishes to seek the method for that supreme siddhi, the practitioner should, according to the ritual, arrange the painted image of the World-Honored Tathāgata within the cloth painting (paṭa)."

Next, one should follow the ritual application of the maṇḍala of those four great beings (*mahāsattva*), adorning it with whatever colors and forms one prefers; therein, one should paint the four great beings seated within moon discs, and in the four corners of the cloth, paint the noble beings (*ārya*) of their respective families.
Having thus completed the painting, the practitioner should extensively arrange offerings before that painted image, as prescribed in the instructions.

After reciting with a focused mind for four full months, one should then recite throughout the entire night until dawn; at that time, one will immediately attain the supreme *siddhi* methods of the reality of all Tathāgatas.
"This is the Vajradhara Dharma-gate taught by this Buddha.

If one wishes to seek the accomplishment of those mudrās, the practitioner should, before the painted image, bind the Sarvātathāgatasattvavajra-mudrā; according to their inclinations, they shall attain whatever accomplishment they seek."

If one does not understand this seal as it is taught, one should recite the great mantra with vajra speech one hundred thousand times; thereafter, one should recite it throughout the night with a focused mind.

When one becomes fatigued, one should rest for a short while; then, according to the ritual procedures of the original rite, one should resume the recitation until, at last, a blazing light appears and an awakening verbal manifestation arises. Thereafter, the practitioner releases the previously bound mudrā and immediately attains mastery over invisibility in whatever form one desires, being able to accomplish all activities whatsoever.
In the midst of binding all mudrās, one shall achieve all accomplishments as described.
This is the Vajradhara Dharma-gate taught by the Buddha.
"If one desires to seek the accomplishment of samādhi, one should first visualize the subtle vajra."

Thereafter, if there is a gateway of samādhi that one finds pleasing, one should practice the preliminary rites with the corresponding heart-mantra for a full four months; thereafter, throughout the entire night, one should remain sitting upright in the lotus posture, with a straightened mind, withdrawn, and tranquil.
When the following morning arrives, one will immediately attain the manifestation and perfect fulfillment of all samādhis, such as those of the Tathāgatas.
Thereafter, one will achieve accomplishment in whatever dharmas one desires.
"This is the Dharma-gate of Vajrasattva spoken by the Buddha.
If one wishes to seek the accomplishment of *karma*, one should likewise recite according to the ritual for one month, aspiring with a focused mind toward accomplishment."
However, if one recites [the mantra] throughout the final watch of the night, one will immediately attain all *karmasiddhi* (accomplishments of activity).
Next, the various rites for accomplishment shall be explained.
Any practitioner who, according to the ritual, recites the Great Mantra (*mahāvidyā*) even once, will be able to protect their own and others' provinces, cities, and villages.

"If one wishes to create various emblems to awaken and bring about accomplishment, the practitioner should bind the armor mudrā; these various emblems may be smeared with gośīrṣa sandalwood incense, or they may be accomplished even without being smeared."
These are the hand-mudrās of the vajra, hook, arrow, jewel, sun disc, banner with rows of teeth, lotus, conch, wheel, tongue, activity (karma), mace, armor, fangs, and fist.
These various signs and marks, when produced according to the ritual, are all capable of awakening [the practitioner].

If one wishes to empower an object or image for accomplishment, one should, according to the ritual, take a peacock’s tail to make a whisk (*cāmara*), pierce its center with a vajra to form a hole, and bind it with colored thread.

The practitioner binds the Sattvavajra mudrā, holds the whisk that has been prepared, and recites the root mantra while performing empowerment according to the rite; until all Tathāgatas awaken him through their mudrās, he shall behold various signs within the whisk.
From this point onward, that peacock-feather whisk will manifest all manner of forms and appearances within the body of the practitioner according to the ritual method.
Furthermore, if one empowers this peacock-feather whisk once and moves it over the body, one will immediately be able to manifest all manner of forms and appearances.
“Furthermore, this whisk can manifest all the worldly activities that are like illusions.

Moreover, this whisk can manifest the images of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, as well as all the Tathāgatas throughout all Buddha-fields in the ten directions, together with their assemblies, the subduing of Māra’s armies, and so forth—all the miraculous feats of a Buddha’s supernormal powers it can manifest; even the physical majesty of a Buddha’s body, complete with all its marks, it can fully manifest.”

Furthermore, if one wishes to achieve the accomplishment of *vaśitā* (mastery over others' affection), the practitioner should bind the *sarvatathāgatasattva-mudrā* and recite the mantra according to the rite; when the light of that mudrā becomes intensely radiant, the dharma-accomplishment is attained.
From this point forward, at the very moment one binds the aforementioned seal, all Tathāgatas will appear before one to perform acts of loving-kindness; how much more so for other rites!

Furthermore, if one desires to seek the supreme mundane accomplishment (*laukika-siddhi*), the practitioner should recite the mantra according to the ritual rules. Having completed one month of reciting eight thousand times, one should then bind the seal and recite throughout the entire night until the seal blazes with intense light, at which point the rite is accomplished.
From this point forward, if one binds the aforementioned seal, one shall attain the supreme worldly accomplishment of a Vidyādhara.
This is the Dharma-gate of Vajradhara taught by the Buddha.
"Thus concludes the ritual procedure for the accomplishment of the activities of the Tathāgata family.
From the *Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha-mahāyānābhisamaya-mahākalparāja*, spoken by the Buddha, Volume Twenty-Eight."
The Great King of Tantras of Samādhi, Scroll Twenty-Nine.

Translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Imperially Appointed Grand Officer of the Court of State Ceremonial, Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, Great Master of the Transmission of the Dharma, and Purple-Robed Śramaṇa Subject Shi Hu, et al., by Imperial Decree. Section Twenty-Six, Part Two: The Supreme Doctrine and Principles of the Ritual Procedures for the Authentic Compendium of All Tathāgatas. "Furthermore, the ritual procedures for the accomplishment of the activities of the Vajra Family are proclaimed."

"Regarding this, once the practitioner has completed the preliminary practices according to the ritual, they should then recite the mantra for one hundred thousand times (*lakṣa*) in accordance with their desired objective for accomplishment."

Once the count is complete, by reciting throughout the night until dawn, one attains the accomplishment of the dharma and becomes capable of performing all that is to be undertaken for the gathering of sentient beings and all that is to be performed for their training.
"This is the Vajradhara Dharma-gate taught by the Buddha.

Furthermore, if one wishes to perform the rite of accomplishment (*sādhana*), one should paint a cloth-scroll (*paṭa*) according to the ritual rules, install it as prescribed, and perform offerings. Thereafter, the practitioner shall enjoy all desired objects according to their will; subsequently, whatever accomplishment they seek according to their inclination, they should recite the Great Mantra with the Vajra-speech daily according to the ritual rules for a period of one month, completing eight thousand recitations."

After one month has passed, one should again arrange offerings before the painted image; the practitioner shall then bind the Great Seal of Trailokyavijaya and, according to the ritual, recite the great mantra throughout the night until that seal spontaneously emits the sound of the syllable *HŪṂ*.
When dawn arrived, Maheśvara and the other lords of the gods, together with their retinues, appeared before him. The vidyādhara then addressed them, saying:
"O gods, you have come here; as I have spoken, I pray that you grant me your labor, and that whatever I seek may be brought to fulfillment."
The gods and others replied:
"Whatever you desire, we shall grant it all to you.

From that time forward, the practitioner immediately becomes the sovereign who exhausts the entirety of the three realms; according to his will, in a mere instant, he can cause the entire three realms to tremble, and furthermore, he can gather them into a single mass and completely bring about their formation and destruction.

Within the three realms, they are able to enjoy all subtle and exquisite objects of pleasure; in all their actions, they attain mastery, and even all the celestial lords and other such beings of exquisite love comply with their every wish, so that none among them cause them any affliction or disturbance.

At that time, if the vidyādhara utters the syllable HŪṂ, all those most malevolent deities and others will immediately fall; thereafter, the vidyādhara’s lifespan shall reach a full hundred thousand kalpas.
"This is the Vajradhara Dharma-gate taught by the Buddha.

Furthermore, if one wishes to seek the accomplishment of the mudrā, one should recite according to the instructions for a full month. Thereafter, the practitioner shall bind the Vajra Trailokyavijaya Samādhi-mudrā and recite throughout the night until dawn; at that time, the accomplishment of the mudrā will be attained."

From this point forward, as taught, whenever one performs the mudrās while simultaneously uttering the syllable *HŪṂ*, the practitioner will be able to travel through the sky, manifest various forms, and become invisible; they will be able to perform feats of illusory transformation, carry out all activities of awakening, summoning, and magnetizing, cause all beings to experience great joy, seize all precious treasures before them, manifest vast and blazing majestic light, rain down a great shower of jewels, and display a laughing countenance, thereby purifying all sentient beings everywhere.
It is capable of severing or shattering all things, and can further transform time and circumstances as appropriate; according to what is suitable, it can initiate all discourse on ultimate truth.

It can transform all phenomena, provide excellent protection, restrain and prohibit, terrify and slay; furthermore, it can seal and sustain all sentient beings and serve as their source of play and joy.

One who is able to bestow the empowerment of all-giving is able to cause all bodies to spontaneously break into song, to cause them to whirl and dance while summoning and drawing them in, and to cause them all to remain bound by fetters; all such activities as these can be performed.
"This is the Vajradhara Dharma-gate taught by the Buddha.
If one wishes to seek the accomplishment of subtle and wondrous wisdom, the practitioner should rely upon the Vajra Trailokyavijaya Samādhi to initiate it as a preliminary practice."
Next, one should perform the recitation according to the ritual procedures for mantra-recitation for one month, with the resolve to attain accomplishment.

After the month has passed, one should rely on this very samādhi method and recite throughout the night until dawn; thereby, one will attain the five wisdoms and supernormal powers (*pañca-abhijñā*), and be able to perform all acts of gathering in and disciplining sentient beings as required.
"This is the Vajradhara Dharma-gate spoken by the Buddha.
If one wishes to seek the accomplishment of karma (*karmasiddhi*), one should likewise recite according to the ritual for one month to seek accomplishment."
After one month has passed, if one recites throughout the entire night until dawn, one will immediately attain the accomplishment of all *karmas*.
From that time forward, when performing any *karma*, by reciting [the mantra] once, one will be able to accomplish all *karmas* according to one's wishes, such as providing protection and so forth.
“This is the Vajradhara-dharmaparyāya spoken by the Buddha.
The above constitutes the ritual procedure for the accomplishment of activities of the Vajra Family.
Next, the ritual procedure for the accomplishment of activities of the Lotus Family is proclaimed.”

"The practitioner, having first completed the preliminary practice by reciting the mantra one hundred thousand times according to the ritual, should thereafter seek accomplishment in accordance with the dharma. Next, one should install the painted image as instructed, depicting the holy form of the Great Being who subdues all worlds and possesses every virtue."

On its four sides, one should paint the four great beings according to the ritual procedures of the four-seal maṇḍala; in the four corners, one should paint the forms of the four noble ones. After reciting the mantra before the painted image according to the dharma for one month, one continues the recitation throughout the entire night until dawn; then, the Great Being who subdues all worlds will appear before one, and whatever aspirations the practitioner desires shall be accomplished.
“This is the Dharma-gate of the Vajra of Dharma taught by this Buddha.

If one wishes to seek the accomplishment (*siddhi*) of the mudrā, the practitioner should form the Dharma-vajra mudrā and recite it eight thousand times according to the ritual of the Dharma-vajra. Having completed the recitation in four sessions every day, one should thereafter continue forming the mudrā and reciting throughout the night until dawn; thus, one attains the accomplishment of the mudrā.”
From this point forward, whenever one forms mudrās, one will be able to subdue all the world just as it has been taught.
This is the Dharma-gate of Avalokiteśvara spoken by the Buddha.

"If one wishes to attain the accomplishment of samādhi, the practitioner should recite the mantra according to the ritual for a full month. Thereafter, throughout the entire night, one should focus the mind with devotion upon whichever gate of samādhi is desired and recite according to that ritual procedure until dawn; thus, one will immediately attain the manifestation of all samādhis."
"This is the Dharma-gate of the Vajra Dharma taught by this Buddha.

If one wishes to seek the accomplishment of *karma*, one should likewise recite according to the ritual for one month; after the month has passed, one should recite throughout the entire night, and one will then be able to accomplish all *karmas*."
“This is the Dharma-gate of the Vajra-dharma taught by this Buddha.
The above constitutes the ritual procedure for the accomplishment of the activities of the Lotus Family.
Next, the ritual procedure for the accomplishment of the activities of the Jewel Family shall be proclaimed.”

"The practitioner should first pay homage to all Tathāgatas of the four directions; next, they should recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times. Thereafter, having installed the painted image according to the ritual, they should depict the holy form of the Great Being Sarvārthasiddhi, endowed with all virtues, according to the procedure for the Maṇḍala of the Four Mudrās, and perform various offerings while reciting for one month."

After one month has passed, he should recite throughout the entire night; when dawn arrives, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha—the Jewel of the Empowerment of All Tathāgatas endowed with virtue—will appear before him to bestow empowerment. Having received this empowerment, the practitioner immediately becomes the sovereign of the vidyādharas and the wheel-turning monarch of the trichiliocosm.
"This is the Vajraratna Dharma-gate taught by the Buddha.

If one desires to seek the accomplishment of the mudrā, the practitioner should, in accordance with the ritual applications of Karma-vajra, bind the Vajraratna-mudrā; as taught, one should seek accomplishment, and shall immediately attain the accomplishment of all intended Karma-mudrās."

"If one wishes to seek the accomplishment of the jewel-like wisdom, the practitioner should, according to the ritual and in its proper sequence, visualize within the vajra-ratna-samādhi that space is fundamentally devoid of intrinsic nature."
In this regard, how can these jewels be produced? They are produced from these very jewels themselves.
Furthermore, how is it that the body of a bodhisattva is produced?
For one month, during the four periods of each day, one should perform visualization and recitation as appropriate within this samādhi-gate.

After the month has passed, one should continue the recitation throughout the entire night according to the method of this samādhi until dawn; then all Tathāgatas will appear before one and bestow the sublime empowerment according to one's aspirations.
"This is the Dharma-gate of Ākāśagarbha spoken by the Buddha.
If one wishes to seek the accomplishment of *karma*, one should likewise recite according to the ritual for one month."

After one month has passed, if one recites throughout the night until dawn, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Guṇasāgaragarbha (Vajrapāṇi) will bestow upon that practitioner the accomplishment of all aims; thereafter, one will be able to perform all ritual activities.
"This is the Vajradhara-dharmaparyāya spoken by the Buddha.
The above constitutes the ritual procedure for the accomplishment of the activities of the Ratnakula.
Furthermore, the ritual procedures for all the activities of the various families shall now be proclaimed."
"In this regard, first the ritual procedure for the functions of all heart-mantras (*hṛdaya-mantra*) is explained:
The practitioner should speak as follows:
'Whatever one desires, the fundamental heart-mantra itself accomplishes everything.'"

Having spoken thus, one should recite the heart-mantra according to one's inclination and perform the rites for accomplishment in accordance with the ritual manual; thereafter, one will attain accomplishment as appropriate.
"The Ritual Manual for the Functions of All Mudrās:
The practitioner should speak these words:
'May all mudrās be accomplished as I desire.'"

Having spoken thus, one should immediately form the samādhi-mudrā and, according to one's inclination and capacity, recite the mantra in accordance with the ritual rules; thereafter, as taught, one will attain accomplishment.
“The Ritual Procedure for the Efficacy of All Mantra Syllables:
The practitioner should speak as follows:
‘Free from discursive elaboration, may I attain siddhi; I shall recite according to the Dharma within the accomplishment methods of all Tathāgatas.’”
Having spoken thus, one should recite the mantra syllables according to one's own preference and shall attain accomplishment.
Regarding the ritual procedure for the activities of all great vidyās,
the practitioner should speak as follows:
"May these sentient beings, who possess the darkness of ignorance, attain the realization of the Great Illumination of all Tathāgatas, which is accomplished through pure ethical discipline.
Having spoken thus, one should recite the Great Illumination mantra according to one's preference; by following the ritual, one shall attain accomplishment as sought.
"This is the noble Vajradhara Dharma-gate taught by the Buddha.

All practitioners should first take as their cause the practice of all heart-mantras (*hṛdaya*), seals (*mudrā*), incantation-words (*mantrapada*), and great vidyās according to their preference; thereafter, relying upon the ritual procedures for the recitation of the Vajra-holder, they should perform the recitation according to the Dharma using the heart-mantras, seals, incantation-words, and great vidyās appropriate for each sentient being."
Whether for oneself or for others, one should seek all accomplishments from the chosen deity (*iṣṭadevatā*).
This is the Dharma-gate of Vajrasattva as taught by the Buddha.
The above constitutes the ritual procedures for all activities of the various families (*kula*).
"Furthermore, I shall proclaim the extensive ritual procedures for accomplishment common to all families.
There are four types of accomplishments common to the Tathāgata family:
namely, the accomplishment of the perfection of purpose, the accomplishment of supernormal powers, the accomplishment of the vidyādhara, and the great accomplishment."

Regarding the "perfection of the accomplishment of benefit therein": if the practitioner suspects there is a hidden treasure (nidhi) at a certain location, they should immediately form the mudrā according to the ritual at that spot and, through the method of their own samādhi, observe that place with vajra-gaze.

If one sees signs of movement in the vajra, one should know that there is a hidden treasure at that spot; the practitioner shall then form the Vajra-Opening Samādhi Mudrā and, according to the rite, excavate it, obtaining it before long.
"Take whichever you prefer.
This is the Dharma-gate of Vajrasattva spoken by the Buddha.
"As for the accomplishment of supernatural powers (*abhijñā-siddhi*), when the practitioner wishes to perform the rite, they should speak as follows:"
"Regarding all mudrās, one should seek the accomplishment of vajra-ṛddhi (vajra-supernatural power).
Having spoken thus, one should act according to the ritual.
This accomplishment of supernatural power is of four kinds:

These are the supernormal powers of walking and sitting upon water; the supernormal power of manifesting physical forms such as those of the Tathāgata; the supernormal power of concealing one's body immediately according to one's wish; and the supernormal power of moving freely through the air for a thousand yojanas, ascending and descending, appearing and disappearing, and coming and going at will.
This [power] enables one to travel through the various directions for a distance of a thousand yojanas, proceeding at will according to one's pleasure and returning by way of rotation;

furthermore, it enables one to transcend a thousand yojanas to fully know the intentions of all sentient beings, to see all bodily forms with the eyes, and to hear all sounds and speech with the ears.

Furthermore, across all directions for more than a thousand yojanas, he can summon the bodies of all those who are lovely and pleasing according to his wish; he can gather all gold, jewels, *maṇi* gems, pearls, and so forth, and ultimately there is no one at all who can obstruct him. The practitioner can even conceal his body within that vajra, let alone being unable to withstand the strength of ten thousand men!
Furthermore, the practitioner shall always be free from illness, constantly enjoy all sensual pleasures, and always possess the youthful and exquisite marks of physical form.
Upon seeing him, all those Tathāgatas and Vajrasattvas will offer worship, and he shall attain the unsurpassed Vajra-accomplishment, obtaining a lifespan of a full four thousand years.
"This is the Dharma-gate of the Vajra Accomplishment of All Tathāgatas as taught by the Buddha.

O Vidyādhara-siddhas, if a practitioner seeks only the accomplishment of the mudrās, by performing them according to the ritual, they shall attain the accomplishment of a Vajra-vidyādhara; and because they have become a Wheel-Turning King of Vajra-vidyādharas, they will obtain the enjoyment of all desires at will."

In a single kṣaṇa, one is able to travel through and return from a thousand Buddha-fields, experiencing all manner of bliss; one’s countenance is youthful and beautiful as if sixteen years of age, with hair coiled like a conch, deep blue, spiraling, and lustrous. By virtue of attaining the accomplishment of the Great Vajra Vidyādhara, the Vajrasattva of all Tathāgatas, one immediately attains a lifespan of a great kalpa.
"This is the Dharma-gate of the Vidyādharas of all Tathāgatas, as taught by the Buddha.

Great Accomplished One, the practitioner should seek accomplishment according to the ritual through their own mudrā and heart-mantra (*hṛdaya*). By attaining the accomplishment of the physical form of the Great Being (*mahāsattva*) of one's own mudrā, in a single instant they are able to manifest various forms and perform various deeds throughout all worlds in the ten directions."

Having been seen by all those Tathāgatas and Vajrasattva, they then performed offerings; having brought benefit to the entire realm of sentient beings without exception, they returned once more to their original places.

Furthermore, one will be able to experience all forms of delight and happiness in all worlds, endowed with every excellence and enjoying them according to one's wish; one will become equal to the Great Bodhisattva Vajrasattva without distinction, and shall attain a lifespan of a full great kalpa.
"This is the Great Sādhana-Method of All Tathāgatas as taught by the Buddha.
Furthermore, regarding the general sādhanas of the Vajra Family, there are four types:
namely, the Sādhana of Trailokyavijaya, the Sādhana of All Consecrations, the Sādhana of All Joyful Dharmas, and the Supreme Sādhana."

"In this regard, for the accomplishment of Trailokyavijaya, the practitioner should form the Trailokyavijaya mudrā and visualize his left foot treading upon Maheśvara while performing the rite of accomplishment, until that deity utters cries of lamentation; thereafter, the practitioner should recite the syllable HŪṂ."

When the syllable HŪṂ is recited, all the sovereign lords of the three realms, such as Maheśvara and his retinues, will assemble and stand before the practitioner to perform acts of veneration and affection, and they will become his servants at his command.

From this point onward, the practitioner becomes a Vajra-holder of vidyā, the sovereign lord of all the three realms; they are able to arise in mid-air and travel and circulate with mastery throughout the three realms, returning once more as they please.

All extremely malevolent devas and all sentient beings can be completely subdued through the method of the syllable HŪṂ; like the form of Vajra Trailokyavijaya of all Tathāgatas, everything throughout the entire triple world shall turn according to his commands.
All those Tathāgatas and Vajrasattva, having seen him, will regard him with affection; his lifespan shall be a thousand years.
This is the Dharma-gate of Trailokyavijaya taught by the Buddha.

"All those who have achieved consecration should perform the accomplishment of the mudrā; that is to say, having first performed the self-consecration by binding the Jewel Consecration Mudrā of all Tathāgatas, they should thereafter seek the accomplishment of the four types of consecration."
These four types are:
the Vajra Initiation, the Jewel Initiation, the Dharma Initiation, and the Karma Initiation.
Once one has received the Vajra Initiation, one immediately becomes a Vajradhara of all Tathāgatas.
If one receives the jewel empowerment (*ratnābhiṣeka*), one immediately becomes the supreme sovereign over all jewels.
If one receives the dharma empowerment (*dharmābhiṣeka*), one immediately becomes a Dharma King.
If one receives the activity empowerment (*karmābhiṣeka*), one shall attain all mundane and supramundane accomplishments of activity (*sarvakarmasiddhi*).
"This is the Dharma-gate of the Empowerment of All Tathāgatas taught by the Buddha.

Regarding the accomplishment of all joyful dharmas: it means that by constantly performing secret offerings to all Tathāgatas, one immediately attains the accomplishment of all the satisfactions and pleasures of all Tathāgatas."
"This is the Dharma-gate of the Delight of All Tathāgatas, as taught by the Buddha.
'The supreme accomplishment' refers to attaining the accomplishment of the Vajra Honored One."
"This is the Vajradhara-dharmaparyāya spoken by the Buddha.
Furthermore, regarding the general methods for accomplishment (sādhana) common to the Lotus Family (Padmakula), there are four types:
namely, accomplishment through desire, accomplishment through love, accomplishment through protection, and lotus-accomplishment."

"In this regard, as for the accomplishment of 'following love and delight,' one should, as taught, visualize the Lotus of Sublime Love; by doing so, one can cause all Tathāgatas to likewise give rise to love and delight."
Furthermore, by simply directing one's thoughts toward the Honored One Avalokiteśvara of this very family, one can likewise cause all sentient beings to give rise to reverence and affection.
Moreover, if one abides in samādhi and extensively radiates a mind of loving-kindness, one is able to secretly provide protection for the entire world.

Furthermore, if one abides in the Lotus Samādhi of the Honored One and, having taken hold of a lotus flower in hand, seeks the accomplishment of the goal, one will immediately obtain a wondrous form like that of the Honored One Avalokiteśvara, endowed with all the marks, and a lifespan of four thousand years.
“This is the Lotus Dharma-gate of all Tathāgatas as taught by the Buddha.
Furthermore, there are four general methods for accomplishment in the Ratna Family:
namely, the accomplishment of the empowerment of all Tathāgatas, the accomplishment of great majestic light, the accomplishment of fulfilling all aspirations, and the accomplishment of jewels.”

"In this context, it means that one should offer to all the Tathāgatas by means of the self-consecration rite; by bestowing the light of lamps, one fulfills the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā) and performs the rites for the accomplishment of jewels according to one's capacity."
These four types of ritual applications for accomplishment should all be used to constantly make offerings to all Tathāgatas; before long, one shall attain the desired accomplishments.
"This is the sublime jewel dharma-gate of all Tathāgatas as spoken by the Buddha."
"The above constitutes the extensive ritual manual for accomplishment common to all sections.
Furthermore, I shall now proclaim the principles of the skillful means for accomplishment within all rituals; this is the fundamental dharma-gate of the Great Being’s lack of intrinsic nature."
"In this regard, the ritual procedures for the accomplishment of the heart-mantra (hṛdaya-mantra) are first explained.
The verse says:
'Just as for the sake of subduing the world, one attains accomplishment according to what is appropriate for each.'"
In this context, the seal (*mudrā*) of skillful means (*upāya*) serves as the cause, capable of bestowing all vast accomplishments (*siddhi*).
Regarding the "Teaching on the Accomplishment of Seal-Means" (*Mudropāyasādhananaya*):
"To subdue the world, one must transcend desire; yet the accomplishment of seals arises from desire."
By practicing those skillful means as appropriate, one is able to accomplish all matters of siddhi.
Regarding the instructional principles for accomplishing through the skillful means of mantra-syllables:
"If there is truly any disturbance in the world, no accomplishment of mantra-syllables can be attained."
Accomplished through the skillful means of transcending conceptual proliferation, one then achieves the supreme siddhis.
Regarding the "Instructional Principle for Accomplishing the Skillful Means of Great Illumination" (*Mahāvidyā-upāya-sādhananaya*):
"If one here clings to the signs of ignorance, there will be no accomplishment of the Great Illumination."
"By means of this vast gateway of skillful methods, one is able to bestow all manner of vast accomplishments.
The above constitutes the instructional principles for the accomplishment of skillful methods within all ritual manuals."
"Furthermore, the teaching on the accomplishment of merit within all ritual procedures (*vidhi*) is the dharma-gate of all Tathāgatas.
Herein, first is explained the teaching on the accomplishment of merit through the heart-mantra (*hṛdaya*):
'By performing the four kinds of offerings according to the rite, One thereby attains a great mass of merit.'"
The supreme gateway of merit for making offerings to all Buddhas is accomplished herein without doubt.
Regarding the instructional principles for the accomplishment of the merit of mudrās:
"With the secret samaya as protection, one thereby attains a great mass of merit."
By the cause of being empowered by this samādhi, even those who lack merit will achieve success.
Regarding the instructional principle for the accomplishment of the blessings of the mantra-words:
"That which was first spoken by all the Buddhas shall, as appropriate, result in the attainment of a great mass of merit."
The equality of the gift of Dharma is the cause; through this, one swiftly accomplishes that which is not a gateway to merit.
Regarding the "Instructional Principle for Accomplishing the Great Mantra’s Merit":
"Giving is the supreme among all merits; by means of it, one obtains a great mass of merit."
Having perfected the pāramitā of generosity, one will swiftly attain Buddhahood as appropriate.
The above constitutes the instructional principle for the accomplishment of merit within all ritual procedures.
Furthermore, the teaching on the principle for the accomplishment of wisdom (*prajñā-siddhi*) within all ritual manuals (*kalpa*) is proclaimed.
Herein, first, the teaching on the principle for the accomplishment of wisdom through the heart-mantra (*hṛdaya-vidyā*) is stated:
“In phenomena, there are no syllables to enter; yet one fully understands all syllables.”
Through the gateway of one’s own speech and the gateway of another’s speech, one attains accomplishment by visualizing accordingly.
This is the Dharma-gateway of the Great Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī spoken by the Buddha.
The *Mudrājñānasiddhinaya*: "Wisdom is so named because it discerns; this is what is taught regarding samādhi.
Within that, through the gateway of mudrā-siddhi, one attains accomplishment in an instant of visualization."
"This is the Dharma-gate of Supreme Wisdom taught by the Buddha.
The instructional principle for the accomplishment of mantra-wisdom is as follows:
'The name is established according to the sound of wisdom; it is the conceptual discourse of samādhi.'"
Within that, one visualizes the gateway of accomplishment; accordingly, the mantra syllables attain accomplishment.
"This is the Dharma-gateway of Vajra Wisdom spoken by the Buddha.
The instructional principle for the accomplishment of Great Illuminating Wisdom: "
"The Great Illuminating Mantra has two distinctions; within these, there is no distinction whatsoever.
By contemplating this with right wisdom in accordance with it, one will certainly and swiftly attain accomplishment."
"This is the Dharma-gate of the wisdom of all Tathāgatas as spoken by the Buddha.
The above constitutes the instructional principle for the accomplishment of wisdom among all ritual procedures."
Furthermore, the teaching on the principles for accomplishing the practice within all ritual procedures is proclaimed.
This is the gateway of the Vajra-hand method.
Within this, the principles for accomplishing the practice of the heart-mantra (hṛdaya-mantra) are first explained:
"If one performs all acts of offering, one will be able to increase sublime conduct;
as those various wholesome dharmas accordingly increase, one shall attain the perfection of the dharma."
The *Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Practice of Mudrās*:
"By entering into various secret wheels, and by arraying various maṇḍalas,
through the supreme gateway of offerings with all mudrās, the vast matters of accomplishment are increased."
The *Tantra of the Accomplishment of Mantra Practice*:
"By means of superior dharmas such as sympathetic joy (*anumodana*), and likewise by reciting the True Dharma,
through the extensive application of various gates of offering, the mantra syllables will certainly attain accomplishment."
The *Sādhana-vidhi of the Great Illumination*:
"Wisdom-light thoroughly severs the nature of ignorance; This is the principle of the perfection of generosity (*dāna-pāramitā*).
By means of this cause of fulfilling sublime conduct, One swiftly attains accomplishment according to the Dharma."
“Thus concludes the doctrine for the accomplishment of activities within all ritual manuals.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi further expounded the doctrine for the accomplishment of the wisdom of the true emergence of the insignia of the various families:
“In this regard, how does the vajra emerge?”
The verse says:
"This very venerable Great Being, possessing all virtues, from whose own mind all minds arise—
his body, speech, and mind-vajras, the firm *sattva*, are born spontaneously."
The supreme among all great beings, the Great Being, Arising from the heart through vajra-accomplishment, Is given the name Vajrasattva; He dwells within that vajra.
This very state, in union with such wisdom, is the non-dual principle of all Buddhas;
from the gateway of skillful activity emerging from one’s own mind, all manifold signs are thereby accomplished.
As numerous as the atoms in all worlds, so too are all the Buddhas, the Holy Honored Ones;
from all those bodies of the Buddhas, they emerge from Vajrasattva.
From this, moreover, arise all the Great Beings (mahāsattva) and all their respective emblems;
those Great Beings and the gateways of their emblems—all are born together within this principle (naya).
If there are those who hear this Dharma, and are able to give rise to pure faith or uphold it,
contemplating it with a mind of constant joy, they will swiftly attain accomplishment as appropriate.
"This is the Dharma-gate of Vajrasattva spoken by the Buddha.
As above, this is the instructional principle for the accomplishment of the wisdom arising from the reality of the insignia of all families."
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *tantra* of the great wisdom accomplishment that arises from all the ritual procedures (*vidhi*) of the various families (*kula*).
"Within this, first is explained the instructional principle for the accomplishment of Great Wisdom arising from the ritual manuals of all Tathāgatas:
'The great wisdom of all Buddhas is non-conceptual; the phenomena produced by that wisdom abide eternally.
Through the gateway of wisdom that arises subsequent to non-conceptuality, this conceptualization is taught as non-conceptuality.'"
From the *Tattvasaṃgraha* of the Tathāgata Family, the Instructional System for the Accomplishment of Great Wisdom:
"Through the conceptualization of a self that is non-conceptual, this conceptualization gives rise to further conceptualization;
the Great Being Vajrasattva declares that very conceptualization to be the skillful means."
From the *Vajrakulakalpa*: The Doctrine for the Accomplishment of Great Wisdom:
"Just as one arranges various painted images, And achieves accomplishment according to the ritual procedures of painting, So too are the methods of application therein;
That which I have here explained is free from conceptual construction."
From the *Mahājñānasiddhi-tantra* within the *Padmakula-vidhi*:
“Arising from the conceptualization of the nature of desire, this nature is established within the lotus;
it likewise abides for a long time, and thus all accomplishments arise according to the principle.”
From the *Ratnakula-vidhi*, the *Mahājñānasiddhinaya*:
"This jewel is by nature free from conceptual differentiation, yet its majestic radiance is naturally exalted.
Such is the subtle gateway of accomplishment; though that which arises therefrom is without conceptual differentiation."
“This is the Vajra-Jewel Dharma-gate taught by the Buddha.
As above, this is the instructional principle for the accomplishment of Great Wisdom arising from all the ritual manuals of the various families.”
Furthermore, the teaching on the principles of wisdom for the arising of the heart-mantra (hṛdaya) within all ritual procedures is proclaimed as follows:
“Whatever ritual applications one desires, One should seek accomplishment according to that desire;
Abiding in the mind through meditative concentration (samādhi), This is called the method of the heart-mantra.”
The *Mudrā-utpatti-jñāna-naya*: "One must not transgress or destroy it;
This refers to the King’s supreme seal-command, The gateway of all marks and signs of the Great Being (Mahāsattva). This teaching is likewise like a royal seal."
The Principle of the Wisdom Arising from Mantra-syllables:
“It cannot be transgressed nor destroyed; Such is the gateway of secret mantras.
Once the mantra has been recited, the secret dharma is accomplished; Therefore, it is called a ‘mantra-syllable’.”
The *Mahāvidyā-utpatti-jñāna-tantra*:
"The principle for accomplishing the supreme vidyā-mantra speech, Which is able to destroy ignorance;
Through clear wisdom, one realizes the perfection of phenomena, And thus the Great Vidyā is established."
"This is the Vajradhara-dharmaparyāya spoken by the Buddha.
As stated above, this is the teaching on the wisdom that gives rise to the heart-mantras and so forth within all ritual manuals."
Furthermore, the teaching on the arising of supreme wisdom within all ritual procedures is proclaimed.
Herein, first is the teaching on the arising of supreme wisdom through the heart-mantra (hṛdaya-mantra):
"Once the wise one has recited the heart-mantra, whether for oneself or for another, according to the appropriate rite,"
Throughout the three times—past, future, and present—all shall hear and behold [this].
Regarding the "Instructional Principle for the Arising of the Supreme Wisdom of Mudrā":
"Truly focusing the mind, bind the mudrā; perform it according to the Dharma as taught."
Having performed [this], one should observe the world; all that is to be known is as explained above.
Regarding the instructional principle for the arising of the supreme wisdom of the mantra-words:
"Recite the mantra-words once according to the rite, proclaiming them from one's own tongue."
Throughout the three times—past, future, and present—those true dharmas are accomplished.
This is the Dharma-gate of Avalokiteśvara spoken by the Buddha.
It is the teaching on the principles for generating the Great Mantra of Supreme Wisdom:
"Recite the great mantra once according to the ritual, With a mind focused and in accord with reality, understanding it clearly;
Throughout the three periods of past, future, and present, That vajra speech is exactly as it has been attained."
"The above constitutes the teaching on the arising of supreme wisdom within all ritual procedures (*kalpa*).

From the *Mahāyāna-abhisamaya-samādhi-mahātantra-rāja*, the Great King of Tantras Revealing the Mahāyāna Abhisamaya of the Reality-Gathering of All Tathāgatas, spoken by the Buddha, Volume Twenty-Nine."
The Great King of Tantras of Samādhi, Scroll Thirty.

Translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Imperially Appointed Grand Officer of the Court of State Ceremonial, Acting Minister of the Ministry of Rites, Dharma-Transmitting Master, and Purple-Robed Śramaṇa, Subject Shi Hu, et al., by Imperial Decree.

Part Three of the Twenty-Sixth Section: The Supreme Doctrine and Principles of the Ritual Procedures for the True Gathering of All Tathāgatas. "Furthermore, the doctrine and principles for the accomplishment of the Secret Body, Speech, and Mind Vajra Mudrās, which are common to all families, shall now be proclaimed."
"Within this, first is explained the teaching on the accomplishment of the secret body-mudrā of the Tathāgata family.
The verse says:
'Sitting in accordance with the Dharma wherever one may be, Assuming the full-lotus posture, one seeks accomplishment.'"
By practicing in accordance with what has been depicted, one immediately attains the accomplishment of the Great Being’s Dharma.
This is the Dharma-gate of Vajrasattva spoken by the Buddha.
The *Vajrakula-guhyakāyamudrā-siddhi-naya*: "Performing according to the ritual of the vajra-stride, and practicing in accordance with what has been drawn,
when seeking accomplishment and generating wrath, therein one will achieve success without doubt."
“This is the Dharma-gate of Vajra Trailokyavijaya spoken by the Buddha.
Regarding the secret body-mudrā accomplishment method of the Lotus Family:
‘One should assume the vajra-paryaṅka posture and bind the two hands in the vajra-bond.’”
The body of samādhi is accomplished according to the ritual; one should perform the rite of the lotus’s emergence.
This is the Dharma-gate of the Lotus-Sattva taught by the Buddha.
The *Ratnakula-guhyakāyamudrā-siddhi-naya*: Whether the practitioner stands,
sits peacefully, or wanders in walking meditation wherever they may be,
by means of the gateway of the Vajra-Ratna consecration, they shall accomplish the rite of siddhi without doubt.
"This is the Dharma-gate of Vajragarbha spoken by the Buddha.
Regarding the *tantra* for the accomplishment of the secret speech-mudrā of the Tathāgata family:
'According to the ritual, remain unmoving at the tip of the tongue, and again join the two features of the lips and teeth.'"
By uttering the vajra speech with a subtle sound, one can achieve all accomplishments through recitation.
This is the Dharma-gate of Vajra Speech taught by the Buddha.
The *Vajrakula Secret Speech Mudrā Sādhana-nyāya*:
"Uttering the roar of clouds and thunder with the syllable HŪṂ, one proclaims the profound words of majestic wrath;
this is the accomplishment of the speech of the Great Vajra of Fierce Destruction."
"This is the Dharma-gate of Vajra Trailokyavijaya spoken by the Buddha.
Regarding the ritual principles for the accomplishment of the Secret Speech Mudrā of the Lotus Family:
'One should cease the subtle inhalation and exhalation of breath, and utter sublime speech with supreme brilliance.'"
When all rely upon this while performing recitation, they will accomplish the treasury of samādhi wisdom.
This is the Dharma-gate of the Treasury of Samādhi Wisdom of All Tathāgatas, as spoken by the Buddha.
The *Ratnakula-guhyavāg-mudrā-siddhi-tantra*:
"Uttering those most exquisite and radiant words, and constantly prostrating to the Supreme Honored One,
reciting according to the ritual procedures as appropriate, all that is undertaken will be swiftly accomplished."
"This is the Dharma-gate of the Vast Karmic Rite for Making Offerings to All Tathāgatas, as taught by the Buddha.
Regarding the *siddhi* of the Secret Heart-Seal of the Tathāgata Family, the teaching states:
'The World-Honored One constantly employs the Dharma of sublime desire to universally bestow happiness upon all sentient beings.'"
The vast body of Vajrasattva— By meditating upon this within, one swiftly attains accomplishment.
This is the Dharma-gate of Sublime Desire taught by the Buddha.
The Ritual for Accomplishing the Secret Heart-Seal of the Vajra Family:

"For the sake of benefiting all sentient beings, I shall set forth the methods for subduing all evil dharmas and causing them to provide protection and support for the Buddha's teaching; thus, I shall explain the rites for the accomplishment of wrathful deities."
"This is the Dharma-gate of Vajra Trailokyavijaya taught by all the Tathāgatas.
Regarding the secret heart-seal (*hṛdaya-mudrā*) accomplishment method of the Lotus Family (*Padmakula*):
'Just as a lotus is inherently unstained, its locus of reliance is sublime love.'"
"My own Sublime Love Purity is likewise; thus one attains the accomplishment of the Dharma of Sublime Love.
This is the Lotus Dharma-gate of Sublime Love spoken by the Buddha.
The *Ratnakula-guhyacittamudrā-siddhi-tantra*:
"What accords with all sentient beings, Causing all matters to be accomplished,
Raining down a shower of various jewels in full perfection, All are swiftly accomplished as appropriate."
"This is the Dharma-gate of Ākāśagarbha spoken by the Buddha.
Regarding the Secret Vajra-mudrā Accomplishment Teachings of the Tathāgata Family:
Whether the practitioner remains standing, sits in a settled posture, or wanders in walking meditation according to the occasion,"
Binding the mudrā with the left hand according to the ritual procedure, all that is undertaken shall be accomplished.
This is the Dharma-gate of the Secret Vajra Hand of All Tathāgatas, as taught by the Buddha.
The *Vajrakula-guhyavajramudrā-siddhi-tantra*:
“The practitioner dwells according to the ritual at any location;
performing whatever actions are appropriate for that place, one accomplishes the *vajra-krodha-aṅgulimudrā*, and achieves accomplishment by covering oneself with a garment.”
"This is the Dharma-gate of the Vajra-Wrath-King of All Tathāgatas, as spoken by the Buddha.
Regarding the *Sādhana-śāstra* of the Secret Vajra-Mudrā of the Lotus Family:
'Form the Lotus Fist Mudrā with the left hand, and then one should cover over that hand-mudrā.'"
"By performing the mudrā-formation in accordance with the method at any location, one will swiftly attain the siddhi of the Lotus Family.
This is the Dharma-gate of Avalokiteśvara as taught by the Buddha.
Regarding the *ratnakula* secret Vajra-mudrā Siddhi-tantra:"
"With the left hand, one should form the Jewel Rain mudrā; this mudrā should then be held as a canopy.
Whatever rite is performed according to the original ritual manual, one will accordingly attain the accomplishment of jewels."
"This is the Dharma-gate of Ākāśagarbha taught by the Buddha.
As above, this constitutes the secret ritual system for the accomplishment of the Vajra Seals of Body, Speech, and Mind, common to all families."
Furthermore, the secret Vajrasattva mudrā common to all families is proclaimed:
"By employing the supreme method of that Great Seal, in the samādhi of the deity-sattva,
performing the vajra-gaze and vajra-speech, one swiftly attains the method of the most supreme accomplishment."
“This is the Dharma-gate of Vajrasattva for all Tathāgatas, as taught by the Buddha.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, endowed with virtue, addressed all the Tathāgatas, saying:
“World-Honored One, Tathāgata!
"Regarding this ritual procedure of mine, I only pray that the Tathāgatas will empower my practice.
At that time, all the Tathāgatas once again gathered like clouds and together praised the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi.
The verse says:
“Excellent, O Vajrasattva! Excellent, O Great Vajraratna! Excellent, O Vajradharmamukha! Excellent, O Supreme Vajrakarma!”
One is able to skillfully proclaim this sublime Dharma, the unsurpassed Vajra Secret Vehicle,
the secret gateway of all Tathāgatas, which is subsumed within the Mahāyāna dharma of direct realization.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi rose from his seat and, with one hundred and eight names, praised and entreated all the Tathāgatas.
The verse says:
"Great Vajradhātu Mahāsattva, supreme lord who benefits sentient beings,
Śākyarāja endowed with great wisdom— homage and refuge to the Vajra-body!"
Brave in producing true benefit, acting as the great principle for the cause of sentient beings,
the Great Being who accomplishes supreme victory and sublime deeds— homage to the Being among Beings!
Possessing all Buddha-dharmas and the vast Dharma, you who skillfully turn all wheels of Dharma;
with great speech, most supreme and exquisitely luminous, I bow my head and take refuge in the Great Reality.
Performing the great karma and great empowerment, the accomplisher of all karmas, the Great Hero,
the Honored One of supreme practice— I take refuge in the Lord of the True Cause, the Sattva.
Having attained all the pāramitās, the Knower who perceives with all-encompassing wisdom,
the great skillful means for all sentient beings— to you of great supreme intelligence, I bow my head and take refuge.
Possessing the supreme and most excellent mind of great compassion, you who have already exercised compassion as the sovereign of mercy,
and who extensively bestow the heart of universal loving-kindness— to you who perform all that is virtuous, I bow my head and take refuge.
Śākyasiṃha, the Great Capable One, the Honored One of Silent Stillness who is capable among the capable,
who has mastered the worldly and is the great tamer— to the Dharma of the supreme path, I bow my head and take refuge.
Having attained equality within the great dharmadhātu, the Great Tathāgata of the pure dharmadhātu,
the Vajra Honored One and the further vast Honored One— I prostrate and take refuge in the assembly of the valiant.
Great radiance and great illumination, Vast diligence and great victorious power,
Great heroism and supreme, ultimate valor— I take refuge in the majestic and courageous one born of tranquility,
The Great Brahmā, World-Honored One, self-arisen, Śākyamuni, fearless and great in silent stillness.
To the Sage who possesses the purity of all bodies, the King of Dharma—to you I bow and take refuge.
To the one without body who manifests the supreme body, the cultivator of the three perfected bodies;
To the one possessing all bodies and the vast body—to the Vajra-body, I bow and take refuge.
Speechless yet manifesting speech, the supreme speaker; Who proclaims through the perfection of the three modes of speech;
Possessing all speech, the wondrous great speech— I bow my head and take refuge in the Vajra Speech.
The supreme mind that manifests from the mindless, The one who manifests the three minds in their perfection—
Possessing all minds, the Great Vajra, I prostrate and take refuge in the Vajra Mind.
Non-vajra manifests as that vajra; the supreme vajra of the three vajras, the pure and vast universal vajra—to the vajra within the vajras, I pay homage.
Surpassing the three realms of existence through universal observation, The Sovereign Sugata, the most supreme one,
The Great Dharma King within the three worlds— I prostrate and take refuge in Mahāvairocana.
If there are those who hear the one hundred and eight names of the Tathāgata, and whether by reciting,
chanting, or reading them with sincere resolve, such persons shall attain the fruit of Buddhahood.
I now entreat the Buddha, the Holy Honored One, to turn the vast wheel of Dharma for the benefit of all sentient beings, arising from a heart of great compassion.

At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, having heard the words of exhortation from Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva—the sovereign lord of all Tathāgatas—addressed all the Tathāgatas, saying:
"I pray only that the Tathāgatas will graciously accept this practice."
Then all the Tathāgatas gathered once more like clouds and spoke these verses:
"For the sake of benefiting all sentient beings, Throughout all worlds and in every place,
By means of whatever gateways of form are necessary to discipline them, This great wheel of Dharma is turned according to what is appropriate."

When these verses were spoken, throughout all Buddha-fields and all worlds, and in every direction and location for all sentient beings, they all beheld the Bhagavān Tathāgata Śākyamuni before each of them within maṇḍalas as numerous as atoms, turning the sublime wheel of Dharma.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi spoke these verses:
"For the benefit of all sentient beings, In every world and in every place,
The Great Vajra Wheel turns as appropriate, Through the various gateways of those to be disciplined."

When these verses were spoken, throughout all Buddha-fields and all worlds, and in every direction and location for all sentient beings, they all beheld within maṇḍalas as minute as atoms, the World-Honored One Vajradhātu Tathāgata residing before each of them, turning the vajra-wheels of the Vajradhātu and all other such cycles.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Trailokyavijaya spoke these verses:
"For the sake of benefiting all sentient beings, throughout all worlds and in every place,
the great wheel of wrathful fury revolves as appropriate, through the various gateways of those who are to be disciplined."

When this verse was spoken, throughout all Buddha-fields and all worlds, and in every direction and location for all sentient beings, they all beheld within maṇḍalas as minute as atoms the Bhagavān Trailokyavijaya Tathāgata, each stationed before them, turning the great wheel of the wrathful deities of all Tathāgatas.
At that time, the Noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara spoke these verses:
"For the benefit of all sentient beings, In every world and in every place,
The pure lotus wheel turns as is appropriate, Through the various gateways of those to be disciplined."

When this verse was spoken, throughout all Buddha-fields and all worlds, and in every direction and location for all sentient beings, they all beheld within maṇḍalas as minute as atoms the World-Honored One, the Dharma King Tathāgata, each dwelling before them and turning the Lotus Wheel.
At that time, the Noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha spoke these verses:
"For the sake of benefiting all sentient beings, In every world and in every place,
The great and wondrous jewel wheel turns as is appropriate, Through the various gateways for those to be disciplined."

When these verses were spoken, all sentient beings dwelling in every buddha-field, whether small or large, in every direction, all beheld those Tathāgatas within the Great Pavilion of Vajra-Maṇi-Jewel Peaks atop Mount Sumeru, seated upon the lion thrones of all Tathāgatas, turning the wheel of Dharma of the Vajradhātu and all other [mandalas].
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi spoke these verses:
"For the sake of benefiting sentient beings, the Noble Lord, through the great skillful means of his own practice,
has manifested as the most supreme one descending into the human world, turning the Great Vajra Wheel according to what is appropriate."
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, again addressed all the Tathāgatas, saying:
"World-Honored Tathāgatas!
We pray that you will once more assemble in clouds and graciously accept our practice."
At that time, all the Tathāgatas and their equals gathered once more and entered the heart of the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana.

Then, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, having fully awakened [them] through the vajra-body of the body, speech, and mind of all the Tathāgatas, addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:
“O son of good family!
All the Tathāgatas within my heart, as well as all those maṇḍalas of the Vajra Family, have entered entirely from within my heart; you now likewise enter from my heart.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, having understood the Buddha’s instructions as they were spoken, spoke these verses:
"For the sake of benefiting all sentient beings, I shall act everywhere throughout all realms.
All Buddhas enter into my heart; I abide in the vajra of body, speech, and mind."

When this verse was spoken, throughout all worlds—equal in number to the atoms of all buddha-fields—all the Tathāgatas currently residing therein each manifested a vast physical form as extensive as the atoms of all worlds, and these forms all entered the heart of the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, together with all those Tathāgatas and the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, merged all bodies, transformed all speech, and gathered all minds. Through the continuity of their seed-syllables, from every part of his body, every state, every mark and excellence, and every pore, he brought forth maṇḍalas as numerous as atoms, including all the Vajra Teachings and so forth; having entered through the heart, they abided according to the principle.

At that time, not long after the World-Honored One had manifested his perfect enlightenment, having awakened to himself through the vajra of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas within the bodies of all Tathāgatas, he proceeded from the summit of Mount Sumeru to the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa).
Having arrived, he immediately performed his transformative deeds beneath the Bodhi tree in accordance with worldly custom. Taking hold of auspicious grass, he spoke this verse:
"How great! Having already perfected the supreme self-benefit, you extensively teach all sentient beings for their benefit.
Through the cause of diligent vigor, you subdue those who hold false and heterodox views."
All those in the world who are unsubdued, and all the dark, evil views—
through the pure and greatly beneficial light of wisdom, one attains Buddhahood therein as is appropriate.
When these verses were spoken, the devas of the desire realm did not understand this true speech of the World-Honored One, and they immediately said:
"Why is it that this śramaṇa is now able to perform such a difficult task for the sake of seeking bodhi?"
"Be resolute, overcome fatigue, and endure all sufferings.
Then, at that place, the World-Honored One spread out grass for a seat and addressed that deva, saying:
"O Deva, Noble One!"
"Based on the conduct I have practiced, it is fitting that you should bestow upon me the fruit of Great Bodhi.
At that time, the various devas of the desire realm were likewise unable to understand what the Buddha had said;
they immediately went together to the abode of Śakra, Lord of Devas, and having arrived, they related the aforementioned matter in detail before the Lord of Devas.

At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, together with the hosts of deva-lords of the desire realm, went to the abode of Mahābrahmā, the Lord of the devas of the form realm, and once again presented the aforementioned matter for mutual deliberation.
At that time, Mahābrahmā, together with the hosts of celestial lords of the desire realm and the form realm, as well as Maheśvara—the sovereign lord of all three realms—deliberated upon this matter.
At that time, Maheśvara addressed all the celestial lords, including Nārāyaṇa—the sovereign ruler of the entirety of the triple world—and said:
"O noble celestial beings!

You should know that the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, in accordance with the ways of the world, carries out his transformative activities by manifesting the attainment of the fruit of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; do not think that he is comprised within the realms of humans or devas.
Therefore, you should know that although they have been born in the heavens and achieved excellence therein, they ultimately cannot realize the fruit of Buddhahood.
Regarding their virtuous conduct, we ought to go together to make offerings to them.
Then the hosts of celestial lords, headed by Maheśvara, immediately went together to the place where the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata, was seated at the site of Great Bodhi.
Having arrived, they prostrated with their heads at the feet of the World-Honored One and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
As the Buddha has commanded us to practice accordingly, we pray only that the World-Honored One will compassionately accept us.
We further entreat the World-Honored One to rise from this seat of grass and accept the exquisite, supreme throne offered by us, and upon that throne, realize the fruit of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the various lords of the devas, saying: "O divine sages!
In accordance with my practice, you should bestow upon me the fruit of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*."
The lords of the devas addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
It is not within our power to bestow the Buddha’s bodhi. If we possessed such power, would we not have realized the fruit of the Buddha’s bodhi for ourselves?”
At that time, in order to bring about the full understanding of this meaning, the World-Honored One spoke these verses:
"Know that it is neither form nor formlessness, Neither real nor unreal, and not even pure;
This is the gateway to the great wisdom of the Buddha’s Bodhi; Having truly awakened to it, one attains Buddhahood."
Those lords of the gods remained silent for a moment.
Then, the World-Honored One rose from his grass seat and again addressed the lords of the gods, saying:
"O noble ones, gods!
“Are you able to open up and clarify this Buddha-wisdom?
The lords of the devas and others replied to the Buddha,
“World-Honored One!”
"We are unable to fully comprehend the Buddha's wisdom.
At that time, the World-Honored One, while seated upon his sublime throne, spoke again in verse:
"The pure mind is awakened according to what is appropriate; The great bodhicitta is born with steadfast resolve."
“Visualize the Buddha’s body according to the principle, and manifest Vajrasattva with firm resolve.
Then all the lords of the gods and others addressed the Buddha together, saying,
“In accordance with the Buddha’s instruction, we shall act accordingly.”
Having spoken thus, they immediately departed from the Buddha’s assembly.

At that time, during day and night, the World-Honored One, in accordance with the ways of the world, performed various transformative deeds to subdue the armies of Māra; having realized the fruit of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, he extensively brought benefit and happiness to all sentient beings throughout the entire realm of sentient beings without exception.

All that has been accomplished is universally gathered and abides within one's own mind. Then, one praises the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi with these one hundred and eight names, reciting these verses:
“Vajrasattva, Great Sattva, Unsurpassed Great Vehicle, Great Sovereign, Vast, Pure, and Great Radiance— I bow my head and take refuge in the Great, Most Victorious One.”
Noble Vajrarāja, Great Vajra, Vajra of all Tathāgatas, Vastly Diligent,
Great Heroic Honored One, I prostrate and take refuge in you, the Great Expedient Means.
Vajra-mañju-rati, great and utterly pure, All-encompassing delight, the great sublime bliss, The gate of supreme joy,
without beginning or end— I bow my head and take refuge in the Great Desire.
Vajra, Well-Said, Great Joy; acting according to reality, virtuous and supreme delight;
vast joy, great king of joy—homage and refuge to the most excellent joy.
Vajra-mañju-ratna, Great Sovereign, Great Lord of the self-familial empowerment,
Possessor of all jewels, Great Auspicious Radiance— I bow my head and take refuge in you, O Supreme Ornament.
Vajra-majesty, great brilliance, vast radiance, and great illumination;
possessing the supreme light of great intensity—homage and refuge to the Buddha’s radiant marks.

The vajra-jewel banner is exceedingly high and manifest; as the great victorious banner that bestows wealth, possessing the great jewel-staff and the banner of space, I bow my head and take refuge in the one whose mark is the banner of generosity.
Manifesting the great laugh of the Vajra-smile, you who possess great jubilation and great joy;
you whose supreme bliss proceeds with swift delight—to that Great Dharma-Joy, I bow my head and take refuge.
The supreme Vajra Dharma, the great and wondrous Dharma, Possessing all dharmas and being perfectly pure,
The most excellent gateway to the dharmas of all Buddhas— I prostrate and take refuge in the Dharma of Wondrous Love.
The great sword of wisdom, sharp as a vajra, Great insight, further serving as wisdom for the wise,
A great instrument for severing the gates of transgression— I bow my head and take refuge in the Buddha’s sword of benefit.
The vast wheel of the vajra pinnacle, the great treasury of the wheels of all Buddhas,
the most auspicious and supreme dharma-gate— homage and refuge to the cause of the Wheel of Dharma.

The sublime speech of the Vajra, the great assembly of words, The great syllables of speech free from conceptual proliferation— Within the absence of syllables, you recite and uphold the Great; I bow my head and take refuge in the Buddha’s true speech.
Vajra-karma, the most excellent activity, The great karma that skillfully accomplishes all deeds;
Secret offering, the great offering— I prostrate and take refuge in the Buddha-offering.
Vajra-protection, great and supreme armor, Supreme mail, most firmly solid, Vast, true,
and great gateway of protection— I bow my head and take refuge in the diligence of awakening.
Vajra Subduer, Great Wrathful One, who terrifies all malevolent beings;
gateway of the great skillful means of all Buddhas—to you, whose mark is the supreme tusk, I bow and take refuge.
The great mudrā of the Great Vajra Fist, the supreme binder through the Great Samaya-bond,
the most excellent mudrā and the fist of great wisdom— I take refuge in the form of the Supreme Vajra Fist.
Venerating, honoring, and making offerings—these are the constant practices of all those Tathāgatas.
Within this Dharma-gate that is without beginning or end, you have spoken of the Great Bodhicitta.
You are the supreme refuge for all Buddhas, And the great heroic courage of all Bodhisattvas;
In those past and future births, You shall be the most excellent cause for the Buddha-enlightenment.
I take refuge in the Great Vajrasattva; I take refuge in the Great Vajra-Wondrous Jewel;
I take refuge in the Vajra Gate of the True Dharma; I take refuge in the Supreme Vajra-Karma.
I praise your supreme name; I prostrate to you because your self-nature is vajra.
May the mass of merit thus generated be bestowed upon sentient beings, so that they may attain the fruit of buddha-enlightenment.
If a person, with a focused mind, recites these one hundred and eight supreme names,
or even recites but one while giving rise to sincere resolve, that person shall attain the fruit of all Buddhas.
"This is the Dharma-gate of awakened wisdom taught by the Buddha.
At that time, all the Tathāgatas praised the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi with one voice.
The verse says:
“Excellent is Vajrasattva; excellent is the Great Vajra Jewel!
Excellent is the Vajra Dharma-gate; excellent is the Supreme Vajra Karma!”
One is able to skillfully proclaim this sublime Dharma, the unsurpassed Vajra Secret Vehicle,
the secret gateway of all Tathāgatas, which is subsumed within the Mahāyāna dharma of direct realization.
When the Buddha had spoken this sutra, all the Tathāgatas,

together with the assembly of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, having heard what was taught by the Buddha, the World-Honored One, and the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, were all greatly rejoiced, and they faithfully accepted and practiced it.

The Great King of Teachings on the Samādhi of Direct Realization of the Mahāyāna, Truly Encompassing All Tathāgatas, Spoken by the Buddha. Fascicle Thirty. This entire scripture consists of four thousand ślokas in the Sanskrit original; it has been translated into thirty fascicles, comprising twenty-six sections in total.
From the first section through the fifth section, the end, they are all subsumed under the Mahāyāna Abhisamaya-samādhi;
from the sixth section through the fourteenth section, the end, they are all subsumed under the Vajra-samādhi;
and from the fifteenth section through the eighteenth section, the end, they are all subsumed under the Dharma-samādhi.
From the nineteenth section through the end of the twenty-second section, these are all subsumed under the *karmavācanā* and *samādhi*.
From here on, the four sections are all subsumed under the secret teachings and principles of the various *varga*s.
He passed away on the fifteenth day of the eighth month in the fifth year of the Dazhong Xiangfu era of the Imperial Dynasty, at the age of eight, on the sixteenth day of the fourth month.
